This should wait until *after* we have test coverage for the component as I don't want to do that much refactoring without more guardrails.

subject: Fix VCR cassette matching for tests with variable document IDs
message:
Fix VCR cassette matching for tests with variable document IDs

The test_ask_document_tool_nested_agent test was failing in the full
test suite because VCR couldn't match requests - the request bodies
contained document/corpus IDs that differed between test runs.

When running tests in isolation, document IDs start from low numbers
(2, 3 as expected by cassettes). But in a full test suite, previous
tests create documents, causing IDs to be much higher (5000+).

The ID normalization logic only applied during recording, not during
playback/matching. Since VCR matches on request body by default, it
couldn't find cassette entries when IDs differed.

Fix: Exclude "body" from match_on in create_vcr_with_id_normalization.
Matching on method+path+query is sufficient to identify the correct
OpenAI API cassette entry, and allows tests to pass regardless of
actual document IDs.

message:
Fix non-PDF document export functionality

Resolves #449

The build_document_export function previously assumed all documents were PDFs,
causing failures when exporting non-PDF file types (e.g., DOCX, TXT). This
commit modifies the function to:

2. For PDF documents: continue burning annotations into the PDF as before
3. For non-PDF documents: skip PDF processing but still return annotation data
4. Return empty string for PDF bytes when document is not a PDF

Changes:
- Modified build_document_export() to conditionally process PDFs based on file_type
- Moved PyPDF2 imports inside the PDF-specific processing block
- Added comprehensive test suite for non-PDF export functionality
- Tests cover PDF (backward compatibility), text files, DOCX, and documents without pdf_file

All tests pass successfully, ensuring both backward compatibility and new functionality.

Implements separate cookie consent handling for anonymous and authenticated users:
- Anonymous users: consent stored in localStorage
- Authenticated users: consent stored in database via GraphQL mutation

- Added cookie_consent_accepted (BooleanField) to User model
- Added cookie_consent_date (DateTimeField) to User model
- Created migration 0018_user_cookie_consent_accepted_and_more
- Added AcceptCookieConsent GraphQL mutation with @login_required
- Registered mutation in schema

- Added ACCEPT_COOKIE_CONSENT GraphQL mutation to mutations.ts
- Updated CookieConsent component to check authentication status
- For authenticated users: calls mutation to save consent to database
- For anonymous users: saves consent to localStorage
- Added loading states and error handling with fallback to localStorage
- Added toast notifications for success/error states

This ensures cookie consent is properly tracked and persisted based on user type,
preventing the modal from repeatedly appearing after acceptance.

   - Avoids disruptive page reloads that lose unsaved changes

   - Added errorLink test suite for auth state management
   - All tests passing with improved auth flow validation

Benefits:
- Better user experience when sessions expire
- Preserves user context and navigation state
- Allows continued browsing of public content
- Reduces disruption from authentication errors

subject: Fix corpus chat viewport overflow on desktop
message:
Fix corpus chat viewport overflow on desktop

The chat container was growing beyond the viewport height, causing the
input field to be positioned offscreen and requiring page-level scrolling.

This fix establishes a proper CSS constraint chain from the root app
container down to individual chat components, ensuring the chat input
stays within 99vh from the viewport top and messages scroll within their
container rather than causing page overflow.

Changes:
- App.tsx: Added max-height: 100vh constraint to root div to prevent
  growth beyond viewport
- CardLayout.tsx: Added max-height constraints to CardContainer and
  ScrollableSegment to respect parent boundaries
- Corpuses.tsx: Added max-height: 99vh to CorpusViewContainer and
  max-height: 100% to MainContentArea and wrapper divs. Fixed wrapper
  div display from block to flex to properly constrain flex children
- CorpusChat.tsx: Added max-height: 100% to MessagesArea and
  conversation view motion.div to fill parent without exceeding it

The messages area now properly scrolls when content overflows while
keeping the input field fixed at the bottom within the viewport.

subject: Fix GraphQL integration for SoftDeleteManager in conversations
message:
Fix GraphQL integration for SoftDeleteManager in conversations

This commit fixes the pytest failure in PR #583 by resolving two issues with
the SoftDeleteManager and ConversationType GraphQL integration:

1. **SoftDeleteManager missing visible_to_user()**: Made SoftDeleteManager
   inherit from BaseVisibilityManager instead of models.Manager. This provides
   the visible_to_user() method required by the GraphQL layer.

2. **ConversationType missing get_queryset()**: Added get_queryset() classmethod
   to ConversationType following the same pattern as other GraphQL types
   (DocumentType, CorpusType, NoteType, UserFeedbackType).

Root cause: When GraphQL queries conversations, it calls visible_to_user() on
the manager (config/graphql/base.py:54), but SoftDeleteManager didn't have
this method. This caused AttributeError in all conversation GraphQL queries.

Fixes:
- opencontractserver/conversations/models.py:46 - SoftDeleteManager now extends BaseVisibilityManager
- config/graphql/graphene_types.py:1404 - Added get_queryset() to ConversationType

Testing:
- All 10 conversation API tests pass (opencontractserver.tests.test_long_conversation_api)
- Pre-commit hooks pass (black, isort, flake8, pyupgrade)

subject: Fix telemetry test failure by overriding MODE setting
message:
Fix telemetry test failure by overriding MODE setting

Root cause: The record_event() function has an early return that blocks
telemetry in TEST mode, but the tests were not overriding MODE setting.

The telemetry.py implementation checks:
```python
if settings.MODE == "TEST":
    return False
```

This check happens before TELEMETRY_ENABLED is evaluated, causing tests
that expect True to fail when MODE is not overridden.

Changes:
- Add MODE="DEV" to override_settings in test_record_event_success
- Add MODE="DEV" to override_settings in test_record_event_posthog_error
- Add MODE="DEV" to override_settings in test_record_event_without_properties

This allows the telemetry code path to execute during testing while still
preventing actual telemetry collection in test environments by default.

Fixes: opencontractserver/tests/test_telemetry.py:29,76,84

subject: Issue #554: Add GraphQL mutations for voting with rate limiting
message:
Issue #554: Add GraphQL mutations for voting with rate limiting

Implemented complete GraphQL voting system for messages:

**New Mutations (voting_mutations.py):**
- VoteMessageMutation: Create or update votes on messages
  - Rate limit: 60 requests/minute
  - Supports upvote and downvote
  - Allows changing vote type
  - Prevents voting on own messages

- RemoveVoteMutation: Remove user's vote from message
  - Rate limit: 60 requests/minute
  - Handles non-existent votes gracefully

**Features:**
- Full permission checks (conversation access required)
- Rate limiting (60/m for active voting)
- Vote type validation (upvote/downvote only)
- Self-vote prevention
- Idempotent operations (changing votes updates existing)
- Proper error handling and messages

**Tests (test_voting_mutations_graphql.py):**
- 11 comprehensive test cases covering:
  - Upvoting and downvoting messages
  - Changing vote types
  - Removing votes
  - Self-vote prevention
  - Invalid vote type handling
  - Permission enforcement
  - Non-existent message/vote handling
  - Multiple users voting

All mutations registered in schema and ready for frontend integration.

  - Rate limit: 20 requests/minute

  - Rate limit: 20 requests/minute
  - Allows new messages again

  - Rate limit: 20 requests/minute
  - Makes threads prominent

  - Rate limit: 20 requests/minute
  - Returns thread to normal position

- AddModeratorMutation: Add moderators to corpus
  - Rate limit: 20 requests/minute
  - Only corpus owners can add

- RemoveModeratorMutation: Remove moderators
  - Rate limit: 20 requests/minute
  - Only corpus owners can remove

- UpdateModeratorPermissionsMutation: Update moderator permissions
  - Rate limit: 20 requests/minute
  - Modify existing moderator permissions

**Features:**
- Permission validation (corpus owner or designated moderator)
- Rate limiting on all moderation actions
- Granular moderator permissions system
- Moderation action audit trail
- Proper error handling and messages

All mutations registered in schema and ready for frontend integration.

aggregated statistics about corpus participation for dashboards and leaderboards.

### Backend Models & Database
- **CorpusEngagementMetrics model** (#566)
  - OneToOne relationship with Corpus
  - Denormalized metrics for fast queries
  - Tracks threads, messages, contributors, and voting activity
  - Time-based metrics (7-day and 30-day windows)
  - Auto-updated timestamps
  - New migration: 0023_corpusengagementmetrics.py

### Celery Async Tasks (#567)
- **update_corpus_engagement_metrics** task
  - Calculate metrics for a specific corpus
  - Performance target: <200ms per corpus
  - Filters exclude soft-deleted content
  - Idempotent and safe for repeated execution
- **update_all_corpus_engagement_metrics** batch task
  - Queue updates for all corpuses
  - Ready for celerybeat scheduling

### GraphQL API (#568)
- **CorpusEngagementMetricsType** GraphQL type
- **Corpus.engagementMetrics** field
  - Returns metrics or null if not calculated
- **User.reputationGlobal** field
  - Returns global reputation score
- **User.reputationForCorpus(corpusId)** field
  - Returns corpus-specific reputation
- **corpusLeaderboard(corpusId, limit)** query
  - Top contributors by corpus reputation
  - Respects corpus permissions
- **globalLeaderboard(limit)** query

and messages, enabling semantic search and discovery of discussions within

subject: Implement configurable agent/bot profiles for conversations (Issue #634)
message:
Implement configurable agent/bot profiles for conversations (Issue #634)

This commit implements the backend for configurable agent/bot profiles
that can participate in conversations, supporting both global and
corpus-specific agents.

**Backend Implementation:**
- New `agents` app with `AgentConfiguration` model
- Support for GLOBAL and CORPUS-scoped agents
- Configurable system instructions, tools, and badge display
- Permission-based visibility using django-guardian
- FK relationship from ChatMessage to AgentConfiguration

**GraphQL API:**
- Query: `agents` (filtered, paginated) and `agent` (single item)
- Filter by corpus_id for corpus-specific agents
- Mutations: createAgentConfiguration, updateAgentConfiguration,
  deleteAgentConfiguration
- Permission checks: superusers for global agents, corpus owners for
  corpus-specific agents
- Proper IDOR prevention with user-scoped queries

**Database Schema:**
- AgentConfiguration table with constraints ensuring GLOBAL scope has
  no corpus and CORPUS scope requires corpus
- Permission tables (UserObjectPermission, GroupObjectPermission)
- ChatMessage.agent_configuration FK with SET_NULL on delete
- Indexes on scope/is_active and corpus/is_active for performance

**Tests:**
- 20 comprehensive tests covering model validation, visibility logic,
  GraphQL mutations and queries, and permission checks
- All tests passing with proper mocking and context handling

**Future Work:**
- Data migration to populate default agents (skipped - requires Docker
  access in production)
- Frontend integration to display and use agent configurations

Closes #634

subject: Add badge display support for user and bot badges in conversations (Issue #610)
message:
Add badge display support for user and bot badges in conversations (Issue #610)

This commit implements the display of user-earned badges and bot/agent badges next to usernames in conversation threads and chat messages, as specified in issue #610.

## Changes

### Frontend Types (`src/types/graphql-api.ts`)
- Added `AgentConfigurationType` to represent bot/agent configuration
- Added `UserBadgeType` and `BadgeType` for badge data structures
- Updated `ChatMessageType` to include `agentConfiguration` field

### GraphQL Queries (`src/graphql/queries.ts`)
- Updated `GET_THREAD_DETAIL` query to fetch `agentConfiguration` for messages
- Updated `GET_CHAT_MESSAGES` query to include agent configuration and creator info
- Both queries now fetch badge display data (name, description, badgeConfig, avatarUrl)

### Badge Display Component (`src/components/badges/MessageBadges.tsx`)
- New unified component for displaying both user badges and agent badges
- Renders compact pill-style badges with icons and tooltips
- Supports limiting number of badges displayed (default: 3)
- Shows "+X more" indicator when user has additional badges
- Consistent visual styling for both user and bot badges

### Badge Fetching Hook (`src/hooks/useMessageBadges.ts`)
- New hook `useMessageBadges` to fetch user badges for message creators
- Returns a Map of user ID → badges for efficient lookup
- Supports filtering by corpus for corpus-specific badges
- Uses cache-first fetch policy to avoid redundant requests

### Thread Components Integration
- **MessageItem** (`src/components/threads/MessageItem.tsx`):
  - Added `userBadges` prop to display badges next to username
  - Updated layout to show username and badges on same row
  - Integrated `MessageBadges` component into message header

- **MessageTree** (`src/components/threads/MessageTree.tsx`):
  - Added `badgesByUser` prop to pass badge data to child messages
  - Recursively passes badge map through message tree
  - Looks up badges for each message creator

- **ThreadDetail** (`src/components/threads/ThreadDetail.tsx`):
  - Uses `useMessageBadges` hook to fetch badges for all message creators
  - Extracts unique user IDs from messages
  - Filters out agent messages (only fetch badges for human users)
  - Passes badge data down to MessageTree

## Implementation Details

### Badge Priority
- Agent badges are shown first (for bot-generated messages)
- User badges are shown next (up to maxBadges limit)
- Badges beyond the limit show "+X more" indicator

### Performance Considerations
- Badge fetch uses cache-first policy to minimize API calls
- Single batch query for all user badges in a thread
- Efficient Map-based lookup for rendering

### Visual Design
- Mini-sized badge pills (0.7em font size)
- Icon + label display format
- Hover tooltips with detailed badge information
- Consistent with existing Badge component styling

## Testing
- All code passes prettier formatting checks
- No linting errors
- Ready for component tests in follow-up work

## Related Issues
- Depends on: #634 (Backend: Configurable Agent/Bot Profiles)
- Part of: #572 (Social Features Epic)
- Implements: #610 (Display user badges in conversation/chat UI)

Closes #610

subject: fix: Enable anonymous user access to public conversations
message:
fix: Enable anonymous user access to public conversations

Fixes #621 - Allows anonymous users to view public discussion threads in the corpus forum view.

## Changes

### Frontend
- Fixed GraphQL query type: Changed `$conversationType: String` to `$conversationType: ConversationTypeEnum` in GET_CONVERSATIONS query

### Backend - Permission Fixes
1. **Removed login requirements** (config/graphql/queries.py):
   - Removed `@login_required` from `resolve_conversations`, `resolve_conversation`, and `resolve_search_conversations`
   - Added anonymous user handling in search (user_id=None)

2. **Fixed manager delegation** (opencontractserver/conversations/models.py):
   - Added `visible_to_user()` to `ConversationManager` and `ChatMessageManager` to properly delegate to queryset
   - Ensures custom visibility logic in `SoftDeleteQuerySet` is used

3. **Fixed Relay Node resolution** (config/graphql/graphene_types.py):
   - Added `get_node()` classmethod to `ConversationType`
   - Prevents Graphene Relay from bypassing permission checks on single conversation queries

### Tests
Added comprehensive anonymous user test suite (5 new tests):
- Anonymous users can see public conversations
- Anonymous users cannot see private conversations
- Single conversation query respects permissions
- Corpus filtering works for anonymous users

All 8 conversation query tests pass.

## Security
Anonymous users can only view `is_public=True` conversations. Private conversations and user-specific shares remain protected.

subject: feat: Add document-specific discussions view (Issue #622)
message:
feat: Add document-specific discussions view (Issue #622)

Implements discussion threads within the DocumentKnowledgeBase viewer as a sidebar
tab, following the query parameter routing pattern for document-scoped features.

## Changes Made

### Core Components
- **DocumentDiscussionsContent**: New bridge component for sidebar integration
  - Handles thread list/detail switching within document sidebar
  - Uses ?thread= query param for navigation (keeps document in view)
  - Supports back navigation to thread list
  - Includes CreateThreadButton for starting new discussions

### Type Updates
- Updated SidebarViewMode union type to include "discussions" mode
- Maintains type safety across all sidebar view modes

### Component Enhancements
- **ThreadList**: Added optional `onThreadClick` callback prop
  - Enables custom navigation behavior (sidebar vs full-page)
  - Passes callback through to ThreadListItem components

- **ThreadListItem**: Added navigation callback support
  - Uses callback if provided, otherwise falls back to default navigation
  - Maintains backward compatibility with existing usage

- **ThreadDetail**: Added `compact` and `documentId` props
  - Compact mode optimizes layout for sidebar (narrower padding)
  - documentId reserved for future document-specific filtering

### DocumentKnowledgeBase Integration
- Auto-opens sidebar when ?thread= param detected
  - Uses unstable_batchedUpdates to prevent render cascade
  - Sets mode to "half" to keep document visible alongside sidebar
  - Listens to selectedThreadId reactive var for URL changes

- Added Discussions tab to all sidebar states:
  - Desktop (panel open) - toggleable tab
  - Desktop (panel closed) - expandable tab
  - Mobile - bottom tab bar
  - All tabs show MessageSquare icon

- Integrated DocumentDiscussionsContent for discussions mode rendering

### Documentation
- Updated routing_system.md to document ?thread= query parameter
  - Added to Selection Parameters table with "Component-local" designation
  - Added example URL: /d/john/corpus/doc?thread=thread-456
  - Noted as document-sidebar specific (not CentralRouteManager-managed)

### Code Quality
- Fixed TypeScript diagnostics (unused imports)
- All 412 existing tests continue to pass
- Linting passes with no issues

## Implementation Notes

- Follows routing mantra: uses query params for document context
- Different from corpus discussions (which use full-page routes)
- Query param approach keeps document in view while browsing threads
- Reactive var (selectedThreadId) manages thread selection state
- Component-local URL management (not in CentralRouteManager)

## Optional Enhancements (Not Implemented)
- Thread count badge on Discussions tab (requires additional GraphQL query)
- Component tests for DocumentDiscussionsContent (can be added in follow-up)

Both marked as "not critical for MVP" in issue specification.

Related to Epic #581 (Discussion System)
Closes #622

subject: security: Implement write-permission-required mention filtering
message:
security: Implement write-permission-required mention filtering

**Problem:**
Current mention system uses `.visible_to_user()` which only checks READ
permission. This allows read-only users to autocomplete/mention resources
they can't meaningfully contribute to, potentially creating confusion and
revealing the existence of private resources through autocomplete.

**Solution:**
Implemented comprehensive mention permission model requiring write access
for private resources:

### Backend Changes (config/graphql/queries.py)

**Corpus Mentions** (`@corpus:slug`):
- Requires CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE permission on corpus
- OR user is creator
- OR corpus is public
- Anonymous users cannot mention

**Document Mentions** (`@document:slug` or full path):
- Requires CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE permission on document
- OR user is creator
- OR document is in a corpus where user has write permission
- OR document is public AND (no corpus OR public corpus OR user has read access)
- Anonymous users cannot mention

### Security Improvements

1. **IDOR Protection**: Autocomplete never reveals inaccessible resources
2. **Write Permission Required**: Private resources require contribution access
3. **Public Resource Access**: Public resources mentionable by anyone
4. **Viewer-Filtered Rendering**: `mentionedResources` filters per viewer (already implemented)
5. **Graceful Degradation**: Inaccessible mentions render as plain text

### Documentation

**New Spec Document** (`docs/permissioning/mention_permissioning_spec.md`):
- Complete permission model specification
- IDOR protection strategies
- Backend/frontend implementation details
- Test requirements and scenarios
- Security audit checklist

**Updated Permissioning Guide** (`docs/permissioning/consolidated_permissioning_guide.md`):
- Added "@ Mention Permissions" section
- Permission rules for corpuses and documents
- Example scenarios with different user roles
- Integration with existing permission system
- DRY approach leveraging guardian permissions

### Testing Requirements

**Backend Tests** (to be written):
- Corpus autocomplete respects write permissions
- Document autocomplete respects write + corpus permissions
- Public resources mentionable with read access
- Anonymous users blocked from mentioning
- IDOR protection verified

**Frontend Tests** (existing - no changes needed):
- Autocomplete displays backend-filtered results
- Frontend trusts backend (no client-side filtering)

### Migration Notes

- No data migration needed (query-time filtering only)
- Existing mentions gracefully degrade if permission changes
- Permission changes take effect immediately
- Backward compatible with existing mention system

**Rationale:**
Mentioning a resource implies drawing attention to it in a collaborative
context. Read-only viewers shouldn't be mentioning resources they can't
contribute to. This aligns with the principle that mentions are for active
collaboration, not passive viewing.

See: docs/permissioning/mention_permissioning_spec.md

Related to #623

feat(backend): Implement write-permission-required mention system with comprehensive tests

BREAKING CHANGE: Mention autocomplete now requires write permissions on resources instead of just read access. This change enhances security by ensuring only users who can contribute to a resource can mention it.

## Security Enhancements
- Implemented write-permission-required model for mention autocomplete
- Added IDOR protection with silent filtering (no information leakage)
- Ensures private resources never appear in autocomplete for unauthorized users

## Backend Changes
- Updated `resolve_search_corpuses_for_mention` to check CREATE/UPDATE/REMOVE permissions
- Updated `resolve_search_documents_for_mention` to check document AND corpus write permissions
- Fixed guardian permission mapping (DELETE → 'remove_corpus', not 'delete_corpus')
- Fixed Document-Corpus relationship (ManyToMany via Corpus.documents, reverse: 'corpus')

## Test Coverage
- Created `test_mention_permissions.py` with 18 comprehensive tests (all passing ✅)
  - CorpusMentionPermissionTestCase: 8 tests
  - DocumentMentionPermissionTestCase: 7 tests
  - MentionIDORProtectionTestCase: 3 tests
- Created `test_mention_graphql_integration.py` with 7 GraphQL integration tests
- Frontend component tests: 14/14 passing (ResourceMentionPicker, MentionChip)

## Documentation
- Created `docs/permissioning/mention_permissioning_spec.md` (608 lines)
  - Complete permission model specification
  - IDOR protection strategies
  - Security audit checklist
  - Implementation examples
- Updated `docs/permissioning/consolidated_permissioning_guide.md` (+249 lines)
  - Added "@ Mention Permissions" section
  - Documented core principles and rules
  - Added backend/frontend implementation patterns

## Key Permission Rules
**Corpuses**: Mentionable if user is creator, has write permission (CREATE/UPDATE/REMOVE), or corpus is public
**Documents**: Mentionable if user is creator, has direct write permission, has write permission on containing corpus, or document is public AND (standalone OR in public/accessible corpus)
**Anonymous Users**: Cannot mention any resources (must be authenticated)

## Technical Fixes
- Discovered Document model uses ManyToMany relationship with Corpus (via Corpus.documents field)
- The reverse relation is accessible via 'corpus' (not 'corpus_set')
- Fixed all test setup to use `corpus.documents.add(document)` instead of FK assignment
- Fixed permission codename mapping: PermissionTypes.DELETE → 'remove_corpus'

## Files Changed
- `config/graphql/queries.py`: Updated search queries with write permission filtering
- `opencontractserver/tests/test_mention_permissions.py`: New file (755 lines, 18 tests)
- `opencontractserver/tests/test_mention_graphql_integration.py`: New file (331 lines, 7 tests)
- `docs/permissioning/mention_permissioning_spec.md`: New file (608 lines)
- `docs/permissioning/consolidated_permissioning_guide.md`: Updated (+249 lines)

Closes #623 (backend portion with comprehensive test coverage)

subject: Fix corpus discussion thread navigation and routing
message:
Fix corpus discussion thread navigation and routing

Fixes #646

**Problem:**
Clicking on discussion threads in the Corpus Discussions tab failed to navigate to the thread detail view due to:
1. Missing onThreadClick callback prop in ThreadList component
2. Incomplete GraphQL queries missing slug data needed for URL construction
3. CorpusThreadRoute not integrated with CentralRouteManager routing system
4. Apollo Client cache returning stale null responses without hitting backend
5. GraphQL schema mismatches (non-existent userVote and deletedBy fields)

**Solution:**

Backend:
- Added comprehensive logging to ConversationType.get_node() for debugging
- Fixed GraphQL schema by removing non-existent fields (userVote, deletedBy)
- Updated mutations to return conversation objects in responses

Frontend:
- Integrated thread routing into CentralRouteManager following "One True Routing Mantra"
  - Added openedThread reactive var for entity state
  - Added Phase 1 thread resolution with corpus context
  - Implemented proper thread route parsing (/c/user/corpus/discussions/threadId)
- Refactored CorpusThreadRoute to be a "dumb consumer" that only reads reactive vars
- Fixed CorpusDiscussionsView to pass onThreadClick prop to ThreadList
- Enhanced GET_CONVERSATIONS and GET_THREAD_DETAIL queries to fetch full corpus slug data
- Updated CREATE_THREAD mutation to return conversation object
- Fixed ThreadListItem to use proper slug-based navigation URLs
- Added cache eviction before thread queries to force fresh data fetches
- Changed thread query fetchPolicy to "network-only" to bypass stale cache
- Added navigation utilities for corpus thread routing
- Added comprehensive debug logging throughout the navigation flow

**Testing:**
- Verified thread navigation from Discussions tab works correctly
- Confirmed GraphQL queries successfully fetch conversation data
- Tested URL construction with proper corpus/user slugs
- Validated cache eviction forces backend queries

subject: feat: Resolve dual source of truth between M2M corpus.documents and DocumentPath (Closes #654)
message:
feat: Resolve dual source of truth between M2M corpus.documents and DocumentPath (Closes #654)

This commit implements a comprehensive solution for migrating from the legacy M2M
corpus.documents relationship to the new DocumentPath-based versioning system while
maintaining backward compatibility.

## Key Changes

### 1. Custom M2M Manager (`opencontractserver/documents/managers.py`)
- Implemented `DocumentCorpusRelationshipManager` that intercepts M2M operations
- Reads from DocumentPath as source of truth
- Writes create DocumentPath records transparently
- Shows deprecation warnings to guide migration
- Maintains full backward compatibility with existing code

### 2. Thread-Local Context (`DocumentPathContext`)
- Provides user and path context for legacy M2M operations
- Uses contextvars for async-safe thread-local storage
- Auto-generates filesystem paths from document titles
- Supports custom folders and path prefixes

### 3. Explicit Corpus Methods
- `add_document()`: Recommended replacement for corpus.documents.add()
- `remove_document()`: Soft-delete with full audit trail
- `get_documents()`: Query active documents via DocumentPath
- `document_count()`: Efficient count of active documents

### 4. Migration Management Command
- `sync_m2m_to_documentpath`: Syncs existing M2M relationships
- Supports dry-run mode for safety
- Handles path conflicts automatically
- Provides detailed progress reporting

### 5. Auto-Installation
- Custom manager installs automatically via AppConfig
- No manual intervention required for existing deployments

### 6. Comprehensive Test Suite
- Unit tests for all components
- Integration tests for M2M sync
- Backward compatibility tests
- Edge case coverage

## Benefits
✅ Single source of truth (DocumentPath)
✅ Full backward compatibility
✅ Audit trail for all operations
✅ Graceful migration path
✅ No breaking changes

## Migration Strategy
1. Deploy with custom manager (automatic)
2. Run sync command for existing data
3. Update code to use new methods incrementally
4. Remove M2M field in future major version

## Testing
All tests pass with comprehensive coverage of:
- DocumentPathContext functionality
- Custom manager operations
- New Corpus methods
- Migration command with edge cases
- Backward compatibility scenarios

subject: refactor: Preserve document identity in add_document() and separate import_content()
message:
refactor: Preserve document identity in add_document() and separate import_content()

This commit completes Issue #654 Phase 2 by:

1. Refactoring add_document() to preserve document identity:
   - Returns the SAME document object (unchanged ID)
   - Simply creates a DocumentPath link to the corpus
   - Same document can exist at multiple paths in same corpus
   - Status codes: 'added' (new link) or 'already_exists'

2. Adding new import_content() method:
   - Content-based imports with SHA-256 deduplication
   - Handles cross-corpus deduplication (I1 rule)
   - Status codes: 'created', 'updated', 'unchanged', 'cross_corpus_import'

3. Removing backward compatibility layer:
   - Disabled custom M2M manager in apps.py
   - All code must use new explicit API methods

4. Updating all test files (50+) to use new API:
   - corpus.add_document(document=doc, user=user)
   - corpus.get_documents() instead of corpus.documents.all()
   - corpus.document_count() instead of corpus.documents.count()

Key architectural insight: Document versioning (Content Tree) is independent
from corpus path tracking (Path Tree). Adding a document to a corpus creates
a link, not a copy. Content deduplication is reserved for file imports.

message:
feat: Comprehensive revamp of corpus export/import for V2.0 (#502)

This PR completely revamps the corpus export/import functionality to support
all features added since the original design, while maintaining full backward
compatibility with V1 exports.

## New Features Supported

### Structural Annotations
- Export/import StructuralAnnotationSet with content-based deduplication
- Shared structural annotations avoid duplication across corpus copies
- Preserves parser metadata and structural relationships

### Corpus Folders
- Export complete folder hierarchy with full paths
- Import reconstructs tree structure preserving parent relationships
- Supports folder metadata (color, icon, tags)

### Document Versioning
- Export complete DocumentPath version trees
- Preserves version history including deleted versions
- Maintains parent-child version relationships

### Relationships
- Export both document-level and corpus-level relationships
- ID mapping during import maintains annotation references
- Separate handling for structural vs user relationships

### Agent Configuration
- Export corpus and document agent instructions
- Preserves custom system prompts per corpus

### Markdown Descriptions
- Export current markdown description
- Full revision history with diffs and snapshots
- Preserves author attribution and timestamps

### Conversations (Optional)
- Optional export of discussion threads and messages
- Includes message votes and engagement data
- Controlled via include_conversations flag

## Technical Implementation

### Export Pipeline (export_tasks_v2.py)
- package_corpus_export_v2: Main V2 export orchestration
- Comprehensive export utilities in utils/export_v2.py
- Enhanced packaging.py with V2 corpus fields

### Import Pipeline (import_tasks_v2.py)
- import_corpus_v2: Detects format version and routes appropriately
- _import_corpus_v1: Preserves original V1 import logic
- _import_corpus_v2: New comprehensive V2 import
- Full import utilities in utils/import_v2.py

### Type Definitions (types/dicts.py)
- OpenContractsExportDataJsonV2Type: Main V2 export format
- StructuralAnnotationSetExport: Structural annotations
- CorpusFolderExport: Folder hierarchy
- DocumentPathExport: Version trees
- AgentConfigExport: Agent configurations
- DescriptionRevisionExport: Markdown revisions
- ConversationExport, ChatMessageExport, MessageVoteExport: Discussions

## Backward Compatibility

✅ V1 exports remain fully importable
✅ Version detection via "version" field in data.json
✅ V1 import logic preserved in _import_corpus_v1
✅ V2 adds new fields without changing V1 fields
✅ Graceful handling of missing V2 fields

## What's NOT Exported

Vector embeddings are intentionally excluded:
- Can be regenerated from content
- Make exports very large
- Different deployments use different embedders
- Regeneration ensures consistency with target system

## Design Goals Achieved

1. ✅ Backward Compatibility - V1 exports still work
2. ✅ Completeness - ALL corpus data captured
3. ✅ Shareability - Perfect for publishing datasets
4. ✅ Efficiency - Structural annotations deduplicated
5. ✅ Flexibility - Optional conversation export

## Files Changed

- docs/architecture/corpus_export_import_v2.md (NEW)
  Comprehensive documentation of V2 system

- opencontractserver/types/dicts.py (MODIFIED)
  Added V2 TypedDict definitions for all export components

- opencontractserver/utils/packaging.py (MODIFIED)
  Enhanced package_corpus_for_export with v2_format flag

- opencontractserver/utils/export_v2.py (NEW)
  Export utilities for all V2 components

- opencontractserver/utils/import_v2.py (NEW)
  Import utilities for all V2 components

- opencontractserver/tasks/export_tasks_v2.py (NEW)
  Main V2 export task orchestration

- opencontractserver/tasks/import_tasks_v2.py (NEW)
  V2 import with backward compatibility

## Next Steps

- Add GraphQL mutations for V2 export/import
- Write comprehensive unit and integration tests
- Update frontend to support conversation export toggle
- Performance testing with large corpora

## Related Issues

Closes #502

Co-authored-by: u7aab0165b0b1162a <u7aab0165b0b1162a@users.invalid>

subject: fix: Use singleton PostHog client to ensure events are sent
message:
fix: Use singleton PostHog client to ensure events are sent

The previous implementation created a new PostHog client for each
telemetry event but never called shutdown() or flush(). Since the
PostHog SDK is async by default (sync_mode=False), events were queued
in memory but never sent before the client went out of scope.

Changes:
- Implement singleton pattern for PostHog client in config/telemetry.py
- Add atexit handler to flush events on process shutdown
- Add _reset_posthog_client() helper for test isolation
- Update tests to reset singleton between test runs

subject: refactor: Always create new document for new path uploads
message:
refactor: Always create new document for new path uploads

Changed document import behavior: uploads to a new path ALWAYS create
a new document, even if content already exists elsewhere. This simplifies
the mental model and ensures pdf_file is always populated.

Previous behavior:
- Same corpus, same content, new path → "linked" to existing document
- Different corpus, same content → "created_from_existing" with provenance

New behavior:
- Any new path → "created" with new document
- Artifacts (pawls, txt_extract, etc.) are still shared from existing docs
- Provenance is tracked via source_document field
- Each document gets its own version_tree_id

This ensures:
1. Every upload results in a document with populated pdf_file
2. Simpler reasoning about document ownership
3. No unexpected document reuse

Updated all affected tests to reflect new behavior.

message:
fix: resolve migration failure for existing installs (documents.0023)

Migration 0023 added version_tree_id with default=uuid.uuid4 and immediately
added a UniqueConstraint. The problem is that Django evaluates uuid.uuid4
once at migration time, so all existing rows got the same UUID, causing
the unique constraint to fail.

Fix:
- Changed version_tree_id to null=True in 0023 (no default)
- Moved AddConstraint to 0024 after data migration populates unique UUIDs
- Added AlterField in 0024 to make field non-nullable after population

subject: feat: Add Cloudflare Worker for social media preview (OG) metadata
message:
feat: Add Cloudflare Worker for social media preview (OG) metadata

Implements a Cloudflare Worker that intercepts crawler requests and
injects Open Graph metadata for rich social media previews on platforms
like Twitter, LinkedIn, Slack, and Discord.

Components:
- Cloudflare Worker (cloudflare-og-worker/)
  - Detects social media crawlers via User-Agent
  - Parses SPA routes to extract entity type and slug
  - Fetches metadata from Django GraphQL API
  - Generates HTML with OG/Twitter meta tags
  - Returns original SPA for regular browsers

- Django Backend additions
  - OgMetadataType GraphQL type for metadata queries
  - ogMetadata query supporting corpus/document/user entities
  - Generates appropriate titles, descriptions, and image URLs

- Documentation
  - docs/architecture/social-media-previews.md with full architecture

Supported entities:
- Corpuses: /c/{user_slug}/{corpus_slug}
- Documents: /c/{user_slug}/{corpus_slug}/document/{doc_id}
- Users: /u/{user_slug}

See docs/architecture/social-media-previews.md for deployment guide.

subject: fix: Use atomic conditional update for race condition prevention
message:
fix: Use atomic conditional update for race condition prevention

Replace select_for_update() with atomic conditional update to prevent
race conditions without connection issues in async context.

The new approach:
1. get_or_create() to get/create the record
2. If created, we own it (status already RUNNING)
3. If not created, atomically try to claim by updating status to RUNNING
   only if current status is NOT already RUNNING or COMPLETED
4. If atomic update affects 0 rows, another task owns it - skip

This avoids the connection issues caused by select_for_update() with
database_sync_to_async while still preventing duplicate execution.

subject: fix: Use DocumentPath as source of truth for corpus action triggers
message:
fix: Use DocumentPath as source of truth for corpus action triggers

The document versioning architecture (Issue #654) introduced DocumentPath
as the source of truth for corpus-document relationships, but the corpus
action trigger system still relied on the M2M relationship. This caused
actions to not fire when documents were added via import_document().

Root cause: import_document() creates DocumentPath records but doesn't
update the Corpus.documents M2M relationship. The signal handlers queried
the M2M to find corpuses, returning empty results.

Solution: Replace signal-based triggering with direct invocation:

- set_doc_lock_state(): Now queries DocumentPath to find corpuses and
  triggers process_corpus_action directly when processing completes

- add_document(): Triggers actions directly if document is ready
  (backend_lock=False), with comment pointing to set_doc_lock_state
  for locked documents

- import_document(): Same pattern as add_document() - triggers actions
  directly if document is ready

- Removed redundant signal handlers (handle_document_added_to_corpus,
  handle_document_processing_complete) that relied on M2M queries

This ensures DocumentPath is consistently used as the source of truth
for determining corpus membership throughout the action trigger system.

subject: fix: Add database connection cleanup for serial tests
message:
fix: Add database connection cleanup for serial tests

The tests in test_agent_corpus_action_task.py were failing with:
- psycopg2.OperationalError: terminating connection due to administrator command
- django.db.utils.InterfaceError: connection already closed

Root cause: These tests use asyncio.run() which creates a new event loop for
async Django ORM operations. When asyncio.run() finishes, it closes the event
loop but the database connections opened during async execution may be left
in a corrupted/stale state in the connection pool. Subsequent tests then fail
when they try to use these stale connections.

Fix: Add database connection management to the pytest setup/teardown hooks:
- In setup: Call db.close_old_connections() to clear stale connections
- In teardown: Call db.connections.close_all() to fully reset the pool

This ensures each serial test starts with fresh database connections,
preventing connection pool corruption from async code.

transactions are thread-bound. When asyncio.run() closes its event loop,

and "terminating connection due to administrator command" errors.

- Add try/except around teardown cleanup for robustness

The teardown hook runs AFTER the test completes, when database access
is still available, so connection cleanup works correctly there.

subject: fix: Add network recovery on mobile screen unlock
message:
fix: Add network recovery on mobile screen unlock

Resolves #697 - Adds automatic reconnection when the app resumes from
background (e.g., screen unlock on mobile).

Changes:
- Add useNetworkStatus hook to detect page visibility and network changes
- Add NetworkStatusHandler component to refetch Apollo queries on resume
- Update useThreadWebSocket to reconnect WebSocket on visibility change
- Update useAgentChat to detect disconnection on visibility change
- Show toast notifications for connectivity changes

The solution monitors:
- visibilitychange event for page visibility (suspend/resume)
- online/offline events for network status

On mobile, when the screen is locked, the app may be suspended and
connections dropped. This fix detects when the app resumes and:
1. Refetches all active Apollo Client queries
2. Reconnects WebSocket connections that were dropped
3. Informs users of connectivity status via toast notifications

subject: fix: Add processing indicator for agent responses before content arrives
message:
fix: Add processing indicator for agent responses before content arrives

Closes #687

Previously, when an agent started processing a response, a shell/placeholder
message would appear instantly without any visual indication that work was
ongoing. Users had no way to know the system was actively processing.

This change adds an animated "Agent is thinking..." indicator that displays
when:
- The message is from the assistant (isAssistant: true)
- The message is not yet complete (isComplete: false)
- No content has been received yet (content.trim().length === 0)
- No timeline entries have been received yet (effectiveHasTimeline: false)

The indicator uses an animated bouncing dots pattern with the app's blue
color scheme, providing clear visual feedback that the agent is working.
Once the agent starts sending content or timeline entries, the indicator
smoothly transitions to either the timeline view or message bubble.

subject: feat: Migrate badge notifications from polling to WebSocket (Issue #637)
message:
feat: Migrate badge notifications from polling to WebSocket (Issue #637)

## Overview
Replaces Apollo Client polling (30s intervals) with real-time WebSocket-based
notification delivery for ALL notification types (BADGE, REPLY, MENTION,
THREAD_REPLY, moderation actions). Provides instant notification delivery
with zero latency and dramatically reduces server load.

## Backend Changes

### WebSocket Consumer
- **New file**: `config/websocket/consumers/notification_updates.py`
  - `NotificationUpdatesConsumer`: Async WebSocket consumer for real-time notifications
  - User-specific channel groups (`notification_user_{user_id}`) prevent IDOR
  - Handles NOTIFICATION_CREATED, NOTIFICATION_UPDATED, NOTIFICATION_DELETED
  - Heartbeat/ping-pong for connection health monitoring
  - Graceful error handling and cleanup on disconnect

### Signal Broadcasting
- **Modified**: `opencontractserver/notifications/signals.py`
  - Added `broadcast_notification_via_websocket()` helper function
  - Integrated WebSocket broadcasting in all signal handlers:
    - `create_reply_notification` (REPLY notifications)
    - `create_mention_notification` (MENTION notifications)
    - `create_badge_notification` (BADGE notifications)
    - `create_moderation_notification` (moderation actions)
  - Broadcasts to user-specific channel groups via Django Channels layer
  - Bulk notifications properly broadcast individual items
  - Failures don't break signal handlers (notifications still save to DB)

### ASGI Routing
- **Modified**: `config/asgi.py`
  - Registered `ws/notification-updates/` WebSocket endpoint
  - Uses existing authentication middleware (Auth0/JWT)
  - Logs registered WebSocket patterns on startup

## Frontend Changes

### WebSocket Hook
- **New file**: `frontend/src/hooks/useNotificationWebSocket.ts`
  - `useNotificationWebSocket`: Complete WebSocket connection lifecycle management
  - Auto-reconnection with exponential backoff (2s → 4s → 8s → 16s, max 8x)
  - Heartbeat monitoring every 30s to detect stale connections
  - Integrated with `useNetworkStatus` for mobile screen unlock reconnection
  - Callbacks for notification created/updated/deleted events
  - Recent notifications buffer (last 50) for UI state
  - Connection state tracking (disconnected/connecting/connected/error)

### Badge Notifications Migration
- **Modified**: `frontend/src/hooks/useBadgeNotifications.ts`
  - Completely refactored from polling to WebSocket
  - Maintains backward-compatible interface (`newBadges`, `clearNewBadges`)
  - Added `connectionState` export for debugging/UI feedback
  - Zero latency badge delivery (instant vs 0-30s polling delay)
  - Removed Apollo Client polling logic entirely

### WebSocket URL Helper
- **Modified**: `frontend/src/components/chat/get_websockets.ts`
  - Added `getNotificationUpdatesWebSocket()` function
  - Handles protocol conversion (http→ws, https→wss)
  - Token parameter encoding for authentication

## Testing

### Backend Tests
- **New file**: `opencontractserver/tests/test_notification_websocket.py`
  - Authentication and authorization tests
  - IDOR prevention (user isolation) tests
  - Ping/pong and heartbeat functionality
  - Channel layer broadcasting tests
  - Multi-user concurrent connection tests
  - Disconnect cleanup verification
  - Signal integration tests

## Security

- **IDOR Prevention**: User-specific channel groups ensure users only receive their own notifications
- **Authentication**: WebSocket middleware validates JWT/Auth0 tokens before accepting connections
- **Authorization**: Consumer validates user is authenticated before subscribing to channel
- **No data leakage**: Notifications filtered on backend, not frontend
- **Rate limiting**: Exponential backoff prevents reconnection spam

## Performance

- **User-specific channels**: Each user has dedicated channel group (not global broadcast)
- **Database indexes**: Leverages existing indexes on Notification model
- **Bulk operations**: Thread participant notifications use bulk_create + batch broadcasting
- **Efficient serialization**: Minimal JSON payloads with only essential fields
- **Connection pooling**: Multiple tabs for same user share channel group
- **Graceful degradation**: WebSocket failures don't break notification creation

## Impact

- **Zero latency**: Badge awards appear instantly (vs 0-30s polling delay)
- **Reduced server load**: Eliminates continuous polling from all connected clients
- **Scalability**: WebSocket connections more efficient than repeated HTTP polls
- **Real-time UX**: Instant feedback for all notification types
- **Mobile friendly**: Auto-reconnection on screen unlock via useNetworkStatus integration

## Documentation

- **Updated**: `CHANGELOG.md`
  - Added comprehensive feature description
  - Technical architecture details
  - Security and performance notes
  - File locations and line numbers

Closes #637

discussion threads. When new threads are created or messages are posted,
configured corpus actions can trigger AI agents to review content and
take moderation actions.

- Celery tasks for processing thread-based corpus actions
- Frontend UI updates with moderation tool info

Use cases enabled:
- Auto-delete messages with prohibited content
- Auto-lock threads discussing prohibited topics
- Welcome messages for new threads
- Auto-pin important announcements

Includes comprehensive backend (30 tests) and frontend (18 tests) coverage.

subject: fix: Default first-time visitors to anonymous mode instead of prompting login
message:
fix: Default first-time visitors to anonymous mode instead of prompting login

Previously, when Auth0's getAccessTokenSilently() failed with login_required,
AuthGate would always redirect to login - even for first-time visitors who
had never authenticated before.

Now AuthGate uses a localStorage flag (oc_has_authenticated) to distinguish:
- First-time visitors: default to anonymous mode (no login prompt)
- Returning users with expired sessions: redirect to Auth0 login

This improves UX by not forcing login prompts on users who are just browsing.

preventing duplicates and only showing the error if the query truly failed.

message:
fix: properly signal token expiration to frontend (closes #744)

The Auth0RemoteUserJSONWebTokenBackend.authenticate() method was catching
all exceptions including JSONWebTokenExpired and returning None. This
caused the GraphQL layer to return a generic "User is not authenticated"
error instead of "Signature has expired", preventing the frontend from
detecting token expiration and triggering automatic token refresh.

Changes:
- Re-raise JSONWebTokenExpired in Auth0RemoteUserJSONWebTokenBackend so
  frontend receives "Signature has expired" message
- Add auth_error dict to WebSocket middleware scope with code and message
- Add WS_CLOSE_TOKEN_EXPIRED (4001) and WS_CLOSE_TOKEN_INVALID (4002)
  close codes for WebSocket connections
- Add comprehensive tests for token expiration handling

Frontend's errorLink.ts already handles "Signature has expired" by clearing
auth state and triggering page reload for silent Auth0 token refresh.

  behavior (no PAWLS token generation)

subject: fix: resolve auth race conditions causing NS_BINDING_ABORTED errors
message:
fix: resolve auth race conditions causing NS_BINDING_ABORTED errors

Fixes multiple race conditions in the authentication flow:

1. GET_ME query aborted on refresh: Added authInitCompleteVar reactive
   variable that's only set true AFTER cache operations complete. The
   GET_ME query now waits for both auth_token AND auth_init_complete.

2. Auth0 callback race condition: During Auth0 callback, isAuthenticated
   is briefly false while SDK updates state. Now verify auth status via
   getAccessTokenSilently instead of checking URL for auth code. Added
   authFlowInProgressRef to prevent duplicate auth flows.

3. Forced login after logout: Removed auto-redirect behavior. Users now
   stay anonymous after logout and can login via UI if desired.

Changes:
- cache.ts: Add authInitCompleteVar reactive variable
- AuthGate.tsx: Verify auth via getAccessTokenSilently, prevent duplicate
  flows, remove auto-redirect to login
- App.tsx: Update GET_ME skip condition to include auth_init_complete
- AuthGate.test.tsx: Update tests for new behavior

Closes #741

subject: fix: Reconnect notification WebSocket when auth token becomes available
message:
fix: Reconnect notification WebSocket when auth token becomes available

The WebSocket was failing to connect because:
1. App loads and useBadgeNotifications() runs before auth completes
2. Initial connection attempt has no token → 403 error
3. Token change effect only reconnected if connectionState === "connected"
4. Since initial connection failed, state was never "connected" → ignored

Fix: Reconnect when token becomes available regardless of current state.

setTimeout to simulate async token fetch. This timer could fire after
the test completed, polluting subsequent tests with the wrong token
value. Using vi.useFakeTimers() and vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync()
ensures the timer is controlled and doesn't leak between tests.

subject: fix: Route MCP endpoints through Traefik and add SSE transport support
message:
fix: Route MCP endpoints through Traefik and add SSE transport support

The root cause of MCP connection failures with Claude and OpenAI clients
was that Traefik production routing was missing /mcp and /sse paths,
causing requests to be routed to the frontend (which returned HTML)
instead of the Django MCP server. This resulted in clients receiving
'text/html' instead of the expected 'text/event-stream'.

Changes:
- Add /mcp and /sse path prefixes to Traefik Django routing rules
- Add deprecated SSE transport at /sse for backward compatibility
- Update ASGI router to dispatch both /mcp/* and /sse/* to MCP app
- Update documentation to reflect both transport options

Fixes #759

subject: Add secure zip import with folder structure preservation
message:
Add secure zip import with folder structure preservation

Implements a safe, performant way to import zip files to a corpus while
preserving the folder structure from the zip. Key features:

Security:
- Path traversal protection (rejects .., drive letters, absolute paths)
- Zip bomb detection (compression ratio monitoring, size limits)
- Symlink rejection
- Resource limits (max files, folders, depth - all configurable)
- Hidden file filtering (.DS_Store, __MACOSX, Thumbs.db, etc.)

API:
- GraphQL mutation: importZipToCorpus with rate limiting
- Celery task: import_zip_with_folder_structure for async processing
- Three-phase processing: validation, folder creation, document import

- opencontractserver/constants/zip_import.py
- opencontractserver/utils/zip_security.py
- opencontractserver/tests/test_zip_security.py (49 tests)
- opencontractserver/tests/test_zip_import_integration.py (17 tests)

uses network-only and was working correctly.

subject: Fix close navigation to use React Router history index
message:
Fix close navigation to use React Router history index

document.referrer only captures the referrer on initial page load,
NOT during SPA navigation. Instead, use window.history.state.idx
which React Router v6 maintains for the history stack.

- idx = 0 means first page in session (no back history)
- idx > 0 means there's at least one page to go back to

This correctly handles navigation from /annotations → document → close
returning to /annotations.

subject: Fix flaky MCP telemetry test failing in parallel CI execution
message:
Fix flaky MCP telemetry test failing in parallel CI execution

The test_call_tool_records_telemetry test was failing in CI with:
  psycopg2.OperationalError: terminating connection due to administrator command

Root cause: The test used TestCase with a manual asyncio event loop and
sync_to_async to run database queries. Under heavy parallel execution in CI,
PostgreSQL connections were being terminated due to resource contention.

Fix: Mock the TOOL_HANDLERS dict directly instead of hitting the database.
This makes the test a true unit test that verifies telemetry recording
without depending on database availability during parallel test execution.

subject: Add image token support to PDF processing pipelines
message:
Add image token support to PDF processing pipelines

This commit adds comprehensive image extraction and annotation support
for PDF documents, enabling LLMs to work with images embedded in PDFs.

Key changes:

1. PAWLs Type Definitions (opencontractserver/types/dicts.py):
   - Add PawlsImageTokenPythonType for image data (base64, path, metadata)
   - Add ImageIdPythonType for referencing images in annotations
   - Extend PawlsPagePythonType with optional 'images' field
   - Extend OpenContractsSinglePageAnnotationType with 'imagesJsons' field

2. BaseEmbedder Multimodal Support (pipeline/base/embedder.py):
   - Add is_multimodal, supports_text, supports_images class attributes
   - Add _embed_image_impl() method for image embedding
   - Add embed_image() and embed_text_and_image() public methods
   - Enable future multimodal embedder implementations

3. PDF Image Extraction Utility (utils/pdf_token_extraction.py):
   - Add extract_images_from_pdf() for embedded image extraction
   - Add crop_image_from_pdf() for bounding box region cropping
   - Add _crop_pdf_region() helper using pdf2image
   - Add get_image_as_base64() and get_image_data_url() helpers
   - Support base64 encoding, content hashing, and format options

4. LlamaParser Updates (pipeline/parsers/llamaparse_parser.py):
   - Add image extraction configuration options
   - Extract embedded images from PDFs during parsing
   - Add images to PAWLs pages
   - For figure/image annotations, find matching images or crop region
   - Add _find_images_in_bounds() helper method
   - Update _create_annotation() to support image_refs parameter

5. Docling Parser Updates (pipeline/parsers/docling_parser_rest.py):
   - Add image extraction configuration options
   - Post-process microservice response to add images
   - Add _add_images_to_result() method for image extraction
   - Add _add_image_refs_to_annotation() for figure/image annotations
   - Add _find_images_in_bounds() helper method

6. GraphQL Schema Updates (config/graphql/graphene_types.py):
   - Add is_multimodal, supports_text, supports_images to PipelineComponentType

7. Registry Updates (pipeline/registry.py):
   - Add multimodal fields to PipelineComponentDefinition
   - Update _create_definition() to populate multimodal flags
   - Update to_dict() to include multimodal fields for embedders

8. Tests (tests/test_pdf_token_extraction.py):
   - Add TestExtractImagesFromPdf test class
   - Add TestCropImageFromPdf test class
   - Add TestImageHelperFunctions test class
   - Test image extraction, cropping, and helper functions

message:
Isolate StructuralAnnotationSets per corpus for multimodal embeddings

Previously, StructuralAnnotationSets were shared across corpus-isolated
document copies. This caused issues with per-corpus embeddings since
different corpuses may use different embedders with incompatible vector
dimensions (e.g., CLIP 768d vs sentence-transformer 384d).

message:

3. Retry: document.structural_annotation_set is None, tries create again
4. Fails because content_hash already exists

Fix: Use get_or_create instead of create to handle retry scenarios
gracefully by reusing the existing set.

subject: Fix preloaded files not appearing in upload modal
message:
Fix preloaded files not appearing in upload modal

When files are dropped in the corpus document browser, the modal opens
but files weren't appearing due to a timing issue with React batching.

The fix separates preloaded file handling into its own effect that:
- Uses a ref to track if files have been processed for this modal open
- Handles files arriving after the modal's initial render
- Resets the processed flag when modal closes

This ensures files dropped externally always appear in the modal.

subject: Mark additional MCP TransactionTestCase classes as serial
message:
Mark additional MCP TransactionTestCase classes as serial

Add @pytest.mark.serial and @override_settings(DATABASES={"default":
{"CONN_MAX_AGE": 0}}) to 5 more TransactionTestCase classes that use
manually created event loops with sync_to_async Django ORM operations:

- MCPScopedServerTest
- MCPScopedASGIRoutingTest (contained failing tests)
- MCPUppercaseSlugTest
- MCPScopedLifespanManagerShutdownTest
- MCPScopedASGIErrorHandlingTest

Also added CONN_MAX_AGE=0 to the existing MCPPermissionChangeTest.

These tests were failing intermittently in CI when run in parallel with
pytest-xdist due to database connection corruption. The issue occurs
because asyncio.run() creates event loops in different thread contexts
while Django's database connections are thread-bound. The CONN_MAX_AGE=0
setting prevents connection pooling issues.

Fixes test failures:
- MCPScopedASGIRoutingTest::test_asgi_returns_404_for_nonexistent_corpus
- MCPScopedASGIRoutingTest::test_asgi_returns_404_for_private_corpus

message:

conversation_type:

  (creator + explicit guardian permission + public only)
- THREAD ("thread"): Collaborative discussions with context-based
  permissions (inherits visibility from linked corpus/document)

Key changes:
- Override ConversationQuerySet.visible_to_user() with bifurcated logic
- THREAD type inherits from corpus/document (AND logic when both set)
- ChatMessageQuerySet.visible_to_user() now leverages conversation visibility
- Add ConversationQueryOptimizer helper class for request-level caching
- Add 22 comprehensive tests for permission scenarios
- Update permissioning documentation with bifurcated model details

This ensures CHAT conversations remain private to their creators while
THREAD discussions are visible to anyone who can read the linked corpus
or document, enabling collaborative discussions while protecting
personal agent conversations.

subject: Fix calc_oc_file_path missing sub_folder argument for image_content_file
message:

in the forking pipeline.

to the function call in both the model and migration.

subject: Fix test expectations for bifurcated conversation permissions
message:
Fix test expectations for bifurcated conversation permissions

The test_conversation_search tests incorrectly expected THREAD type
conversations to have restrictive (private) permissions. However, by
design, THREAD conversations inherit visibility from their linked
corpus - anyone who can see the corpus can see its threads.

Changed `other_conv` and `user2_private_conv` to use CHAT type instead
of THREAD type. CHAT type conversations have restrictive permissions
(only creator, explicit guardian permissions, or public).

This aligns the tests with the bifurcated permission model documented
in ConversationQuerySet.visible_to_user().

subject: Fix permissions on forked documents to enable annotation counts
message:
Fix permissions on forked documents to enable annotation counts

The fork task was setting permissions on the intermediate cloned document
instead of the corpus-isolated document returned by add_document(). This
caused annotation queries to fail permission checks since the actual
document in the corpus (corpus_doc) had no permissions set.

Moved set_permissions_for_obj_to_user() call to after add_document()
so permissions are set on corpus_doc, not the intermediate document.

subject: Refactor document forking to eliminate orphan intermediate documents
message:
Refactor document forking to eliminate orphan intermediate documents

The fork task was creating unnecessary intermediate documents:
1. Clone original doc via pk=None trick
2. Copy files to intermediate doc
3. Pass intermediate to add_document() which creates ANOTHER doc

This created orphan document records that were never used in any corpus,
only serving as source_document for provenance tracking.

Simplified to call add_document() directly on the original document:
- add_document already handles version_tree_id, file blob sharing,
  source_document provenance, and DocumentPath creation
- Removed ~40 lines of redundant code
- Removed unused uuid import
- Original document is now the source_document (cleaner provenance)
- No more orphan records in the database

violations.

- Old: `_{corpus_id}` or `_{uuid}`

This ensures forked corpuses have the same annotation count as originals
when documents share structural annotation sets.

subject: Fix flaky MCP validate_corpus_slug tests in parallel CI
message:
Fix flaky MCP validate_corpus_slug tests in parallel CI

Mock the Corpus.objects.visible_to_user queryset in the async
validate_corpus_slug tests to avoid database connection corruption
when running with pytest-xdist. The tests were failing intermittently
with "terminating connection due to administrator command" errors
because sync_to_async database calls in manually created event loops
can corrupt connections in parallel test environments.

The mocked approach still validates the function's logic (checking
queryset calls and return values) without hitting the actual database
in the async context.

subject: Fix anonymous user thread visibility tests to match permission model
message:
Fix anonymous user thread visibility tests to match permission model

The tests had incorrect expectations. Per the permissioning guide:
- Context inheritance: threads on public corpuses are visible to anonymous
  users regardless of the thread's own is_public flag
- Thread's is_public provides direct visibility; context inheritance
  provides inherited visibility from the resource
- MIN permission: threads on private corpuses are NOT visible to anonymous

Changes:
- Updated test_conversation_query.py AnonymousUserConversationTestCase to
  correctly test context inheritance (added private corpus for isolation)
- Updated test_conversation_search.py test_visible_to_user_with_none_user

subject: Add graceful transient failure handling for document processing pipeline
message:
Add graceful transient failure handling for document processing pipeline

This implements pipeline hardening to prevent documents from being marked
as "ingested successfully" when parsing fails due to transient errors.

Key changes:
- Add DocumentProcessingStatus enum (PENDING, PROCESSING, COMPLETED, FAILED)
- Add processing_status, processing_error, processing_error_traceback fields
- Create DocumentParsingError exception with is_transient flag
- Update parsers to raise typed exceptions instead of returning None
- Add automatic retry with exponential backoff for transient errors
- Keep failed documents locked (backend_lock=True) to prevent broken state
- Add retry_document_processing task for manual retry after infra fixes
- Add DOCUMENT_PROCESSING_FAILED notification type
- Add GraphQL processing status fields and RetryDocumentProcessing mutation
- Include migration with data backfill for existing documents
- Add 24 unit tests for new functionality

Documents now stay locked on failure, error details are captured for
debugging, and users can manually retry processing via GraphQL.

Previously, when a caller passed a tool with the same name as a default
tool, the caller's tool was silently dropped and the default was used.
This could cause unexpected behavior when callers intended to override
tool configurations (e.g., requires_approval, description).

Now caller tools replace defaults with the same name, allowing full
customization of tool behavior. This applies to both create() and
structured_response() methods.

- Add test verifying caller's tool configuration is actually used
- Update info-level logging when overrides occur

trigger the post_save signal which starts Celery tasks that try to
process documents. Since test documents have no actual files, this
causes IsADirectoryError when the parser tries to read the file.

Fix: Add session-scoped autouse fixture in conftest.py that disconnects
document/annotation processing signals for all pytest runs. Tests that
specifically need signals can use the enable_doc_processing_signals
fixture to temporarily re-enable them.

Also add redundant signal handling in AsyncTestDuplicateTools as a
safety net for non-pytest test runs (e.g., manage.py test).

message:
Fix parser creating duplicate documents when document already in corpus

The parser's _save_data_to_doc() was calling add_document() unconditionally
when a corpus_id was passed, creating a second corpus copy even when the
document was already in the corpus via DocumentPath (e.g., from import_content).

duplicate document creation during bulk uploads.

- Update UnifiedToolFactory.create_tool() to accept inject_params
- Update _convert_tools_for_framework() to build and pass inject_params
- Update create_document_agent() and create_corpus_agent() to pass context
- Add comprehensive tests for validation and injection

subject: Unify text file versioning with binary file versioning pipeline
message:
Unify text file versioning with binary file versioning pipeline

Text files (text/plain, application/txt) now use the same import_document()
versioning pipeline as PDFs and other binary formats:

- Text files stored in txt_extract_file field, binary files in pdf_file
- Path-based versioning works for all file types (uploading to same path
  creates new version with proper parent-child relationship)
- Content hash computed for all file types
- M2M corpus.documents maintained for backwards compatibility

Key changes:
- versioning.py: Add TEXT_MIMETYPES constant and _is_text_file() helper,
  update both "path exists" and "new path" branches to route text files
  to txt_extract_file instead of pdf_file
- models.py: Update import_content() to route ALL file types through
  import_document(), deprecate _create_text_document_internal() and
  create_text_document() aliases
- import_tasks.py: Simplify import_zip_with_folder_structure() to use
  unified import_content() for all file types instead of separate
  text file handling
- test_document_versioning.py: Add TextFileVersioningTestCase with 6 tests
  covering text file storage, versioning, hash computation, and MIME types

subject: Fix structural annotations not appearing in corpus-wide queries
message:
Fix structural annotations not appearing in corpus-wide queries

The GetAnnotationsForCards query was returning no structural annotations when
querying by corpusId without a documentId. This was caused by two issues:

1. AnnotationQuerySet.visible_to_user() filtered out structural annotations
   because they have document=NULL (linked via structural_set instead) and
   the filter checked document__is_public/document__creator which fails
   on NULL relations.

2. resolve_annotations() filtered by corpus_id=X, but structural annotations
   have corpus_id=NULL since they're shared across corpuses via structural_set.

Changes:
- Added AnnotationQueryOptimizer.get_corpus_annotations() method for
  corpus-wide annotation queries that properly includes structural
  annotations by checking their structural_set__documents relationship
- Updated resolve_annotations() to use the new optimizer when querying
  by corpus without a document
- Fixed AnnotationQuerySet.visible_to_user() to handle structural
  annotations with document=NULL by checking structural_set__documents
- Added comprehensive tests for the new functionality

   - Add _get_safe_redirect_url() using url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme()

   - Add _parse_boolean_claim() helper function

   - Handle numeric values (0, 1)
   - Ignore invalid claim values instead of crashing

subject: Use fixed redirect_uri for Auth0 callback URL matching
message:
Use fixed redirect_uri for Auth0 callback URL matching

Auth0 requires exact matching of callback URLs in the allowed list.
Previously the redirect_uri included dynamic ?next= query parameter
which broke the callback URL matching.

Changes:
- Store next URL in localStorage before Auth0 redirect
- Use fixed redirect_uri (just the login page path)
- Restore next URL from localStorage after successful callback
- Clean up localStorage on both success and error paths

Now you only need to whitelist http://localhost:8000/admin/login/
in Auth0's Allowed Callback URLs.

subject: Fix settings schema resolution and add per-component secret management
message:
Fix settings schema resolution and add per-component secret management

The pipelineComponents GraphQL resolver was never passing settingsSchema
to the frontend, and the dict keys ("type") didn't match Graphene field
names ("setting_type"). This meant settingType, hasValue, and all schema
data was always null.

Fix the resolver to call PipelineSettings.get_component_schema() which
augments the schema with per-key has_value status, then construct proper
ComponentSettingSchemaType instances with correctly-mapped fields.

On the frontend, replace the raw JSON secrets modal with a structured
per-component form: each secret key shown individually with its name,
required badge, and Set/Not-set indicator. Remove the standalone
Component Secrets section since secrets are now managed inline per
component's Advanced Settings panel.

Replace custom geometric SVG icons for Docling, LlamaIndex, and
Sentence Transformers with their official brand logos.

Add cache cleanup to prevent PipelineSettings leaking across tests

Tests that modify PipelineSettings and call get_instance() within a

transaction. The 128-dim temp_embedder.TestEmbedder path was leaking
to subsequent tests on the same xdist worker, causing

addCleanup ensures the cache is cleared before rollback so the next
test gets a fresh read from the (now-reverted) database.

message:

Fix three categories of issues preventing relationship creation and
display for text documents:

1. File type detection: Multiple components only checked
   startsWith("text/"), missing "application/txt" documents. Add
   centralized isTextFileType()/isPdfFileType() utilities and update

   HighlightItem, and annotationSelectedViaRelationship() only

   ServerTokenAnnotation | ServerSpanAnnotation union, enabling the
   sidebar relationship display and creation flow for text documents.

subject: Freeze embedder binding per corpus to prevent search inconsistencies
message:
Freeze embedder binding per corpus to prevent search inconsistencies

Addresses Issue #437 - when supporting multiple embedders, keeping track
of which ones to use for creating embeddings and searching gets fragile.
The core problem: if DEFAULT_EMBEDDER changes or a corpus's embedder is
modified after documents exist, annotations end up with mixed embeddings
and search silently returns incomplete results.

Changes:
- Auto-populate preferred_embedder from DEFAULT_EMBEDDER at corpus creation
  so every corpus has a stable, frozen embedder binding
- Add created_with_embedder audit field (immutable after creation)
- Reject preferred_embedder changes via UpdateCorpusMutation after documents
  exist, with clear error directing users to reEmbedCorpus mutation
- Add reEmbedCorpus mutation + reembed_corpus task for controlled embedder
  migration (locks corpus, queues batch re-embedding, unlocks on completion)
- Add preferred_embedder parameter to forkCorpus mutation for creating forks
  with a different embedder
- Use corpus.preferred_embedder for corpus-scoped search instead of global
  DEFAULT_EMBEDDER setting
- Add Django system check that warns at startup if DEFAULT_EMBEDDER has
  changed since existing corpuses were created
- Migration 0040 backfills both fields on existing corpuses
- Comprehensive test coverage for all new behavior

Closes #437

subject: Fix MCP telemetry SynchronousOnlyOperation in async context
message:
Fix MCP telemetry SynchronousOnlyOperation in async context

The MCP server runs inside Daphne's async event loop, but the telemetry
functions were calling record_event() synchronously, which triggers
Installation.objects.get() — a sync ORM call that raises
SynchronousOnlyOperation in async contexts.

Add async variants (arecord_event, arecord_mcp_tool_call,
arecord_mcp_resource_read, arecord_mcp_request) that wrap the sync
telemetry through sync_to_async, running the ORM lookup in a thread pool.
Update all MCP server call sites to await the async versions.

Closes the "Failed to get installation ID: You cannot call this from an
async context" warning that fired on every MCP request.

subject: Pin griffe<2 to fix corpus agent action TypeError
message:
Pin griffe<2 to fix corpus agent action TypeError

griffe 2.0.0 (released 2026-02-09) removed the **options catch-all
parameter from all docstring parsers. pydantic-ai 0.2.x unconditionally
passes returns_named_value and returns_multiple_items as parser_options
to all parsers including numpy, causing:

  TypeError: parse_numpy() got an unexpected keyword argument 'returns_named_value'

This broke all run_agent_corpus_action tasks during agent creation via
the call chain: UnifiedAgentFactory.create_document_agent →
PydanticAIDocumentAgent.create → doc_descriptions() → parse_numpy().

Pin griffe>=1.3.2,<2 to keep the **options parameter that silently
absorbs these Google-specific options when the numpy parser is selected.

subject: Propagate sub-agent tool approval gates to corpus chat level
message:
Propagate sub-agent tool approval gates to corpus chat level

When a corpus agent delegates to a document sub-agent via ask_document,
the sub-agent may encounter tools that require user approval (e.g.,
update_document_summary). Previously, the ApprovalNeededEvent from the
sub-agent was silently ignored, causing the tool to fail without user
interaction.

Changes:

Backend (pydantic_ai_agents.py):
- Detect ApprovalNeededEvent in ask_document_tool's sub-agent stream
- Raise ToolConfirmationRequired with the sub-agent's tool details,
  preserving _sub_tool_name and _sub_tool_arguments for UI display
- Re-raise ToolConfirmationRequired from CallToolsNode exception handler
  instead of swallowing it with the generic Exception catch
- Add skip_approval parameter to ask_document_tool so resumed calls
  create sub-agents with skip_approval_gate=True
- Strip internal metadata keys (prefixed with _) in resume_with_approval
  before passing args to the tool function

Frontend (CorpusChat.tsx, ChatTray.tsx, useAgentChat.ts):
- Add ASYNC_APPROVAL_RESULT and ASYNC_RESUME message types
- Handle ASYNC_APPROVAL_RESULT to clear pending approval state
- Handle ASYNC_RESUME to maintain processing indicator
- For sub-agent approvals (ask_document), unwrap _sub_tool_name and
  _sub_tool_arguments so the approval modal shows the actual tool
  being approved rather than the coordinator's ask_document wrapper

message:

Three issues addressed:

   and CorpusDetailsView (in header) that opens the sidebar bottom sheet,
