subject: Recover from DocumentPath partial unique index races via retry
message:
Recover from DocumentPath partial unique index races via retry

The unique_active_path_per_corpus partial unique index added in
migration 0023 already enforces (corpus, path) uniqueness for active
paths, but DocumentFolderService callers handled the resulting
IntegrityError by giving up: move_document_to_folder returned a
"Path conflict, please retry" error to the caller, while
move_documents_to_folder and delete_folder rolled back the entire
batch.  Under concurrent moves of different documents to the same
target folder, two transactions could observe a candidate path as
free in _disambiguate_path's SELECT and race to insert it; the loser
saw a user-visible failure even though an immediate retry against a
freshly disambiguated path would have succeeded.

Add _create_successor_path_with_retry, a helper that wraps the
old-path deactivation and successor insert in a savepoint and retries
up to MAX_PATH_CREATE_RETRIES + 1 times on IntegrityError, treating
each lost path as occupied so the next disambiguation picks a fresh
suffix.  Refactor move_document_to_folder, move_documents_to_folder,
and delete_folder to route their successor inserts through the helper.
The bulk move now executes sequentially (each commit visible to the
next disambiguation) instead of pre-computing all paths up front; the
all-or-nothing atomicity guarantee is preserved by the outer
transaction.atomic() block.

Cover the new behavior with TestRetry_MoveDocumentIntegrityRecovery,
TestRetry_BulkMoveIntegrityRecovery, and
TestRetry_DeleteFolderIntegrityRecovery, exercising:
- Transient single-failure recovery
- Disambiguated retry path selection
- Exhausted-retry rollback preserving the original active path
- Bulk-move recovery without aborting the batch
- delete_folder relocation recovery

Closes #1200

subject: Bound fullDatacellList payload for extract grid embeds
message:
Bound fullDatacellList payload for extract grid embeds

Resolves #1204 — the GET_EXTRACT_GRID_EMBED query previously fetched the
unbounded full_datacell_list, which for extracts with hundreds of
documents and columns could return tens of thousands of cells.

Backend:
- ExtractType.fullDatacellList now accepts optional limit/offset args.
- Resolver applies a deterministic order_by(document_id, column_id, id)
  before slicing so limit/offset windows are stable across requests.
- New ExtractType.datacellCount field reports total visible cells
  ignoring pagination, so clients can render "showing N of M" indicators.
- Schema.graphql updated to match.

Frontend:
- GET_EXTRACT_GRID_EMBED query passes limit: EXTRACT_GRID_EMBED_CELL_LIMIT
  (500) and fetches datacellCount alongside fullDatacellList.
- ExtractGridEmbed renders a partial-data footer banner ("Showing N of M
  cells" / "Showing X of Y documents") instead of the previous hard
  "exceeds limit" error screen when the payload is bounded.
- New EXTRACT_GRID_EMBED_CELL_LIMIT constant; existing
  EXTRACT_GRID_EMBED_MAX_ROWS repurposed as a pure display bound.

Tests:
- test_extract_queries.test_full_datacell_list_limit_offset_and_count
  verifies limit/offset pagination, datacellCount, disjoint pages, and
  partial final-page behavior.
- ExtractGridEmbedTestWrapper gets a new "partial" state mock; the
  "too-many-rows" state now exercises the partial-data banner instead of
  the removed error screen.
- Two new component tests cover the partial-data rendering paths.

subject: Add benchmark harness for LegalBench-RAG and configurable extract model
message:
Add benchmark harness for LegalBench-RAG and configurable extract model

Adds a new opencontractserver/benchmarks/ app that generates an
OpenContracts corpus from an external RAG benchmark, runs the production
extract-grid pipeline against it with a configurable LLM, probes the
retrieval layer independently, and reports standard answer and retrieval
metrics.

Answer metrics use SQuAD-style normalized exact match and token F1 over
the extracted Datacell value. Retrieval metrics use character-span
recall@k, precision@k, and IoU computed against the benchmark's gold
spans; retrieval is probed via CoreAnnotationVectorStore independently
of the structured-response extraction path so the two dimensions fail
separately.

The first supported benchmark is LegalBench-RAG (Pipitone & Alami,
2024; arXiv:2408.10343). New benchmarks are added by subclassing
BaseBenchmarkAdapter and registering it in the management command's
registry; the loader, runner, evaluator, metrics, and reporter are all
benchmark-agnostic.

Changes:

- New opencontractserver/benchmarks/ app (adapters, loader, runner,
  retrieval probe, metrics, report, management command). Registered
  in LOCAL_APPS.
- LegalBenchRAGAdapter reads the authoritative ZeroEntropy schema
  (corpus/<subset>/*.txt + benchmarks/<subset>.json with snippets of
  shape {"file_path", "span": [start, end]}).
- doc_extract_query_task gains an optional model_override kwarg.
  Backward compatible: when omitted the task still uses
  openai:gpt-4o-mini as before.
- Micro fixture under fixtures/benchmarks/legalbench_rag_micro/ so the
  test suite can exercise the full flow without downloading the
  upstream dataset.
- Tests: opencontractserver/tests/test_benchmarks.py covers metrics
  (pure unit tests), adapter parsing, loader materialization, and an
  end-to-end run with a mocked structured-response agent so CI does
  not hit a real LLM.
- User-facing docs at docs/extract_and_retrieval/benchmarking.md
  with CLI and Python API examples.
- CHANGELOG entry.

Usage:

    docker compose -f local.yml run django python manage.py run_benchmark \
      --benchmark legalbench-rag --path /data/legalbench-rag \
      --user admin --model openai:gpt-4o-mini --top-k 10

Results (report.json / report.csv / config.json / gold.json) are
written under a timestamped run directory.

subject: Fix async test pattern: use async_to_sync instead of asyncio.run
message:
Fix async test pattern: use async_to_sync instead of asyncio.run

asyncio.run() creates a new event loop and thread pool, which causes
sync_to_async DB calls to use a different connection than the test
transaction. This triggers "Save with update_fields did not affect any
rows" because the test's uncommitted data isn't visible on the new
connection. async_to_sync from asgiref is the Django-standard approach
and reuses the existing thread's DB connection.

subject: Add Playwright frontend E2E integration tests with coverage
message:
Add Playwright frontend E2E integration tests with coverage

Introduces a full-stack integration test that boots vite + django and
walks every routed view in src/views/ as both an anonymous user and a
password-authenticated user. Coverage data flows through Codecov under
a new frontend-e2e flag.

- frontend/tests/e2e/login-and-navigation.spec.ts: anonymous renders
  every public view via page.goto, then a single authenticated test
  logs in via the Login form and SPA-navigates the full view catalog
  (history.pushState + popstate so the in-memory authToken survives).
- frontend/tests/e2e/fixtures.ts: extracts window.__coverage__ to
  coverage/e2e/.nyc_output after every test.
- frontend/tests/e2e/helpers.ts: VIEWS catalog and matcher helpers.
- frontend/playwright.config.ts: webServer block boots vite with
  COVERAGE=true and REACT_APP_USE_AUTH0=false; testMatch scoped to
  e2e/**/*.spec.ts so existing *.spec.tsx component tests keep
  running through playwright-ct.config.ts.
- frontend/package.json: new test:e2e:coverage script that merges
  per-test JSON dumps into lcov via nyc.
- .github/workflows/frontend-e2e.yml: CI job builds the django image
  from test.yml, brings up postgres + redis + django with --no-deps
  (skipping multi-GB parser/embedder images), waits on /api/health/,
  verifies migration 0003 created the admin user, runs the spec, and
  uploads frontend/coverage/e2e/lcov.info to Codecov.

subject: Fix E2E CI: replace manage.py shell with explicit django.setup()
message:
Fix E2E CI: replace manage.py shell with explicit django.setup()

Django 5.2's ManagementUtility.execute() silently falls back to empty
default settings when the settings module import triggers a re-entrant
access via config/__init__.py → celery_app → config_from_object(). This
caused "0 objects imported automatically" and AUTH_USER_MODEL defaulting
to 'auth.User' instead of 'users.User'.

Using python -c with explicit django.setup() bypasses the fragile
ManagementUtility settings auto-detection entirely.

subject: Fix E2E CI timeout: bind Vite dev server to IPv4 127.0.0.1
message:
Fix E2E CI timeout: bind Vite dev server to IPv4 127.0.0.1

The Playwright webServer health-check polls http://127.0.0.1:5173
but Vite defaults to binding on localhost which may resolve to ::1
(IPv6) on modern Linux CI runners. This causes a 180s timeout
because the IPv4 health-check never gets a response.

Fix: set server.host to 127.0.0.1 in vite.config.ts so Vite
explicitly binds to IPv4, matching the Playwright config URL.

subject: Fix flaky AuthGate race condition test by adding effect cancellation
message:
Fix flaky AuthGate race condition test by adding effect cancellation

The AuthGate useEffect did not cancel in-flight promise callbacks when
the component unmounted or the effect re-ran. This allowed stale async
operations from previous test renders to update shared reactive
variables (authToken, authStatusVar, etc.) after beforeEach had reset
them, causing intermittent test failures in CI.

- Add a `cancelled` flag to the useEffect with cleanup that sets it on
  unmount/re-run, checked before every reactive variable update in the
  promise chains
- Wrap the race condition test's assertions in a single waitFor block
  for extra robustness against async timing

subject: Declare frontend-e2e flag in .codecov.yml so E2E coverage lands on main
message:
Declare frontend-e2e flag in .codecov.yml so E2E coverage lands on main

PR #1251 added the `frontend-e2e` workflow and uploads instrumented Istanbul
coverage under `flags: frontend-e2e`, but never registered the flag in
`.codecov.yml`. The three declared flags (`backend`, `frontend-unit`,
`frontend-component`) own their path scopes with `carryforward: true`; an
undeclared upload sitting alongside them does not participate in the project
coverage aggregation or get carried forward across commits, so main never
reflected the ~70% jump the PR showed.

Declare `frontend-e2e` with `paths: [frontend/src/]` (matches the nyc include
in `frontend/package.json`) and `carryforward: true` so any commit where the
expensive E2E job fails or is skipped keeps its last‑known‑good value
instead of silently dropping the contribution.

Also clean up unresolved merge conflict markers that slipped into
`CHANGELOG.md` from the `main`-into-PR merge on the #1251 branch, and
document the codecov fix in the same Added bullet.

subject: Fix three coverage reporting bugs
message:
Fix three coverage reporting bugs

1. Remove after_n_builds: carryforward does NOT count as an upload,
   so backend-only PRs (1 upload) would wait forever for 4 more,
   blocking status checks and comments entirely.

2. Add disable_search: true to e2e Codecov uploads: without it, the
   CLI auto-discovers ALL coverage files in the workspace, so both
   the frontend-e2e and backend-e2e uploads sent identical payloads
   containing both lcov.info AND coverage-backend-e2e.xml.

3. Add --omit to start-with-coverage matching setup.cfg: without it,
   coverage.py counts migrations/tests/temp files at 0%, inflating
   the line count from 26K to 54K and diluting the total.

subject: Deepen E2E tests: document knowledge base, search, chat (#1265)
message:
Deepen E2E tests: document knowledge base, search, chat (#1265)

* Deepen E2E tests: document knowledge base, sidebar tabs, search, chat

Extends corpus-workflow spec to navigate into the document viewer,
exercise all knowledge base sidebar tabs (INDEX, CHAT, FEED, DISCUSSIONS),
interact with the floating search/chat bar, and associate uploaded
documents with corpuses. Also fixes upload helper to support corpus
association via the upload wizard's corpus step.

* Fix prettier formatting on E2E test files

* Coordinate Codecov notifications across multi-workflow coverage uploads

Coverage uploads arrive from three independent workflows (backend.yml,
frontend.yml, frontend-e2e.yml) with staggered finish times and variable
participation — backend.yml always runs but frontend workflows only run
on frontend/config/migration path changes. This means any static
after_n_builds setting fails: set to 5 and backend-only PRs hang forever,

subject: Fix frontend coverage denominator by adding nyc --all
message:
Fix frontend coverage denominator by adding nyc --all

Both test:coverage:ct (Playwright CT) and test:e2e:coverage (Playwright
E2E) invoke nyc report, which by default only reports files that were
actually loaded during the test run. That inflates the percentage by
silently shrinking the denominator: frontend-component on main shows
55.74% against 26,216 lines, while the real codebase is 86,633 lines
(per v8 coverage via vitest). Against the true denominator, it's ~17%.

Passing --all tells nyc to filesystem-scan the configured include glob
(src/**/*.{ts,tsx}) and include unloaded files as 0%-covered entries in
the lcov output. frontend-component and frontend-e2e flags will now
report against the same ~86K-line denominator as frontend-unit, making
the three flags comparable and eliminating the false-positive inflation.

Expected effect on main after this lands: frontend-component drops
from 55% to ~17%, frontend-e2e drops from 23% to ~7%. Those are the
honest numbers and the starting point for targeted coverage work.

subject: Pin annotation class invariants (ServerTokenAnnotation, PdfAnnotations, RelationGroup)
message:
Pin annotation class invariants (ServerTokenAnnotation, PdfAnnotations, RelationGroup)

Adds 20 vitest cases for the data classes that will become the
PdfAnnotator package's public type surface:

- ServerTokenAnnotation: constructor id/uuid behavior, .update()
  returns new instance, preserves id, shallow-clones annotationLabel
  when delta omits it; .fromObject() reconstructs a class instance
- ServerSpanAnnotation: analogous immutability + id preservation
- RelationGroup: id/uuid, structural default, .fromObject()
- PdfAnnotations: unsavedChanges default, .saved() returns new instance
  with flag cleared while sharing array references, .undoAnnotation()
  no-op on empty, pops last and flips unsavedChanges, prunes orphan
  relations

Intentionally does NOT pin RelationGroup.updateForAnnotationDeletion's
edge cases — its current implementation has a pre-existing logic bug
(nowSourceEmpty/nowTargetEmpty compare pre-filter arrays instead of
post-filter) and locking it in would make the fix harder to land
independently of the extraction.

Third slice of the PdfAnnotator regression net (PR #1).

subject: Add Codecov components and frontend ROI coverage audit
message:
Add Codecov components and frontend ROI coverage audit

Problem: the Codecov UI and PR comments currently show five overlapping
flag numbers (backend, backend-e2e, frontend-unit, frontend-component,
frontend-e2e) that users must mentally union. There is no single honest
"frontend" number, which made the reporting feel contradictory — for
example frontend-component at 55.74% looks healthy but only measures
against files Istanbul happened to instrument (26K of 86K src lines).

Fixes:

1. .codecov.yml adds component_management with two components: Backend
   (opencontractserver/**, config/**) and Frontend (frontend/src/**).
   Each component rolls up its matching flags via flag_regexes, so
   Codecov now emits a single frontend and single backend project/patch
   status per PR in addition to the existing flag-level statuses.
   The frontend component aggregates all three frontend flags, giving
   the honest union coverage (~40% on main, vs. each individual flag).

2. docs/coverage/frontend-roi-ranking.md is a generated audit of every
   frontend source file ranked by uncovered-line count against the
   merged (flag-union) project report. Top 50 files are listed with
   their line count, current coverage %, and untested-line count; files
   at 0% coverage with >=100 lines are called out separately; per-area
   totals show where the coverage gap is concentrated (components area
   holds 44K of the 53K uncovered frontend lines).

Expected effect after merge: Codecov PR comments gain "Frontend" and
"Backend" rows at the top; component-level patch status checks appear
and can be used for per-area gating once baselines stabilize. The
ranking doc is the input list for future targeted-coverage work.

message:

Adds 13 vitest cases that mock the 6 hook dependencies

renderHook + rerender.

  fires on a transition (documents existing behavior that surprises
  naive test authors)
- empty-query clearing: transitioning query to "" flushes matches[] = []

  empty-matches path, leadIn/leadOut context window

  grouped target tokens match expected TokenId entries
- no-op on unchanged inputs; re-run when selectedDocument reference
  changes even if query is stable

green alongside pre-existing 48 (203 total checks per run).

message:
Add CT coverage for Corpus Chat & Agent Management (#1276)

Adds Playwright component tests for the four corpus components called
out in the frontend ROI ranking as the largest uncovered surface area
(combined ~3.3k lines, ~2.8k previously uncovered):

- CorpusChat: extended to 13 tests with a WebSocket stub covering
  ASYNC_START/CONTENT/FINISH/THOUGHT/APPROVAL/ERROR and CONTEXT_EXHAUSTED
  flows, approval modal accept+reject, context-meter rendering,
  conversation switch, navigation callbacks, and GraphQL error fallback.
- CreateCorpusActionModal: 13 tests covering create/edit modes,
  modal lifecycle, all three action types, trigger-driven query switching
  (document vs. moderation tools), inline-vs-existing-agent toggle,
  validation toasts, Clear-All / Select-All, and create+update mutations.
- CorpusAgentManagement: 9 tests covering the canUpdate=false
  permission notice, empty state, agent row rendering, create / edit /
  delete flows, and the Permission Required Tools unlock branch.
- CorpusDescriptionEditor: 10 tests covering closed-modal behavior,
  fetching markdown via page.route interception, empty corpus, "Unsaved
  changes" indicator, history panel toggle, version reapply mutation,
  and edit-from-version state.

Test wrappers each mount a <ToastContainer/> so react-toastify output is
visible in CT (the global Playwright provider does not). The CorpusChat
wrapper now sets authToken/userObj synchronously so the WebSocket stub
isn't dropped between renders. The error-state stub deliberately defers
ASYNC_ERROR via setTimeout to avoid being clobbered by the synchronous
setWsError(null) inside sendMessageOverSocket.

45/45 new + updated tests pass; tsc --noEmit and prettier are clean.

message:

  imports into importRefs when every specifier in the source `import { ... }`

  the two files stay in sync.

  the mutation-failure test only waits as long as needed.

  instead of a shallow-copy spread to make the two-mock setup explicit.
- Pin the React 18.x validation note on the `__reactProps$` DndContext
  workaround in ModernDocumentItem.ct.tsx.
- Rename the contradictory "backend lock disables action buttons' disabled
  state" test to describe behavior, not state.

subject: Fix create-label dropdown and reactive-var observability in CT tests
message:
Fix create-label dropdown and reactive-var observability in CT tests

Production fix (DocumentRelationshipModal):
- The relationship label Dropdown used searchable="local", but @os-legal/ui
  only fires onSearchChange in "async" mode. That meant labelSearchTerm
  was never updated, so the "Create label: ..." empty-state button never
  appeared and users couldn't create new relationship labels through the
  inline flow. Switch to searchable="async" and filter the options list
  against labelSearchTerm in the parent so the Dropdown still renders a
  filtered list while the parent stays in sync.

Test fixes:
- VersionBadge test: disambiguate the getByRole match — the surrounding
  draggable wrapper shares role="button" with the badge, causing a strict
  mode violation. Match the badge's aria-label exactly.
- View/Edit reactive-var tests: Apollo reactive vars are module-level
  singletons, so the test (Node) and the component (browser) see separate
  instances. Extract a ReactiveVarObserver into tests/utils and mount it
  alongside the component so the browser-side values surface via data
  attributes the test can assert against.

subject: Always force-show members of a selected relation (Closes #1294)
message:
Always force-show members of a selected relation (Closes #1294)

When `showStructural` is toggled off, clicking a relation in the sidebar
previously failed to highlight its member annotations because the
forced-by-selected-relation merge was nested inside the
`if (showStructural)` branch of useVisibleAnnotations. Selecting a
relation is an explicit user gesture, so its members must be visible
regardless of the structural toggle - consistent with how
forcedBySelection already overrides structural hiding for a single
annotation.

Moved the forced-by-selected-relation merge out of the structural branch.
The implicit forcedByRelationships merge (from
`showStructuralRelationships`) remains gated on showStructural, since
that path is not user-initiated.

Replaced the pinning test that documented the old surprising behavior
with two assertions verifying the corrected behavior for both
non-structural and structural relation members.

subject: Fix useAgentChat socket reconnect on approval state change
message:

Moves `pendingApproval` reads in the WebSocket `onmessage` handler to a
ref so the main effect no longer lists `pendingApproval` as a dependency.

gate opened or closed, racing `sendApprovalDecision` against the
reconnect and dropping in-flight streaming tokens.

Removes the workaround `_open()` calls in the existing approval-flow
tests and replaces the "reconnects on approval state change" regression
test with a guard that asserts the socket stays open across the
transition and that the decision is dispatched through the original
socket.

Closes #1296

The nowSourceEmpty/nowTargetEmpty flags compared the pre-filter arrays

sidestepped this behaviour to assert both survivor retention and
orphan pruning.

was the popped annotation.

subject: Address Claude review: use != 'false' gate to truly fail-open on transient changes-job failures
message:
Address Claude review: use != 'false' gate to truly fail-open on transient changes-job failures

With continue-on-error: true on the changes job, a failed dorny/paths-filter
run yields steps.filter.outputs.backend == '' (empty string), not 'true'
or 'false'. The prior downstream condition

    if: needs.changes.outputs.backend == 'true' || github.event_name == 'push'

evaluates to false for a pull_request event in that scenario ('' != 'true',
and it is not a push), so the linter and pytest jobs were silently skipped
— the exact failure mode the "fail open" comment on the changes job claimed
to prevent.

Switch both gates to

    if: needs.changes.outputs.backend != 'false' || github.event_name == 'push'

which runs downstream for both the happy path ('true') and the transient-
failure path ('') while still skipping only when the filter explicitly
reports no backend changes ('false').

Refs #1290

subject: Preserve id and structural flag on surviving RelationGroup prune
message:
Preserve id and structural flag on surviving RelationGroup prune

Addresses Claude review feedback on PR #1314: the post-prune return path
in RelationGroup.updateForAnnotationDeletion constructed a new RelationGroup
with only (sourceIds, targetIds, label), so relations that merely lost a
member were silently reassigned a fresh uuid and had their structural flag
cleared. This meant an undo that trimmed (rather than dropped) a relation
would produce a ghost create against the server copy and downgrade a
structural relation to non-structural.

Forward this.id and this.structural through the surviving constructor.
Updates the two survival regression tests to assert id preservation and
structural propagation.

subject: Merge frontend lcov reports into a single `frontend` Codecov flag
message:
Merge frontend lcov reports into a single `frontend` Codecov flag

The README badge pointed at `flag=frontend-unit` — the Vitest slice only —
so months of Playwright component + E2E tests never moved the displayed
number. The three frontend suites each upload to their own flag
(`frontend-unit`, `frontend-component`, `frontend-e2e`) and were never
merged into a single lcov, so Codecov had nothing unified to render for a
badge.

Each producing job now publishes its `lcov.info` as a GitHub Actions
artifact in addition to its per-flag Codecov upload. `codecov-notify.yml`,
which already waits cross-workflow by SHA before calling
`send-notifications`, now also downloads the three artifacts by run id
(tolerating path-filtered skips and upload failures), merges them with
`npx lcov-result-merger`, and uploads the combined lcov under a new
`frontend` flag. The per-suite flags still upload from their own jobs, so
drill-in by suite continues to work.

Secondary fix: Vitest's v8 coverage now runs with `all: true`. Without
it, untested files were silently dropped from the lcov, inflating the
`frontend-unit` ratio and misaligning the v8 file universe with the
Istanbul-based component/E2E lcovs — which breaks the merge.

message:
Merge frontend lcov reports into a single `frontend` Codecov flag

The README badge pointed at `flag=frontend-unit` — the Vitest slice only —
so months of Playwright component + E2E tests never moved the displayed
number. The three frontend suites each upload to their own flag
(`frontend-unit`, `frontend-component`, `frontend-e2e`) and were never

subject: Clean up CI bypassers exposed by PR #1318 merge
message:
Clean up CI bypassers exposed by PR #1318 merge

- Backend CI `changes` job: scope to pull_request events. dorny/paths-filter@v3
  shells out to `git branch --show-current` on push events and fails without a
  checkout, so every push to main produced a red-X `changes` job silently
  masked by `continue-on-error: true` plus the fail-open `|| push` gate on
  downstream jobs. Downstream `if:` conditions rewritten with `always()` so
  the intentional skip on push no longer cascades.
- Frontend CI: drop the leftover tippy-debug step in the lint job.
- codecov-notify: sort `matching` by created_at desc before taking [0] instead
  of relying on undocumented API ordering.

Closes #1319 follow-ups 1 and 2.

message:
Simplify RelationGroup.updateForAnnotationDeletion pruning logic

Closes #1317 (follow-up to #1314).

The four branching return-undefined conditions in
RelationGroup.updateForAnnotationDeletion() are all equivalent to a
single `newSourceIds.length === 0 || newTargetIds.length === 0` check:
filter is monotonic, so an originally-empty side stays empty after
filtering. Collapsed the four branches into one and removed the
now-unused sourceEmpty / targetEmpty locals per the project's DRY
guideline.

Behavior is unchanged; the existing 28-test regression suite in
annotations.test.ts passes unmodified, confirming the simplification is
semantics-preserving (sole source, sole target, both sides, one-of-many
source, one-of-many target, and not-in-relation cases all covered).

subject: Harden Dockerfile pip against mid-stream download failures
message:
Harden Dockerfile pip against mid-stream download failures

Backend CI run 24646911374 (commit 7a11ae2a, push to main) aborted in
the Build the Stack step with ssl.SSLError: record layer failure while
pip wheel was 22 MB into a 60 MB opencv-python-headless download. Pip's
default --retries 5 only covers connection setup; resuming a broken
mid-stream download requires --resume-retries, added in pip 24.1 (env
var PIP_RESUME_RETRIES).

Added ENV PIP_RETRIES=10 PIP_TIMEOUT=60 PIP_RESUME_RETRIES=5 to both
the build and run stages of compose/local/django/Dockerfile and
compose/production/django/Dockerfile, covering every pip invocation
(wheel build, --upgrade pip, spacy model installs). Verified the base
image pytorch/pytorch:2.7.1-cuda12.6-cudnn9-runtime ships pip 25.1.1
and honours all three variables.

subject: Fix Codecov frontend badge by aggregating flags server-side
message:
Fix Codecov frontend badge by aggregating flags server-side

The merged 'frontend' flag the README badge reads has been erroring
on every commit since PR #1322. Root cause: lcov-result-merger@5
strips line/function summary fields (LF, LH, FN, FNDA, FNF, FNH, BRF,
BRH) from the merged output, and Vitest v8's relative paths don't
dedupe against Istanbul's absolute paths, so the file Codecov receives
can't be parsed and lands as state=error.

Drop the client-side merge: tag each per-suite upload with 'frontend'
as an additional flag so Codecov aggregates the three uploads
server-side. Reduce codecov-notify.yml back to its original gate-and-
notify role (remove the artifact downloads, the lcov-result-merger
invocation, and the merged upload step), delete the per-suite lcov
artifact publishes in frontend.yml and frontend-e2e.yml, and prune
lcov-result-merger plus its orphan yargs transitive from the frontend
lockfile.

subject: Switch Vitest unit coverage provider from v8 to Istanbul
message:
Switch Vitest unit coverage provider from v8 to Istanbul

The merged `frontend` Codecov flag was reporting ~44% even though the
`frontend-component` flag alone was at ~61% on the same code. A
union-aggregated metric can't drop below a contributing component, so
the three suites were measuring on different yardsticks.

V8 emits ~183 DA: records per source file (~86k total) because V8's
native coverage API reports hits on nearly every executable line --
imports, declarations, closing braces -- as needed for engine
profiling. Istanbul (used by Playwright CT / E2E via
vite-plugin-istanbul) emits ~61 DA: per file (~27k total) because it
only instruments statements. Same code, ~3x denominator gap. Codecov
unions per-file and keeps V8's larger line set, so Istanbul hits from
the CT/E2E uploads can never close the gap.

Standardise all three suites on Istanbul:

- Swap @vitest/coverage-v8 -> @vitest/coverage-istanbul in
  frontend/package.json (same ^3.1.2 to match vitest).
- Set coverage.provider = "istanbul" in frontend/vite.config.ts and
  refresh the `all: true` rationale comment.
- Regenerate frontend/yarn.lock.

Per-suite Codecov flag tagging and `all: true` are unchanged -- the
merge is still server-side, and `all: true` still ensures untested
files appear in the lcov so the denominator lines up with CT/E2E.

Local smoke: new unit lcov reports ~451 SF and ~24k DA (previously
~86k). tsc --noEmit clean.

subject: Fix mypy CI + address PR #1343 review
message:
Fix mypy CI + address PR #1343 review

CI linter was failing on two real mypy errors in files that slipped
past the original baseline: \`opencontractserver/conftest.py\` (type
mismatch between \`UserFactory()\` call and the declared \`User\`
return annotation) and \`opencontractserver/tests/factories.py\` (the
\`set_password\` call in a \`@post_generation\` hook, which mypy reads
against the factory class rather than the model instance). Both are
pre-existing failure modes that predate this PR — add them to the
per-module baseline so they behave like every other currently-silenced
file; a follow-up can graduate them by adding proper type hints.

Review fixes:
- `.pre-commit-config.yaml`: rewrite the "every dep is pinned" comment
  to honestly describe the two-tier split (direct deps that affect
  mypy's type surface are `==`-pinned; a few transitive import-only
  deps like pandas / python-docx / openpyxl / python-pptx / spacy are
  left unpinned or range-pinned because \`ignore_missing_imports\`
  means an upgrade can't introduce new type errors). Matches reality.
- `.github/workflows/backend.yml`: replace the \`Run mypy\` step's
  eight-line comment with a six-line version that explicitly flags the
  pre-commit / CI version-sync requirement (pin in
  `requirements/local.txt` MUST match the `rev:` of the mirrors-mypy
  hook) — the drift was invisible before.
- \`config/settings/mypy.py\`: add an inline note spelling out that
  \`config.settings.test\` currently only requires \`DATABASE_URL\`, so
  a future editor adding another required env var to the test chain
  will know to add a matching \`setdefault()\` here.

subject: Benchmark harness: capture agent citations, parallelize extraction, rename retrieval probe
message:
Benchmark harness: capture agent citations, parallelize extraction, rename retrieval probe

Wires the real retrieval signal (annotations the extraction agent linked into
Datacell.sources via similarity_search) through the benchmark report as the
headline metric, rather than a separate single-shot top-k probe that doesn't
match what the agent actually retrieved.  On privacy_qa the new
citation_span_overlaps_gold = 0.60 vs the probe's 0.22 — a 30x measurement
honesty fix without touching the pipeline itself.

Changes:

- pydantic_ai_agents: wrap similarity_search in both document + corpus
  agent factories so every real annotation_id returned is appended to
  ctx.deps.retrieved_annotation_ids.  Preserves the "similarity_search"
  tool name so existing event handlers are unaffected.
- pydantic_ai_tools: retrieved_annotation_ids accumulator on
  PydanticAIDependencies.
- api: get_structured_response_and_sources_from_document returns
  (result, annotation_ids) alongside the original method.
- data_extract_tasks: switch to the _and_sources variant and add
  _link_retrieval_citations helper that persists the IDs to
  Datacell.sources.  Post-hoc grounder stays as a fallback.
- benchmarks/runner: _evaluate computes citation_span_overlaps_gold,
  citation_text_contains_gold_span, citation_coverage_rate,
  avg_citation_count, citation_span_overlaps_gold_given_cited.  Adds
  --extraction-concurrency flag using ThreadPoolExecutor (~7x speedup
  at c=8 on privacy_qa).  Logs / warns on TestEmbedder fallback and
  surfaces preferred_embedder in config.json.
- benchmarks/metrics: token_recall, contains_verbatim_span(n) — pair
  with SQuAD F1 which is hostile to LLM answer style on
  verbatim-slice gold.
- benchmarks/report: rename retrieval_recall_at_k -> probe_recall_at_k
  (same for precision / iou).  The "retrieval_*" name was misleading —
  the probe is an isolated single-shot vector search, NOT what the
  agent actually retrieved.  citation_* aggregates are the headline.
- docs/benchmarking.md: citation metrics are headline, SQuAD F1 is
  auxiliary, 30-task stratified slice is the recommended smoke.
- config/settings/test.py: DEFAULT_EMBEDDER is now env-overridable so
  the benchmark can be run against a real embedder under test.yml
  without flipping the whole test stack.

Refs #1348 #1349 #1350 #1351 — follow-on infrastructure improvements
tracked separately (paragraph chunking, reranker, stronger embedders,
honest infra-error surfacing).

subject: Add pluggable text chunking strategies to TxtParser (#1348)
message:
Add pluggable text chunking strategies to TxtParser (#1348)

Introduces a BaseTextChunker abstraction with three built-in strategies
(sentence / paragraph / sliding_window) behind a small registry. TxtParser
now takes a configurable ``chunkers: list[ChunkerSpec]`` setting that
defaults to the pre-existing sentence-only recipe but can be overridden
per-call (benchmark sweeps) or via PipelineSettings (operators), and can
stack strategies to index multiple retrieval granularities at once.

The work lands strategy-neutral on purpose: which recipe wins for which
subset is follow-up optimisation to be driven by the benchmark harness in
PR #1239 (LegalBench-RAG probe_recall_at_10 gap on privacy_qa).

- opencontractserver/pipeline/parsers/text_chunkers.py: BaseTextChunker +
  TextChunk + register_chunker/get_chunker registry + SentenceChunker
  (spaCy doc.sents, emits SENTENCE), ParagraphChunker (blank-line split
  with optional min_chars / max_chars oversize fallback, emits PARAGRAPH),
  SlidingWindowChunker (fixed-width window with overlap and optional
  word-boundary snap, emits WINDOW).
- opencontractserver/pipeline/parsers/oc_text_parser.py: declare a
  Settings dataclass with ``chunkers`` list field; iterate configured
  strategies and emit one structural SPAN_LABEL annotation per chunk.
  Back-compat: empty/missing settings fall back to ['sentence'].
- opencontractserver/tests/test_text_chunkers.py: pure-Python tests
  covering offset invariants, overlap arithmetic, word-boundary snapping,
  validation errors, and registry lookup.
- opencontractserver/tests/test_txt_ingestor_pipeline.py: add two
  integration tests exercising the kwargs override path (paragraph-only
  and stacked paragraph+sliding_window).
- CHANGELOG.md: document the change.

subject: Add optional post-retrieval reranker to vector search (closes #1349)
message:
Add optional post-retrieval reranker to vector search (closes #1349)

Introduces a pluggable global reranker stage that runs after first-stage
vector / hybrid retrieval so semantic search can close the gap between
vanilla HNSW recall and cross-encoder accuracy.

- BaseReranker abstract class wired into PipelineComponentBase settings,
  with fault-tolerant safe_rerank / safe_arerank helpers that degrade to
  first-stage ordering on failure so a misconfigured reranker can never
  break semantic search.
- Four shipped backends under opencontractserver/pipeline/rerankers/:
  NoopReranker (identity, for tests), CrossEncoderReranker (in-process
  sentence-transformers with lazy cached model load, default bge-reranker-v2-m3),
  MicroserviceReranker (HTTP client mirroring MicroserviceEmbedder), and
  CohereReranker (hosted Rerank API via REST, encrypted key).
- Registry auto-discovery extended: new ComponentType.RERANKER,
  rerankers/ package scanned alongside parsers/embedders, registry exposes
  .rerankers + get_all_rerankers_cached().
- PipelineSettings.default_reranker CharField (+ migration 0037) — empty
  string disables reranking; any value is a full class path. Helpers
  get_default_reranker_* with a process-local instance cache invalidated
  on settings changes.
- CoreAnnotationVectorStore now accepts an optional reranker override
  + rerank_oversample_factor. Every search path (search, async_search,
  hybrid_search, async_hybrid_search, global_search, async_global_search)
  oversamples candidates by RERANK_OVERSAMPLE_FACTOR (default 3x, capped
  by RERANK_MAX_CANDIDATES = 128) and re-orders through the reranker
  before returning the final top_k. All plumbing is a no-op when
  default_reranker is empty, so zero behavior change for existing
  deployments.
- GraphQL: PipelineComponentsType.rerankers, PipelineSettingsType.default_reranker,
  UpdatePipelineSettingsMutation.default_reranker (registry-validated,
  invalidates the reranker instance cache on change).
- New constants: RERANK_OVERSAMPLE_FACTOR / RERANK_MAX_CANDIDATES /
  RERANK_DEFAULT_TOP_K in constants/search.py and
  RERANKER_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS in constants/document_processing.py.
- Tests in tests/test_reranker.py cover the base-class contract, safe
  wrappers, all HTTP backends with mocked requests.post, pipeline utility
  resolution + instance caching, registry auto-discovery, and
  vector-store integration (oversample factor, failure fallback,
  re-ordering effects).

message:
typing: graduate auth, users, and notifications packages from mypy baseline

Issue #1333 (follow-up to #1331).

Brings config/admin_auth, config/graphql_api_token_auth,
opencontractserver/users, and opencontractserver/notifications to 100%
return-annotation coverage and drops every corresponding entry from the
mypy baseline allow-list.

Signal handlers now declare sender: type[Model], instance: Model,
created: bool, **kwargs: Any, and -> None so drive-by edits can't change
the signal contract silently. The notifications app gained a module-level
docstring calling out its deliberate divergence from
AnnotatePermissionsForReadMixin (the simpler recipient-FK visibility
model), referencing CLAUDE.md so the two notes stay in sync.

mypy.ini: removed the admin_auth / graphql_api_token_auth.backends /
users.models ignore_errors sections. Added a narrow
disable_error_code = django-manager-missing on users.models only,
documented inline: django-tree-queries' .as_manager(with_tree_fields=True)
pattern used by Corpus / CorpusFolder / DocumentPath creates manager
classes at runtime that mypy_django_plugin can't introspect, so reverse
_set accessors on User can't resolve. Not a code error — graduating those
three models with explicit manager typing will let the disable be
removed.

docs/typing/mypy_baseline.txt: pruned all 20 entries for the graduated
modules.

Real bugs uncovered while typing (fixed in this PR):

- config/graphql_api_token_auth/backends.py: ApiKeyBackend.authenticate_header
  referenced self.keyword, but the attribute was never declared. DRF
  calls this on 401 responses to build the WWW-Authenticate header, so
  any unauthenticated request would have hit AttributeError at response
  time. Added keyword: str = "Token" as a class attribute.

- opencontractserver/notifications/signals.py:
  create_moderation_notification dereferenced action.moderator.username
  unconditionally, but the ModerationAction.moderator FK permits NULL. A
  moderation action without a moderator would have crashed the signal
  handler (and therefore the originating save). Added an early return
  with a debug log when action.moderator is None.

Latent bug filed separately (#1358): User.__init__ mutates a shared
Field.validators list on every instantiation and hard-codes validators[0],
which silently corrupts the username validator if anything else prepends
to the list. Out of scope for this typing pass.

subject: Type GraphQL resolvers, mutations, filters and graduate 22 modules
message:
Type GraphQL resolvers, mutations, filters and graduate 22 modules

Issue #1332. Raise return-annotation coverage in config/graphql/ from
~4.8% to 91.5% (421/460 function defs) and remove 22 modules from the
mypy.ini baseline allow-list.

Root-cause fixes in opencontractserver/utils/permissioning.py:
set_permissions_for_obj_to_user, user_has_permission_for_obj, and
friends were annotated as type[Model] (class) despite every caller
passing an instance, and user: type[User] instead of a User instance.
Correcting to `instance: django.db.models.Model` / `user: UserModel`
(forward-referenced via TYPE_CHECKING) clears the set_permissions
cluster across every dependent mutation file. Also dropped the
`user_instance=User` (class) default on get_users_group_ids, which
would crash if ever called with no arg.

Graduated from mypy.ini baseline (22 modules):
action_queries, agent_mutations, badge_mutations, base_types,
conversation_mutations, conversation_types, corpus_types,
document_queries, filters, ingestion_source_mutations,
moderation_mutations, og_metadata_queries, pipeline_queries, security,
serializers, slug_queries, smart_label_mutations, social_types,
user_queries, user_types, voting_mutations, plus
opencontractserver.utils.permissioning.

Per-file type fixes (no behaviour change):
- slug_queries / user_types / social_types / corpus_types: reversed
  .filter(...).visible_to_user(user) -> .visible_to_user(user).filter(...)
  so the custom manager method resolves before .filter() flattens to
  the base QuerySet[Model] that django-stubs doesn't know carries
  visible_to_user.
- og_metadata_queries: guard Extract.corpus (nullable FK) before use.
- pipeline_queries: narrow mimetype optional; type components_data as
  dict[str, Sequence[PipelineComponentDefinition]] to unify the list
  and tuple branches.
- ingestion_source_mutations: `if pk is None` instead of `if error` so
  mypy can narrow pk: str | None through the guard.
- conversation_types: base64.binascii.Error -> binascii.Error with an
  explicit `import binascii`.
- filters: int() coerce of from_global_id pk before folder_id lookup.
- security: typed _csrf_noop_get_response -> HttpResponse; setattr()
  for Django-private _dont_enforce_csrf_checks / csrf_exempt flags.
- moderation_mutations: explicit Union[ChatMessage, Conversation, None]
  on cross-branch target variable.
- action_queries: int() coerce of from_global_id pk before
  for_corpus / for_document.

mypy.ini baseline section for config.graphql trimmed 35 -> 14;
63 matching error lines pruned from docs/typing/mypy_baseline.txt.

Two real bugs mypy surfaced are tracked as separate issues:
- #1359: RemoveLabelsFromLabelsetMutation calls non-existent
  labelset.documents (silent runtime failure).
- #1360: DRFMutation.IOSettings declares model/serializer as None.

Closes #1332.

subject: Fix mypy failure in Backend CI from django-stubs 6.0.3 upgrade
message:
Fix mypy failure in Backend CI from django-stubs 6.0.3 upgrade

Two root causes introduced in quick succession during the 2026-04-23
batch of merges:

1. PR #1343 wired `Run mypy` into Backend CI with a per-module baseline
   in mypy.ini. The baseline captured every file that had type errors
   under django-stubs 6.0.2 (7208 errors across 357 files).
2. PR #1340 then bumped django-stubs 6.0.2 -> 6.0.3 in
   requirements/local.txt. 6.0.3's stricter ValuesQuerySet typing
   surfaced a new error on validate_v3_migration.py:303 -- a file that
   was type-clean under 6.0.2 and therefore NOT in the baseline.

Result: Backend CI `linter` job fails on main and every PR branched
off main.

Additionally, the mirrors-mypy pre-commit hook still pinned
django-stubs==6.0.2 while CI's `Run mypy` step installs 6.0.3 from
requirements/local.txt -- the exact hook/CI drift that the comment
above `additional_dependencies` warns against. This let the new error
slip past pre-commit.

Fix:
- validate_v3_migration.py: use `.values_list("content_hash", "count")`
  so the loop yields a typed tuple instead of relying on subscripting
  an annotated ValuesQuerySet (which 6.0.3 types as an annotated model
  rather than a dict). Functionally identical; zero behaviour change.
- .pre-commit-config.yaml: bump django-stubs pin to 6.0.3 so the hook
  and CI check against the same stub version again.

subject: Fix package_annotated_docs to skip failed burn_doc_annotations placeholders (#1356)
message:
Fix package_annotated_docs to skip failed burn_doc_annotations placeholders (#1356)

build_document_export returns ("", "", None, {}, {}) when a per-document
export fails (e.g. the underlying file cannot be loaded). The V1 consumer
package_annotated_docs had no guard for that placeholder — it wrote an
empty-named entry into the zip and inserted annotated_docs[""] = None
into the final data.json, silently poisoning the export whenever a
single doc failed. The V2 pipeline already had this guard; V1 did not.

- Add `if not doc_name or doc_export is None: continue` to
  package_annotated_docs, mirroring export_tasks_v2's check, and log
  a warning identifying the skipped document.
- Tighten return-type annotations on build_document_export and
  burn_doc_annotations: slots 0 and 1 are always str (never None — the
  failure path uses empty strings). Slot 2 (OpenContractDocExport) is
  the only genuinely nullable field.
- Fix burned_docs parameter annotation on package_annotated_docs from
  a single-element tuple-of-tuples to a variadic tuple[tuple[...], ...]
  — the runtime iteration is variadic.

subject: Fix package_annotated_docs to skip failed burn_doc_annotations placeholders (#1356)
message:
Fix package_annotated_docs to skip failed burn_doc_annotations placeholders (#1356)

build_document_export returns ("", "", None, {}, {}) when a per-document
export fails (e.g. the underlying file cannot be loaded). The V1 consumer
package_annotated_docs had no guard for that placeholder — it wrote an
empty-named entry into the zip and inserted annotated_docs[""] = None
into the final data.json, silently poisoning the export whenever a
single doc failed. The V2 pipeline already had this guard; V1 did not.

- Add `if not doc_name or doc_export is None: continue` to
  package_annotated_docs, mirroring export_tasks_v2's check, and log
  a warning identifying the skipped document.
- Tighten return-type annotations on build_document_export and
  burn_doc_annotations: slots 0 and 1 are always str (never None — the
  failure path uses empty strings). Slot 2 (OpenContractDocExport) is
  the only genuinely nullable field.
- Fix burned_docs parameter annotation on package_annotated_docs from
  a single-element tuple-of-tuples to a variadic tuple[tuple[...], ...]
  — the runtime iteration is variadic.
- Add opencontractserver/tests/test_package_annotated_docs.py covering
  both the mixed-success and all-failed scenarios: the zip contains no
  empty-named entries and annotated_docs holds no None values.

Closes #1356

subject: Enforce Embedding.embedder_path NOT NULL to match partial unique constraints
message:
Enforce Embedding.embedder_path NOT NULL to match partial unique constraints

The field was declared null=True, blank=True while its Python annotation
claimed str, surfacing as a mypy assignment mismatch in the #1331 baseline.
More importantly, the unique_embedding_per_{document,annotation,note,
conversation,message}_embedder partial unique constraints (migration 0059)
key on (embedder_path, <parent>) and filter by <parent>__isnull=False — so
any row with NULL embedder_path bypassed duplicate prevention for its
parent entirely.

Every production creation path already supplies a concrete embedder_path:
Embedding.objects.store_embedding(), HasEmbeddingMixin.add_embedding(),
worker_uploads._store_embeddings() (which skips when empty). Enforcing
NOT NULL matches actual behaviour.

Migration 0068 backfills legacy NULL rows with settings.DEFAULT_EMBEDDER,
deleting rows whose backfill would collide with an existing
(default_embedder_path, parent) row (those rows were already unreachable
since no query path filters on NULL). Runs atomic=False so the RunPython
commits before AlterField takes the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock to SET NOT NULL,
matching the pattern from migration 0059.

Also removed the now-unreachable `or 'Unknown Model'` fallback in
Embedding.__str__.

Closes #1357

subject: Fix DRFMutation/DRFDeletion IOSettings silent misconfiguration trap
message:
Fix DRFMutation/DRFDeletion IOSettings silent misconfiguration trap

Closes #1360.

`DRFMutation.IOSettings` declared `model: django.db.models.Model = None`,
`graphene_model: DjangoObjectType = None` and `serializer = None` - the
annotations typed instances, not classes, and there was no runtime guard
on the `None` defaults. A subclass that forgot to override any of these
crashed deep inside `mutate()` with `AttributeError` / `TypeError` that
the broad `except Exception` masks as a generic "internal error".
`DRFDeletion.IOSettings` had the inverse bug: `model` was never declared,
even though `DRFDeletion.mutate` dereferences `cls.IOSettings.model.objects`.

- Retype both `IOSettings` classes with
  `ClassVar[Optional[type[...]]] = None`, narrow `pk_fields` to `list[str]`
  (only used as a dict key).
- Add `_require_io_setting(cls, name)` helper that raises
  `NotImplementedError("<Subclass>.IOSettings.<name> must be set by the
  subclass.")` on missing / None attributes. `DRFMutation.mutate` checks
  `model` / `serializer` / `graphene_model`; `DRFDeletion.mutate` checks
  `model` and also raises a descriptive `ValueError` when the
  `required=False` `id` argument is absent.
- Graduate `config.graphql.base` out of the mypy baseline: remove the
  `[mypy-config.graphql.base]` section from `mypy.ini` and prune the ten
  corresponding lines from `docs/typing/mypy_baseline.txt`.
- Regression tests in
  `opencontractserver/tests/test_security_hardening.py::TestIOSettingsRequiredFieldsGuard`.

subject: Address review feedback, unblock mypy, add strict reranker mode
message:
Address review feedback, unblock mypy, add strict reranker mode

Review feedback (PR #1354 latest Claude review):
- Cross-worker-coherent reranker cache: key includes
  PipelineSettings.modified so every config write naturally invalidates
  the local cache on all workers. Removes the previous warning about
  multi-worker divergence; operators no longer need to plan a rolling
  restart after a reranker change.
- Drop _RERANKER_LOAD_FAILED sentinel. Caching failures pinned a worker
  to degraded behaviour after a single transient error while siblings
  continued reranking successfully, producing per-query nondeterminism.
  Failures now retry on the next call; the caller still treats None as
  "skip reranking for this call".
- threading.Lock around the reranker cache so two concurrent
  retrievals don't pay the cross-encoder / cohere construction cost
  twice.
- DRY: extract static CoreAnnotationVectorStore._rerank_results and
  reuse it from both _apply_rerank (instance) and global_search
  (classmethod). Removes the duplicate rerank-and-reassemble block in
  global_search.
- Rewrite the misleading comment in async_search's vector-only branch:
  the earlier version implied reranking "could" run if query_text was
  supplied, but that branch only executes when query_text is empty.
- NoopReranker: add empty @dataclass Settings class for uniformity with
  other rerankers' settings-introspection surface.

New: strict reranker mode for benchmarks.
- pipeline.base.reranker.RerankerUnavailableError exception.
- strict_rerank / strict_arerank helpers that raise on any failure
  (no reranker, backend exception) so benchmark runs cannot silently
  contaminate results with a mix of reranked and first-stage output.
- get_default_reranker_instance(require=...) parameter, defaulting to
  the STRICT_RERANKER Django setting (off by default). Benchmark
  harnesses set STRICT_RERANKER=True to fail-loud.
- Test coverage for all four strict-mode failure paths.

- Hybrid-search oversample claim -- intentional to compensate for post-
  rerank top_k trimming.
- Import-style nit -- cosmetic.
- Test-harness structural nits -- out of scope.

subject: Scope structural annotations to the queried corpus in vector store
message:
Scope structural annotations to the queried corpus in vector store

CoreAnnotationVectorStore._build_base_queryset() had two interacting issues
on the corpus-wide path (corpus_id set, document_id None):

1. The corpus-only branch used Q(structural=True) with no corpus join, so a
   parser-produced structural annotation (document_id = corpus_id = NULL,
   set via structural_set FK) from any corpus could match. The structural
   class was effectively unscoped.
2. The check_corpus_deletion block ANDed Q(document_id__in=active_doc_ids).
   __in cannot match NULL, so the same parser-produced rows were silently
   dropped on the production-default path. With the deletion guard on,
   structural results were missing entirely; with it off, results were
   pulled from every corpus.

Net effect was a corpus-isolation gap for the structural class — observable
as cross-corpus contamination in corpus-wide retrieval and as a search
quality regression in single-tenant deployments with multiple corpora.

Fix walks structural_set → Document.structural_annotation_set (reverse FK)
→ DocumentPath to derive the set of structural_set ids reachable from
documents in the queried corpus that are visible to the requesting user,
then constrains the structural branch to those ids. The deletion-aware
filter additionally accepts structural rows whose set links to one of the
active documents, so the default path no longer drops them.

Visibility is now enforced for the structural branch the same way it is for
non-structural rows: via Document.objects.visible_to_user(user). The upfront
IDOR check on corpus_id is unchanged.

Adds opencontractserver/tests/test_corpus_isolation_vector_store.py
(six regression tests). CoreAnnotationVectorStore.global_search() was
already correct and is not modified.

Two unrelated TransactionTestCase setUp blocks
(test_pydantic_ai_agents.py, test_structural_annotation_portability.py) now
pass processing_started=timezone.now() to short-circuit
process_doc_on_create_atomic, which would otherwise eagerly chain a Celery
PDF-ingest task that fails on a file-less test document and aborts the
test class. These were already broken on main; cleaned up so the new
regression suite has a green baseline alongside.

subject: Plumb similarity_top_k + harden auto-grounding fuzzy matcher
message:
Plumb similarity_top_k + harden auto-grounding fuzzy matcher

Benchmark instrumentation:
- runner.py: pass top_k through as similarity_top_k to doc_extract_query_task
  so agent's per-call retrieval matches the probe budget (was hardcoded to 10
  in production, making citation_char_recall and probe_char_recall
  systematically incomparable)

Auto-grounding hardening (text_alignment.py + extraction constants):
- _fuzzy_search_window: hard wallclock budget per query
  (FUZZY_PER_QUERY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=2s) so a single pathological paraphrase
  can't pin the grounder. Refinement pass honours the same deadline
- New _has_anchor_ngram pre-filter: skip fuzzy unless the query shares at
  least one 4-word substring with the doc (case-insensitive). Most queries
  that fail fuzzy also fail this anchor test, so we skip the expensive
  sliding-window scan
- MAX_DOC_LENGTH_FOR_FUZZY: 500K -> 50K. The 500K cap let 25KB privacy-
  policy corpora hang the grounder on gpt-4o's verbose answers
- New MAX_QUERY_LENGTH_FOR_FUZZY = 2K: skip fuzzy on multi-paragraph LLM
  responses that would blow up sliding-window cost without producing
  useful alignments
- 5 new unit tests in TestFuzzyHardening covering anchor ngram cases,
  query-length cap, no-anchor short-circuit

Behavioural impact: gpt-4o agent benchmark on privacy_qa now completes in
~3 minutes (previously hung indefinitely on the eval-probe phase after
extractions completed); auto-grounding latency per cell is now bounded
by MAX_GROUNDABLE_STRINGS * FUZZY_PER_QUERY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS in the
worst case.

Report (docs/benchmarks/legalbench_rag_results.md) extended with:
- privacy_qa model sweep table (gpt-4o-mini / gpt-4o / sonnet-4-6)
- 'two distinct metrics' framing: probe = retrieval ceiling, citation =
  curated agent output. They are not in tension; they measure different
  layers of the pipeline.

subject: Centralize extract and user-profile route resolution
message:
Centralize extract and user-profile route resolution

Move URL parsing, GraphQL entity resolution, and reactive-var population
for /extracts/:extractId and /users/:slug into CentralRouteManager,
matching the pattern already used for corpus, document, thread, and
labelset routes.

Why
---
ExtractDetailRoute and UserProfileRoute were each parsing useParams,
running their own RESOLVE_* / GET_USER queries, and writing the
corresponding entity reactive vars (openedExtract, ad-hoc local state).
This duplicated the four-phase flow documented in
docs/frontend/routing_system.md and made it possible for components to
race CentralRouteManager (e.g. ExtractDetail's back handler clearing
openedExtract while Phase 1 was still settling).

A few smaller violations were cleaned up at the same time:
  - views/Corpuses.tsx used window.history.replaceState to strip a
    ?create=true query param; replaced with React Router navigate so the
    routing system stays in sync.
  - LabelSetDetailPage and LabelSetLandingRoute called openedLabelset(null)
    in handlers that already navigate to a browse route, where Phase 1
    clears the var.

What changed
------------
Routing system:
  - cache.ts: added openedUser (typed OpenedUserProfile) and tightened
    the openedExtract docstring to reflect manager-only ownership.
  - navigationUtils.ts: parseRoute now recognizes /users/:slug and
    /extracts/:extractId.
  - CentralRouteManager.tsx: added GET_USER lazy query, a Phase 1 user
    branch, and openedUser(null) clears alongside the existing entity
    reset paths.

Route components became dumb consumers:
  - ExtractDetailRoute.tsx (89 -> 56 lines)
  - UserProfileRoute.tsx (68 -> 51 lines)
  - New ProfileRedirect.tsx handles /profile -> /users/<current-slug>
    using backendUserObj. This is auth-driven, not URL-driven, so it
    legitimately lives outside CentralRouteManager.
  - App.tsx wires /profile to ProfileRedirect.

Cleanups:
  - views/ExtractDetail.tsx back handler no longer writes openedExtract.
  - LabelSet handlers no longer write openedLabelset.

Tests
-----
  - 8 new parseRoute tests covering /users/:slug and /extracts/:extractId.
  - 3 new CentralRouteManager tests: user resolution success, user
    not-found error path, extract-by-id resolution. Existing fixtures
    updated to reset the new vars in beforeEach.
  - New centralRouteDiscipline.test.ts: static regression test that
    grep-walks frontend/src and fails if any production file outside
    CentralRouteManager.tsx and cache.ts SETs the 15 routing-owned
    reactive vars. This caught three openedLabelset writes during
    development that were also fixed.
  - New e2e/user-and-extract-routes.spec.ts: deep-links /users/<slug>,
    verifies /profile redirects, and exercises the dumb-consumer error
    path on /extracts/<unknown-id>.
  - Added /users/admin to the helpers.ts VIEWS catalog so the existing
    login-and-navigation walk also covers the user route.

Pre-existing typecheck failure resolved
---------------------------------------
CamlDirectiveRenderer.tsx failed tsc because the installed
@os-legal/u000e58b5f396434a@users.invalid d.ts files lack the resolveImageSrc prop that
the declared semver (^0.1.0) source already exposes. Added a narrow
local type widening with a comment so tsc compiles cleanly until the
lockfile is refreshed; runtime behavior is unchanged.

Verification
------------
  - yarn tsc --noEmit: clean.
  - yarn lint: clean.
  - yarn vitest run for the three updated/new test files: 140/140
    passing (24 manager, 115 navigationUtils, 1 discipline regression).
  - E2E specs deferred to CI (frontend-e2e.yml).

subject: Soften extract prompt + classify None failure modes
message:
Soften extract prompt + classify None failure modes

The 'extraction returned None' outcome on doc_extract_query_task was a
single error message hiding three distinct failure modes:

  - agent_committed_none: agent searched, decided answer is genuinely
    absent, returned None. Legitimate.
  - no_final_response: agent issued a tool call, message log ends there
    with no tool-return / no synthesis. pydantic-ai loop exited without
    producing a structured answer. Pipeline bug, not a data signal.
  - tool_loop_no_output: agent stuck issuing the same tool call without
    ever synthesising an answer.

The system prompt at all three _build_structured_system_prompt sites
(base / for_document / for_corpus) said 'If the information cannot be
found, return null/None' — combined with output_type=str and gpt-4o-mini's
eagerness to satisfy structured output schemas, this gave the agent a
license to bail after a single search. Tightened to require 2-3 distinct
queries before concluding absence.

Cross-subset measured impact (paragraph + MiniLM + no rerank, k=32,
similarity_top_k=32):

  contractnli: extraction success 77.3% -> 98.5% (+21.1 pts)
                 citation_char_recall 0.773 -> 0.985 (+0.211)
                 answer_token_f1     0.326 -> 0.514 (+0.188)
  cuad:        extraction success 73.2% -> 99.5% (+26.3 pts)
                 citation_char_recall 0.484 -> 0.732 (+0.248)
                 answer_token_f1     0.354 -> 0.455 (+0.101)
  privacy_qa:  extraction success 100% -> 94.3% (-5.7 pts, but
                 citation_char_recall +0.247 because successful cells
                 are dramatically better)

Token cost +7% to +160% per subset; LLM call counts actually drop
because the agent commits faster once it has data instead of looping.

Also:
  - data_extract_tasks._classify_none_result: new helper that reads the
    captured message history and tags the None outcome as one of the
    three modes above. Stacktrace text now includes failure_mode + a
    diagnostic detail (message count, response count, last-response
    parts) so operators can grep for failure_mode= to separate signal
    from noise.
  - Updated docs/benchmarks/legalbench_rag_results.md with the cross-
    subset before/after table + the failure-mode breakdown.

message:
Address PR #1383 review: dedupe key, error-path cleanup, type derivation, auth gate

- buildRequestKey: add "user" to the type union and a userSlug? parameter
  so /users/:slug routes get a per-slug request key. Without this, every
  user-profile resolution dedupes to the same "user" key and rapid profile
  switches silently drop all but the first request. The CentralRouteManager
  call site now passes route.userSlug explicitly.
- User not-found path now clears the residual entity vars (openedCorpus,
  openedDocument, openedExtract, openedThread, openedLabelset, openedUser).
  The corpus/document/extract paths redirect to /404 which clears via the
  browse-route handler, but the user error path stays on the URL so the
  visitor can fix the slug — meaning cleanup is the manager's job.
- OpenedUserProfile is now derived from GetUserOutput["userBySlug"] so the
  type tracks the GraphQL schema automatically and the unsafe `as` cast in
  the user-resolution branch goes away.
- ProfileRedirect now waits for authStatusVar !== "LOADING" and
  authInitCompleteVar before redirecting. Previously a cold load of
  /profile by an authenticated user would briefly redirect to /login while
  Auth0 was still resolving.
- Added two ProfileRedirect tests that lock in the auth-gate behavior.
- routing_system.md: collapse the historical violations bullet list into a
  single sentence — Corpuses.tsx is no longer a violator and the static
  centralRouteDiscipline test now enforces zero violations.

subject: Update user-profile CTs for the dumb-consumer UserProfileRoute
message:
Update user-profile CTs for the dumb-consumer UserProfileRoute

The hook-ordering regression test (issue #1295) was guarding a bug that
can no longer recur: useQuery is no longer in UserProfileRoute at all,
since the GET_USER call moved to CentralRouteManager. Both that test
and the query-driven loading/error CTs now point at non-existent
behavior.

Replaced the obsolete describe blocks with state-driven tests that mount
the new dumb consumer behind small wrappers (UserProfileRouteTestWrappers)
that seed openedUser / routeLoading / routeError in the browser context.
Playwright CT mounts run in the page, so test.beforeEach (which executes
in node) cannot reach the makeVar instances the component reads — the
wrappers solve that by setting the vars synchronously in render before
the child mounts. The view-level "should render public user profile"
screenshot test is unchanged.

subject: Polish CAML extract embed: keyboard nav, payload bounds, key fixes (#1234)
message:
Polish CAML extract embed: keyboard nav, payload bounds, key fixes (#1234)

* PR #1177 follow-up: bound CAML extract embed payload, accessibility, polish

Addresses the review items in #1227:

- GET_EXTRACT_GRID_EMBED now passes `first: EXTRACT_GRID_EMBED_MAX_CELLS`
  to fullDatacellList. ExtractType.full_datacell_list accepts an optional
  `first` arg and slices the queryset after permission filtering, so
  pathological extracts no longer transmit thousands of cells just to
  trigger the row guard. New constants EXTRACT_GRID_EMBED_MAX_COLS and
  EXTRACT_GRID_EMBED_MAX_CELLS make the cap explicit. Server-side
  pagination is still tracked by #1204.

- resolveComponentMarker now receives the marker string as its React key
  from both call sites (useCamlComponentRenderer and CamlDirectiveRenderer),
  silencing the "missing key prop" warning when an article contains
  multiple [component:...] blocks. Added regression tests in
  camlComponents.test.ts.

- formatCellValue truncates JSON cell values on code-point boundaries
  via Array.from(json) instead of String.substring, preventing
  surrogate-pair corruption (U+FFFD) when cells contain emoji or
  other non-BMP characters.

- The "Insert Extract Grid" picker in CamlArticleEditor now supports
  full keyboard navigation: Arrow / Home / End move the focused option,
  Enter selects, and Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger
  button. Active option is reflected via aria-activedescendant and a
  $active highlight on ExtractPickerItem.

- buildSourceLink: added an explanatory comment clarifying that
  Annotation.page is 1-based and only used for the chip label — the
  document viewer navigates by annotationId alone.

- Verified GET_EXTRACTS already selects fullDocumentList and that
  CamlDirectiveRenderer still wires resolveImageSrc through to
  MarkdownMessageRenderer (verification items, no code change required).

Closes #1227

* Address review: accessibility fixes, keyboard nav tests, datacell first-arg tests

- Move aria-activedescendant from listbox to trigger button per ARIA spec
- Replace outline:none with focus-visible ring on ExtractPickerItem
- Add ArrowUp wrap-around comment explaining WAI-ARIA intent
- Add console.warn for column-bound datacell cap in ExtractGridEmbed
- Add backend tests for resolve_full_datacell_list first argument
- Add keyboard navigation component tests for extract picker
- Add ComponentEmbedErrorFallback component test with docScreenshot
- Add GET_EXTRACTS mocks to CamlArticleEditorTestWrapper

* Address review: move warn to useEffect, optimize formatCellValue, cap datacell first

- Move console.warn from render body into useEffect to avoid side effects
  during React renders (fires on every render and doubles in StrictMode)
- Add fast-path in formatCellValue to skip Array.from allocation when the
  JSON string is already short enough in UTF-16
- Add MAX_DATACELL_FIRST constant (10,000) and enforce server-side cap in
  resolve_full_datacell_list to prevent unbounded payloads from API clients
- Add test for server-side cap path

* Fix server-cap test to actually verify ceiling binds, document mock counts

- test_first_capped_at_server_maximum now patches MAX_DATACELL_FIRST to 2
  (below the 3 fixture cells) so the assertion proves the cap actually
  limits the result count, not just that the query succeeds.
- Add explanatory comment on CamlArticleEditorTestWrapper mock array
  explaining why 4 article mocks and 3 extract mocks are needed.

* Fix datacell list tests: add M2M relation, superuser, correct mock target

The 6 failing ExtractFullDatacellListFirstArgTestCase tests had three
root causes:

1. Documents were never added to extract.documents M2M, so the resolver
   iterated an empty set and returned no results (5 tests).
2. The test user lacked permissions to read documents through the
   permission-filtering code path.
3. test_first_capped_at_server_maximum patched the wrong module --
   MAX_DATACELL_FIRST is imported locally inside the resolver function,
   so the patch target must be the source module
   (opencontractserver.constants.annotations), not the consuming module.

Also moves the too-many-rows console.warn from a render-time side
effect into the existing useEffect in ExtractGridEmbed, addressing
review feedback about React Strict Mode double-invocation.

* Address review: harden ARIA, dev warnings, and test patch target

- Set aria-controls on trigger button only when listbox is rendered,
  fixing ARIA spec compliance (references must point to existing DOM)
- Add event.stopPropagation() on Enter key handler to prevent event
  leaking to parent Modal
- Guard useEffect dev warnings with useRef to fire only once per mount,
  avoiding repeated console noise on re-renders / Apollo cache updates
- Hoist MAX_DATACELL_FIRST import to module level in extract_types.py
  and patch at the resolver lookup site in the test, making the mock
  resilient to future import reorganization
- Document omission of Enter-key insertion test (requires additional
  GET_EXTRACT_GRID_EMBED mocks not yet in the test wrapper)

* Apply unconditional server-side cap on fullDatacellList resolver

Previously first<=0 bypassed MAX_DATACELL_FIRST entirely, allowing
any API client to retrieve unbounded payloads by sending first:0.
The resolver now always applies the ceiling: positive values are
honoured up to MAX_DATACELL_FIRST, and zero/negative/omitted values
fall back to the default cap.

Adds regression test (test_first_zero_still_capped_by_server_maximum)
and updates existing test names/docstrings to reflect the new semantics.

* Address review: fix file handle leaks, reset warning refs per extract

- Fix resource leak in test setUp: use context manager for PDF file reads
  instead of bare open() that leaks file descriptors
- Reset useRef warning guards when extractId changes so each extract gets
  its own dev warning instead of silencing warnings for subsequent extracts
- Add clarifying comments for $active/hover visual parity and useEffect
  dependency rationale

* Address review: fix ContentFile reuse bug, document breaking default cap

Fix ContentFile reuse across loop iterations in
ExtractFullDatacellListFirstArgTestCase.setUp -- ContentFile wraps a
BytesIO whose pointer advances after Django's storage backend reads it,
so subsequent loop iterations produced empty PDF files. Now creates a
fresh ContentFile per iteration from pre-read bytes.

Add a Changed section to the CHANGELOG documenting that fullDatacellList
is now capped at MAX_DATACELL_FIRST (10,000) by default. Previously
unbounded, this is a breaking change for any caller that relied on
receiving all cells without passing an explicit `first` argument.

* Move aria-activedescendant to listbox element and fix dep-array comment

aria-activedescendant is only valid on composite roles (listbox, combobox,
grid, etc.) per WAI-ARIA 1.2, not on role="button". Move it from the
trigger button to the ExtractPickerDropdown (role="listbox") where it is
spec-compliant. The aria-selected attribute on each option and the visual
$active highlight continue to provide accessible selection feedback.

Also fix the contradictory useEffect dependency comment in
ExtractGridEmbed that said "[extract] is the real driver" while including
rows and columns in the array — the deps satisfy the exhaustive-deps lint
rule.

* Address review feedback: fix aria placement, improve test coverage

- Move aria-activedescendant from listbox to trigger button per WAI-ARIA spec
- Return focus to trigger after Enter key selection for consistent keyboard UX
- Export formatCellValue and add unit tests for all branches including emoji
- Fix coverage collection for ExtractGridEmbed and ComponentEmbedErrorFallback
  CT tests (were importing directly instead of via coverage wrapper)

* Address review feedback: ARIA fix, string truncation, f-strings, cross-ref

- Move onKeyDown handler from wrapper div to trigger button in
  CamlArticleEditor extract picker, so keyboard events and
  aria-activedescendant share the same DOM focus context (WAI-ARIA
  virtual-focus listbox pattern)
- Add code-point-safe truncation for raw string values in
  formatCellValue (previously only objects were truncated), with
  two new unit tests covering long strings and emoji
- Add cross-reference comment in frontend constants linking
  EXTRACT_GRID_EMBED_MAX_CELLS to the backend MAX_DATACELL_FIRST cap
