subject: Address P0 STRIDE findings: T-1 IDOR, I-1 cascade, I-10 IDOR, T-7 worker checks
message:
Address P0 STRIDE findings: T-1 IDOR, I-1 cascade, I-10 IDOR, T-7 worker checks

T-1 / T-1b — AddAnnotation and AddDocTypeAnnotation accepted attacker-supplied
corpus_id and document_id without checking visibility or CREATE permission on
the parent corpus. Both mutations now load the parents through visible_to_user
and gate on user_has_permission_for_obj(CREATE). Errors are uniform "not found"
to mask existence. Regression test in test_add_annotation_idor.py.

I-10 — bulk_document_upload_status called celery_app.AsyncResult(job_id) with
no ownership check. Any logged-in user with a leaked job_id could read another
user's import results (document_ids, errors). Now binds job_id → user_id in
the cache at enqueue time and refuses status reads for non-matching callers.
Cache miss fails closed. Regression tests in test_bulk_document_upload.py.

T-7 — ingest_doc and retry_document_processing accepted (user_id, doc_id) and
operated on the doc without verifying the supplied user actually had access
to it. Adds defense-in-depth permission checks at the top of each task with
SECURITY-tagged logging on rejection. Regression test in
test_ingest_doc_permission_check.py.

I-1 — Corpus._propagate_public_status_to_documents bulk-updated every doc in
the corpus to is_public=True with no audit trail. The cascade now (a) skips
documents that also live in a private corpus owned by a different user
(defensive — does not fire in the normal add_document flow which creates
corpus-isolated copies, but guards against direct DocumentPath flows and
future code paths), and (b) emits DOCUMENT_PUBLICIZED notifications to each
affected document creator. New NotificationTypeChoices value + migration
0004. Regression test in test_corpus_public_flip_propagation.py.

mypy.ini — adds the three new test modules to the existing per-test
ignore_errors baseline.

T-1 follow-up — corpus-membership IDOR closer (review concern, medium):
add a private `_resolve_annotation_parents` helper that loads doc + corpus
through `visible_to_user`, gates `CREATE` on the corpus, AND verifies the
document is actually a current member of the corpus via DocumentPath.
Closes the cross-corpus path the reviewer flagged: "user has visibility
to doc D and CREATE on corpus B but D is not in B." Both AddAnnotation
and AddDocTypeAnnotation now route through the helper, removing the
duplicated try/except block and unifying the not-found message via a
module-level constant. New test `test_cannot_annotate_doc_into_unrelated

`bulk_document_upload_status` now coerces the cached owner_id to int
before comparing with `info.context.user.id`. Some Django cache backends
(Redis with custom serializers, certain LocMemCache configs) deserialize
ints as strings; without coercion the legitimate owner would be silently
denied (`"42" != 42`). Failure path falls through to the same opaque
"not found" response.

I-1 follow-up — atomic snapshot+update (review concern, low):
`Corpus._propagate_public_state_to_documents` wraps the publicize
snapshot, the bulk update, and the notification fan-out in a single

a concurrent publicize cannot slip in between snapshot and update and
trigger a stale notification for a doc that didn't actually transition
in this call.

(`test_pipeline_hardening`, `test_doc_tasks::RetryDocumentProcessing`,
`test_txt_ingestor_pipeline`, `test_base_pipeline_parser`,
`test_caml_pipeline_coverage::CamlIngestDocSkipTest`) created users +
documents directly without the guardian permissions production upload
mutations grant on creation. Updated each setUp to call
`set_permissions_for_obj_to_user(user, doc, [PermissionTypes.CRUD])`
so the worker permission check passes. Behavior the tests verify is
unchanged. The IDOR test file's setUp was also updated to capture
the corpus-isolated copy returned by `Corpus.add_document()` (the
real annotation target) instead of the original document.

subject: Add Document.objects.unique_blob_paths() for shared-blob detection (#1464)
message:
Add Document.objects.unique_blob_paths() for shared-blob detection (#1464)

Implements a manager method that returns the set of file-field blob paths
on a given Document that are not referenced by any other Document row.
Corpus-isolated copies share blobs with their source by design; callers
that delete blobs from storage must consult this method first to avoid
silently destroying files still in use by other Documents.

Includes regression tests covering: solitary ownership, shared-blob
exclusion for both source and copy, per-field uniqueness after overwrite,
and empty-field filtering.

message:
Guard memory-doc blob delete against shared-blob siblings (#1464)

When corpus.add_document() creates a corpus-isolated copy of the memory
document, the copy shares the same txt_extract_file blob. The previous
unconditional delete-then-save in update_memory_content() clobbered the
shared file, corrupting the sibling's content. Now consults
DocumentModel.objects.unique_blob_paths() before deleting: if the blob
is referenced by another Document row, the field is cleared to None
instead (leaving the blob alive), letting Django storage allocate a
fresh unique path for the new content.

Fixes the silent data-loss bug flagged in the PR #1489 review and the

subject: Generalise shared-blob protection to every Document FileField (#1464)
message:
Generalise shared-blob protection to every Document FileField (#1464)

Move the inline shared-blob check out of agents/memory.py and onto the
Document model itself as ``safe_delete_field_blob(field_name, *, save)``.
The primitive is now the single, public chokepoint for freeing a blob in
storage and works uniformly across every ``FileField`` on Document
(``pdf_file``, ``txt_extract_file``, ``pawls_parse_file``, ``icon``,
``md_summary_file``).

Behaviour:
- Empty / unset field → no-op, returns ``False``.
- Unique blob path → ``FieldFile.delete()``, returns ``True``.
- Shared blob path → field cleared on this row only (and saved if
  ``save=True``), blob retained in storage, returns ``False``.

Validates that ``field_name`` resolves to a ``FileField`` and raises
``ValueError`` for typos / non-FileField names so silent no-ops can't
hide. Field coverage is derived from ``Document._meta`` so adding a new
``FileField`` extends protection automatically.

agents/memory.py refactored to a single
``locked_doc.safe_delete_field_blob("txt_extract_file")`` call.

Tests: new ``SafeDeleteFieldBlobTestCase`` parameterizes shared / unique
/ empty / invalid-field / non-FileField cases across every ``FileField``
on Document. Existing ``DocumentDeleteBlobRetentionTestCase`` broadened
to assert the row-delete invariant for every FileField (still passes
trivially today; becomes the primary contract test once the orphan-
cleanup work in #1492 lands a row-delete blob-removal mechanic).

Forward pointer: #1492 will reuse this primitive for the orphan-cleanup
half of the contract — \"reclaim truly orphaned blobs at row-delete\".

subject: Fix corpus-home annotation deep-links by decoupling embedded from click routing
message:
Fix corpus-home annotation deep-links by decoupling embedded from click routing

DocumentAnnotationIndex overloaded a single `embedded` prop for two distinct
purposes: visual layout ("render without an outer container") and click
routing ("we are already on the document page, just rewrite ?ann="). The
corpus-home Table of Contents (DocumentTableOfContents) needed the visual
flavor but is rendered on a /c/... URL — yet handleSectionClick treated the
shared prop as proof we were on a document page and silently rewrote ?ann=
onto the corpus URL, swallowing the deep link.

Split the concern: `embedded` is now purely visual, and a new explicit
`onDocumentPage` prop controls click routing. RightPanelContent (the only
call site actually on a document page) opts in.

Regression test in DocumentAnnotationIndex.test.tsx pins the contract —
verified to fail against the pre-fix code path and pass against the fix.

backend_lock=True and no parsed content.

the new settings + their Django→Celery namespace propagation with a

subject: Remove PyTorch/CUDA dependency and slim production image to <1.5GB (#1500)
message:
Remove PyTorch/CUDA dependency and slim production image to <1.5GB (#1500)

* Drop CUDA/torch base from Django image; remove in-process cross-encoder reranker (#1494)

Switches compose/{production,local}/django/Dockerfile from
pytorch/pytorch:2.7.1-cuda12.6-cudnn9-runtime (~6 GB) to
python:3.11-slim-bookworm with strict multi-stage build/runtime separation.
Removes the optional in-process CrossEncoderReranker and its torch-pulling
side-effects so the new slim base is sufficient for every code path that
ships in the image; reranking remains available via MicroserviceReranker
and CohereReranker.

Companion cleanups:
- Delete cross_encoder_reranker.py (auto-discovered, so no registry edits).
- Delete CrossEncoderRerankerTest / CrossEncoderRerankerTests stub-based
  test classes and their now-unused MagicMock import.
- Drop tokenizers pin from requirements/base.txt (orphaned once
  sentence-transformers is gone; nothing imports it directly).
- Drop SENTENCE_TRANSFORMER_MODELS_PATH setting and its
  production-stack.yml env var (only consumer was the deleted backend).
- Tighten .dockerignore to exclude frontend/, docs/, fixtures/, locale/,
  cloudflare-og-worker/, tools/, model_preloaders/, .github/, editor
  state, top-level READMEs, and Python caches.
- Add CI image-size budget (1.5 GiB) to docker-build-release.yml that
  fails the release build on regression.
- Delete docker-build-cuda.yml workflow and docs/deployment/docker-gpu-setup.md
  (and its mkdocs nav entry); both documented the now-removed CUDA path.

Closes #1494

* Fix opencv-python-headless runtime deps on slim-bookworm

The pytorch base image masked these because Ubuntu+CUDA shipped them
already; on python:3.11-slim-bookworm 'import cv2' fails with
ImportError on libgthread-2.0.so.0 / libgomp.so.1 until libglib2.0-0
and libgomp1 are installed.

Adds the two missing apt packages to both Dockerfiles plus a
'python -c "import cv2"' smoke test so a future opencv release that
introduces a new shared-library dep fails the build immediately
instead of silently shipping a broken image.

#1494

* Restore brotli decoder so httpx can decompress Content-Encoding: br

The previous PyTorch base image shipped `brotli` incidentally via conda,
so httpx registered a `br` decoder and transparently decompressed
brotli-encoded responses. The new `python:3.11-slim-bookworm` base does
not, leaving httpx's SUPPORTED_DECODERS at {identity, gzip, deflate,
zstd}. Without a brotli decoder, httpx hands the still-compressed bytes
to callers and the OpenAI SDK raises
`json.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)` when
it tries to parse them.

This surfaced as `test_structured_response_uses_document_tools`
failing — its VCR cassette is the only one in the repo recorded with
`Content-Encoding: br`. Live OpenAI traffic was equally affected
whenever the API negotiated brotli.

Adding `brotli>=1.1.0` re-enables httpx's `br` decoder for both VCR
replay and production HTTP.

Add default LabelSet seeding and pre-fill corpus creation form (#1503)

* Pre-fill new-corpus modal with install-wide defaults

- Seed a public default LabelSet (owned by first superuser) with a small
  starter palette (Important / Question / Definition / Reference); add
  LabelSet.is_default flag with a partial unique constraint and a
  seed_default_labelset management command for re-seeding after the
  first superuser exists.
- Expose the seeded labelset via a new defaultLabelset GraphQL query;
  CreateCorpusMutation falls back to it when the caller omits label_set
  so corpuses created via the API land with a usable starter palette.
  Defaulting lives at the mutation layer (not Corpus.save) so direct
  ORM creates remain opt-in.
- CorpusModal CREATE mode pre-fills embedder + labelset selectors via
  a single GET_CORPUS_CREATE_DEFAULTS query and seeds license to
  CC-BY-4.0; users can clear any of these before submitting.

* Expand default labelset for corporate-contract review

Replaces the four-label starter (Important, Question, Definition,
Reference) with a 12-label palette. Three general research labels
(Important, Question, Reference) plus a light contract palette covering
the most common corporate-operations concepts: Definition, Party,
Governing Law, Effective Date, Termination Date, Expiration,
Termination, Renewal, Limitation of Liability.

Idempotency: the seed loop already skips labels whose text is already
attached to the labelset, so re-running 'python manage.py
seed_default_labelset' on an existing install just appends the new
contract labels — no duplicates, no overwrites.

* Fix CI for default-labelset PR: split migration, fix queryset, add tests

The original 0069 migration mixed schema DDL (AddField with db_index,
AddConstraint) with a RunPython data seeder. PostgreSQL refused to create
the new index because FK trigger events queued by the seed INSERTs were
still pending in the same transaction. Split into 0069 (schema) and 0070
(data seed) so the schema commit clears the trigger queue before the
seeder runs.

Also fixes an order-of-call bug in CreateCorpusMutation: visible_to_user
is a manager method, so it must be called on .objects, not on a queryset
returned by .filter(). The previous order would raise AttributeError on
the first corpus create that hits the default-prefill branch.

Backend tests (test_default_labelset.py) cover create_default_labelset
idempotency, demote-other-default behaviour, no-superuser path, reverse
migration including shared-label preservation, the management command,
the defaultLabelset GraphQL resolver, and the CreateCorpusMutation
prefill path. Adds the file to mypy ignore_errors per project pattern.

Frontend tests (corpus-modal.ct.tsx) cover the new pre-fill behaviour:
default license, GraphQL-sourced labelset/embedder, and the silent
fallback when the defaults query fails. Existing CREATE/EDIT/VIEW tests
get the new GET_CORPUS_CREATE_DEFAULTS mock.

Also fixes included_in_labelsets -> included_in_labelset in the existing
reverse_migration filter (it's the related_query_name, not related_name).

* Address review: atomic seed, trim comments, drop dead interface

- Wrap default-LabelSet seeding in transaction.atomic() with get_or_create
  on title to close the race between concurrent migration workers and the
  seed_default_labelset management command.
- Trim WHAT-not-WHY commentary in label_set_seeds.py per CLAUDE.md.
- Remove unused GetCorpusCreateDefaultsInput interface.

subject: WebSocket auth handshake: tokens off URLs, in-band refresh (#1502)
message:
WebSocket auth handshake: tokens off URLs, in-band refresh (#1502)

* Rewrite WS JWTAuthMiddleware to read token from Sec-WebSocket-Protocol only

Removes the historical query-string (?token=) and Authorization-header token
extraction paths. Tokens are now read exclusively from the Sec-WebSocket-Protocol
handshake header (format: "opencontracts.jwt.v1, <jwt>"), which is the only
channel a browser WebSocket constructor can populate without a custom header.

The subprotocol marker is always echoed on scope["accepted_subprotocol"] when
present — even on auth failure — so consumers can close cleanly with a 4xxx code
rather than failing at the transport layer. Auth errors are surfaced on
scope["auth_error"] with a typed close code (4001 expired, 4002 invalid).

Exports: WS_AUTH_SUBPROTOCOL, WS_CLOSE_UNAUTHENTICATED, WS_CLOSE_TOKEN_EXPIRED,
WS_CLOSE_TOKEN_INVALID, WS_CLOSE_RATE_LIMITED. Backwards-compat alias
GraphQLJWTTokenAuthMiddleware kept until consumers are updated.

Adds JWTAuthMiddlewareSubprotocolTests (6 tests) covering: no header →
anonymous, marker-only → anonymous + echoed subprotocol, valid token →
authenticated, invalid token → 4002 error + echoed subprotocol, ?token=
ignored, Authorization header ignored.

* Add AuthHandshakeMixin for in-band WS token refresh + security guards

* Wire AuthHandshakeMixin into UnifiedAgentConsumer; refactor resource perm checks

- UnifiedAgentConsumer now inherits AuthHandshakeMixin (before AsyncWebsocketConsumer
  in MRO) and calls accept_with_auth() / cleanup_auth_handshake() in connect /
  disconnect.
- Extracted corpus/document permission checks into _validate_resource_permissions()
  override so the mixin can re-validate on in-band token refresh.
- receive() fast-paths AUTH frames to handle_auth_message() before rate-limit
  gates or agent dispatch.
- JWTAuthMiddleware._parse_subprotocol_token() now also checks
  scope["subprotocols"] (ASGI spec field set by WebsocketCommunicator in tests)
  in addition to the Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header; production browser behaviour
  is unchanged.
- Updated GraphQLJWTTokenAuthMiddlewareTestCase to use subprotocol transport
  and drain the initial AUTH_OK frame before sending queries.
- Added UnifiedAgentHandshakeTests covering in-band refresh success and
  user-mismatch rejection.
- Added type: ignore comments to suppress pre-existing mypy mixin attr errors
  in auth_handshake.py and the method-assign error in the test fixture.

* Wire AuthHandshakeMixin into ThreadUpdatesConsumer

- Add AuthHandshakeMixin to MRO before AsyncWebsocketConsumer
- Replace accept() with accept_with_auth() to emit initial AUTH_OK frame
- Add AUTH fast-path at top of receive() for in-band token refresh
- Add _validate_resource_permissions() override re-checking conversation
  access (owner, superuser, corpus/document visibility) on refresh
- Call cleanup_auth_handshake() in disconnect()
- Add ThreadUpdatesHandshakeTests (3 tests: valid token, no token 4000,
  in-band refresh)

* Wire AuthHandshakeMixin into NotificationUpdatesConsumer

- Add AuthHandshakeMixin to MRO before AsyncWebsocketConsumer
- Replace accept() with accept_with_auth() to emit initial AUTH_OK frame
  before the existing CONNECTED frame
- Add AUTH fast-path at top of receive() for in-band token refresh
- Call cleanup_auth_handshake() in disconnect()
- No _validate_resource_permissions() override needed; consumer is bound
  to the authenticated user themselves (user-pk swap already forbidden by
  the mixin)
- Add NotificationUpdatesHandshakeTests (3 tests: AUTH_OK+CONNECTED pair,
  no token 4001, in-band refresh)

* Add frontend websocketAuth helpers (subprotocol + AUTH frame builders)

* Add useWebSocketAuth shared hook (subprotocol + in-band refresh)

* Strip token from WS URL builders; delete deprecated DocumentQuery/CorpusQuery wrappers

Tokens are now carried exclusively via the Sec-WebSocket-Protocol subprotocol
header (useWebSocketAuth). The three remaining URL builders — getUnifiedAgentWebSocket,
getThreadUpdatesWebSocket, getNotificationUpdatesWebSocket — no longer accept or embed
token parameters. getDocumentQueryWebSocket and getCorpusQueryWebSocket are deleted.

* Refactor useNotificationWebSocket to compose useWebSocketAuth

Replaces bespoke WebSocket lifecycle with the shared useWebSocketAuth hook.
Token rotation is now in-band (no socket churn). The autoReconnect option is
removed from the public API since reconnect behavior is owned by useWebSocketAuth.
Callers that passed autoReconnect: true have the option removed (it remains the default).

* Refactor useAgentChat to compose useWebSocketAuth (no token in URL)

Deletes local getEnvVar / resolveWsBaseUrl / getUnifiedAgentWebSocketUrl helpers;
delegates to getUnifiedAgentWebSocket from get_websockets.ts. The WebSocket lifecycle
(open, close, reconnect, in-band token refresh) is now owned by useWebSocketAuth.
reconnectTrigger state and auth_token reactive-var read are removed.
Test file updated to import getUnifiedAgentWebSocket from get_websockets and
assert no token in URL.

* Migrate CorpusChat and document utils to tokenless WS URLs

CorpusChat: import getUnifiedAgentWebSocket instead of getCorpusQueryWebSocket;
drop auth_token from URL builder call and effect dep array.
document/utils.ts: drop token parameter from getWebSocketUrl; remove @deprecated
JSDoc block.
ChatTray: update getWebSocketUrl call to drop token arg; remove now-unused
auth_token reactive-var read and authToken import.

* Add WS auth handshake manual test script + CHANGELOG entry

* Ratchet any-baseline after WS auth refactor (460→454)

* Address PR #1502 review: migrate CorpusChat/ChatTray, harden refresh

Critical fixes from claude-review feedback:

- CorpusChat.tsx and ChatTray.tsx now compose useWebSocketAuth instead of
  bare `new WebSocket(url)`. Without this both chat surfaces would have
  authenticated as anonymous against the new middleware (no subprotocol →
  no token). Sub-tool unwrapping for ask_document approvals stays in
  CorpusChat; ChatTray keeps its message-state-derived processing
  indicator. pendingApproval is mirrored into a ref so the once-installed
  onmessage closure reads the latest value without retriggering connect.

- AuthHandshakeMixin.handle_auth_message now enforces a 1-second
  per-connection cooldown before any DB work (token validation +
  resource permission check). Stops a malicious client from spamming
  AUTH frames to burn queries; legitimate Auth0 refreshes are ~50 min
  apart so unaffected.

- useWebSocketAuth now treats close codes 4000 (UNAUTHENTICATED) and
  4001 (TOKEN_EXPIRED) as auth-invalid signals (was: silently fell
  through to exponential-backoff reconnect, hammering a server that
  would just reject them the same way). The hook also no longer returns
  the underlying ws reference — it was stale on first render and a
  footgun for callers; useAgentChat's socketRef mirror is dropped.
  useNotificationWebSocket drops the no-op disconnect()/connect aliases
  for the same reason.

- Each consumer's receive() parses the incoming text frame once and
  dispatches AUTH or non-AUTH from the single parsed payload (was
  double-parsing). thread_updates.py consolidates Corpus/Document/
  Conversation imports to the module level.

Test wrappers (CorpusChat, ChatTray) needed `static OPEN = 1` on their
StubSocket so the hook's `ws.readyState !== WebSocket.OPEN` send guard
works after `window.WebSocket = StubSocket`. useAgentChat unit tests
also adjust three stale assertions left over from the URL-token
removal: token=test-token in URL → expect not to contain token=, and
the two _fail()-driven error tests now drive errors via close 4002 +
onAuthInvalid (the post-migration path that actually surfaces errors
to consumers).

CHANGELOG updated. New CT screenshot:
knowledge-base--chat-tray--conversation-list.png.

* WS auth: address codecov gaps + silence React 18 act warnings

The codecov patch coverage check on PR #1502 flagged seven WS-auth files
under the 70% target. None of the gaps were behavioural — the new code
was almost entirely covered by integration paths — but several branches
(empty-token send, AUTH_FAILED routing, exponential backoff, rate-limit
backoff, transport error, disabled mode, env-var URL resolution,
heartbeat lifecycle) had no direct unit assertion.

This commit closes the gaps with focused unit tests and, in the
process, retires the legacy `@testing-library/react-hooks`
dependency in this file (it pulled in a `ReactDOM.render`
deprecation warning on every test run under React 18).

- New `src/test-utils/renderHook.tsx`: minimal React-18-native
  `renderHook` + `cleanup` + `act` re-export built on
  `react-dom/client` `createRoot` + `react`'s `act`. Tracks live
  roots so `cleanup()` can unmount them before each test's own
  teardown, preventing stale `useReactiveVar` listeners from firing
  setState on torn-down trees (which would otherwise surface as
  "update was not wrapped in act(...)" warnings).

- `setupTests.ts`: set `IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT = true` so React 18
  recognises the new helper's act calls.

- `useWebSocketAuth.test.ts`: migrated off `@testing-library/react-hooks`
  to the new helper. Added 11 cases for `enabled=false` short-circuit,
  `send()` open-state guard, AUTH_FAILED handling, `onerror` →
  `lastError`, non-auth `onMessage` forwarding, AUTH frame
  non-forwarding, exponential backoff, 4x rate-limited backoff,
  forced reconnect, empty-token AUTH suppression, and unmount
  close-code.

- `useNotificationWebSocket.test.ts`: new file covering connection
  states, AUTH_OK transition, CONNECTED session capture,
  NOTIFICATION_CREATED/UPDATED/DELETED routing, missing-field
  guards, pong/heartbeat_ack swallowing, malformed-frame logging,
  clearRecent, sendPing, heartbeat interval lifecycle, forced
  reconnect, and post-close state.

- `get_websockets.test.ts`: new file covering env-var resolution
  precedence (VITE_WS_URL > VITE_API_URL > location), trailing-slash
  stripping, http→ws normalisation, process.env fallback, and the
  `getWebSocketUrl` document-utils wrapper.

- `websocketAuth.test.ts`: added AUTH_FAILED / AUTH_REFRESH_REQUIRED
  parsing, plus null-on-non-object and null-on-missing-type cases.

* Add full-stack E2E spec + workflow for websocket auth handshake

PR #1502 introduced subprotocol-based JWT transport with in-band
refresh, but coverage stopped at the WebsocketCommunicator boundary —
nothing exercised the real browser → Vite proxy → Daphne ASGI →
consumer pipeline. This adds:

  * frontend/tests/e2e/websocket-auth.spec.ts — 6 tests across all
    three consumers covering authenticated subscribe, anonymous
    rejection, ?token= regression, anonymous-on-private rejection,
    authenticated agent chat (via VCR cassette), and in-band token
    refresh on a public document. Asserts on real frames captured via
    page.on('websocket'); triggers a real BADGE notification via
    docker exec to prove signal-driven broadcast end-to-end.

  * .github/workflows/frontend-e2e-websocket.yml — mirrors the extract
    workflow (local.yml stack with Daphne, VCR replay, Codecov upload
    under flags frontend-e2e/frontend/websocket and
    backend-e2e/websocket).

  * config/websocket/consumers/unified_agent_conversation.py — wraps
    _stream_agent_response and _handle_approval_decision in
    maybe_vcr_cassette() so the cassette covers both LLM-touching code
    paths. No-op in production.

  * .github/workflows/codecov-notify.yml — adds the new workflow to
    the wait list so the merged Codecov status accounts for it.

  * Recorded cassette at
    opencontractserver/tests/fixtures/cassettes/e2e_websocket_auth/agent_chat.yaml.

  * Documented in CHANGELOG and docs/test_scripts/websocket-e2e-spec.md.

Notable finding (recorded in the spec and CHANGELOG): real browsers
see close code 1006 — not the application-level 4001/4003 — for any
auth rejection that happens before the consumer calls accept().
Channels translates a pre-accept close() into an HTTP 403 handshake
rejection, which never produces a WebSocket close frame with the
application code. The unit tests still see the application code
because Channels exposes it directly to WebsocketCommunicator. The
e2e tests assert the real browser surface so a future change to
accept-then-close (which would let the browser see the application
code) is caught and the test gets updated.

All 6 tests verified passing locally against the full local.yml stack
under VCR replay.

* Add WebSocket readyState statics to test stubs

useWebSocketAuth.send() guards on `ws.readyState !== WebSocket.OPEN`.
When tests replace `window.WebSocket` with a `StubSocket` class,
`WebSocket.OPEN` resolves to `StubSocket.OPEN`. Without the static
constants the comparison evaluates `1 !== undefined` and the hook
silently refuses to send, leaving CT tests blocked on chat input.

Add `static CONNECTING/OPEN/CLOSING/CLOSED` to ContextMeter,
DocumentKnowledgeBase, DocumentKnowledgeBaseCorpusless, and
DocumentRenderingCornerCases stub sockets to match ChatTray and
CorpusChat, which already declare them.

* Address PR #1502 review feedback

Frontend (useWebSocketAuth):
- Hold onMessage/onOpen/onClose/onAuthInvalid in refs and read through
  them inside the long-lived ws handlers. Eliminates the stale-closure
  hazard that the eslint-disable was masking.

Backend (AuthHandshakeMixin):
- Track _handshake_connected on the mixin itself instead of relying on
  an _is_connected attribute that only UnifiedAgentConsumer set. The
  refresh grace timer now has reliable connection state across all
  three consumers.

Backend (ThreadUpdatesConsumer):
- Collapse _check_conversation_access and _validate_resource_permissions
  onto a single sync helper with a cache_conversation flag. Removes the
  drift hazard between two near-identical permission queries and the
  nested @database_sync_to_async wrapper.

Backend (middleware):
- Add WS_CLOSE_NORMAL = 1000 alongside the 4xxx application codes.
- Document the Sec-WebSocket-Protocol passthrough requirement for
  reverse proxies in the module docstring with a concrete nginx snippet.

CHANGELOG: note the useNotificationWebSocket return-shape change
(connect/disconnect → reconnect) under the Unreleased Security entry.

* Migrate WS test suites to Sec-WebSocket-Protocol JWT transport

The middleware rewrite in this PR only honors tokens via the
Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header. Update the notification, token-expiration,
document-approval, unified-agent-consumer, and permission-escalation test
suites to use the new transport. Drain the initial AUTH_OK frame emitted
by AuthHandshakeMixin before asserting on consumer messages.

Also align _DummyConsumer with the new _handshake_connected attribute
that replaces the consumer-specific _is_connected flag.

Verified locally:
- test_notification_websocket.py — 18/18 pass
- test_token_expiration.py + test_websocket_document_approval.py +
  test_unified_agent_consumer.py — 38/38 pass
- test_agent_permission_escalation.py — 49/49 pass
- test_websocket_auth.py (AuthHandshakeMixinTests) — 9/9 pass

* Address Claude review on PR #1502

S1 — Consolidate WS_CLOSE_PERMISSION_DENIED in middleware.py with the
other close-code constants; auth_handshake.py imports from there. Keeps
the wire-protocol vocabulary in a single canonical home.

S3 — Wrap _validate_resource_permissions in try/except inside
handle_auth_message. An unexpected error in a consumer override (DB
timeout, stale FK, etc.) is now treated as PERMISSION_REVOKED → close
4003 rather than letting the exception propagate and leave the
consumer half-swapped. New test
test_handle_auth_resource_permission_exception_closes_4003 locks this
in.

C3 — Document the no-reconnect-after-auth-fail contract on
useWebSocketAuth.onAuthInvalid. The hook intentionally stops scheduling
reconnects when the server returns 4000/4001/4002 (no point retrying
with the same stale token); callers must obtain a new token and call
reconnect() to resume.

C4 — Fix misleading comment in middleware._parse_subprotocol_token:
the scope["subprotocols"] branch is the primary Daphne production
path, not just the test-communicator path. The HTTP-header branch is
a fallback for non-spec ASGI servers.

* Fix notifications WS rejecting on first mount before token settles

The notification updates hook (useNotificationWebSocket) is mounted at
the App root and was opening a token-less socket on first render. The
NotificationUpdatesConsumer rejected anonymous connections with close
code 4001 (TOKEN_EXPIRED), which the shared useWebSocketAuth hook
interprets as terminal "session invalid" and stops scheduling
reconnects. Eventual recovery only happened by accident, when something
else (route transition, context refresh) caused the hook to remount.

Three coordinated changes:

* useWebSocketAuth gains `requireAuth?: boolean` (default false). When
  true, the connect effect skips opening while the auth-token reactive
  var is empty AND re-runs automatically on the empty → non-empty
  transition. Backward compatible — endpoints that accept anonymous
  (e.g. /ws/agent-chat/ on a public doc) keep working unchanged.

* useNotificationWebSocket sets `requireAuth: true`.

* notification_updates.py was closing 4001 (TOKEN_EXPIRED) when the
  scope had no user at all. That's a category error — TOKEN_EXPIRED
  means the middleware decoded a token and found it stale, not "no
  token was sent". Switched to 4000 (UNAUTHENTICATED) so the frontend
  surface matches the actual reason. Even with `requireAuth` blocking
  most anonymous opens, this keeps the close-code semantics honest for
  cases like a stale tab whose token field cleared after logout.

* Lift ChatTray showLoad onto chatTrayStateAtom + WS diagnostics

* Lift the conversation-list overlay state (`showLoad`) out of
  DocumentKnowledgeBase's local useState and onto chatTrayStateAtom.
  Previously DKB owned `showLoad` and passed `setShowLoad` through
  RightPanelContent → ChatTray; ChatTray's mount-time
  `loadConversation`/`startNewChat` paths invoked the parent setter,
  which React flagged with "Cannot update a component
  (DocumentKnowledgeBase) while rendering a different component
  (ChatTray)" once the chain crossed the render boundary. ChatTray now
  reads/writes `showLoad` through the atom via a local helper that
  preserves the previous `setShowLoad(false)` call surface.

  Files:
    UISettingsAtom.tsx     — add `showLoad` to ChatTrayPersist + default
    DocumentKnowledgeBase  — drop the useState + prop pass-through
    RightPanelContent      — drop the prop interface + JSX forwarding
    ChatTray               — drop props, derive setShowLoad from atom
    ChatTrayTestWrapper    — drop the no-longer-passed props (kept as
                             accepted-but-ignored options for source
                             compatibility with existing tests)

  CorpusChat is unrelated and keeps its own showLoad prop.

* Diagnostic logs (temporary) for the CorpusChat reset-cycle thread:
    useWebSocketAuth.ts    — log open/close/cleanup with per-effect ids,
                             token-effect skip reason, requireAuth gate
    CorpusChat.tsx         — instance-tagged mount/unmount, wsUrl/enabled
                             change tracker, forceNewChat effect log,
                             loadConversation / startNewChat / initialQuery
                             effect logs

  These are easy to remove (single grep for `[CorpusChat ` / `[useWebSocketAuth `).

* Strip WS chat diagnostic logs

Remove the [CorpusChat <id>] / [useWebSocketAuth <id>] console.info
lines added during the chat-cycle investigation. Issue diagnosed and
the noisy log spew is now back out.

* Address Claude review v2: 4001 test, anon stale-perm, doc + cleanup

* test_handshake_no_token_closes_4001 → renamed to _4000 and fixed to
  assert the actual close code. The notification consumer was changed
  to close 4000 (UNAUTHENTICATED) earlier in the branch but this test
  wasn't updated, so it would fail in CI. ThreadUpdates' equivalent
  test was already correct.

* unified_agent_conversation._validate_resource_permissions: the
  anonymous fallback was reading is_public from the in-memory Corpus /
  Document loaded at connect time. If an owner flips the resource to
  private mid-connection, an anonymous AUTH refresh would pass on
  stale state. Re-fetch from the DB on the anonymous path. The

message:
Fix Discover search crash on null annotation/note documents (#1511)

Running a search from the Discover view could throw
"TypeError: can't access property 'slug', e is null" when the backend
returned an annotation or note edge whose `document` was null (visibility
filtering, soft-deletes). `getDocumentUrl` accessed `document.slug`

subject: Fix corpus list reload loop and move tab filtering to backend (#1512)
message:
Fix corpus list reload loop and move tab filtering to backend (#1512)

* Fix corpus list reload loop and move tab filtering to backend

Two related Corpuses-view bugs:

1. Documents tab "loading → idle → loading" infinite render loop
   - In CorpusDocumentCards, document_items was rebuilt with .map().filter()
     on every render, so the [document_items] effect saw a fresh dep ref each
     time. Its cleanup→set cycle thrashed currentViewDocumentIds, which
     re-rendered FolderDocumentBrowser, which re-rendered CorpusDocumentCards,
     and so on.
   - Memoize document_items on the stable Apollo edges reference and key the
     effect on a primitive id-string so it only fires when the actual id set
     changes.
   - Also drop two leftover console.log debug calls in DocumentCards.

2. "My Corpuses" tab filter happened on the frontend, so deleting a corpus
   didn't remove it from the visible list until enough fetchMore calls
   reloaded the affected page.
   - Add mine / isPublic / sharedWithMe filter args to the corpuses
     connection (CorpusFilter) and a new corpusFilterCounts query for
     accurate tab badges across the entire visible set, both respecting
     visible_to_user permissions.
   - Lift activeFilter state up to Corpuses.tsx and feed it into the
     GET_CORPUSES variables; remove client-side filtering from
     CorpusListView.
   - Add the filter args to the corpuses cache keyArgs so each tab gets
     its own paged connection.
   - Add an update callback to DELETE_CORPUS that evicts the deleted
     corpus from cache, so the list updates instantly without waiting on
     refetch.
   - Refresh the counts query alongside refetchCorpuses on
     create/update/delete.

Tests: new opencontractserver/tests/test_corpus_list_filters.py covers
the three filter args, count totals, text-search interaction, and the
anonymous-user paths.

* Apply Black formatting (pre-commit fixups)

* Update CorpusListView tests for server-side tab filtering

The CorpusListView component now requires activeFilter, onFilterChange,
and filterCounts props (server is the source of truth for tab
filtering). The test wrapper now manages activeFilter state internally
and computes counts from the static corpus list, replicating server
semantics for tests. The 'shows correct stats summary' test was scoped
to .oc-stat-block__value to avoid strict-mode collision with the new
filter tab badge counts.

* Address review: collapse counts query, dedupe types, document filter contract

Backend:
- resolve_corpus_filter_counts now uses a single .aggregate() with
  conditional Count(filter=Q(...)) instead of four separate COUNT(*)
  round-trips against the same visible queryset.
- CorpusFilterCountsType fields are required=True so generated TS types
  don't force null-guards everywhere on the frontend.
- is_public_method now treats False as a no-op, matching mine_method
  and shared_with_me_method instead of inverting to filter(is_public=False).
- Documented the 'opt-in only, one flag per call' contract on the tab
  filter methods so the no-op-on-False behavior isn't a footgun.

Frontend:
- CorpusListView imports CorpusFilterCounts from queries.ts instead
  of redefining a structurally identical CorpusFilterCountsLocal.
- totalCorpuses stat is now scoped to the active tab so the badge and
  stat agree (was previously always showing the global total).
- CorpusDocumentCards: derive document_ids as a memoized array and
  hand it to the reactive var directly, using document_ids_key only
  as the effect's primitive dep key. Removes the split-by-comma
  assumption about Relay GlobalIDs.
- Comment in Corpuses.tsx delete handler explains that refetchCorpuses
  is load-bearing for pagination cursor correctness, not redundant
  with cache.evict.

subject: Fix encrypted secrets merging in parser kwargs resolution (#1516)
message:
Fix encrypted secrets merging in parser kwargs resolution (#1516)

* Merge encrypted secrets into get_parser_kwargs (#1515)

PipelineSettings.get_parser_kwargs returned only parser_kwargs[path]
verbatim and silently dropped any decrypted secret stored under
encrypted_secrets[path]. Parsers like LlamaParseParser whose api_key
lives only in encrypted_secrets (the documented secure location) were
invoked with an empty placeholder and failed with "API key not
configured".

Fix:
- get_parser_kwargs now overlays encrypted_secrets[path] on top of
  parser_kwargs[path]; secrets win on key collision. Operators may
  keep api_key="" as a schema marker without clobbering the real key.
- Build the merged dict per call so decrypted secrets are not retained
  on a long-lived PipelineSettings reference.
- updatePipelineSettings mutation rejects non-empty plaintext values
  for SettingType.SECRET fields in both parser_kwargs and
  component_settings, directing operators to updateComponentSecrets.
  Empty/None values are still allowed as schema markers.

Tests cover merge, secret-wins, secret-only, no-mutation, log
redaction, and mutation-side rejection (parser_kwargs and
component_settings) plus the empty-placeholder allow-list.

Closes #1515

* Address review: symmetric secret merge + deterministic mutation tests

- get_component_settings now overlays encrypted_secrets like
  get_parser_kwargs does, so direct callers (and the
  get_full_component_settings wrapper) cannot silently drop secrets.
  Empty placeholders still allowed; merged dict built per call so
  decrypted secrets are not retained on the model.

- Replace skipTest-based mutation validation tests with a fake
  registry + fake parser fixture so plaintext-secret rejection is
  exercised regardless of which real components are installed in the
  CI image (previously all three tests silently skipped when no
  registered component declared a SECRET field).

- Add test_update_parser_kwargs_rejects_non_dict_value to cover the
  isinstance(kwargs, dict) guard that had no test.

- Add test_get_component_settings_merges_encrypted_secrets mirroring
  the existing parser_kwargs regression coverage.

- Lift get_secret_settings import in pipeline_settings_mutations to
  module level (no circular concern).

---------

subject: Stop double-write loop in CorpusDocumentCards reactive var sync (#1517)
message:
Stop double-write loop in CorpusDocumentCards reactive var sync (#1517)

* Stop double-write to currentViewDocumentIds / documentsLoading vars

The cleanup-then-set pattern (cleanup returns a reset, body writes the
new value) fires two reactive-var notifications per dep change. With
FolderDocumentBrowser subscribing to both currentViewDocumentIds and
documentsLoading via useReactiveVar, every subscriber re-renders twice
per change, and any upstream reference instability turns it into an
infinite reload loop in production.

Split unmount-only reset into a separate []-deps effect, and gate writes
on value equality so identical IDs / loading state don't notify
subscribers at all.

* Restore cheap JOINs and user-perm prefetches under lightweight=True

GET_DOCUMENTS was running with Document.objects.visible_to_user(...,
lightweight=True), which dropped *every* select_related and
prefetch_related on the queryset. The GraphQL field set, however,
still asks for creator { slug }, myPermissions, and (when
annotateDocLabels=true) doc_label_annotations on every node — none
of which the lightweight resolver was prepared to satisfy. Each list
row therefore paid for:

  - 1 SELECT for creator (no select_related)
  - 2 SELECTs for myPermissions (resolve_my_permissions falls back to
    documentuserobjectpermission_set / documentgroupobjectpermission_set
    queries when _prefetched_user_perms is missing)
  - ~12 round-trips for docAnnotations(annotationLabel_LabelType=
    DOC_TYPE_LABEL) — resolve_doc_annotations_optimized's prefetched
    branch is unreachable without the prefetch, so it falls through
    to a per-document AnnotationQueryOptimizer.get_document_annotations
    call which itself re-fetches the document and runs five
    user_has_permission_for_obj checks on doc + corpus.

The original lightweight switch was an all-or-nothing flag, but the
expensive prefetches and the cheap ones aren't the same thing:

  cheap (always wanted on list views):
    - select_related("creator", "user_lock", "parent")
    - user-scoped guardian permission prefetches

  heavy (skip on list views):
    - full doc_annotations (with select_related on label/corpus/
      analysis/creator)
    - rows
    - source_relationships
    - target_relationships
    - notes

Apply only the cheap optimisations under lightweight=True. Add an
opt-in with_doc_label_annotations flag that adds a focused
Prefetch("doc_annotations", ...) filtered to label_type=DOC_TYPE_LABEL,
populating _prefetched_doc_annotations so the list-view badge
resolver short-circuits instead of fanning out per row.

resolve_documents now opts in to the focused prefetch when the
operation actually selects docAnnotations(annotationLabel_LabelType:
"DOC_TYPE_LABEL") under documents → edges → node, detected by walking
info.field_nodes (with fragment-spread support and
operation-variable resolution).

Tests: update test_lightweight_skips_prefetch to reflect the new
contract (cheap JOINs / user-perm prefetches kept; heavy fan-outs
still skipped) and add coverage for the focused doc-label prefetch
and for the AST helper itself, including the variable-bound and
fragment-spread paths.

* Drop redundant Corpuses GET_DOCUMENTS lazy refetch + normalize creator selections

The corpus document view was firing GET_DOCUMENTS twice on every open:

1. CorpusDocumentCards's useQuery, scoped to the current folder
   (inFolderId="__root__" or a real folder id).
2. A separate, corpus-wide query from a useLazyQuery in Corpuses.tsx
   triggered by useEffect(() => refetch_documents(), [meta_filter]).
   useLazyQuery.refetch executes immediately — including on mount when
   the dep starts as undefined — so the lazy query fired with the
   variables baked into its config (no inFolderId).

The two responses overlapped on the same DocumentType cache nodes
with different `creator` shapes. UserType has no `id`/keyFields, so
Apollo couldn't normalize the user — every write replaced the parent
DocumentType.creator field, fired a merge warning, invalidated the
cache entry, and re-emitted to all watchers (FolderDocumentBrowser
via useReactiveVar). The user-visible symptom was the document list
loading, displaying, and reloading in a tight loop.

Two fixes:

- Drop the useEffect → refetch_documents() in Corpuses.tsx. The list
  in CorpusDocumentCards already re-runs on metadata-filter changes
  via its own variables (hasAnnotationsWithIds is read from a
  reactive var that the queryVariables literal captures). The lazy
  refetch was producing a duplicate, less-precise response.
- Add `id` to every GraphQL `creator { ... }` selection that didn't
  already have it (19 blocks across queries.ts, mutations.ts,
  landing-queries.ts, AddToCorpusModal). Apollo can now normalize
  UserType across queries instead of merging-by-replacement on every
  write, eliminating the merge warning and the cache thrashing.

* Ignore local .worktrees/ scratch directory

* Cut N+1 storms in GetDocumentKnowledgeAndAnnotations

Six structural problems were stacked in this query, each multiplying
the work by the number of annotations on the document (~2000 in the
reported case):

1. AnnotationQueryOptimizer.get_document_annotations annotated
   feedback_count=Count("user_feedback") on the queryset. With
   select_related("annotation_label", "creator", "analysis") in the
   same select, Postgres ran a LEFT JOIN user_feedback + GROUP BY
   annotation.id over the joined row set for every annotation, even
   when 99% of annotations have no feedback at all.
2. .distinct() then ran a sort/hash unique pass over that joined
   result. The filters in this resolver don't introduce duplicates
   (analysis/extract visibility uses subqueries, not JOINs), so
   distinct was paying a per-row cost for nothing.
3. user_feedback was never prefetched. The GraphQL query selects
   userFeedback { edges { node { id approved rejected } } totalCount }
   on every annotation. Without a Prefetch on the annotation queryset
   the connection resolver fired self.user_feedback.all() per row.
4. UserFeedbackType.get_queryset re-applied .visible_to_user(user) to
   the related manager, which threw away any prefetch cache that did
   exist and forced a fresh SELECT per parent row.
5. CountableConnection.resolve_total_count called QuerySet.count(),
   which never consults _result_cache. Even when the prefetch worked,
   totalCount fired a fresh COUNT(*) per row.
6. _compute_effective_permissions did Document.objects.get(...) and
   Corpus.objects.get(...) plus 5+5 user_has_permission_for_obj calls
   per invocation. Three sibling resolvers in this query
   (allAnnotations, allRelationships, allDocRelationships) each
   triggered the same path with the same arguments.

Fixes:

- Drop feedback_count=Count(...) and the trailing .distinct() from
  get_document_annotations. The _can_read/_can_create/... constant
  Value annotations stay (cheap, used by AnnotatePermissionsForReadMixin).
- Prefetch("user_feedback", queryset=UserFeedback.objects.only("id",
  "approved", "rejected", "commented_annotation_id")) on the
  annotation queryset.
- AnnotationType.resolve_feedback_count now reads the prefetched list
  before falling back to .count().
- UserFeedbackType.get_queryset detects when the related manager has
  prefetched data on the parent (instance._prefetched_objects_cache)
  and passes the queryset through unchanged, preserving the cache.
- CountableConnection.resolve_total_count consults _result_cache and
  uses len(...) when the queryset is already evaluated.
- _compute_effective_permissions accepts a context argument and
  caches the (user, document, corpus) result on
  context._effective_perms_cache; sibling resolvers in the same
  request hit the cache instead of re-running the permission walk.
  The Document and Corpus instance lookups it performs are also
  cached on context._document_instance_cache /
  context._corpus_instance_cache.
- get_document_relationships threads context through, sharing the
  cache with the annotation resolver.
- resolve_all_annotations / resolve_all_relationships /
  resolve_doc_annotations_optimized pass info.context.

Tests cover the new caches (permissions, document, corpus) and assert
that the user_feedback prefetch + cached feedback_count produce zero
queries scaling with annotation count.

* Fix mypy and lint errors in optimizer and tests

- Add with_doc_label_annotations parameter to AgentConfigurationManager,
  AgentActionResultManager, and CorpusActionExecutionManager visible_to_user
  overrides to match BaseVisibilityManager signature.
- Cast graphql AST nodes to OperationDefinitionNode and FragmentDefinitionNode
  in test_requests_doc_label_annotations to satisfy mypy attribute checks.
- Annotate setUpTestData class attributes in
  test_get_document_knowledge_optimizations and import the concrete User
  model so mypy can resolve cls.owner.pk.
- Drop unused Corpus/Document module imports from
  AnnotationQueryOptimizer._compute_effective_permissions.
- Apply black reformatting touches in custom_resolvers and user_types.

* Address review and CI follow-ups for document-list-infinite-loop fix

Review feedback (Claude):
- Restore select_related("structural_annotation_set") on the request-cached
  document fetcher so the structural-set FK dereference inside
  get_document_annotations stays a single round-trip; drop the no-op pass
  block that previously gestured at the dropped optimisation.
- Document that with_doc_label_annotations is intentionally only consulted
  in lightweight mode (the full prefetch already loads all doc_annotations).
- Drop the redundant "or {}" fallback in resolve_feedback_count — getattr
  with a default never returns None.
- Add comments noting the Django-internal coupling for _result_cache,
  _prefetched_objects_cache, prefetch_cache_name, and instance, with
  pointers to the correctness-preserving fallback paths.
- Reach into the prefetched user_feedback list via the public
  RelatedManager API in test_user_feedback_is_prefetched.
- Add a comment in queries.ts noting the AST coupling between GET_DOCUMENTS
  and requests_doc_label_annotations so a future restructuring updates
  both in lockstep.

Component tests (AddToCorpusModal):
- Sync the test mock query with the new creator { id email } selection so
  Apollo MockedProvider can match the request shape.
- Add maxUsageCount: Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY so the modal's open-trigger
  refetch effect doesn't exhaust the single-use mock and surface the
  "No more mocked responses" error.

Backend coverage:
- Add ComputeEffectivePermissionsBranchTests covering the anonymous /
  private-doc / private-corpus / authenticated-no-permission branches that
  the previous suite skipped via the superuser fast-path.
- Add GetDocumentAnnotationsBranchTests covering corpus-less calls
  (structural-only return shape, structural=False short-circuit) and the
  no-active-DocumentPath branch.
- Add GetAnnotationsForPathTests for the corpus-scoped path lookup,
  including the unknown-path and missing-version branches.
- Add RequestCachedFetcherTests for _get_document_for_request and
  _get_corpus_for_request, including DoesNotExist caching and the
  context=None fallback used outside GraphQL request flows.

subject: Bound peak memory in PDF image extraction step (#1532)
message:
Bound peak memory in PDF image extraction step (#1532)

* Bound peak memory in PDF image extraction step

The post-reassemble image-extraction step in the Celery ingest_doc
pipeline previously rasterised each PDF page once *per embedded image*
via pdf2image.convert_from_bytes and never explicitly closed the
resulting PIL Image / BytesIO buffers. Peak RSS scaled with
page_count * images_per_page, so a 127-page document OOM'd workers
that handled 30-page documents without issue.

Refactor extract_images_from_pdf to process pages one at a time:
  * Split _crop_pdf_region into _render_pdf_page and
    _crop_region_from_rendered_page so a page is rasterised at most
    ONCE per call regardless of how many images live on it.
  * Close PIL Image and BytesIO buffers eagerly in inner finally
    blocks (per-image) and after the page loop (rendered page).
  * Flush pdfplumber's per-page parse cache via page.flush_cache()
    so its lazy caches don't accumulate across the iteration.
  * Force gc.collect() every IMAGE_EXTRACTION_GC_INTERVAL_PAGES pages
    (default 1) to reclaim Poppler subprocess buffers under default
    CPython GC thresholds.

Peak working set per call is now
``len(pdf_bytes) + 1 rendered page + 1 decoded image bytes`` --
independent of total page count, so a 30-page document and a 300-page
document of similar shape produce the same RSS profile.

New env vars (defaults preserve current behaviour):
  IMAGE_EXTRACTION_DPI=150              page-render RSS scales as ~DPI^2
  IMAGE_EXTRACTION_GC_INTERVAL_PAGES=1  set to 0 to disable explicit GC

Regression tests in
opencontractserver/tests/test_pdf_token_extraction.py::TestExtractImagesMemoryBound
pin the render-once-per-page contract, rendered-page closure,
pdfplumber cache flush, gc.collect cadence, eager per-image buffer
close, and synthetic 100-page scaling. Operator memory budget and
tuning knobs documented in docs/pipelines/pipeline_overview.md.

Closes #1498

* Fix PIL image leak on mode conversion, add RGBA/LA/P and coverage tests

- In _extract_images_for_page and crop_image_from_pdf: when converting
  RGBA/LA/P images to RGB for JPEG encoding, close the original PIL
  image before rebinding the variable to the converted copy. Without
  this, the pre-conversion pixel buffer was dropped without close(),
  leaking memory until the next GC cycle.

- In crop_image_from_pdf: add explicit _close_quietly calls for both
  the PIL image and BytesIO buffer after use, so those allocations are
  reclaimed immediately rather than waiting for the caller's GC.

- Add TestCloseQuietly to cover the _close_quietly helper (None, no
  close method, swallowed exceptions).

- Add tests in TestExtractImagesMemoryBound for RGBA, LA, and P mode
  conversion paths (verifying original image is closed, convert() is
  called, and the converted copy is also closed by the finally block).
  Add test for RGB image (no spurious convert() call, but close still
  happens). Add size-limit test that patches MAX_TOTAL_IMAGES_SIZE_BYTES
  to a small value to avoid gigabytes of test data.

- Add TestCropImageFromPdfModeConversion covering the same RGBA/LA/P
  close-before-rebind contract in crop_image_from_pdf, plus a test that
  the PIL image is closed after getvalue().

- Fix pre-existing mypy error in utils/embeddings.py: get_embedder
  return type declared tuple[Optional[type[BaseEmbedder]], ...] but
  get_component_by_name returns type[PipelineComponentBase] | None;
  add cast() at the return site.

subject: Replace base64-over-GraphQL uploads with multipart REST endpoints (#1513)
message:
Replace base64-over-GraphQL uploads with multipart REST endpoints (#1513)

* Move document upload off base64-over-GraphQL onto multipart REST

The bulk-upload (and large single-file) path was failing with Apollo's
"Payload allocation size overflow" before the network request fired.
Root cause: the entire file was base64-encoded into a single GraphQL
String variable, then JSON.stringify'd by Apollo into the request body —
V8 cannot allocate a contiguous string of that size for moderately
large zips (~33% inflation pushes past V8's string limit / heap
fragmentation ceiling).

Fix: introduce two multipart/form-data REST endpoints under
/api/uploads/ (single doc + bulk zip) and switch the frontend
useUploadMutations hook to fetch+FormData. The binary bytes never
become a JS string, so the request streams normally.

Both endpoints route through opencontractserver.document_uploads.services,
which the existing UploadDocument and UploadDocumentsZip GraphQL
mutations now also delegate to — REST and GraphQL transports validate
identically (visibility + EDIT permission with unified IDOR-safe error
message; usage-cap enforcement; folder-in-corpus check; allowed-MIME
enforcement; bulk-job owner cache binding). The GraphQL surface is
preserved for backwards compatibility with external automation; only
the frontend's transport changed.

Tests:
- opencontractserver/tests/test_document_uploads_rest.py — both views
  (auth, owned/inaccessible/read-only corpus IDOR uniformity, folder-
  in-corpus check, unsupported MIME, oversize 413, usage-cap, custom-
  meta JSON pass-through, owner-cache binding) plus direct service
  tests for the bytes/UploadedFile branches.
- frontend uploadHttp.test.ts (8 cases) verifies FormData (not JSON),
  correct URL, bearer header, blank-string omission, structured error
  parsing.
- frontend useUploadMutations.test.tsx (8 cases) covers sequential
  upload semantics, status callbacks, partial-failure resilience, and
  refetch+onComplete exactly-once.

Cleanup: toBase64 removed from frontend/src/utils/files.ts (dead after
the hook switched off the GraphQL mutations).

* Rename document upload REST app to document_imports

Both new endpoints terminate in import_content / process_documents_zip
(the latter literally lives in opencontractserver/tasks/import_tasks.py),
so "imports" is the more accurate verb for what they do; "upload" is
just the transport. Renames are cosmetic only — no behaviour change.

Changes:
- App: opencontractserver/document_uploads -> opencontractserver/document_imports
- URL prefix: /api/uploads/ -> /api/imports/
- Service funcs: upload_document_for_user -> import_document_for_user;
  upload_documents_zip_for_user -> import_documents_zip_for_user
- Result dataclasses: UploadResult -> ImportResult; ZipUploadResult -> ZipImportResult
- View classes: DocumentUploadView -> DocumentImportView;
  DocumentsZipUploadView -> DocumentsZipImportView
- Serializer classes: DocumentUploadSerializer -> DocumentImportSerializer;
  DocumentsZipUploadSerializer -> DocumentsZipImportSerializer
- Setting: MAX_DOCUMENT_UPLOAD_SIZE_BYTES -> MAX_DOCUMENT_IMPORT_SIZE_BYTES
  (env var name follows the same rename)
- Frontend helpers: uploadDocumentMultipart -> importDocumentMultipart;
  uploadZipMultipart -> importDocumentsZipMultipart
- Frontend module: hooks/uploadHttp.ts -> hooks/importHttp.ts
- Test files renamed correspondingly

* Address PR review and unblock CI for multipart document imports

- Move importHttp.ts to frontend/src/utils/ and default API root to ""
  so requests go same-origin (Vite proxy / same-origin prod).
- Validate ZIP magic bytes before staging so non-zip uploads fail loud
  instead of producing a confusing downstream celery error.
- Hoist `from celery import chain` to module level and collapse the
  eager/non-eager branches around a single task signature.
- Rename _check_usage_cap -> check_usage_cap and call it before
  ingestion-source resolution in UploadDocument.mutate so capped users
  see the cap error instead of "Ingestion source not found".
- Tighten _enforce_size_cap nullability (`is not None`) and drop the
  dead seek(0) finally block on the single-document REST path.
- Annotate _resolve_pk return as Optional and fix latent bug: graphql
  from_global_id() does not raise on non-relay input — it returns
  ('', '') — so raw PKs round-tripped to empty strings. Fall back to
  raw whenever the decoded type or pk is blank.
- Mypy/Prettier cleanups so the linter and lint jobs go green.

* Update any-baseline after dropping one any in frontend changes

* Update test mocks to track set_permissions move into shared service

The upload mutation was refactored to delegate to
opencontractserver.document_imports.services.import_document_for_user,
which now owns the call to set_permissions_for_obj_to_user. The four
previously-passing upload tests patched the symbol at its old location
(config.graphql.document_mutations) and so leaked unmocked permission
writes that violated the documents_documentuserobjectpermission FK
against the mock Document(id=1/999999) returned by the patched
import_content.

* Address review: clarify size cap, hoist imports, log resolver fallback

- _enforce_size_cap: switch to explicit `if limit > 0` and default the
  setting fallback to 0 so the disable-by-zero contract is no longer
  reliant on implicit truthiness (review item #1).
- document_mutations.py: hoist the deferred local imports of
  check_usage_cap / import_document_for_user / import_documents_zip_for_user
  to the module top — there is no circular import, the deferred form was
  just left over from the initial extraction (review item #3).
- Annotate the redundant check_usage_cap call in UploadDocument.mutate
  to explain that the early call is what gives capped users the cap
  error (rather than "Ingestion source not found") and that the
  service-level call covers transports without that resolution step
  (review item #2).
- _resolve_pk: log a debug line when from_global_id raises so a
  malformed client-supplied id surfaces in operator logs without
  weakening the IDOR-safe "Corpus not found" response (review item #4).

* Harden REST import endpoints: pin JWT auth, throttle, security tests

- Pin authentication_classes=[GraphQLJWTAuthentication] on both
  /api/imports/ views so they no longer inherit the global tuple
  (Session + Token fallback). Bearer JWT only — endpoints are
  CSRF-safe by construction and future changes to
  DEFAULT_AUTHENTICATION_CLASSES cannot silently widen the surface.
- Add DocumentImportThrottle (scope document_imports, 120/hour) on
  both views; default user rate (1000/hour) is too permissive when a
  single request can be hundreds of MB.
- Add three security-focused test classes:
  * DocumentImportRealJWTAuthTests — exercises the real bearer-JWT
    auth path via client.credentials() (force_authenticate bypasses
    auth classes); covers valid token, missing header, tampered
    signature, expired token.
  * DocumentsZipNonZipRejectionTests — PDF and random bytes both 400
    against /api/imports/documents-zip/ via _peek_zip_magic.
  * DocumentImportFolderIDORTests — cross-user folder ID with own
    corpus rejected as "Folder not found"; cross-user folder + cross-
    user corpus collapses to CORPUS_NOT_FOUND_MSG. Both assert no
    document is created.

* Fix mypy regression and address review feedback

- embeddings.py: annotate embedder_class type and cast get_component_by_name
  results to type[BaseEmbedder] (mypy regression from removed type: ignore)
- services.py: lift ContentFile import to module level; log warning when
  ZIP magic peek seek fails so truncation isn't silent
- CHANGELOG.md: correct importHttp.ts path (frontend/src/utils/, not
  modals/UploadModal/hooks/)

* Add coverage for new code paths surfaced by codecov/patch

Backend: services.py 90% -> 100%, views.py 99% -> 100%
- _resolve_pk(None), bad-input fallback, malformed b64 exception path
- detect_mime_type markdown extension promotion
- _peek_zip_magic seek-failure warning
- _normalise_optional blank-string -> None
- import_document_for_user disallowed mime, storage failure wrapping
- import_documents_zip_for_user staging-failure wrapping, eager dispatch

Frontend importHttp.ts 81% -> 100% lines
- DRF field-validation error parsing
- custom_meta JSON serialisation (single + zip paths)
- 2xx body with ok:false branch

Frontend useUploadMutations.ts 93% -> 100% lines
- thrown error inside the upload loop catch block
- non-Error thrown value fallback toast

embeddings.py: cover the explicit-embedder_path short-circuit branch
that was hit by my new cast() lines (TestGetEmbedderExplicitPath).

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

Follow-up to #1540 (merged) addressing issues raised in the Claude code review:

- Issue 3: Remove internal `cast(dict[str, Any], source)` from

subject: typing: graduate opencontractserver.mcp.{server,tools} from mypy baseline (#1537)
message:
typing: graduate opencontractserver.mcp.{server,tools} from mypy baseline (#1537)

* typing: graduate opencontractserver.mcp.{server,tools} from mypy baseline (#1486)

Sub-issue of #1447. Drains the next two MCP modules from the per-module
ignore_errors baseline established in #1331:

  opencontractserver.mcp.server  (6 errors)
  opencontractserver.mcp.tools   (1 error)

The 319-error opencontractserver.mcp.tests.test_mcp module is
intentionally left for a dedicated follow-up PR per the issue's
recommendation, so the runtime-code graduation lands first and clean.

What changed in the two graduated modules
-----------------------------------------

opencontractserver/mcp/server.py
  - resources annotated as list[Resource]
  - Resource(uri=...) wrapped with pydantic.AnyUrl(...) at the three
    construction sites (corpus://, document://, thread://) to match
    Resource.uri's Annotated[AnyUrl, UrlConstraints(host_required=False)]
    field; AnyUrl is the runtime no-op for these URI schemes
  - {MCP,ScopedMCP}LifespanManager._run_context typed as
    AbstractAsyncContextManager[None] | None instead of bare None,
    fixing the __aenter__ / assignment errors
  - new ASGIScope/ASGIReceive/ASGISend/ASGIApp aliases backed by
    MutableMapping[str, Any] so the ASGI app callable is contravariantly
    compatible with what StreamableHTTPSessionManager.handle_request
    and Starlette expect (dict[str, Any] would have been rejected as
    a Send target type)
  - handle_sse_connection now (request: Request) -> Response
  - __init__ / main / inner _check get explicit -> None / -> bool

opencontractserver/mcp/tools.py
  - .search_by_embedding(...) gets a single # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    mirroring the existing pattern in opencontractserver/discovery/views.py
    (django-stubs cannot model the custom DocumentQuerySet method through
    the from_queryset(...) manager + chained .filter())
  - _text_search_fallback signature filled in
    (corpus: Corpus, user: User | AnonymousUser)

Cross-module ripples (kept type-honest, no behavior change)
-----------------------------------------------------------

  config/ratelimit/keys.py            get_client_ip_from_scope
  config/ratelimit/decorators.py      check_mcp_rate_limit
  opencontractserver/mcp/telemetry.py get_user_agent_from_scope
    All three previously took scope: dict[str, Any]. Widened to
    MutableMapping[str, Any] so the ASGI app's typed scope can flow
    through them. dict literals in their tests remain valid callers.

  opencontractserver/corpuses/folder_service.py
    check_corpus_read_permission and get_corpus_documents widened from
    user: User to user: User | AnonymousUser. Both already handled the
    anonymous case at runtime (user.is_anonymous / user.is_superuser
    branches); the type widening just removes the need for casts at the
    public-corpus MCP entry points, which only ever pass AnonymousUser.

Baseline bookkeeping
--------------------

  - mypy.ini: removed [mypy-opencontractserver.mcp.server] and
    [mypy-opencontractserver.mcp.tools] blocks
  - docs/typing/mypy_baseline.txt: pruned the 7 corresponding entries

mcp.server's "public corpora only" contract is preserved — no permission
or visibility logic was touched.

* Address review: align MCP tools UserOrAnonymous with folder_service alias

Use the project's concrete User model and PEP 604 '|' syntax in
opencontractserver/mcp/tools.py (was AbstractBaseUser + Union[X, Y]).
Matches the alias style already in
opencontractserver/corpuses/folder_service.py and removes the unnecessary
type widening.

* Address review: consolidate UserOrAnonymous alias, add AnyUrl regression test

Two follow-ups from the Claude review on PR #1537:

- Centralise the UserOrAnonymous = User | AnonymousUser alias in
  opencontractserver/users/types.py (TYPE_CHECKING-guarded module so
  there's zero runtime cost). folder_service and mcp.tools both
  import from there now instead of re-declaring the alias locally.
  Resolves the DRY-rule observation per CLAUDE.md §2 — pre-empts the
  duplication that the upcoming test_mcp typing graduation would
  otherwise trip on.

- Add TestAnyUrlCustomSchemes to test_mcp_extended.py with regression
  assertions that pydantic.AnyUrl accepts the corpus://, document://,
  and thread:// schemes the MCP server now constructs. If pydantic
  ever tightens URI validation, this fails immediately rather than
  surfacing as a 500 during a live MCP list_resources call.

subject: Documents view: fix refetch storm and over-fetched query (#1553)
message:
Documents view: fix refetch storm and over-fetched query (#1553)

The /documents view was firing ~7 GET_DOCUMENTS requests on every visit
and asking for ~22 fields per row when the UI renders 7. Fix:

- New slim GET_DOCUMENTS_FOR_LIST query (id, slug, title, fileType,
  backendLock, pageCount, icon, created, creator { id, slug, email }).
  Drops per-row N+1 versionCount, per-row canViewHistory/canRetry
  permission checks, four file-URL signing fields, and the
  doc_label_annotations connection. Shared GET_DOCUMENTS preserved for
  its other consumers.
- Six redundant useEffect(refetchDocuments) hooks deleted; useQuery
  refetches on variables change automatically. nextFetchPolicy:
  "network-only" removed; default cache-first restored.
- Initial query passes explicit first: 20 (was implicitly capped at
  RELAY_CONNECTION_MAX_LIMIT = 100). document_items memoized on the
  stable Apollo edges ref.
- Latent avatar-initials bug fixed (UI read creator.email but query
  selected creator.slug only).
- useUploadMutations and cacheManager.invalidateRelatedQueries include
  GET_DOCUMENTS_FOR_LIST alongside GET_DOCUMENTS in their refetch
  lists so uploads/document-CRUD elsewhere still refresh the view.
- Deleted unused frontend/tests/DocumentsTestWrapper.tsx.

Regression coverage via Vitest source-level test pinning the four
structural fixes — counter-style CT tests can't catch the storm
because Apollo's query deduplication merges concurrent in-flight
requests into one before they reach MockLink.

subject: Documents view: backend-aggregate stats so tile counters match permission scope (#1556)
message:
Documents view: backend-aggregate stats so tile counters match permission scope (#1556)

* Documents view: backend-aggregate stats so tile counters match permission scope

The Documents view tile counters previously reduced over the paginated
client subset of `document_items` (initial 20 docs, +20 per fetchMore),
so totals reflected whatever happened to be loaded into Apollo's cache
rather than the user's full visible-to-user document set.

Adds a `documentStats` GraphQL field that mirrors `corpus_filter_counts`:
single `aggregate()` over `Document.objects.visible_to_user(user)`,
filters reused from `DocumentFilter` so list and stats can never drift,
`id__in` subquery on the aggregation base so a `has_label_with_id` join
into `doc_annotation` cannot inflate `Sum(page_count)` or `Count`.

Frontend swaps the `useMemo` reduce for `useQuery(GET_DOCUMENT_STATS)`
keyed off the same filter primitives. Status-filter tab badges and
hero tiles now show the full permission-scoped counts.

Test: opencontractserver/tests/test_document_stats.py covers anonymous,
authenticated owner, cross-user, text-search-narrowing, and a regression
guard for the doc_annotation join inflation.

* Extract documentStatsVariables builder for branch coverage

The three conditional spreads in documentStatsVariables (search, label,
corpus) were the patch's uncovered partials on codecov — only the falsy
branches were exercised by the existing CT tests. Pulling the builder into
its own module lets a focused unit test cover each combination of filter
inputs without spinning up the full Documents view.

Also has the side benefit of making the wire-payload contract for the stats
query a single named function rather than an inlined object literal, which
matches how the list query's variables flow through the same component.

* Address review: stats fetch policy, error logging, narrowing tests

- Switch GET_DOCUMENT_STATS to ``cache-and-network`` so the tile counters
  refresh on revisit (e.g. after a doc finishes processing in another
  session) instead of staying pinned to whatever was cached the first
  time the variables matched.

- Destructure and log ``stats_error`` from useQuery — previously a
  failing stats fetch silently rendered as zero counts, indistinguishable
  from the loading state. Console logging is the lightest signal that
  surfaces the failure to ops without breaking the rest of the view.

- ``test_text_search_narrows_counts`` now actually narrows: re-tag a
  single fixture with a unique substring and assert the search returns
  only that doc. The previous version reused the broad prefix and would
  have stayed green even if text search broke entirely.

- Add ``test_in_corpus_filter_narrows_counts`` covering the corpus path
  the frontend exercises (with ``includeCaml=True`` mirroring what the
  Documents view actually sends). Seeds DocumentPath rows directly since
  ``DocumentFolderService.add_document_to_corpus`` clones the document
  into a corpus-isolated copy, which would obscure the membership-only
  contract under test.

- Collapse the multi-paragraph docstrings on ``resolve_document_stats``
  and ``DocumentStatsType`` to one line per CLAUDE.md.

* Add CT coverage + docs screenshot for permission-scoped stat tiles

The new test mounts the Documents view with 2 loaded edges but a stats
mock returning {totalDocs: 47, totalPages: 1234, processedCount: 40,
processingCount: 7}. The pre-fix client-side reduce would have shown 2;
the new backend aggregate shows 47. The test asserts both the four hero
StatBlock values and the "All Documents" filter-tab badge align with
the stats query rather than ``document_items.length``.

Also captures the populated tile state via docScreenshot so the docs
site can show the contract this PR fixes.

message:
Graduate 11 opencontractserver.utils modules from mypy baseline (chunk 2, #1481) (#1531)

* Graduate 11 opencontractserver.utils modules from mypy baseline (chunk 2)

Removes per-module ignore_errors blocks for export_v2, files, import_v2,
importing, logging, mention_parser, multimodal_embeddings, packaging,
pdf_token_extraction, sharing, and storages. Pre-commit mypy now runs clean
on the full project surface for these files (44 baseline errors resolved,
54 entries pruned from docs/typing/mypy_baseline.txt).

Notable typing improvements:

- export_v2 builders emit narrowly typed TypedDict payloads
  (StructuralAnnotationSetExport, CorpusFolderExport,
  OpenContractsRelationshipPythonType, DescriptionRevisionExport) instead
  of dict[str, Any]; pawls_file_content and annotation_json are cast to
  their respective TypedDicts before assignment.
- packaging.unpack_corpus_from_export discriminates V1 vs V2 input via the
  OpenContractCorpusV2Type overlay so the V2-only fields no longer trip
  TypedDict-key errors.
- multimodal_embeddings propagates PawlsTokenPythonType through the
  image-token pipeline (get_annotation_image_tokens, embed_images_average,
  load_images_from_annotation_file).
- import_v2 and packaging move runtime ``User = get_user_model()`` out of
