subject: Fix Browse Annotations loading UX and image card error states (#1564)
message:
Fix Browse Annotations loading UX and image card error states (#1564)

* Browse Annotations: skeleton loader, graceful image-empty state, partial-stat labels (#1560)

Three defects on /annotations:

A. Inverted LoadingOverlay painted a tall, near-black band over a
   flex container with no positive min-height while items were empty.
   Replaced with shimmer-animated card-shaped skeletons that match the
   eventual ModernAnnotationCard layout and participate in normal flow,
   so the grid has predictable height while data loads. Removes the
   now-unused loadingMessage prop from AnnotationsPanelProps and its
   two call sites.

B. Image annotation cards rendered "Failed" whenever the REST endpoint
   returned anything other than 200 — including 401 when the JWT was
   not yet in the authToken reactive var on initial Browse Annotations
   load. useAnnotationImages now also tracks hasFetchedEmpty and treats
   401/403/404/429 the same as a successful empty payload (the IDOR-safe
   backend already returns {images: []} for missing/unauthorized).
   AnnotationImagePreview accepts the new flag and renders a neutral
   "No thumbnail" placeholder for the empty-success case while keeping
   the genuine error branch for 5xx/network/parse failures. Both
   consumers (ModernAnnotationCard, HighlightItem) wire the flag
   through.

C. Doc Labels / Text Labels / Human Annotated stat tiles were filtering
   only the first batch of rawItems (~20 of ~30k), making "0 Doc Labels"
   look authoritative. The stats memo now exposes loadedCount and
   isPartial; when partial, breakdown labels gain an "(in view)" suffix
   and tiles get a tooltip explaining the count is from N of M loaded
   so far. Total stat is unchanged — it was already accurate.

Tests: new useAnnotationImages.test.tsx pins the empty-vs-error matrix
(no fetch when not IMAGE, empty 200, 401, 404, 500, populated 200).
AnnotationsPanel Loading State test rewritten to assert skeleton render.
HighlightItem.scroll mock updated for new return shape.

Closes #1560

* Address review: don't poison image cache on 401/403/429; guard NoThumbnailState

Two follow-up fixes from the Claude review on PR #1564.

useAnnotationImages.tsx:
  Split the single TREATED_AS_EMPTY_STATUSES set into CACHE_AS_EMPTY_STATUSES
  ({404}) and TREAT_AS_EMPTY_NO_CACHE ({401, 403, 429}). The original code
  cached ALL non-200 statuses as a permanent empty array in the module-level
  imageCache, which silently broke the JWT-resolves-after-first-render flow:
  the [annotationId, hasImage, token] dependency array would re-fire the
  effect, but the cache check ran before any fetch and returned the poisoned
  empty entry. Users who landed on Browse Annotations before their JWT was
  ready never saw thumbnails until a hard refresh. The new policy caches only
  permanent absence (404) and successful empty (200 + []), and clears
  fetchedRef on 401/403/429 so a re-mount with a fresh token re-fetches.

AnnotationImagePreview.tsx:
  Short-circuit to null while images === null so the NoThumbnailState
  placeholder doesn't flash between mount and the first effect tick. The
  previous condition (hasFetchedEmpty || !images || images.length === 0)
  matched the pre-fetch state (loading=false, images=null, hasFetchedEmpty
  =false) and rendered "No thumbnail" before the loading spinner appeared.

Tests:
  Two new cases in useAnnotationImages.test.tsx pin the cache policy:
  - 401 followed by a 200 hits the network twice for the same id (the
    cache-poisoning regression guard).
  - 404 followed by a second mount calls fetch only once (cache hit).

Refs PR #1564 review.

subject: GraphQL: batch resolve_version_count and scope to visible_to_user (#1554) (#1562)
message:
GraphQL: batch resolve_version_count and scope to visible_to_user (#1554) (#1562)

DocumentType.versionCount was issuing one COUNT(*) per document row,
producing N+1 storms on any paginated documents connection that selected
the field (the shared GET_DOCUMENTS query and every consumer of it).

Fix mirrors the request-level cache pattern already established for
doc_relationship_count in the same file:

- New DocumentVersionQueryOptimizer.get_version_counts_by_tree computes
  {version_tree_id: count} for every visible tree in one aggregated SQL
  query and caches the result on info.context.
- Aggregation is scoped to Document.objects.visible_to_user(user) so the
  badge cannot leak the existence of versions hidden from the requester.
- Resolver returns 1 (not 0) on cache miss because the resolver is only
  reachable on a document the user can already see.

Closes #1554

subject: Fix infinite scroll regression and loading overlay UX (issue #1559) (#1565)
message:
Fix infinite scroll regression and loading overlay UX (issue #1559) (#1565)

* Documents view: fix infinite-scroll never firing and dim overlay covering grid

Two cooperating bugs were preventing the documents grid from paginating
and made the page look broken on first paint (issue #1559):

1. ``Documents.tsx`` rendered an ``inverted`` full-cover ``LoadingOverlay``
   over the grid for the entire ``documents_loading === true`` window —
   including refetches and ``fetchMore`` — painting a near-black band over
   already-rendered rows. The overlay is now scoped to the *initial* load
   only (no data yet) and a small footer-pinned spinner indicates additional
   pages are being fetched.

2. ``FetchMoreOnVisible.tsx`` left ``fetchNextPage`` / ``fetchPreviousPage``
   out of its observer effect's deps. Once Apollo's ``loading`` flag toggled
   true→false during the first ``fetchMore``, the parent's ``useCallback``
   handler was re-created and subsequent intersection events fired the stale
   closure, silently dropping every later fetch. The callbacks are now held
   in ``useRef`` slots refreshed every render and dereferenced inside the
   effect, so observer events always invoke the latest closure. Also adds a
   ``rootMargin`` prop defaulting to ``"200px 0px"`` so the sentinel triggers
   ~one viewport's worth before the absolute bottom — fixing the secondary
   complaint that the spinner was "positioned far below the visible viewport"
   and giving the next page time to load while the user is still scrolling.

Regression coverage: new Playwright CT in ``Documents.ct.tsx`` mounts the
view with a 20-doc first page (``hasNextPage: true``, distinct cursor) and a
single distinctively-named second-page mock keyed on the cursor, scrolls the
``.FetchMoreOnVisible`` sentinel into view, and asserts the second-page
document title appears. The test uses an inline ``InMemoryCache`` with the
same ``relayStylePagination`` keyArgs as ``graphql/cache.ts`` so ``fetchMore``
merges into the existing connection. On the pre-fix code the second mock is
never consumed and the assertion times out.

Closes #1559

* Address review: trim comments, fix CT cache serialization, settle timing

- Trim multi-paragraph comment blocks in FetchMoreOnVisible.tsx,
  Documents.tsx, and Documents.ct.tsx per CLAUDE.md (one-line max).
- Remove 'See issue #1559' inline comments from production code; they
  belong in the PR description.
- Move the infinite-scroll regression test off an inline InMemoryCache
  + MockedProvider into a new DocumentsTestWrapper. The cache instance
  has cyclic refs that Playwright CT can't serialize across the test
  boundary (RangeError: Maximum call stack), per CLAUDE.md pitfall #8.
- Add a 500 ms waitForTimeout between the sentinel scroll and the
  second-page assertion so the IntersectionObserver + Apollo merge
  can settle on slower CI runners.

* Add unit tests for FetchMoreOnVisible covering all branches

Adds Vitest unit tests with mocked useInView covering inView guard,
both scroll directions, fetchWithoutMotion fallbacks, stale-closure
guard via ref pattern, and rendering. Trims verbose comments and
tightens DocumentsTestWrapper mock typing to MockedResponse[].

- embeddings_task: cast ``_create_embedding_for_annotation`` to the
  ``HasEmbeddingMixin``-typed callable signature expected by
  ``_apply_dual_embedding_strategy``; explicit annotation
  ``result: dict[str, Any]`` so the mixed-shape result dict cooperates
  with subscripted update / append.
- export_tasks(_v2): handled None returns from
  ``package_corpus_for_export`` / ``package_label_set_for_export`` by
  raising RuntimeError before constructing the TypedDict; replaced
  ``output_bytes`` (BytesIO) with ContentFile when calling
  FieldFile.save; renamed the inner FUNSD page-data variable to keep its
  ``tuple[int, str, str]`` type distinct from the bytes payload; fixed
  the ``UserExport.error`` typo (the actual field is ``errors``).
- import_tasks(_v2): swapped ``AbstractBaseUser`` for the project's
  concrete ``User`` (same pattern as corpuses/folder_service); tightened
  the V2-only branch so ``data_json.get(...)`` returns the V2-typed
  values instead of the V1∩V2 ``object`` lower bound; widened
  aggregator dict to ``dict[str | int, int]`` to match
  ``import_doc_annotations``'s declared return type.
- fork_tasks: replaced implicit ``Optional[list[str]] = None`` parameter
  defaults; guarded FieldFile.name accesses; annotated the empty
  ``folder_map`` / ``structural_set_map`` accumulators.
- corpus_tasks: dropped a stale ``return summary`` from the
  ``-> None`` task; coerced the ``str | int`` celery args to ``int``
  once at function entry; renamed the inner ``execution`` loop variable
  to avoid shadowing the outer ``for doc_id, execution in
  execution_map.items()`` binding; scoped ``# type: ignore[attr-defined]``
  on Celery's dynamically-attached ``Signature.s`` / ``.si`` attributes.
- extract_orchestrator_tasks: early-return when ``extract_id`` is None;
  scoped ``# type: ignore[attr-defined]`` on ``task_func.si``.

Cross-cutting type tightening
- ``LabelLookupPythonType.{text_labels, doc_labels}`` narrowed from
  ``dict[str | int, AnnotationLabelPythonType]`` to ``dict[str, ...]``
  (the producer in ``utils.etl.build_label_lookups`` already keys by
  ``str(pk)``). Updated the ``corpus_id`` parameter on
  ``build_label_lookups`` from ``str`` to ``int`` to match every call
  site.
- ``utils.importing.load_or_create_labels`` and
  ``utils.importing.import_doc_annotations`` now accept ``Mapping``
  instead of ``dict``, so callers can pass ``OpenContractDocExport`` /
  ``AnnotationLabelPythonType`` TypedDicts directly without ``cast()``.
- ``import_tasks._validate_sidecar_schema`` and ``_apply_sidecar_annotations``
  accept ``str | None`` for the ``sidecar_path`` argument since the
  caller passes a fallback name that can be None.

Verification
- python -m mypy --config-file mypy.ini opencontractserver config
  -> "Success: no issues found in 1032 source files"
- All 16 graduated modules import cleanly under config.settings.mypy.

* Fix linting: pyupgrade, mypy type narrowing, FUNSD int key regression

Fixes:
- Apply pyupgrade rewrites to import_tasks_v2.py
- Fix FUNSD annotation_map key type regression: doc_tasks.py now uses int
  keys consistently, export_tasks.py looks up by int (not str(index)),
  and all return/parameter type annotations updated accordingly
- Narrow dict[str|int,...] to dict[str,...] in etl.build_label_lookups
  and build_document_export (keys are always str(pk))
- Cast get_component_by_name() results in embeddings.py, embeddings_task.py
  and doc_tasks.py to the specific subtype (BaseEmbedder / BaseParser /
  BaseThumbnailGenerator) to satisfy mypy
- Append FunsdAnnotationType directly rather than via dict() to preserve
  the TypedDict type

* Add tests for typing-graduation fixes in tasks.*

Tests added:
- test_convert_doc_to_funsd_annotation_map_uses_int_keys: regression guard
  that annotation_map keys are int, not str (FUNSD key-type fix)
- test_convert_doc_to_funsd_empty_doc_returns_empty_map: empty-annotation path
- test_export_tasks_typing_fixes.py (new file):
  - FinalizeExportTestCase: ContentFile save round-trip, seekable-buffer behaviour
  - OnDemandPostProcessorsTestCase: RuntimeError on missing export file,
    no-op when post_processors is empty
  - PackageFunsdExportsIntKeyTestCase: int-key annotation lookup (regression),
    empty-annotation pages, multi-page multi-annotation packaging
  - PackageCorpusExportV2ErrorsFieldTestCase: export.errors field populated
    on failure (was non-existent export.error before the fix)

* Address review: check None before cast in V2 export; format test fix

- export_tasks_v2.py: reorder so the None check on package_corpus_for_export
  happens before the cast, allowing mypy to actually narrow the type
  (review #1541 nit). Cast is then a runtime no-op for the narrowed value.
- test_export_tasks_typing_fixes.py: black reformat picked up by CI.

* Address review: drop redundant membership test, document temperature ignore, rename UserModel alias

- import_tasks_v2.py: walrus comprehension drops the redundant
  'str(old_id) in annot_id_map' guard. dict.get returns None for unknown
  keys, so the 'is not None' check on the walrus result is sufficient
  (one dict lookup per element instead of two).
- data_extract_tasks.py: explain why temperature=extract_temperature
  carries '# type: ignore[arg-type]'. The downstream stub declares
  temperature: float; we intentionally pass None for Claude models so
  the temperature=0 override engages. Tracked in #1381.
- import_tasks.py: rename TYPE_CHECKING 'User as AbstractBaseUser' to
  'User as UserModel' for consistency with import_tasks_v2.py. The alias
  is required because the runtime 'User = get_user_model()' would
  otherwise collide with the type-only import.

* Address review: drop assert, add #1482 refs to type:ignore, tidy CHANGELOG

Three follow-ups from the Claude review on PR #1541:

- Replace assert s3 is not None in export_tasks.py with a real
  RuntimeError guard. Asserts are stripped under python -O and
  Celery tasks may run with optimisations enabled in production, so
  the assert effectively no-ops in the AWS branch. The new guard
  fails loud with a descriptive message — defence-in-depth for a
  branch that should be unreachable but covers any future ordering
  changes to the s3 initialisation above.

- Add # TODO(#1482) references to the three # type: ignore
  suppressions in import_tasks_v2.py. The dict<->TypedDict bridging
  is not a permanent state — it goes away once
  unpack_label_set_from_export / unpack_corpus_from_export /
  prepare_import_labels widen their signatures to Mapping[str, Any]
  in the next typing-graduation chunk. The TODO refs ensure these
  ignores can't quietly outlive the issue they belong to.

- Drop the stray double blank line between the new tasks-graduation
  changelog entry and the Docker hardening entry. The project norm
  is one blank line between entries.

* Fix CI regressions and address review feedback

CI fixes:
- ``extract_thumbnail`` (``doc_tasks.py``): the typing graduation wrapped
  ``get_components_by_mimetype(file_type)`` in ``FileTypeEnum(file_type)``,
  which raised ``ValueError`` because ``FileTypeEnum`` members are short
  labels (``"pdf"``) and ``file_type`` carries the MIME string
  (``"application/pdf"``). The helper already handles MIME strings via
  ``FileTypeEnum.from_mimetype`` internally, so the wrapping is removed
  and the unused import along with it. Restores
  ``test_pdf_thumbnail_extraction`` (3 orientations) and
  ``test_txt_thumbnail_extraction``.

- ``test_package_annotated_docs.py``: setUp now creates a ``LabelSet`` and
  attaches it to the test corpus. The PR's ``RuntimeError`` guard in
  ``export_tasks.py`` (``Failed to package corpus or label set``) tightens
  the contract — passing ``None`` for ``label_set`` is no longer silently
  accepted into ``OpenContractsExportDataJsonPythonType``. Both
  ``test_skips_failed_placeholder_and_packages_successful_docs`` and
  ``test_all_failed_produces_empty_annotated_docs_without_crashing`` now
  set up a complete corpus + label_set fixture.

- ``test_export_tasks_typing_fixes::test_errors_field_populated_on_failure``:
  the test asserted ``package_corpus_export_v2`` swallows the failure,
  but the production code records the error on the export AND re-raises
  so Celery can mark FAILURE. Test now wraps the call in
  ``assertRaises(Corpus.DoesNotExist)`` and pins both the recording side
  effects (``backend_lock`` cleared, ``errors`` populated) and the
  propagation contract.

Review feedback:
- ``import_tasks_v2.py``: three ``# type: ignore[arg-type] # TODO(#1482)``
  markers retargeted to ``TODO(#1447)`` — the lifts they describe live in
  ``utils.importing``, which is not part of this PR's scope (#1482); the
  broader umbrella tracker (#1447) is the correct destination.

- ``memory_tasks.py``: expand the one-line ``[arg-type]`` ignore comment
  into a paragraph explaining *why* mypy needs the suppression
  (``values_list(..., named=True)`` returns a synthesised ``QuerySet[Row*]``
  that the django-stubs Manager descriptor does not propagate through a
  custom Manager).

- ``corpus_tasks.py``: condense the Celery-int-coercion comment to one
  line per the project's terse-comment style.

* Fix mypy attr-defined error on Mapping.copy()

After widening label_data_dict to Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Any]] in
load_or_create_labels, calling .copy() on the inner Mapping fails because
Mapping is read-only. Build a mutable dict via dict(label_data) instead
and rename the local to label_data_copy for clarity.

* Add coverage for typing-graduated tasks.* paths (#1482)

Targets the previously-uncovered patch lines so codecov ticks above 90%:
- ``pii_highlighter_claude``: new tests directly exercise the

- ``run_extract``: explicit guard test for ``extract_id is None``.

- ``convert_doc_to_funsd``: ValueError test when pawls/pdf files missing.
- ``package_funsd_exports``: AWS S3 + GCS storage-backend branches.
- ``package_corpus_export_v2``: RuntimeError when corpus packager

- ``package_annotated_docs``: RuntimeError tests for None packager

subject: Type-check opencontractserver.llms modules (issue #1484) (#1543)
message:
Type-check opencontractserver.llms modules (issue #1484) (#1543)

* typing: graduate opencontractserver.llms.* (non-tools) from mypy baseline

Closes #1484. Removes the per-module ignore_errors blocks for the nine
remaining llms.* modules (agents, api/client, vector_stores) and fixes
the underlying ~125 type errors so mypy runs clean on this surface.

Notable fixes:
- Replaced `callable`/`any` placeholders with `typing.Callable[..., Any]`
  and `typing.Any` across api/client/vector_stores.
- Made implicit Optionals explicit (`no_implicit_optional` defaults).
- Tightened `_resolve_framework`/`_resolve_tools` helpers in llms.api so
  framework normalisation produces a concrete `AgentFramework`.
- Typed Annotation/ChatMessage querysets as their custom subclasses so
  the `search_by_embedding` extension method resolves.
- Switched `CorpusAgentContext.documents` to a non-Optional list with
  `default_factory=list`; aligned `CoreAgent.stream` /
  `CoreAgent.resume_with_approval` Protocol signatures with their
  PydanticAI implementations.
- Pruned now-unused `# type: ignore` comments and the unused
  `CoreAnnotationVectorStore` annotation from `pydantic_ai_tools`.
- Pruned the corresponding 189 advisory entries from
  `docs/typing/mypy_baseline.txt`.

* Fix mypy after main merge; address review feedback for #1543

- embeddings.py: cast get_component_by_name to type[BaseEmbedder] and
  annotate embedder_class so the Optional return type is satisfied.
- core_vector_stores.py / core_conversation_vector_stores.py: raise
  ValueError when get_embedder() yields no path (search_by_embedding
  requires str, not Optional[str]). Failing fast at construction time
  is preferable to a downstream type error.
- core_agents.py: lift cast import to module-level and replace the
  unreachable-by-NotImplementedError yield with the conventional
  if False: idiom (review nit).
- pydantic_ai_agents.py: log a warning when a paused message's
  pending_tool_call is missing 'name' so malformed persistence state
  doesn't silently drive downstream lookups with an empty tool name.

* Address review: document type:ignore + add behavior guards regression tests

Two follow-ups from the Claude review on PR #1543:

- The async for event in tool_stream:  # type: ignore[assignment]
  in pydantic_ai_agents.py was the only new ignore introduced by the
  typing graduation. Removing it would either require renaming the
  loop variable across ~30 reference sites in the same branch (every
  event.part.* / event.result.* access) or a cast(Any, ...)
  that surfaces unrelated mypy errors downstream (the casted event
  flows into serializable_args whose four assignment branches give
  it different types). Add a multi-line comment explaining why the
  narrow [assignment]-only suppression is the right tradeoff and
  what the runtime contract is, so a future reader can either accept
  the ignore or rename with full context.

- Add test_llms_typing_behavior_guards.py covering the runtime guards
  the PR introduced that the review flagged as untested:
  - _resolve_framework: TypeError on unrecognised non-string objects,
    ValueError on unknown strings, pass-through for str / enum / None
    inputs.
  - PermissionError contract on add_document_note_tool /
    duplicate_annotations_tool / add_exact_string_annotations_tool —
    pinned via the message-string contract (3+ guards in source) so a
    refactor that drops one surfaces here.
  - Anti-regression guards for the sync_to_async(list)(queryset) bug,
    the dataclasses.is_dataclass + isinstance(type) guard, the
    isinstance(ev, ThoughtEvent) dispatch (vs. string-compare), and
    the llm_msg_id is not None persistence guard in _stream_core.
  - CorpusAgentContext.documents default_factory=list (vs. Optional)
    contract, including a runtime check that documents == [] when the
    caller doesn't pre-populate.

These also restore the PR's codecov backend coverage by exercising
the new branches in api.py and pydantic_ai_agents.py.

* Address review: replace asserts, document semantic changes, harden tests

- Convert 8 ``assert ... # nosec B101`` security/invariant guards to
  explicit ``if/raise RuntimeError`` so the checks survive ``python -O``
  optimisation (asserts are stripped under ``-O``). Sites:
    * ``CoreConversationManager.create_for_document`` / ``create_for_corpus``
      (cid resolution)
    * ``CoreConversationManager`` ``store_*_message`` x3 (factory user_id
      invariant)
    * ``ConversationVectorStore`` / ``CoreAnnotationVectorStore`` corpus_id
      auto-detect branches.

- Replace ``vector_store: Optional[Any]`` on ``PydanticAIDependencies``
  with a typed ``Optional[_AgentVectorStoreProto]``. The new Protocol
  declares the only attribute callers actually reach for
  (``similarity_search``) and avoids the circular import that would
  otherwise force ``Union[CoreAnnotationVectorStore,
  PydanticAIAnnotationVectorStore]``.

- Document ``CorpusAgentContext.initialize`` reload semantics: the
  switch from ``is None`` to ``not self.documents`` was deliberate to
  match the post-typing default (``[]`` instead of ``None``); the
  docstring now spells out that callers wanting "no docs — skip load"
  should not invoke ``initialize()`` at all.

- ``VectorStoreAPI.create`` no longer reads
  ``LLMS_DOCUMENT_AGENT_FRAMEWORK`` — the leak from the document-agent
  path was unintentional. New dedicated setting
  ``LLMS_VECTOR_STORE_FRAMEWORK`` with the same fallthrough default
  (``AgentFramework.PYDANTIC_AI``), so existing deployments keep
  working without a settings change.

- ``TimelineBuilder._timeline`` accumulation comment now explains why
  the storage stays as ``list[dict[str, Any]]`` (mutating ``entry``
  dicts post-construction would be rejected by mypy if typed as the
  closed ``TimelineEntry`` TypedDict) and where the schema contract is
  pinned (the property-level ``cast``).

- ``test_llms_typing_behavior_guards``:
    * Rename three importability-only tests
      (``test_aadd_*_is_not_called_when_user_id_is_none``) to
      ``..._is_importable`` so the scope matches what they actually
      assert; behaviour pin remains in
      ``test_permission_error_message_format``.
    * All ``Path("opencontractserver/...")`` source-grep call sites
      now resolve via ``Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]`` so the
      tests work regardless of the runner's CWD.

* Add coverage for typing-graduated llms.* paths

Targets the lines added by the llms.* mypy graduation in PR #1543 that
codecov flagged as uncovered (75.62% patch coverage). New unit tests
cover:

- core_agents: CorpusAgentContext.initialize() both branches (load /
  skip), CoreAgentBase._normalise_source content fallback chain,
  get_default_config defaults dict + None-override filter.
- pydantic_ai_agents: _extract_tool_result_summary (dict/string/None/
  truncation/error), _event_to_text_and_meta (all isinstance branches:
  TextPart, ToolCallPart, TextPartDelta, ToolCallPartDelta, unsupported),
  _usage_to_dict (None / model_dump / dataclass instance / dataclass
  *class*-object guard / unknown).
- client.SimpleLLMClient._chat_openai with and without max_tokens.
- core_vector_stores.CoreAnnotationVectorStore ctor: explicit-path,
  corpus-only, ValueError on unresolved embedder, validation error.
- core_conversation_vector_stores.{CoreConversationVectorStore,
  CoreChatMessageVectorStore} ctors: explicit-path with/without corpus,
  resolution-failure swallowed, auto-detect ValueError, auto-detect
  success.
- timeline_stream_mixin.TimelineStreamMixin.stream: timeline injection,
  _finalise_llm_message hook invocation, default _stream_core
  NotImplementedError.

Tests are mock-heavy and narrow — coverage tests, not behavioural
contracts (those live in test_llms_typing_behavior_guards.py).

* Fix mypy: drop spurious await on async-generator stream()

agent.stream() is an async def with yield — it returns an
AsyncGenerator directly, not an awaitable. async for event in await
agent.stream(...) was a left-over from a pre-typing iteration; mypy
flags it now that the surrounding tasks module type-checks.

* Address review: fix add_document_note bug, harden kwargs, cast corpus_id

- Drop the corpus-required guard on add_document_note_tool: the
  underlying aadd_document_note accepts corpus_id=None, so standalone-
  document agents must keep working. Forward context.corpus.id when
  present and None otherwise.
- _stream_core now raises TypeError on unknown kwargs instead of
  silently swallowing typos.
- Mirror the int(self.corpus_id) cast on the sync Conversation vector
  store search paths so the ORM honours string-typed corpus IDs as
  CoreChatMessageVectorStore.search already does.
- Drop redundant list() wrap in api.py around _resolve_tools, cast
  through the wider factory parameter type instead.
- Document LLMS_VECTOR_STORE_FRAMEWORK in the LLM architecture README so
  operators understand the new setting is intentionally independent of
  LLMS_DOCUMENT_AGENT_FRAMEWORK.
- Add behaviour-guard tests pinning all three contracts.

* Add coverage for _is_public/_assert_access helpers + _resolve_tools branches

* Cover VectorStoreAPI.create framework setting + kwarg passthrough

subject: Fix N+1 queries in Document permission checks via user-scoped prefetches (#1566)
message:
Fix N+1 queries in Document permission checks via user-scoped prefetches (#1566)

* Teach user_has_permission_for_obj to consume prefetched permissions

Closes #1555.

DocumentType.canViewHistory and DocumentType.canRetry are selected by the
shared GET_DOCUMENTS query, so paginated documents pages were paying an
N+1 cost: each call to user_has_permission_for_obj invoked
get_users_permissions_for_obj which did `.filter(user_id=...)` and
`.filter(group_id__in=...)` on the related guardian managers. Calling
.filter() on a related manager bypasses any default prefetch_related
cache, so the prefetches set up by _apply_document_prefetches were
silently ignored — every list-page row issued 2-3 extra round trips.
The same bypass affected resolve_my_permissions for group permissions.

Fix:

- _apply_document_prefetches now writes user-id-suffixed attributes
  (_prefetched_user_perms_uid_<id> and _prefetched_user_group_perms_uid_<id>),
  both pre-joined to permission via select_related. The group-perm
  prefetch is now filtered to the user's own group ids at the SQL
  layer, replacing the unfiltered documentgroupobjectpermission_set__permission/__group
  prefetches that prior consumers were bypassing anyway.

- get_users_permissions_for_obj gains a fast path that consumes those
  prefetched lists when the user-id-suffixed attribute is present. The
  user-id suffix makes the cache safe to consume: a lookup for a
  different user finds no attribute and falls through cleanly to the
  legacy guardian path. An empty list correctly means "user has no
  rows for this object".

- resolve_my_permissions reads from the same attributes, eliminating
  its own group-perm N+1.

Regression coverage in test_permissioned_querysets.py:
UserHasPermissionForObjPrefetchFastPathTest pins zero queries across 5
documents for both direct and group-permission lookups, verifies the
fallback path still works for instances loaded without the prefetch,
and verifies a different-user lookup correctly falls through (the
suffix makes the cache safe under multi-user lookups).

* Address review: centralize prefetch attr names + extend test coverage

- Extract user_perm_attr/user_group_perm_attr helpers into
  opencontractserver/shared/prefetch_attrs.py and use them across the
  producer (Managers._apply_document_prefetches) and both consumers
  (utils/permissioning.get_users_permissions_for_obj,
  mixins.resolve_my_permissions). Keeps the user-id-suffix convention
  in one place.
- Cover the partial-prefetch branch in get_users_permissions_for_obj
  (user perms prefetched but group perms not) with a new test that
  strips the group attribute before invocation.
- Cover the is_public branch on the prefetched fast path.
- Tighten test_different_user_lookup_falls_through_to_guardian to
  assert the per-row guardian queries actually fire (proves the
  fallback ran instead of silently reusing the viewer's prefetched
  list).
- Add the missing self.assertTrue around the include_group_permissions
  call inside the assertNumQueries(0) block.

* Fix SynchronousOnlyOperation in _apply_document_prefetches

list(user.groups.values_list("id", flat=True)) evaluates the group-id
queryset eagerly, which raises SynchronousOnlyOperation when called
from an async ORM path (e.g. async vector store search). Drop the
list() wrap and let the queryset stay lazy; Django then emits an SQL
subquery for the IN clause inside the outer prefetch, which is
evaluated synchronously by the prefetch machinery alongside the rest
of the prefetched query.

Caught by ~30 failing tests under test_pydantic_ai_agents.py,
test_django_annotation_vector_store.py, test_version_aware_vector_store.py,
test_corpus_isolation_vector_store.py, and test_hybrid_search.py.

* Address review and unflake JWT signature test

Trim multi-paragraph comment blocks in prefetch_attrs.py, Managers.py,
permissioning.py, and mixins.py per CLAUDE.md (one short line max).

Tests:
- Add GraphQL-layer test for resolve_my_permissions fast path so
  the prefetched documentuserobjectpermission_set / group_set lists
  are exercised end-to-end through myPermissions.
- Tighten test_different_user_lookup_falls_through_to_guardian to
  assert >= 2 * len(docs) queries (legacy path issues both a user-perm
  filter and a permission-id-to-name map per row).
- Document the intentional coupling in
  test_partial_prefetch_falls_back_for_group_perms_only — the
  delattr() reaches into the suffixed attr name to pin the partial-
  prefetch contract; central name-generation in prefetch_attrs.py
  keeps the convention single-source.

Unrelated CI flake fix:
- test_tampered_jwt_is_rejected flipped the trailing base64url char
  (A→B), but those chars share data bits and only differ in padding,
  so ~6% of HS256 signatures decoded back to the same bytes and the
  tampered token still authenticated. Flip a char at the midpoint of
  the signature segment instead — guarantees a data-bit change.

subject: Reclaim orphan Document file blobs at delete-time (#1492) (#1529)
message:
Reclaim orphan Document file blobs at delete-time (#1492) (#1529)

* Reclaim orphan Document file blobs at delete-time (#1492)

When a Document row is deleted, the FileField blobs (pdf_file,
txt_extract_file, pawls_parse_file, icon, md_summary_file) were
leaked in storage forever. Storage cost grew unbounded.

This change wires the offensive half of the blob-retention contract
that PR #1487 set up:

* `pre_delete` on Document captures every populated FileField path
  on the to-be-deleted instance.
* `post_delete` accumulates paths into a per-DB-connection set and
  registers a single `transaction.on_commit` callback that fires one
  Celery task per transaction with the deduplicated path list.
* `cleanup_orphaned_document_blobs_task` re-checks orphan status at
  execution time across every FileField and only deletes paths with
  zero live references.

The signal-based approach covers both `Model.delete()` and bulk
`QuerySet.delete()` because Django disables its fast-delete path once
listeners are connected. Transaction safety is provided by
`transaction.on_commit`, which never fires on rollback.

A new manager method `Document.objects.unique_blob_paths_for_many()`
gives callers a 2-queries-per-FileField primitive for queryset-scale
orphan checks (vs N+1 per row in `unique_blob_paths`).

Tests cover:

* per-row delete (solitary doc reclaims, sibling-shared retains)
* queryset bulk delete (solitary set reclaims, partial sharing
  retains, full sharing reclaims)
* `permanently_delete_document` cascade — corpus copy delete with
  source alive retains, full sequence reclaims
* sibling-corpus-copy retention
* transaction rollback preserves blobs and Document row
* DocumentPath PROTECT semantics
* corpus.delete() cascade preserves Documents and blobs
* `unique_blob_paths_for_many` empty/single/sharing/queryset/empty-
  field cases
* direct `cleanup_orphaned_document_blobs_task` contract (empty,
  still-referenced, orphan, dedup, missing path)

Coverage is parameterized across every FileField on Document so a
new file field is automatically protected.

Closes #1492

* Address review: drop blob-cleanup scheduled flag, fix linter

The connection-level _BLOB_CLEANUP_SCHEDULED_KEY flag would leak across
transaction rollbacks because Django discards the rolled-back on_commit
callback but cannot reset Python attributes we set on the connection
wrapper. A subsequent delete on the same connection would see the stale
True flag and skip scheduling cleanup, silently dropping blob reclaim.

Fix: drop the flag entirely. Always register on_commit on every
post_delete; the first callback in a commit drains the shared set and
runs the task, subsequent callbacks see an empty set and short-circuit.

Also:
- cleanup_orphaned_document_blobs_task now does set-difference via
  ``2 * len(blob_fields)`` __in queries instead of one filter().exists()
  per path. Same correctness, scales for large delete batches.
- Log path list at INFO before dispatch so ops can recover from broker
  outages.
- Drop the unnecessary refresh_from_db() in _make_doc_with_blobs (the
  FieldFile.name is set in-memory by save(save=True)).
- Rewrite test_transaction_rollback_preserves_blobs to verify the
  meaningful property (blobs still in storage after rollback) instead
  of asserting an unrelated Django guarantee about the doc row.

Linter fixes from CI: pyupgrade, black, isort, mypy on signals.py and
test_blob_retention.py.

* Address PR review: extract Document.blob_field_names, document rollback bleed semantics

- Single source of truth for blob FileField names: new Document.blob_field_names()
  classmethod, cached per process. Replaces three duplicated
  _meta.get_fields() introspections in signals.py, Managers.py, and
  cleanup_tasks.py (per project DRY rule).
- Tighten _schedule_blob_cleanup_post_delete docstring: paths captured by a
  rolled-back delete bleed into the next transaction's accumulator (Python
  attribute on the connection wrapper survives rollback). The orphan
  re-check inside cleanup_orphaned_document_blobs_task is what keeps the
  rolled-back row's blobs alive, not transaction.on_commit suppression.
- New regression test test_rollback_then_successful_delete_does_not_corrupt_cleanup
  pins the cross-transaction bleed contract: rolled-back blobs survive,
  next-transaction blobs are still reclaimed.

* Address review: log broker dispatch failures at ERROR with paths

The Claude review on PR #1529 flagged that
cleanup_orphaned_document_blobs_task.delay() in the on_commit
callback would propagate a broker exception silently — the prior
logger.info before dispatch helped but the failure itself was not
logged at a high enough level for ops to act on.

Wrap .delay() in a try/except that re-logs at ERROR with the full
path list when dispatch fails, so the affected blobs can be
reconciled (eventually via a future management command — issue
#1492). Add a regression test using assertLogs + a mocked .delay()
to pin the contract: dispatch failure does not raise out of the
delete, the ERROR log contains every orphaned path, and the blobs
remain in storage.

subject: Back grounding get_or_create with DB-level uniqueness (#1418)
message:
Back grounding get_or_create with DB-level uniqueness (#1418)

* Back grounding get_or_create with DB-level uniqueness (#1407)

Closes #1407. Follow-up to #1397.

* Adds two partial UniqueConstraints on Annotation that exactly match
  the application-level get_or_create lookup keys in the extraction
  grounding pipeline so concurrent Celery retries can't bypass
  idempotency. Migration 0069 deduplicates any existing rows before
  adding the constraints.
* Moves creator_id into the get_or_create lookup so the new constraints
  back the lookup; without that the race-loser's IntegrityError
  wouldn't fire.
* Documents the PostgreSQL-specific json equality semantics on the
  span path and the rationale for the end-of-function dedup loop.
* Replaces the redundant assertIsNotNone + assert pair with a single
  assert in test_extraction_grounding.py (only the latter narrows for
  mypy / pyright).

* Scope grounding unique constraints to is_grounding_source flag

The original constraint condition (structural=False, annotation_type=...)
applied to ALL non-structural annotations, blocking legitimate flows
that produce duplicates under the key tuple — e.g.
add_annotations_from_exact_strings finding multiple occurrences of the
same word on a page, or hierarchical annotation trees with duplicate
raw_text at different parents (4 backend tests failing in CI:
test_annotation_tree::{test_mid_node_subtree_and_descendants,
test_stress_test} and test_llm_annotation_tools::
{test_add_annotations_pdf, test_async_pdf_and_text}).

Add a boolean Annotation.is_grounding_source (default False), set True
only inside _create_pdf_annotation / _create_span_annotation, and scope
both partial UniqueConstraints to is_grounding_source=True. The
migration backfills True for any pre-existing OC_EXTRACT_SOURCE rows so
historical grounding annotations are also covered, then dedupes and
adds the constraints.

* Address PR #1418 review: constraint-path test, dedup repointing, comment trim

- Add test_db_constraint_blocks_concurrent_token_label_grounding_duplicates
  in TestGroundingPipelinePDFIntegration: directly exercises the
  IntegrityError + get_or_create fallback round-trip the constraint
  enables. Closes the test-coverage gap flagged in review.
- Extend the migration's dedup loop to repoint every realistic
  cross-reference (UserFeedback FK; ChatMessage / AssignmentTask /
  Relationship M2Ms) to the keeper before deleting redundant rows, so
  no cross-domain references are silently dropped. Document why
  Embedding (CASCADE) and Annotation.parent (CASCADE on leaf rows) are
  intentionally not repointed.
- Trim the assertIsNotNone-vs-assert explanation to a single trailing
  comment to match project convention.
- Pin migration dependencies to the latest migration of every app
  whose models the dedup helper touches (conversations, feedback,
  users) in addition to the existing extracts pin.

* Narrow seed.annotation_label for mypy in new constraint-path test

* Address PR #1418 review: M2M dedup collision + minor follow-ups

- Migration 0069: rewrite _repoint_cross_references to delete colliding
  through-table rows before updating annotation_id. The realistic race
  the migration is built to clean up — both keeper and redundant in the
  same datacell.sources — would have hit Django M2M's
  UNIQUE(owner_id, annotation_id) and aborted the dedup transaction.
  Also fix a latent typo (apps.get_model("users", "AssignmentTask"))
  that would have raised LookupError; the model is users.Assignment.
- Migration 0069: inline OC_EXTRACT_SOURCE_LABEL string instead of
  importing the live constant, so replay survives future renames.
- extraction_grounding.py: move structural=False from defaults into
  get_or_create lookup so the constraint condition and lookup match
  exactly.
- tests: add SPAN_LABEL constraint-path test (parallel to the
  TOKEN_LABEL one), assert is_grounding_source=True on the existing
  ground_text/ground_pdf tests, and add a direct test for migration
  0069's M2M dedup helper covering the keeper+redundant collision case.
- CHANGELOG: trim the verbose grounding follow-up entry.

subject: Fix SPA layout: drop redundant 100vh wrappers exposing gradient strip (#1558) (#1561)
message:
Fix SPA layout: drop redundant 100vh wrappers exposing gradient strip (#1558) (#1561)

* Fix SPA layout: drop redundant 100vh wrappers exposing gradient strip (#1558)

App.tsx stacked three full-viewport-height constraints on its layout shell —
minHeight: 100vh on the outer wrapper, a second wrapper with minHeight: 100vh
plus overflow: hidden, and a third with minHeight/maxHeight/height: 100vh
plus overflow: hidden — clamping the routed content area to exactly the
viewport. On short pages (e.g. discovery landing with the empty-state
CompactLeaderboard) the natural-flow CallToAction panel that follows the
content was clipped to a thin band rather than rendered in full, producing
a "blue-to-purple gradient strip" between a flat gray gap and the dark
footer. The footer wrapper carried a marginTop: -1.5rem hack to hide the
resulting visual seam.

Collapse to a single minHeight: 100vh on the outer wrapper, one inner flex
shell with flex: 1 + minHeight: 0, and flex: 1 on the AppContainer main
slot so it grows to push the footer down naturally. Drop overflow: hidden
from the inner wrappers and the -1.5rem margin compensation. Also drop
justifyContent: center on the outer wrapper, which would have negatively
offset overflow content under the new flex flow.

Pages that scroll internally (DiscoveryLanding, Leaderboard, Documents,
Corpuses, etc.) keep working because they own their own
height: 100% + overflow-y: auto containers; pages without internal scroll
containers (PrivacyPolicy, TermsOfService) now scroll the body instead of
being silently clipped.

Closes #1558

* Extract App shell layout styles + add unit tests (issue #1558)

Move the inline JSX style objects on App's outer wrapper, flex shell,
AppContainer, and footer wrapper into named constants in
frontend/src/styles/appShellLayout.ts. Adds a vitest unit-test file
that pins the layout invariants the PR introduced — minHeight: 100vh
as a floor (not a ceiling), no overflow: hidden clamps, no negative
margin compensation on the footer, flex: 1 / minHeight: 0 on inner
wrappers — so a future regression to the prior buggy shape would
fail loudly.

* Extract AppShell component to fully cover layout patch

Move the four nested shell wrapper divs out of App.tsx into a small
AppShell component so the appShellLayout style constants are exercised
by a focused unit-tested component instead of inline JSX in a 600-line
file. AppShell.test.tsx pins each layer's layout constraints — the same
contract that appShellLayout.test.ts encodes at the constants level —
so the patch coverage now reflects actual render behaviour.

* Extract AppDocumentModals to cover #1558 patch branches

The patch coverage on PR #1561 hit 63.6% because four branches in
App.tsx — `{opened_corpus && ...}`, the `opened_document` /
`document_to_edit` / `document_to_view` ternaries, and the inline
`refetch`/`onClose` lambdas on `DocumentUploadModal` — were never
exercised by the existing test suite; the routing-tree mounting cost
made them impractical to test in place.

Move the modal stack hanging off the shell — `SelectAnalyzerOrFieldsetModal`
(corpus-gated), `DocumentUploadModal`, and the EDIT/VIEW `CRUDModal`
pair — into `frontend/src/components/layout/AppDocumentModals.tsx`,
which reads its own reactive vars and only takes `handleUpdateDocument`
as a prop. The shared close lambda for the upload modal is hoisted into
a `useCallback` so `refetch` and `onClose` reference one function
identity instead of two inline arrows.

Companion tests in `frontend/src/components/layout/__tests__/AppDocumentModals.test.tsx`
stub the heavy modal children with prop-capturing spies and pin every
branch: corpus-absent guard, opened_document threading, both
edit/view CRUD modal states, the upload close-callback contract, the
selected_folder_id prop, and the inline `renderForm` arrows.
Coverage on the new file is 100/100/100/100; the surviving App.tsx
diff lines are now just the import + the `<AppDocumentModals />`
invocation.

* Address PR #1561 review: drop minWidth: 100vw, trim doc blocks

- Drop carried-over `minWidth: "100vw"` from `APP_CONTAINER_STYLE`. Without
  the `overflow: hidden` walls this PR removes, the value would force a
  horizontal scrollbar whenever vertical scroll is active on systems with
  non-overlay scrollbars (100vw includes scrollbar width but the parent
  flex container does not). `width: "100%"` already fills the parent.
  New regression assert in `appShellLayout.test.ts` pins minWidth absent.

- Trim multi-paragraph JSDoc blocks on `AppShell`, `AppDocumentModals`, and
  `appShellLayout.ts` to a single sentence each per CLAUDE.md ("never write
  multi-paragraph docstrings"). The reasoning that lived in the doc blocks
  is already encoded in the unit tests and the CHANGELOG entry. Promote the
  AppShell `overlays` placement note from a JSDoc paragraph to a single
  inline comment at the call site.

- CHANGELOG: extend the existing #1558 entry with a sentence covering the
  minWidth drop and the latent horizontal-scroll regression it would have
  exposed.

subject: Fix leaderboard OAuth ID leak and aggressive polling (issue #1557) (#1567)
message:
Fix leaderboard OAuth ID leak and aggressive polling (issue #1557) (#1567)

* Leaderboard: redact OAuth provider IDs + drop aggressive polling

Closes #1557.

A. The USER column was rendering raw Auth0 ``sub`` values like
   ``google-oauth2|114688257717759010643`` because the leaderboard
   resolvers selected ``user.username`` directly, and Django's
   ``User.username`` is set to the OAuth ``sub`` claim for social-login
   users (see ``jwt_get_username_from_payload_handler``). Added a
   ``displayName`` resolver to ``UserType`` with the priority
   ``name`` → ``given_name`` + ``family_name`` → ``first_name`` +
   ``last_name`` → ``username`` (when not a ``provider|sub``) →
   redacted ``user_<last 6>`` fallback. ``GET_LEADERBOARD`` and
   ``GET_DISCOVERY_DATA`` (plus the matching TS types and components)
   now select / render ``displayName``. Backend regression coverage
   in ``test_user_display_name.py`` pins the priority chain and the
   no-leak guarantee.

B. The Community Leaderboard previously polled every 60s
   (``GET_LEADERBOARD``) and 120s (``GET_COMMUNITY_STATS``)
   regardless of tab visibility, which re-rendered rows and reset
   in-flight UI state. Dropped both ``pollInterval``s; queries now
   use ``cache-and-network`` + ``cache-first`` next-fetch + silent
   network-status updates so the user sees instant cached data while
   a single background refresh runs on mount or filter change. A
   ``visibilitychange`` listener performs one refetch when the tab
   returns to the foreground; hidden tabs no longer hit the network.

* Address review: fix short-sub pipe leak in display name redaction

The redacted fallback in UserType.resolve_display_name took the last 6
characters of the raw username, which for sub strings shorter than 7
characters (e.g. auth0|abcde, length 11) included the | separator —
returning user_|abcde. test_redacts_short_oauth_sub asserts the result
must not contain |, so the test failed against the original code.

Fix: split on the last | and slice the suffix from the sub part only,
so the redaction never carries the provider prefix or the separator.
auth0|abcde → user_abcde, google-oauth2|114688257717759010643 →
user_010643 (unchanged), a|b → user_b.

Also extracted the magic 6 into OAUTH_SUB_DISPLAY_SUFFIX_LENGTH in
opencontractserver/constants/auth.py per CLAUDE.md ("No magic numbers"),
and added a comment on the bare "user" fallback documenting that it is
intentionally non-unique because Django enforces non-empty username so
the branch is effectively unreachable.

Verified: docker compose -f test.yml -p opencontracts run --rm django
pytest opencontractserver/tests/test_user_display_name.py — 9 passed.

Refs PR #1567 review.

* Extract leaderboard utilities to shared modules + add unit tests

Extracts the local getInitials and getAvatarColor helpers from
CompactLeaderboard.tsx into frontend/src/utils/leaderboardAvatar.ts
so they can be unit-tested independently of the rendering layer.
Extracts the visibility-driven refresh logic from Leaderboard.tsx
into a small useTabVisibilityRefresh hook (frontend/src/hooks/)
with its own unit tests, replacing the inline useEffect.

Net: same runtime behaviour, but the OAuth/multi-token initial
branches and the visibility-change refetch path are now covered
by direct unit tests instead of indirect rendering coverage.

* Address review: remove issue refs, harden hook, tighten tests

- Drop Issue #1557 inline references from source files per CLAUDE.md
- Make useTabVisibilityRefresh stable across renders via useRef so
  consumers no longer need useMemo on the refresh fn array
- Pin the redacted suffix value in test_redacts_short_oauth_sub
- Add coverage for whitespace-only given_name/family_name
- Move loose hex literals in leaderboardAvatar to named constants
- Drop the SSR-only typeof document guard (Vite SPA, no SSR)
- Migrate the new hook test to the project's React-18-native renderHook

* tests: disable note post_save signal in pytest fixtures

NoteVisibilityTest.setUpTestData was failing in CI with
EmbeddingGenerationError because Note.objects.create(...) triggers
process_note_on_create_atomic, which schedules calculate_embedding_for_note_text
via eager celery. With CELERY_TASK_EAGER_PROPAGATES=True, the embedder
lookup failure (empty default_embedder in PipelineSettings, likely from
cross-worker Redis cache contamination in pytest-xdist) propagates up
through the signal and aborts the class fixture.

The Document and Annotation post_save signals are already disabled in
conftest.py for exactly this reason. Note creation has the same hazard
(it schedules an embedding task) and should be handled the same way.

Mirror the existing disconnect/reconnect pattern for the Note signal in
both `disable_document_processing_signals` (autouse, session-scoped) and
the opt-in `enable_doc_processing_signals` fixture so integration tests
can still exercise the full pipeline when they need to.

* PR #1567: address review + unblock pytest after main rebase

After merging main (which renumbered the conflicting 0069 grounding
migration to 0071 in #1581) the only remaining failing tests on this
branch are the same two typing-test assertion drifts that were failing
on main since #1543. Apply the same fixes already shipped via PR #1575:

- ``test_callable_resolves_via_from_function``: patch
  ``CoreTool.from_function`` (the bound name actually invoked at
  api.py:713), not the unused ``ToolAPI.from_function`` indirection.
- ``test_add_document_note_tool_passes_none_when_corpus_absent``: scope
  the assertNotIn to the ``add_document_note``-specific message so it
  doesn't accidentally match ``add_exact_string_annotations``'s
  legitimate corpus-required guard at line 2497.

Also address Claude bot review on this PR:

- ``leaderboardAvatar.ts``: export ``AVATAR_VIOLET`` /  ``AVATAR_PINK``
  so theme audits can import the literals directly.
- ``user_types.py``: hoist ``_stripped`` from inside
  ``resolve_display_name`` to a module-level private helper — the
  resolver runs per leaderboard query, no need to rebuild a function
  object each call.
- ``useTabVisibilityRefresh``: in development, log refetch errors
  (sync throws + rejected promises) instead of silently swallowing
  them.  Production behaviour is unchanged so caller query state
  remains the source of truth there.

* Address review: gate email at resolver, fix initials whitespace bug, log refresh errors unconditionally

Addresses comments on PR #1567:
- Gate UserType.email at the resolver (self / superuser only) so the leak is closed regardless of which client selects the field; drop email from leaderboard query/type/mocks. Coverage in EmailResolverTestCase pins self / superuser / cross-user / anonymous / blank-email / context-missing matrix.
- Fix getLeaderboardInitials: trimmed-token fallback so leading-whitespace single-token names render the correct initials instead of whitespace; whitespace-only names return "?".
- useTabVisibilityRefresh logs callback errors via console.error unconditionally so production failures surface in the browser console / Sentry.
- Tighten test_redacts_short_oauth_sub to make the OAUTH_SUB_DISPLAY_SUFFIX_LENGTH invariant explicit (assertLess on the test premise).

* Address review: gate OAuth-sub redaction on is_social_user, doc clarifications

Addresses Claude review feedback on PR #1567:

- config/graphql/user_types.py: gate the OAuth-sub redaction in
  resolve_display_name on is_social_user rather than the presence of "|"
  in the username. The project's UserUnicodeUsernameValidator (allows
  | * \ in addition to the Django default set) means a local user named
  e.g. "alice|admin" is legitimate; the previous "|"-only check would
  have falsely redacted them. Redaction now fires only for social-login
  users where username == Auth0 sub.

- opencontractserver/tests/test_user_display_name.py: existing
  redact-OAuth-sub tests now set is_social_user=True; added a new
  test_does_not_redact_local_username_with_pipe pinning the local-user

- frontend/src/hooks/useTabVisibilityRefresh.ts: clarifying notes-for-

  fired here (callers rely on Apollo's cache-and-network), and rapid

subject: Consolidate inline corpus moderation checks onto Corpus.user_can_moderate (#1450) (#1577)
message:
Consolidate inline corpus moderation checks onto Corpus.user_can_moderate (#1450) (#1577)

* Consolidate inline corpus moderation checks onto Corpus.user_can_moderate (#1450)

config/graphql/conversation_queries.py had two resolvers
(resolve_moderation_action, resolve_moderation_metrics) that each
repeated the same hand-rolled corpus-moderation gate:

    if not user.is_superuser:
        is_owner = corpus.creator == user
        is_moderator = corpus.moderators.filter(user=user).exists()
        if not is_owner and not is_moderator:
            return None

This is exactly the "inline access checks that bypass the centralized
helpers" pattern called out by issue #1450. Extracting the logic onto
Corpus consolidates the two call sites and gives a single place for the
moderation decision to evolve.

What changed
- Added Corpus.user_can_moderate(self, user) on the model. Returns True
  iff the user is a superuser, the corpus creator, or has any
  CorpusModerator row for this corpus. Anonymous / None / unauthenticated
  users always get False.
- Replaced both inline blocks in conversation_queries.py with calls to
  the helper.
- Added a regression test suite that pins the existing matrix:
  superuser, creator, moderator-with-permissions,
  moderator-with-empty-permissions (the more permissive branch this
  helper preserves), outsider, anonymous, None, and a cross-corpus
  leak guard.

Behavior preservation
The helper intentionally counts ANY CorpusModerator row (regardless of
the permissions list), which matches what conversation_queries.py was
doing before. This is more permissive than Conversation.can_moderate(),
which additionally requires bool(moderator.permissions). The discrepancy
is documented in the helper's docstring and is out of scope for this
consolidation PR per issue #1450's "consolidation PRs should not also be
behavior-change PRs" rule.

Out of scope
The remaining clusters from the inventory comment on #1450 (corpus
mutation UPDATE/CRUD checks, corpus_mutations.py creator-only
checks, worker_mutations.py group-perm fallback bug) are tracked
separately.

* Fix CorpusModerator test: pass creator to satisfy NOT NULL constraint

CorpusModerator inherits from BaseOCModel which has a non-null creator
field. The new test_corpus_user_can_moderate.py setUp called
CorpusModerator.objects.create(...) without creator, triggering
IntegrityError on every test in the class.

Pass creator=self.owner / self.outsider so the model rows actually
persist and exercise user_can_moderate.

* Fix CI on PR #1577 and address review

- test_callable_resolves_via_from_function: patch the actual call site
  (CoreTool.from_function), not the ToolAPI wrapper that _resolve_tools
  no longer routes through.
- test_add_document_note_tool_passes_none_when_corpus_absent: scope the
  source-grep to the add_document_note_tool body so the corpus-required
  diagnostic on add_exact_string_annotations no longer trips it.
- Address review: prefer user.pk over user.id in user_can_moderate to
  match the Django convention used elsewhere in the file.

subject: Harden Document delete-time orphan blob reclaim (closes #1572) (#1579)
message:
Harden Document delete-time orphan blob reclaim (closes #1572) (#1579)

Six surgical follow-ups to the orphan-blob reclaim path landed in PR #1487
/ issue #1492:

1. Document.blob_field_names() now returns a tuple (immutable) instead of
   sharing a mutable list across callers. No current caller mutated the
   result, but the latent footgun could have corrupted the cache for
   every subsequent caller in the process.

2. _schedule_blob_cleanup_post_delete registers AT MOST ONE on_commit
   flush callback per atomic context. The flush callback is now a
   module-level function tagged with a sentinel marker; we detect prior
   registrations in connection.run_on_commit before adding another. A
   bulk delete of N rows now costs O(1) on_commit registrations instead
   of O(N). Rollback safety preserved — Django drops our callback from
   the queue on rollback, so the next post_delete in a fresh
   transaction re-registers cleanly. The orphan re-check inside the
   cleanup task continues to backstop cross-transaction accumulator
   bleed.

3. cleanup_orphaned_document_blobs_task calls default_storage.delete()
   unconditionally and catches FileNotFoundError at DEBUG, closing the
   TOCTOU window between an exists() probe and the delete. A concurrent
   process removing the blob mid-task is now treated as a benign race
   instead of an alarming ERROR log.

4. cleanup_orphaned_document_blobs_task gained autoretry_for=(Exception,),
   max_retries=3, default_retry_delay=60. The task is idempotent (the
   orphan re-check absorbs whatever happened on a previous attempt) so
   transient worker / DB / storage errors now retry instead of silently
   losing the remaining paths.

5. The __in lookup in the orphan check now passes sorted(candidate_paths)
   (a list) instead of a set, eliminating non-deterministic query plans
   on backends sensitive to set input ordering.

6. The undocumented "store an arbitrary attribute on
   django.db.connections[alias]" pattern is now flagged with a comment
   and a documented escape hatch (WeakValueDictionary keyed by
   id(connection) or threading.local) should the assumption ever break.

Test: new test_bulk_delete_registers_single_on_commit_callback in
test_blob_retention.py deletes 20 rows inside a single atomic block and
asserts exactly one blob-cleanup callback (filtered by the sentinel
marker) is appended to connection.run_on_commit. Pre-fix this would have
been 20.

Note: the existing test_missing_path_is_tolerated was updated to assert
the new idempotency contract (storage absent after the call) rather than
the old "deleted_count == 0" semantic — the unconditional-delete change
shifts that count slightly for backends that swallow FileNotFoundError.

* Fix LoadingOverlay-during-fetchMore in 7 sibling infinite-scroll lists (follow-up to #1565)

PR #1565 fixed the dim-overlay-during-fetchMore antipattern in Documents.tsx
only, but seven sibling views/components copied the same shape and exhibited
the same UX regression: a full-cover (mostly inverted/dark) LoadingOverlay was
shown for the entire `loading === true` window — including fetchMore — dimming

  - frontend/src/components/exports/ExportList.tsx
  - frontend/src/components/extracts/ExtractCards.tsx
  - frontend/src/components/corpuses/CorpusListView.tsx
  - frontend/src/components/analyses/AnalysesCards.tsx
  - frontend/src/components/documents/DocumentCards.tsx

Fix: each call site now scopes LoadingOverlay.active to the initial load only
(`loading && filteredItems.length === 0`, or for DocumentCards the existing
`showEmptyState` gate which already encodes "no items and no folders") and
drops the `inverted` flag — the dark variant is now reserved for genuinely
blocking states.

extracted to a shared component at
frontend/src/components/widgets/infinite_scroll/FetchMoreFooter.tsx

The shared FetchMoreOnVisible stale-closure / rootMargin fixes from #1565

subject: typing: graduate opencontractserver.shared.{Managers,decorators} (closes #1477) (#1533)
message:
typing: graduate opencontractserver.shared.{Managers,decorators} (closes #1477) (#1533)

* typing: graduate opencontractserver.shared.{Managers,decorators} (closes #1477)

Drains the last two `[mypy-opencontractserver.shared.*]` ignore-blocks
from `mypy.ini`. Continues #1470 (which graduated QuerySets/fields/mixins)
and finishes the shared package's mypy migration.

Removed from mypy.ini
- opencontractserver.shared.Managers
- opencontractserver.shared.decorators

Pruned from docs/typing/mypy_baseline.txt
- 37 lines (6813 -> 6776)

Per-file fixes

shared/Managers.py
- Drop the `if TYPE_CHECKING / else AbstractUser as User` aliasing block
  (mypy treated `User` as a value, not a type — root cause of seven
  `valid-type` errors in the baseline). Replace User-as-type with
  AbstractBaseUser on EmbeddingManager.store_embedding(creator=...) and
  UserFeedbackManager.by_creator(creator=...), and Any for
  _apply_document_prefetches(user=...) which duck-types is_anonymous /
  is_superuser.
- Cast self.model to Any once in BaseVisibilityManager.visible_to_user
  so the seven `model_cls.objects.*` sites typecheck. Same cast on the
  one self.model.DoesNotExist site in UserFeedbackManager.get_or_none.
  _default_manager would change call semantics for models that override
  objects, so the cast is preferred.
- Coalesce self.model._meta.model_name or "" so the two .upper() calls
  don't union-attr against None.
- Align PermissionManager.visible_to_user and
  UserFeedbackManager.visible_to_user with
  BaseVisibilityManager.visible_to_user(user, lightweight,
  with_doc_label_annotations) — kwargs accepted for parity, no
  behaviour change. Matches the pattern adopted in
  CorpusActionExecutionManager (PR #1473 review).
- Silence `[misc]` on the PermissionManager.from_queryset(...) dynamic
  base for AnnotationManager and NoteManager. Documented inline.
- Remove three unused `for_user(...)` delegation methods on
  PermissionManager / AnnotationManager / NoteManager. They called
  self.get_queryset().for_user(...) against querysets that never
  implement `for_user`, so any caller would have raised AttributeError
  at runtime. Verified no callers in opencontractserver/, config/, or
  tests.

shared/decorators.py
- Annotate pdf_text_extract as Optional[str] in both wrappers and
  assert it is not None inside the TXT branch (only reachable when
  txt_extract_file is non-empty, so the assert is a no-op at runtime).
- Annotate pdf_data_layer as Any in both wrappers to absorb the
  `[] | PdfDataLayer` union without forcing plasmapdf stubs.
- Add `-> Any` return annotations to the three remaining inner helpers
  (get_analysis_creator, get_analysis_analyzer,
  celery_task_with_async_to_sync.wrapper).

Coverage
- Managers.py: 100% return-annotation coverage (24/24)
- decorators.py: 100% return-annotation coverage (16/16)

Verification
- pre-commit run --all-files -> all hooks pass (mypy: Passed)
- No regressions in mypy across opencontractserver + config (1032
  source files checked).

* Fix model_cls in get_or_none, replace assert with guard, add manager coverage tests

- UserFeedbackManager.get_or_none: hoist model_cls local so
  model_cls.DoesNotExist is evaluated once, not inside except clause
  (cleaner and avoids repeated cast on the hot path)

- opencontractserver/shared/decorators.py: replace bare assert with an
  explicit if/raise guard so the invariant check survives python -O;
  update comment to reflect it is a fast-fail runtime guard, not a
  type-narrowing hint

- opencontractserver/tests/test_shared_managers.py: new test module
  covering PermissionManager, UserFeedbackManager, and
  UserFeedbackManager.get_or_none for the user=None coercion path and
  hit/miss paths (boosts patch coverage for lines graduated from the
  mypy baseline in #1477)

- mypy.ini: remove stray duplicate ignore_errors line left by
  merge-conflict resolution

- opencontractserver/utils/embeddings.py: cast get_embedder return to
  type[BaseEmbedder] | None (get_component_by_name returns the broader
  PipelineComponentBase); fixes new mypy error surfaced after merging
  the utils.embeddings graduation from main

* Add coverage for decorators.py guard paths and manager superuser branch

- test_task_decorators.py: two new tests for the ``pdf_text_extract is None``
  guard (decorators.py lines 273-276) covering both ``text/plain`` and
  ``application/txt`` MIME types
- test_shared_managers.py: two new test classes covering
  BaseVisibilityManager.visible_to_user(superuser) (model_cls.objects.all()
  branch) and PermissionManager.visible_to_user(superuser); also imports
  clean-up (unused Annotation import removed)

* Address review: assert non-None model_name, drop magic pk in get_or_none miss test

- shared/Managers.py: replace silent 'or ""' fallback on
  Options.model_name with an explicit assert so an abstract-model
  invariant violation surfaces as a clear AssertionError instead of
  cascading through the permission table lookup as an empty string.
- tests/test_shared_managers.py: compute a guaranteed-missing pk by
  taking max(pk) + 1 instead of hard-coding 999999999 (CLAUDE.md no-
  magic-numbers rule).

* Fix mypy: remove redundant cast in get_embedder return (#1545)

The cast(Optional[type[BaseEmbedder]], embedder_class) on the return
statement was redundant because mypy infers the correct type from the
assignments throughout the function body. The function's return type
annotation already declares the same type, so mypy reports
[redundant-cast].

This is the only mypy error on main and has been blocking the linter
step of Backend CI for multiple commits, which in turn cascade-skips
the pytest job and prevents Codecov from receiving fresh coverage.

* typing: address review issues from pipeline.* mypy graduation (PR #1540) (#1544)

Follow-up to #1540 (merged) addressing issues raised in the Claude code review:

- Issue 1: Mark `dependencies` and `input_schema` as `ClassVar` on
  `PipelineComponentBase` to prevent shared mutable state across subclasses.
  Remove now-redundant declarations from `BaseParser`, `BaseEmbedder`,
  `BaseThumbnailGenerator`, `BasePostProcessor`, and `BaseReranker`.
  Mark `supported_file_types` and `supported_modalities` as `ClassVar` too.

- Issue 2: Update `find_image_tokens_in_bounds` signature to accept
  `list[PawlsTokenPythonType]` (matches callers) instead of
  `list[dict[str, Any]]`, eliminating 3 `cast()` calls in `llamaparse_parser`.

- Issue 3: Remove internal `cast(dict[str, Any], source)` from
  `LlamaParseParser._build_image_token` — `PawlsTokenPythonType` already
  declares all accessed fields as `NotRequired`, so `source.get(...)` is
  type-safe without widening.

  `tuple[Optional[type[BaseEmbedder]], Optional[str]]` to satisfy mypy, which
  could not infer the narrowed type from a first-element cast alone.

All pre-commit hooks (black, isort, flake8, mypy) pass.

* Demote chatty permissioning INFO logs to DEBUG (#1525)

* Demote chatty permissioning INFO logs to DEBUG

every authenticated request, dominating Django pod logs and inflating
storage costs. Collapses the two lines into one logger.debug() call
using lazy %-formatting so the message is not built unless DEBUG is
enabled. Permission denial logs and WARNING/ERROR paths are unchanged.

Closes #1436

* Merge main and apply embeddings.py mypy fix

The latest main brought a mypy regression in opencontractserver/utils/embeddings.py
where get_component_by_name returns type[PipelineComponentBase], but the function
signature requires type[BaseEmbedder]. Cast the result and annotate the local
embedder_class to satisfy the stricter return type.

return statement, which mypy flags as [redundant-cast]. The variables

embedder_path (Optional[str]) already carry the correct types via

This restores the fix from #1545 and unblocks the linter step on

* Address review: add async TXT guard + retarget BaseVisibilityManager test

Two follow-ups from the Claude review on PR #1533:

   wrapper added: if pdf_text_extract is None: raise ValueError(...)
   inside the text/plain branch. The async post-processing path uses
   span['text'] (not a slice into pdf_text_extract) so the guard is
   defensive rather than required by the immediate code, but the
   contract is the same: TXT processing requires a non-empty
   txt_extract_file. Mirroring the sync invariant fails fast instead
   of silently saving annotations from a doc the analyzer couldn't
   compute spans for. Two new regression tests pin the contract for
   text/plain and application/txt.

2. BaseVisibilityManagerSuperuserTest claimed to exercise
   BaseVisibilityManager.visible_to_user but the test routed through
   Corpus.objects, which is a PermissionManager whose visible_to_user
   is fully overridden — the base manager's superuser / anonymous /
   guardian-fallback branches were never reached. Retarget the test
   to the Embedding model (annotations.Embedding uses
   EmbeddingManager(BaseVisibilityManager) without an override), so
   the call now lands directly in BaseVisibilityManager. Three
   subtests pin the superuser-sees-all branch, the anonymous-only-
   public branch (user=None coercion), and the unrelated-user
   guardian-fallback branch.

Also fixes the embeddings.py redundant-cast regression that resurfaced
during the main merge (post-#1545 cast is genuinely redundant, mypy
was right; restore the no-cast form).

CI fix:

- Drop the duplicated assertIsNotNone before the mypy-narrowing

The patch coverage report flagged 5 missed lines in Managers.py
(84.84% / target 87.98%):

  - line 180  raise RuntimeError on abstract-model guard
  - lines 203/206/209  unreachable branches inside the if/elif chain in
                       BaseVisibilityManager.visible_to_user (None /

                       method already returns early at lines 154-164

  - line 302  user = AnonymousUser() in PermissionManager.visible_to_user

Close corpus-less ModerationAction auth gap (closes #1594) (#1595)

* Mark corpus-less ModerationAction auth gap with TODO (#1594)

resolve_moderation_action falls through to `return action` for
corpus-less actions when the user is a non-superuser, because the
permission check is gated on `if corpus:`. This is pre-existing
behavior, intentionally preserved here. Add a visible TODO at the
branch so the debt isn't lost; tracked by #1594 for the actual fix
(which should mirror resolve_moderation_actions' queryset filter).

* Address PR review: keep canonical user_can_moderate, add TODO above

Reverts the inlined permission re-write in resolve_moderation_action
back to the canonical Corpus.user_can_moderate(user) helper introduced
in #1450/#1577, and places the TODO(#1594) note above that single line
to flag the corpus-less fall-through gap. Restores parity with the
sibling resolve_moderation_metrics resolver. Documents the gap in
CHANGELOG.md under [Unreleased] / Security.

* Close corpus-less ModerationAction auth gap (closes #1594)

Fix the underlying issue rather than just documenting it. The previous
resolver short-circuited to 'return action' whenever
'conversation.chat_with_corpus' was None, which leaked document-only
and orphaned moderation actions to any authenticated user via direct
ID lookup.

Route every case through Conversation.can_moderate (the same canonical
authorization helper used by the moderation mutations themselves).
That helper accepts:
  - superuser
  - conversation creator
  - corpus owner / designated moderator (when chat_with_corpus is set)
  - document owner (when chat_with_document is set)

Actions whose conversation FK is NULL (a rare historical edge — the
column is nullable but every real action has one) fail closed for
non-superusers, mirroring the list resolver's exclusion of those rows.

Tests: new ResolveModerationActionAuthGateTest pins all four allowed
paths plus the previously-leaking unauthorized-user case for both
document-only and corpus-attached conversations, and the orphan
fail-closed branch.

message:
Decompose Corpuses.tsx into thinner composer + sibling files (#1578)

* Decompose Corpuses.tsx into thinner composer + sibling files

`frontend/src/views/Corpuses.tsx` had grown to 3,336 lines — listed in #1446
as oversized. Three extractions land it under 1,900:

- `Corpuses.styles.ts` (new): all sidebar / tab-header / mobile-menu
  styled-components used by the main view, plus the tab-header components
  shared with the extracted ExtractsTabContent.
- `CorpusQueryView.tsx` (new): the corpus dashboard / chat composer rendered
  inside the Home tab, together with its private DashboardContainer /
  ChatNavigationHeader / etc. styled-components. Owns the local search-input
  ↔ expanded-chat transition.
- `ExtractsTabContent.tsx` (new): the split-view extracts tab, together with
  its private ExtractsSplitView / ExtractsListPane / ExtractsDetailPane /
  toolbar styled-components.

Net: main file drops from 3,336 → 1,863 lines (44% reduction) while
remaining behaviorally identical — the public `Corpuses` export, route
wiring, and rendered DOM are unchanged. Dead code removed along the way:
- `ChatTransitionContainer`, `SearchToConversationInput`, `NotificationBadge`
  styled-components (declared, never rendered).
- `opened_corpus_id` prop and `handleSearchSubmit` handler on the inner
  query view (never read).
- Imports that became unreferenced after the extraction (`Home` / `Search`
  / `History` icons, `CorpusHome`, `CORPUS_*` design-token re-exports,
  `showQueryViewState`, `selectedExtractIds`, `updateAnnotationSelectionParams`,
  `CorpusExtractCards`, `CorpusExtractDetail`).

State doesn't need to be lifted to a Jotai atom for this slice; the two
extracted components own only local UI state, and everything they need from
the parent is already passed as props.

Refs #1446

* Address PR review: design tokens, hoisted constants, dead CSS

- ExtractsTabContent: replace magic 1024px / 768px breakpoints with
  TABLET_LANDSCAPE_BREAKPOINT (new) and TABLET_BREAKPOINT
- ExtractsTabContent: hoist filterItems to module scope as
  EXTRACT_FILTER_ITEMS so the array is not reallocated each render
- CorpusQueryView: replace hardcoded #357abd hover hex with
  OS_LEGAL_COLORS.primaryBlueHover design token
- CorpusQueryView: drop unreachable `background: white` declaration in
  ChatNavigationHeader (immediately overridden by rgba 0.95 below)

* Add ExtractsTabContent interaction coverage tests (#1578)

Three new tests under "Corpus Tabs - ExtractsTabContent - search and
filter interactions" exercise the search/filter branches of the
extracted ExtractsTabContent component that the higher-level navigation
tests don't drive:

- renders search input + all five filter tabs
- typing in the search input updates the SearchBox value
- clicking a non-default filter tab marks it aria-selected
- adds a docScreenshot for the toolbar at corpus--extracts-tab--toolbar

* Add direct-mount coverage tests for CorpusQueryView (#1578)

CorpusTabs.ct.tsx mounts the whole Corpuses tree, which doesn't reach
CorpusQueryView's VIEW-state header or null-corpus placeholder branches
(showQueryViewState resets to "ASK" on each fresh mount and the wrapper
provides no way to inject a different starting value before render).

Add a thin CorpusQueryViewTestWrapper that mounts the component
directly with just MockedProvider + Jotai + MemoryRouter, plus four
tests covering:

- opened_corpus=null -> "No corpus selected" placeholder
- VIEW state desktop header ("Conversation History" + "Back to
