  (ChatNavigationHeader / NavigationTitle / BackButton)
- Back button click flips the reactive var back to ASK
- VIEW header surfaces the "Return to Dashboard" Home action button

Adds docScreenshot at corpus--query-view--conversation-history.

* Address PR review on #1578: cleanup, hoisted constants, drop unused prop

- CorpusQueryView: hoist 99vh/150ms/100ms to module-scoped constants;
  return clearTimeout cleanups from both focus useEffects and track the
  resetToSearch timer in a ref so unmount cancels it (stale-ref guard).
- CorpusQueryView: drop unnecessary `as CorpusType` cast — TS narrows
  after the early null-return.
- Corpuses.styles: remove unused $sidebarExpanded transient prop on
  MainContentArea (declared, never interpolated). Drop the matching
  prop forward in Corpuses.tsx.
- ExtractsTabContent: comment that activeFilter is intentionally
  per-visit local state (matches sibling tabs).

* Boost frontend patch coverage on extracted modules

Add coverage-driven tests that exercise previously-uncovered branches:

CorpusQueryView (CorpusQueryViewCoverage.ct.tsx):
- Click VIEW-state Home button → reactive var flips to ASK
- ASK state with a corpus renders the dashboard container (covers the
  default dashboard render path missed by the existing VIEW-only tests)
- Mobile (375px) VIEW state suppresses the outer navigation header
  (covers the !isDesktop early-return branch)

ExtractsTabContent (CorpusTabs.ct.tsx):
- Typing fires the debounced callback (waits past the 500ms debounce
  so the inner callback executes before tear-down)
- Pressing Enter fires the SearchBox onSubmit handler
- Back button returns to the Home tab (covers setActiveTab(0) and
  the unmount-time debounce cleanup)

Refresh the regenerated docs screenshot for the conversation-history
view at the new viewport.

* Add unit tests for CorpusQueryView handlers; address review

- New CorpusQueryView.handlers.test.tsx mocks CorpusHome / CorpusChat to
  exercise the onChatSubmit / onNavigateHome / onViewModeChange branches
  the CT suite cannot reach without standing up the full composer.
  Targets the 405-422 chat-expansion path and 474-475 navigate-home reset
  flow that codecov flagged as uncovered (raises CorpusQueryView.tsx
  patch coverage above the 80% threshold).
- Add missing 'totalThreads: 0' to GET_CORPUS_STATS mock in the
  CorpusQueryView test wrapper to match the schema field surface.
- Same useTabVisibilityRefresh.test.ts initialProps fix already on
  PRs 1586 / 1585 / 1580 — surfaces post-merge with main.

Dismissed review item: 'activeFilter not wired to ExtractsListPane' is
incorrect — line 196 in ExtractsTabContent.tsx already passes
activeFilter to CorpusExtractCards.

* Address PR review and fix CI: any-baseline, focus timer, naming hygiene

Five follow-ups for the Corpuses.tsx decomposition PR:

- Lint failure was the `any:check:strict` baseline gate, not Prettier
  formatting. The two `(props: any)` stubs in
  `CorpusQueryView.handlers.test.tsx` pushed the count from 453 to 455.
  Replaced with narrow local `MockCorpusHomeProps` /
  `MockCorpusChatProps` interfaces capturing only the prop callbacks
  the stubs surface — the real components accept many more props but
  the stubs don't need them, so a tight local type works without
  dragging the full component signatures into the test file.

- `CorpusQueryView.resetToSearch`: drop the duplicate focus timer.
  `setIsSearchMode(true)` already triggers the existing `useEffect` on
  `isSearchMode`, which schedules + cleans up its own focus timer. The
  ref-owned timer couldn't be cancelled by the effect's cleanup, so a
  second source could fire against a stale ref. Comment explains why
  the explicit timer is gone.

- `ExtractsTabContent.tsx`: add the missing `import React` so the
  `React.FC` namespace reference is explicit and not relying on the
  `react-jsx` global type declaration.

- `Corpuses.styles.ts` / `Corpuses.tsx`: rename `isActive` →
  `$isActive` on `NavItemBadge` and `NavigationItem` so styled-
  components doesn't forward the prop to the DOM (suppresses React's
  unknown-prop warning that the previous non-transient name produced).

- `CorpusQueryViewTestWrapper.tsx`: move the `showQueryViewState`
  reactive-var write into a `useState` initializer so it runs once
  per mount instead of on every parent re-render. Behaviour is
  identical for the existing tests (afterEach already resets state),
  but the intent is clearer and the call no longer fires on
  every render.

subject: Reddit-style auto-assigned user handles (issue #1574) (#1589)
message:
Reddit-style auto-assigned user handles (issue #1574) (#1589)

* Add Reddit-style auto-assigned user handles (issue #1574)

Replace the redacted ``user_<id>`` displayName fallback for Auth0 social-login
users without populated ``name``/``given_name``/``first_name`` claims with an
auto-assigned ``adjectiveNoun`` handle (e.g. ``cleverFox``).

- ``opencontractserver/users/handle_wordlists.py`` — curated 248×227 namespace
  (~56k base combos), all-lowercase ASCII, hand-vetted.
- ``opencontractserver/users/handle_generator.py`` — pure generator with
  scope-queryset uniqueness check, optional pre-seeded RNG for deterministic
  tests, and numeric-suffix promotion when the plain namespace is exhausted.
- ``User.handle`` field with auto-assignment on ``save()`` (mirrors the
  existing slug guard, including the table-has-column check for migrations
  pre-dating the column).
- ``UserType.displayName`` resolver chain: ``name`` → ``given_name +
  family_name`` → ``first_name + last_name`` → ``handle`` → ``username`` (only
  when not a ``provider|sub`` Auth0 identifier) → redacted ``user_<id>``.
- Schema + data migrations 0027/0028 backfill existing users in one pass.
- Management command ``regenerate_user_handles`` for re-running with
  ``--reroll-suffixed`` (after the word list grows) or ``--reroll-all``.
- Tests pin generator uniqueness, no-PII-leakage, fixed-seed determinism,
  suffix promotion under saturation, the resolver chain priority, and the
  three management-command modes.

User-facing handle editing is intentionally out of scope; the resolver still
gracefully degrades to the redacted fallback for any user the migration hasn't
reached yet.

Closes #1574

* Resolve test_user_display_name conflicts; gate redaction on is_social_user

After merging main into PR 1589, test_user_display_name.py (added in main)
exercises the OAuth-sub redaction fallback assuming no auto-assigned handle.
Clear user.handle in the relevant tests to keep that branch reachable, and
switch resolve_display_name's redaction gate from a raw '|' check to the
is_social_user model flag so local users with '|' in their username (legal
per UserUnicodeUsernameValidator) are no longer mistakenly redacted.

Also fix mypy union-attr errors in test_user_handle.py introduced by the
nullable handle field.

* Address review: race retry, constants extraction, comment cleanup

- Bound retry loop in User.save() catches IntegrityError on the handle
  unique-constraint race (generate_handle samples uniqueness with a
  non-locking .exists() so concurrent inserts can collide). Bound is
  HANDLE_INSERT_RETRY_ATTEMPTS to prevent pathological loops.
- Move handle generator tunables (PLAIN/SUFFIXED_ATTEMPTS, SUFFIX_MIN/MAX,
  retry attempts, USER_HANDLE_MAX_LENGTH) to opencontractserver/constants/
  users.py per project convention. Backwards-compatible aliases preserved
  in handle_generator so existing test patches still work.
- Strip 'issue #1574' / 'Issue #1574' references from inline comments,
  docstrings, migrations, and management command help text.
- Correct wordlist count comments (240->248 adjectives, 220->227 nouns).
- Update test_user_display_name.py to use queryset.update(handle=None) so
  the redaction-fallback tests reach that branch (save() would re-trigger
  auto-assignment).

* Address PR review: import hoisting, wordlist hygiene, docstrings

Eight surgical follow-ups to the auto-handle PR:

- Hoist `from django.db import IntegrityError` to module-level imports in
  `users/models.py` so it isn't re-resolved per `save()` call.
- Migration 0028 comment: replace the misleading "we commit each row"
  prose with the correct PostgreSQL READ COMMITTED rationale (RunPython
  wraps the loop in one txn; the connection sees its own uncommitted
  writes between iterations, no per-row commit needed).
- Remove `comet`, `meadow`, `prairie` from ADJECTIVES (they appear in
  NOUNS already and would emit degenerate pairs like `cometComet`).
- Update wordlists module docstring: format constraint loosened from
  3-10 to 3-12 characters (was already violated by `caterpillar`,
  `nightingale`, `grasshopper`, `hummingbird`); add explicit rule that
  no word may appear in both lists.
- Add `test_wordlists_have_no_cross_list_overlap` to
  `tests/test_user_handle.py` so the no-overlap rule is enforced.
- `handle_generator.py`: rename misleading "Backwards-compatible aliases"
  comment (this is a new file, no legacy callers) to clarify these are
  module-local re-exports for callers and tests; emit a `logger.warning`
  when the plain phase exhausts so an operator sees saturation early.
- Restore the longer `resolve_display_name` docstring with the full
  resolution-order / pipe-allowed-in-local-username / OAuth-redaction
  invariants that were lost when it was condensed.
- Adjustment of the wordlists count comment (245, was 248) to reflect
  the three removed entries.

* Address PR review: skip Anonymous, robust collision detection, lint fixes

- Exclude django-guardian's Anonymous user from handle auto-assignment in
  User.save(), the migration backfill, and the regenerate_user_handles
  management command. Anonymous is a system account that never surfaces
  to other users; without this exclusion the post-migrate creation of
  Anonymous (after 0028 ran) could leave it with handle=NULL and skew
  test fixtures that count missing-handle candidates.
- Replace the brittle 'handle' in str(exc).lower() check in User.save()
  with a query-based collision confirmation. The previous heuristic
  silently swallowed non-handle integrity errors if the constraint name
  ever drifted; querying for the chosen handle is database-agnostic and
  proves the conflict belongs to this column.
- Migration 0028: collapse the | queryset union into a single Q() filter
  (one query instead of two via SQL UNION), and document the deliberate
  import of live handle_generator code.
- Word list cleanup: 'flora' and 'ladybug' moved from ADJECTIVES to
  NOUNS — both read more naturally as nouns and the noun-noun pairing
  was producing awkward handles like 'ladybugFox'.

Tests: handle test suite (27 tests) passes; the 'updated 1 user(s)'
expectation in test_default_mode_only_fills_missing now holds because
Anonymous is excluded from the candidates query.

* Address PR review: reroll-suffixed bug, anon test, docs

- regenerate_user_handles: when rerolling, keep the user's own row in
  scope_qs so its current DB handle blocks generate_handle from re-selecting
  the same value. Excluding by pk + python-only handle=None reset let
  cleverFox42 round-trip through the generator.
- Replace get_user_model() with type(self) inside User.save() for
  idiomatic style in a model save() override.
- Drop the unused DEFAULT_HANDLE_FIELD constant; default the handle_field
  parameter to "handle" directly.
- Reconcile word-count comments in handle_wordlists.py (243 adjectives,
  229 nouns).
- Strip remaining "issue #1574" references from code comments / docstrings
  per CLAUDE.md (those belong in the PR description, not the source).
- Add Anonymous-user exclusion tests to pin User.save() and
  regenerate_user_handles --reroll-all both leave Anonymous untouched.
- Document the feature at docs/architecture/user_handles.md (wired into
  mkdocs.yml). Covers resolution chain, generator semantics, migrations,
  management command modes, tunables, and word-list editing rules.
- CHANGELOG entry for the reroll fix and the new test/doc surface.

subject: Add agent tools for step-by-step CAML article citation review (#1575)
message:
Add agent tools for step-by-step CAML article citation review (#1575)

* Add CAML article citation review agent tools

Three new async tools compose into a step-by-step CAML citation review
flow against a corpus's Readme.CAML article, addressing the request to
walk through citations one location at a time with user approval per
edit:

- read_corpus_caml_article (read-only): loads the article via
  Document.objects.visible_to_user and returns blank-line-delimited
  blocks with each block's existing {{@cite ...}} directives plus a
  needs_citation_candidate heuristic flagging prose blocks that lack a
  citation directive. Headings, lists, code fences, blockquotes, table
  rows, and [component:...] markers are excluded so candidates focus on
  prose the user would actually want to cite.

- propose_caml_citation_match (read-only): runs the same
  CoreAnnotationVectorStore.async_search path the renderer's
  useCiteHandler uses, scoped to the invoking user. Returns ranked
  annotation candidates {annotation_id, raw_text, label_text,
  label_color, document_id, document_title, corpus_id, page,
  similarity_score} capped at 25 entries.

- apply_caml_article_edit (requires_approval, requires_write_permission,
  requires_corpus): replaces a single occurrence of target_text with
  replacement_text inside Readme.CAML. Fails closed on zero or multi
  matches so the agent cannot silently rewrite the wrong location.
  Layers an explicit UPDATE check (is_superuser / creator_id ==
  user.id / user_has_permission_for_obj UPDATE) on top of the wrapper's
  READ check. Rewrites Document.txt_extract_file in place via
  FieldFile.save so existing deep-links to Readme.CAML resolve. The
  rationale argument is surfaced in the approval modal.

The frontend's directive registry (caml/directiveRegistry.ts) is
already extensible, and inserted {{@cite scope}} markers are resolved
at render time by the existing useCiteHandler semantic search, so no
frontend changes were required.

Tests cover block parsing, candidate heuristics, IDOR-safe error
messages, the single-occurrence rule, the creator/superuser/UPDATE
matrix, and registry resolution including requires_approval /
requires_write_permission / requires_corpus flags. Test execution
inside the freshly-spun-up sandbox docker daemon was blocked by a TLS
inspection cert that prevents the build container from reaching pypi;
mypy/black/isort/flake8/pyupgrade hooks all pass on the new files.

Also reverts opencontractserver/utils/embeddings.py:132 back to the
bare `return embedder_class, embedder_path` form from PR #1545. Commit
85496ad re-introduced a redundant tuple cast that mypy flagged under
warn_redundant_casts = True; this was the only mypy error on the
branch and blocked any new commit's pre-commit run.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01Y2JQWYwwXQL6Bws1xUTcHL

* PR #1575: fix CI green path

Three classes of fixes that together unblock backend pytest + e2e on
this PR (and on main, which has been failing on every run since
e52e223e0):

1. Resolve dual-leaf annotations migration conflict
   ----------------------------------------------------------------
   ``0069_grounding_annotation_unique_constraints`` (PR #1418, branched
   off ``0068_enforce_embedder_path_not_null``) and
   ``0070_seed_default_labelset`` (descended from
   ``0069_labelset_is_default_and_seed_default``, also off ``0068_*``)
   landed as parallel leaves in the migration graph.  Django's
   ``manage.py migrate`` errors on multiple leaves, blocking pytest +
   e2e on every commit since the merge.  Add an empty merge migration
   ``0071_merge_20260508`` that depends on both leaves.

2. CAML review tests: TestCase -> TransactionTestCase + per-test setUp
   ----------------------------------------------------------------
   ``test_caml_review_tools.py`` saved a Readme.CAML.md file from
   ``setUpTestData`` (class scope), but the autouse ``media_storage``
   fixture in ``conftest.py`` repoints ``settings.MEDIA_ROOT`` at a
   fresh per-test ``tmpdir``, so the file was unreachable from any
   test other than the one that ran setUpTestData.  And the async
   wrapper tests went through ``_db_sync_to_async`` (which forces
   ``thread_sensitive=False``), so the helper thread's fresh DB
   connection couldn't see TestCase's transaction-wrapped fixtures.

   Both classes that touch the CAML file (``ReadCorpusCamlArticleTests``
   and ``ApplyCamlArticleEditTests``) now inherit from
   ``TransactionTestCase`` and recreate users + corpus + Readme.CAML.md
   per test in ``setUp``, so every test sees the file in its own
   ``MEDIA_ROOT`` and async helpers see committed rows.

3. Typing-test assertion drift on main
   ----------------------------------------------------------------
   - ``test_callable_resolves_via_from_function`` patched
     ``ToolAPI.from_function`` but ``_resolve_tools`` actually calls
     ``CoreTool.from_function`` directly (api.py:713), so the patch
     never intercepted the call.  Patch the bound name actually
     invoked.
   - ``test_add_document_note_tool_passes_none_when_corpus_absent``
     used ``assertNotIn('requires the agent to be scoped to a corpus"',
     text)`` against the entire ``pydantic_ai_agents.py`` body.  That
     fragment legitimately appears for ``add_exact_string_annotations``
     (line 2497).  Scope the assertion to the
     ``add_document_note``-specific message.

Address Claude bot review on this PR
----------------------------------------------------------------
- ``_read_caml_content`` now opens the file in binary mode and decodes
  UTF-8 explicitly so non-ASCII CAML articles don't depend on the
  runtime locale.
- Wrap the read-check-write in ``_apply_caml_article_edit`` in
  ``transaction.atomic()`` + ``select_for_update()`` to close the
  concurrent-edit race window (low-severity, but cheap).
- ``_load_caml_document_for_user`` drops the redundant
  ``is_current=True`` filter — ``corpus.get_documents(include_caml=True)``
  already enforces it via DocumentPath.
- ``apropose_caml_citation_match`` gains an inline comment naming the
  wrapper as the corpus-permission enforcement point so a future
  refactor doesn't silently drop that protection.
- ``CamlReviewToolRegistryTests`` moves
  ``ToolFunctionRegistry.reset()`` to ``setUpClass`` /
  ``tearDownClass`` so an unexpected exception in the test body can't
  leak modified registry state into other tests on the same worker.

* Remove redundant 0071_merge_20260508 — main's renumber (#1581) reparents 0071_grounding on 0070_seed_default_labelset, leaving a single linear leaf and making the merge migration both unnecessary and broken (it referenced the now-renamed 0069_grounding)

* Address review: rollback-safe file write, constants relocation, IDOR test

- Move CAML_ARTICLE_TITLE to opencontractserver/constants/document_processing.py
  alongside MARKDOWN_MIME_TYPE; re-export from caml_article.py for back-compat
- _apply_caml_article_edit: use select_for_update().get(pk=) atomically and
  move FieldFile.save() to be the LAST operation in the transaction so a
  rollback after the storage write can never orphan the blob; refresh_from_db
  for the modified timestamp now happens outside the txn (read-only)
- Drop dead "isinstance bytes" branch in _read_caml_content (binary mode read
  always returns bytes)
- Push CAML id intersection as a subquery instead of materialising IDs in Python
- Add test_empty_caml_file_raises_not_found for the empty-body edit path
- Tighten test_outsider_without_access_raises to assert byte-identical
  message templates between "private corpus" and "non-existent corpus" cases

* Address PR #1575 Claude review feedback

Six targeted fixes drawn from the most recent claude-bot review:

1. _looks_like_prose: also exclude "+" CommonMark unordered-list marker
   and pure thematic-break / setext-underline blocks (only "-", "_", "="
   characters), which previously slipped through as prose candidates.

2. _apply_caml_article_edit: pass save=False to FieldFile.save() and
   follow up with locked_doc.save(update_fields=["txt_extract_file",
   "modified"]). Default save=True triggers a full Document.save() which
   would rewrite unrelated columns (backend_lock, processing flags) and
   could clobber concurrent updates.

3. apropose_caml_citation_match: add inline _assert_corpus_visible_to_user
   defense-in-depth check (wrapped via _db_sync_to_async) so the function
   fails closed even when invoked outside the registry wrapper. New test
   pins the guard. ProposeCamlCitationMatchTests upgraded to
   TransactionTestCase since the helper thread now opens a fresh DB
   connection that only sees committed fixtures.

4. apropose_caml_citation_match: drop the redundant results[:capped_limit]
   slice. CoreAnnotationVectorStore.async_search already honours
   similarity_top_k=capped_limit, so the slice was misleading.

5. test_add_document_note_tool_passes_none_when_corpus_absent: scope BOTH
   assertions to the body of add_document_note_tool itself rather than the
   whole pydantic_ai_agents.py file, so a sibling tool sharing the same
   ternary form can't satisfy the assertion if add_document_note_tool
   regresses.

6. user.id -> user.pk in the UPDATE permission check and error message,
   matching the codebase's consistent .pk usage.

* Drop redundant inline 'import re' after merge resolution

The merge conflict in test_add_document_note_tool_passes_none_when_corpus_absent
left a stale local 'import re' that flake8 flags as F811 (re is already
imported at module scope on line 22).

* Address PR review: prose heuristic, __all__, locked_doc, edge tests

Six follow-ups for the CAML article review tools PR:

- ``_looks_like_prose``: tighten the list-marker rule to require a
  following whitespace (``- ``, ``* ``, ``+ ``, or tab variants).
  CommonMark only treats ``-``/``*``/``+`` as a list marker when a
  whitespace follows; a paragraph starting with ``*Force majeure*…``
  is an emphasis run, not a list, and IS a valid citation candidate.
  Re-orders the marker check so headings/blockquotes/tables stay
  rejected via the first-character set.

- ``__all__``: expand to include ``aread_corpus_caml_article``,
  ``apropose_caml_citation_match``, ``aapply_caml_article_edit``
  alongside the re-exported ``CAML_ARTICLE_TITLE`` so the module's
  public API is discoverable via star-import / IDE introspection.

- ``apropose_caml_citation_match``: add a comment noting that
  ``CoreAnnotationVectorStore`` already builds its queryset with
  ``select_related("annotation_label", "document", "corpus")``, so
  the per-result label/document attribute reads in the fanout loop
  are not N+1 queries.

- ``_apply_caml_article_edit``: rename ``locked_doc`` to ``caml_doc``
  after the ``transaction.atomic()`` block exits. The
  ``select_for_update`` lock is released at commit, so the
  "locked" connotation only fits inside the txn body. The post-commit
  reads (``refresh_from_db``, return-dict construction) now read more
  honestly.

- ``CAML_ARTICLE_TITLE`` constant: expand the cross-language sync
  comment to explain *why* the backend uses ``TITLE`` while the
  frontend uses ``FILENAME`` (backend queries by
  ``Document.title``; frontend treats it as a synthetic file in the
  document list). The two names are intentionally divergent so each
  side reads naturally; the sync requirement is the literal value.

- New tests in ``test_caml_review_tools.py``:
  - ``ParseDirectiveArgsTests`` — pin the directive-arg parser's
    behaviour for blank input, unquoted pairs, double-quoted values
    with spaces (``mode="all phrases"``), and mixed quoting.
  - ``LooksLikeProseTests`` — pure-function coverage for the
    prose heuristic, including the new emphasis-run paragraph case
    that the original heuristic rejected.
  - ``ApplyCamlArticleEditPreviewTests`` — pin the ``preview`` window
    in the apply tool's return dict: it centres around the
    replacement, is bounded by ``2 × _PREVIEW_RADIUS_CHARS +
    len(replacement)``, and clamps cleanly at offset 0 when the
    target is at the start of the document.

* Address PR review: storage cleanup, in-txn permission, *** thematic breaks, constants

- Schedule on_commit cleanup of the previous CAML blob after FieldFile.save
  rotates the storage path. Storage operations are non-transactional, so
  deleting before commit could orphan a rolled-back document; on_commit fires
  only after the DB pointer commits.
- Move the UPDATE permission check inside the select_for_update transaction
  so a permission revocation between the initial load and the locked write
  cannot slip through.
- Add '*' to the thematic-break filter set in _looks_like_prose so '***'
  and '* * *' (CommonMark thematic breaks) are excluded from citation
  candidates. Emphasis runs like '*Force majeure*' still pass because
  they include non-asterisk characters.
- Promote _MAX_CITATION_CANDIDATES and _PREVIEW_RADIUS_CHARS to
  CAML_CITATION_MAX_CANDIDATES and CAML_EDIT_PREVIEW_RADIUS_CHARS in
  opencontractserver/constants/document_processing.py.

Tests:
- New test_old_blob_is_deleted_after_edit pins the cleanup behaviour.
- Extended test_rejects_thematic_breaks_and_setext_underlines with
  '***' / '* * *' cases.

* Fix flaky propose_caml_citation_match tests and lift coverage to 100%

- Wrap CoreAnnotationVectorStore construction in the same try/except that
  guards async_search so a missing PipelineSettings default embedder surfaces
  as the friendly 'Semantic search failed' ValueError instead of leaking the
  raw get_embedder() error.
- Patch __init__ alongside async_search in ProposeCamlCitationMatchTests.
  TransactionTestCase truncates the migration-seeded PipelineSettings row
  between tests; under pytest-xdist --dist loadscope, an unrelated class
  running first on the same worker left us without a default embedder and
  the real constructor raised before the patched async_search could run --
  hence the four failures only seen in CI.
- Add coverage for _safe_delete_storage_path, _read_caml_content's falsy
  file path, the User.DoesNotExist branches in all three tools, the empty
  target_text guard, the constructor-failure wrap, and component-marker /
  numbered-list rejection in _looks_like_prose. caml_article.py is now at
  100% line coverage.

subject: Fix infinite navigation loop on extract routes (#1601)
message:
Fix infinite navigation loop on extract routes (#1601)

* Fix infinite navigation loop on /e/:user/:extractId extract route

ExtractLandingRoute.tsx redirected /e/<creator>/<id> to /extracts/<id> as
soon as openedExtract was populated, but CentralRouteManager Phase 3 then
read buildCanonicalPath() (which returns /e/<creator>/<id> for extracts)
and redirected back. The two redirects fought forever, tripping the
navigation circuit breaker after the URL appeared three times.

Route /e/:userIdent/:extractIdent directly at ExtractDetailRoute (which
its own JSDoc and the routing-guide table at routing_system.md:178-179
already declared as the intended setup) and remove the now-dead
ExtractLandingRoute and its test. /extracts/<id> still works: Phase 3
redirects it once to canonical /e/<creator>/<id> and stops, since the
next render is already on the canonical path.

* Address review: ratchet any-baseline + pin canonical-URL contract

The lint gate flagged that this branch dropped one `any` from the
codebase but the baseline file wasn't ratcheted; running yarn any:write
brings the baseline in sync (knowledge_base: 33 instead of the stale
total).

Also adds a regression test in ExtractDetailRoute.test.tsx that mounts
the canonical /e/:user/:extract URL and confirms ExtractDetailRoute
renders without redirecting. The deleted ExtractLandingRoute used to
redirect /e/* → /extracts/:id, which fought CentralRouteManager Phase
3's reverse direction and tripped the circuit breaker. Pinning this
contract here means a future regression that re-introduces a redirect
inside ExtractDetailRoute would be caught loud and early.

* Drop redundant 'as any' cast — mockExtract is already typed

subject: Refactor DocumentKnowledgeBase: extract sidebar tabs and document viewer (#1580)
message:
Refactor DocumentKnowledgeBase: extract sidebar tabs and document viewer (#1580)

* Decompose DocumentKnowledgeBase.tsx into thinner composer + sibling files

Next slice of #1446. DocumentKnowledgeBase.tsx had grown to 2,654 lines —
listed in the issue as oversized. Four extractions land it at 2,136 lines
(20% reduction) while remaining behaviorally identical (public default
export, props, rendered DOM, and all data-testids unchanged).

- SidebarTabs.tsx (new): DesktopSidebarTabs + MobileSidebarTabs. The same
  tab list was duplicated three times inline (panel-closed desktop,
  panel-open desktop, mobile bar) with subtle onClick differences. The
  components each take a unified click-handler factory that branches on
  panelOpen / activeMode, preserving every behavior — including
  Discussions snapping to "half" on desktop and "full" on mobile, and
  the mobile-only toggle-on-active-tap quirk.
- DocumentViewer.tsx (new): The PDF / TXT / DOCX viewer switch with its
  loading + error scaffolding factored into a single ViewerStatus helper
  shared by all three filetype branches.
- useResizeHandle.ts (new): Drag-to-resize state and mouse listeners for
  the right panel, including snap-to-preset (quarter/half/full) within a
  3% threshold and the document-level mousemove/mouseup binding (only
  attached while a drag is in flight).
- useDocumentMarkdown.ts (new): Markdown summary fetcher with explicit
  cancellation on unmount so an unmounted document can't leave stale
  state behind. Drops the unused markdownError local state.

State doesn't need to be lifted to a Jotai atom for this slice; the
extracted pieces own only props they receive and local UI state.

* Extract loader/queries/structural/header into hooks (DocumentKnowledgeBase)

Second pass on #1446. Combined with the previous SidebarTabs/DocumentViewer/
useResizeHandle/useDocumentMarkdown extractions, DocumentKnowledgeBase.tsx
now sits at 1,057 lines — down from 2,654 (60% reduction). All public API
unchanged: same default export, same props, same rendered DOM, same
data-testids.

New extractions (sibling files in document_kb/):

- useDocumentLoader.ts: Owns every async fetch driving the view —
  GET_DOCUMENT_KNOWLEDGE_AND_ANNOTATIONS, GET_DOCUMENT_WITH_STRUCTURE,
  GET_DOCUMENT_ANNOTATIONS_ONLY, GET_CONVERSATIONS — plus the
  processAnnotationsData / processAnnotationsOnlyData / loadDocxDocument /
  PDF-PAWLs page-builder helpers and the analysis/extract refetch effects.
  Both query paths now share a single loadDocumentBody dispatcher; the
  corpus path threads through the cached-URL helpers, the no-corpus path
  goes direct, but the rest of the PDF/TXT/DOCX branches are identical.
  Returns just what the parent needs: combinedData, viewState, loading,
  queryError, refetch, threadCount.
- useStructuralAnnotations.ts: Lazy-loads the structural-annotation set
  (toggle path) and targeted deep-link fetches. Pure side-effect hook;
  manages atoms internally. Resets atoms on documentId change.
- useContainerWidth.ts: Container width tracking + ResizeObserver +
  scrollContainerRefAtom wiring.
- HeaderBar.tsx: Modal title row + metadata + Add-to-Corpus / back
  buttons. Stateless presentation.
- helpers.ts: Pure relationToGroup factory shared between the loader and
  structural-annotation hooks (was duplicated inline at three call sites).

State doesn't need to be lifted to a Jotai atom for this slice — every
extracted hook either already uses atoms internally or takes the props
the parent already had on hand.

Verified:
- tsc --noEmit clean
- prettier formatted
- Component tests pass: Index/chat/feed/extract/analysis tab visibility,
  PDF/TXT/DOCX viewer rendering, analysis selection opens sidebar with
  Analysis tab, extract selection opens sidebar with Extract tab, context
  bar shows correct stats, document renders with and without corpus,
  Add to Corpus modal.

* Replace any with proper PDF.js types in useDocumentLoader

Type pdfDocProxy as PDFDocumentProxy, page proxies as PDFPageProxy, and
pawlsData as PageTokens[]. Updates frontend/.any-baseline.json to ratchet
the gate down by 1 (455 -> 452).

* Address Claude review on PR #1580

- DocumentViewer: tighten createAnnotationHandler prop type from
  (annotation: any) => Promise<any> to (annotation: ServerTokenAnnotation) =>
  Promise<void>; switch styled import to direct path (./EmptyStates).
- DocumentKnowledgeBase: tighten createAnnotationHandler wrapper signature
  to match the new prop contract.
- HeaderBar: stop flashing today's date when metadata.created is null —
  render an em-dash placeholder instead of new Date(Date.now()).
- useDocumentLoader: collapse double setPdfAnnotations into single calls in
  processAnnotationsData and processAnnotationsOnlyData to avoid the
  intermediate render in Apollo's onCompleted (outside React's automatic
  batching). Drop the public setViewState setter from the hook return —
  internal state should not be poked from outside the hook.
- useContainerWidth: create/dispose ResizeObserver inside the ref callback
  so it correctly reattaches on conditional re-mounts of the container.
- SidebarTabs: differentiate Discussions tab (MessagesSquare) from Chat
  (MessageSquare) on both desktop and mobile.
- CHANGELOG: add Changed entry covering the refactor + tightenings.
- frontend/.any-baseline.json: ratchet baseline 452 -> 449 after the type
  tightenings.

* Add component tests + docs screenshots for new document_kb modules

Covers the three new presentational components extracted in PR #1580:

- HeaderBar (5 tests): metadata-complete render, em-dash placeholder when
  metadata.created is null (no today-flash regression), Add-to-Corpus CTA
  visibility under different (hasCorpus, readOnly) combinations.
- SidebarTabs (7 tests): DesktopSidebarTabs default + extract/analysis tabs,
  click-while-closed opens panel, click-active-while-open closes panel;
  MobileSidebarTabs render under <=768px viewport, threadCount in label,
  inactive-tab switch.
- DocumentViewer (2 tests): smoke render of the unsupported-file empty
  state and the unsupported-filetype loading branch — keeps the test
  matrix free of PDF.js / Tiptap / DOCX wasm setup that the supported
  branches need.

Each test that exercises a stable visual state captures a docScreenshot,
landing eight new images under docs/assets/images/screenshots/auto/.

* Address PR #1580 review and add unit-test coverage for new modules

- Hoist useResizeHandle width/snap literals into constants.ts (rule #4 — no
  magic numbers).
- useDocumentLoader.finalizePdfLoad: use functional setPageTextMaps updater so
  pageTextMaps no longer pins the callback dep array.
- Document why setDocument cast and the pdfjs-dist .getPage() Promise cast
  remain (legacy atom shape + PDFPromise vs Promise typing).
- Drop unused (prev) param in processAnnotationsData (only the
  processAnnotationsOnlyData callback genuinely reads prev.docTypes).
- Add Vitest coverage for the four newly extracted modules: helpers.relationToGroup,
  useResizeHandle, useDocumentMarkdown, useStructuralAnnotations.

* Use AnnotationLabelType instead of 'as any' in helpers test (any-baseline)

* Fix post-merge TS error in useTabVisibilityRefresh.test.ts

Same renderHook initialProps fix already applied on PR 1586 / 1585: wrap
inline-array test props in initialProps to match the test-utils
renderHook signature.

* Fix selection action menu silently dropped when mouseup lands on overlapping fixed UI

SelectionLayer's mouseup handler was attached only to the React element
via onMouseUp. When a drag released over a fixed-position sibling (the
right-edge SidebarTab buttons whose z-index sits above the selection
layer's z=1), the synthetic event fired on the sibling instead and the
selection silently dropped — localPageSelection set but no
setShowActionMenu(true), no pendingSelections flush.

This was masked on main because the buggy initial container-width
measurement (captured during the modal open animation) produced a
narrower PDF, keeping the test's calculated drag coordinates inside the
PDF. The useContainerWidth extraction in this PR correctly reports the
settled post-animation container width, so the PDF renders wider and
the test's drag end now lands exactly on a SidebarTab — making the
real production UX bug visible.

Fix: extract finalizeSelection(clientX, clientY, shiftKey) and attach
document-level mouseup + mousemove listeners while localPageSelection
is non-null. Listeners detach as soon as the selection finalises or
the component unmounts. Both the React onMouseUp and the document
fallback call the same helper so single-page release behaviour is
preserved exactly.

* Migrate 3 new hook tests off @testing-library/react-hooks

PR 1580 added unit tests for useDocumentMarkdown, useResizeHandle, and
useStructuralAnnotations that imported renderHook from
@testing-library/react-hooks. Main subsequently removed that package
(closes #1576) in favour of the React-18-native helper at
src/test-utils/renderHook.tsx, but these new test files predated that
migration and never got swept along.

After the merge, CI's Build step failed with
"Cannot find module '@testing-library/react-hooks'" which also
cascaded as the Unit Tests job failure (the same module resolution
error). Switching the imports to the project helper restores both jobs.

useStructuralAnnotations.test.tsx also lost a result.error assertion in
the migration: the new helper returns { current } only — if the hook
throws, renderHook itself throws synchronously, so reaching the
post-call assertions already proves no error. The assertion was
collapsed accordingly.

* Add unit tests pinning SelectionLayer's document mouseup fallback contract

Three vitest cases exercise the new document-level mouseup/mousemove
listener lifecycle the previous commit added: idle layer never arms the
global handlers, mousedown attaches them, and a release on the document
(simulating a mouseup over a fixed-positioned overlay) detaches them.
These pin the no-leak contract that's invisible to the existing CT
permission tests but is the actual mechanism behind the mobile
selection-menu fix.

Also bumps unit coverage for SelectionLayer.tsx so the patch's measured
coverage isn't dragged down by uncovered branches in the new helper.

* Type-check the new SelectionLayer test instead of 'as any'

The baseline script (scripts/check-any-baseline.js) gates the global
'any' count and the previous commit added 3 new uses (labelType, icon,
useCorpusState mock cast). Replace each with a real type:

- LabelType.SpanLabel for the labelType enum (was 'SPAN_LABEL' as any)
- Bare string for icon (the AnnotationLabelType.icon field accepts
  string in the schema)
- vi.mocked(useCorpusState) + a 'as unknown as CorpusStateShape' on the
  return value so the partial mock doesn't need 'any' (unknown is not
  matched by the baseline regex)

any-baseline now reports 449 / 449, all 3 unit tests still pass.

* Address review: hooks-order, double-finalize, tighten props

- Move documentId validity check before any hook call by extracting an
  InvalidDocumentIdModal sibling component, fixing a pre-existing
  Rules-of-Hooks violation that made it unsafe for documentId to
  transition between empty and non-empty.
- SelectionLayer: add finalizingRef reentrant guard so a release on the
  SelectionLayer element doesn't double-finalize when both React's
  onMouseUp and the document mouseup listener fire in the same cycle.
- DocumentKnowledgeBase: read tracked viewport `width` (already in deps)
  inside floatingControlsState memo instead of window.innerWidth so
  resizes actually re-memoize.
- DocumentKnowledgeBase: replace hardcoded 25/50/90 in
  getPanelWidthPercentage with PANEL_WIDTH_QUARTER/HALF/FULL_PCT
  constants already imported by useResizeHandle.
- HeaderBar: tighten onClose to () => void to match call site, render
  empty string instead of literal "undefined" when creator email is
  null.
- useDocumentMarkdown: clear markdownError on the no-summary early return
  so a stale failure from a previous document doesn't leak across.
- useDocumentLoader: comment the eslint-disable-next-line directives so
  future maintainers understand why Apollo lazy-query refs are excluded
  from the dep arrays.
- SidebarTabs: comment the intentionally-ignored showRightPanel prop on
  DesktopSidebarTabs (kept in CommonProps so call sites can spread the
  same prop bag to both variants).

* Address review feedback on PR #1580

- SelectionLayer: pull side effects out of the setMultiSelections updater
  in finalizeSelection so React Strict Mode's double-invoke can no longer
  trip the new finalizingRef toggle (Medium). Compute pendingSelections
  via its own functional updater rather than reusing the
  multiSelections.updater closure.
- DocumentViewer: text branch now uses id="text-container" instead of
  inheriting the misleading "pdf-container" id (Medium). Aligns with the
  pre-existing text-container test selector in
  DocumentKnowledgeBaseCorpusless.ct.tsx and removes a silent-collision
  trap if anything downstream reaches for #pdf-container by id.
- constants.ts: hoist MENU_INTERACTION_COOLDOWN out of SelectionLayer.tsx
  as SELECTION_MENU_COOLDOWN_MS, and add a comment on PANEL_WIDTH_FULL_PCT
  noting the deliberate 90 % stop. Removes the magic numbers per
  CLAUDE.md and addresses the "FULL = 90?" readability flag.
- SidebarTabs: tighten DesktopSidebarTabsProps to
  Omit<CommonProps, "showRightPanel"> so a caller mis-passing the prop
  surfaces as a TS error. Drops the unused destructure + the obsolete
  comment explaining the disuse. Updates the two DesktopSidebarTabs call
  sites in DocumentKnowledgeBase.tsx and the SidebarTabsTestWrapper.
- useDocumentLoader: new __tests__/useDocumentLoader.test.tsx adds six
  smoke tests covering the auth-gated skip path, the document-only TXT
  happy path (LOADING -> LOADED), the null-document ERROR path, the
  threadCount plumbing, the corpus-context skip, and the
  annotations-only refetch skip when no corpusId is bound.

* Address review feedback on PR #1580

- useStructuralAnnotations: stop using ``onCompleted`` with
  ``fetchPolicy: "cache-and-network"``. Apollo fires onCompleted twice
  in that mode (cache hit + network response), and the all-structural
  path's "replace" semantics could overwrite optimistic merges from
  the targeted-fetch path on the second fire. Read ``data`` from a
  ``useEffect`` instead — idempotent across cache and network fires.
- DocumentViewer (knowledge_base): import ``PDFContainer`` as
  ``ViewerContainer`` so the per-filetype branches (PDF / TXT / DOCX)
  don't read as "wrap text or DOCX in a PDF container". The styling
  contract is shared across renderers — renaming the source export is
  out of scope.
- DocumentKnowledgeBase.ct.tsx: the TXT-with-chat-panel test was looking
  for ``#pdf-container`` after PR #1580 split the viewer into per-filetype
  ids. Use ``#text-container`` for TXT documents.

* Fix unit-test waitFor + add PDF/TXT body-load cancellation

- useStructuralAnnotations.test.tsx: switch ``waitFor`` from
  ``@testing-library/react`` to the project's ``act``-wrapping variant
  in ``test-utils/renderHook``. Under
  ``IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT=true`` (set in setupTests.ts) the library's
  own ``waitFor`` does NOT flush React-18 updates from useEffect chains,
  so atom writes triggered by the lazy-query apply effect never reached
  the rendered probe and all 3 data-asserting tests timed out at the
  default 1s budget. With the act-wrapping variant the predicate sees
  post-resolve atom state and the suite passes in <300ms total.

- useDocumentLoader.ts: extend the cancellation guard from DOCX to
  the PDF and TXT body-load branches. Renamed ``docxLoadCancelRef`` →
  ``bodyLoadCancelRef`` and added a ``DocumentLoadCancelled`` sentinel
  so the PDF promise chain can short-circuit cleanly. Without these
  guards a doc switch (or unmount) mid-load would let the in-flight
  ``setViewState`` / ``setPages`` / ``setDocText`` calls land in the
  *next* document's atoms, or fire a stray error toast against an
  unmounted tree. Caught in the latest Claude review on the PR.

- useDocumentLoader.ts: corrected the misleading "Apollo's
  ``useLazyQuery`` returns a new function identity" comment on the
  analysis/extract refetch effects — those use ``useQuery``'s
  ``refetch`` (which IS identity-stable). The real reason to omit
  ``processAnnotationsOnlyData`` is its ``setPdfAnnotations`` dep
  rebuilding the callback each render.

- useDocumentLoader.test.tsx: pin the new TXT-cancellation contract
  with a test that holds the body fetch open past unmount and asserts
  ``viewState`` never advances and no error toast fires.

---------

subject: security: enforce slug-only user privacy across the GraphQL surface (#1600)
message:
security: enforce slug-only user privacy across the GraphQL surface (#1600)

* security: enforce slug-only user privacy across the GraphQL surface

No user can see another user's email, name, first/last name, OAuth
sub, or other PII through the public API. ``UserType`` resolvers gate
every PII field to self-only reads (no superuser exception); the
``displayName`` resolver returns the case-sensitive ``slug`` for
non-self viewers, with a stable ``user_<pk>`` redaction when slug is
unset. ``Meta.exclude`` adds a defensive layer hiding password, IP,
login timestamps, and Auth0 sub from every viewer.

Backend follow-through:
  - ``User.__str__`` no longer concatenates email into log/admin output
  - ``AnnotatePermissionsForReadMixin.resolve_object_shared_with``
    emits only ``id``/``slug``/permissions per collaborator (was
    leaking email + username on every shared corpus/document/labelset)
  - OG metadata, worker queries, and the agent toolchain link
    generator switched from ``creator.username`` to ``creator.slug`` so
    social-media previews and worker dropdowns never surface the raw
    OAuth sub
  - REST ``UserSerializer`` reduced to ``slug + url`` with slug-based
    detail-view lookup

Frontend follow-through:
  - Both leaderboards (``Leaderboard.tsx``, ``CompactLeaderboard.tsx``)
    render ``user.slug`` directly — never ``displayName`` — so a
    logged-in user looking at their own row sees the same public
    handle everyone else does
  - ~30 component sites that compared ``currentUser.email ===
    creator.email`` for ownership migrate to ``isOwnedBy(creator,
    currentUser)`` (id-based, robust to null email returns); display
    sites switch to ``getCreatorDisplay(creator)`` (slug + ``user_<id>``
    fallback). New helpers in ``frontend/src/utils/userDisplay.ts``
  - GraphQL fragments augmented with ``slug`` on every ``creator { ...
    }`` / ``author { ... }`` selection that already had ``id``

Tests:
  - 12 new privacy specs in ``test_user_privacy.py`` (cross-user
    redaction, superuser redaction, anonymous redaction, redacted-
    handle fallback, ``__str__`` privacy, ``object_shared_with``
    slug-only payload)
  - ``test_user_display_name.py`` updated: ``EmailResolverTestCase``
    now asserts superusers do NOT see other users' email through
    GraphQL; new ``CrossUserDisplayNameTestCase`` pins slug-only
    contract for cross-user displayName
  - OG metadata tests read ``self.user.slug`` instead of literal
    usernames (slug sanitizer normalises ``_`` to ``-``)
  - Frontend: 20 new ``userDisplay`` specs; ``ModernAnnotationCard``
    test mocks updated to use ``id`` not ``email``; Leaderboard CT
    asserts on hyphenated slug values

Out of scope (tracked separately): V2 corpus export still writes
``author_email``/``creator_email`` into export ZIPs — deliberate
data-export feature, but does cross the same privacy boundary for
collaborator emails on a shared corpus. Switching to slug-based
author resolution would be a breaking change to the export format.

* Update component-test mocks for slug-based ownership/identity

The slug-only privacy gate makes:
- creator.email return null cross-user (so display falls back to slug)
- ownership comparisons key on creator.id, not creator.email

This breaks 3 component tests where mocks predate the change:

- admin-components.ct.tsx: GET_CORPUS_AGENTS / GET_GLOBAL_AGENTS mock
  queries selected creator { id, username } but the production query
  selects creator { id, slug, username }. Apollo MockedProvider matches
  on the request shape — adding `slug` makes the mocks resolve again so
  Legal Analyst & friends actually render.
- CorpusHome.ct.tsx: dummyCorpus.creator now carries an explicit slug
  ("tester") so getCreatorDisplay surfaces "tester" in the metadata
  bar instead of the redacted user_<id> fallback.
- CorpusListView.ct.tsx + wrapper: mock creators get distinct ids
  derived from the email local-part, and the wrapper now seeds both
  userObj AND backendUserObj with that id (CorpusListView reads
  currentUserId from backendUserObj). Without this seed every card
  read as not-mine, so the Private status badge never appeared.

* Fix admin-components CT mock: align GET_GLOBAL_AGENTS creator selection with source

The test's local GET_GLOBAL_AGENTS mock requested
``creator { id, slug, username }`` but the production query in
``src/components/admin/global_agent_management.graphql.ts`` selects only
``creator { id, username }`` — no slug. Apollo's ``MockedProvider``
matches mocks by the ``print()``ed query body, so this shape mismatch
caused all five GlobalAgentManagement Component tests to fail with
``locator('text=Research Assistant') not found`` (the mock never matched
so the agents query never resolved). Drops the speculative ``slug``
field from the test's local query so the mock matches what the
component actually fires; adds a comment warning future contributors
not to widen the selection set "for safety". GET_CORPUS_AGENTS already
matches its source — left untouched.

* Address review feedback on PR #1600

- _is_self_view: add explicit ``is_active`` check. Django's
  ``AbstractBaseUser.is_authenticated`` is statically ``True`` for any
  User instance regardless of activation status, and AuthenticationMiddleware
  doesn't strip sessions when an admin flips ``is_active=False``. Without
  the new check a deactivated user with a still-live session cookie would
  continue to read their own PII through the GraphQL surface.
- resolve_can_import_corpus: hoist ``from django.conf import settings``
  out of the resolver body to module scope. Deferred imports are
  conventionally reserved for circular-import workarounds; ``django.conf``
  is always available at startup.
- userDisplay.ts: align frontend no-slug fallback with backend
  ``_redacted_handle``. Previously emitted ``user_<full Relay global ID>``
  (e.g. ``user_VXNlclR5cGU6MQ``) while the backend emitted
  ``user_<last 6 chars of pk>`` (e.g. ``user_1``) — two different strings
  for the same user. Frontend now decodes the Relay ID
  (``base64("TypeName:pk")``) and takes the same suffix length as the
  backend constant ``OAUTH_SUB_DISPLAY_SUFFIX_LENGTH=6``. Exports
  ``decodeRelayPk`` so other surfaces can reuse the helper.
- UserSerializer: add a docstring note that ``lookup_field`` only
  controls hyperlinked URL generation; if/when this serializer is wired
  up in production routes, the corresponding viewset must also set
  ``lookup_field = "slug"`` or generated URLs will silently 404.
- Test coverage: 4 new ``test_user_privacy.py`` cases pin the
  ``canImportCorpus`` self-only gate (cross-user → null, anonymous →
  null, self-view → boolean) plus the ``is_active=False`` gate on
  ``_is_self_view``. 7 new ``userDisplay.test.ts`` cases cover the
  Relay-ID decode + pk-suffix fallback alignment with the backend.
- CHANGELOG: flag the ``objectSharedWith`` payload reduction as a
  breaking change for external consumers (``GenericScalar`` means
  schema enforcement won't catch the ``email``/``username`` removal at
  build time — runtime breakage instead).

* Address review feedback on PR #1600 (round 2)

- og_metadata_queries.py: null-coalesce creator.slug to _redacted_handle
  fallback for all five OG resolvers so pre-migration users without slugs
  don't render the literal string "None" in social previews.
- queries.ts/mutations.ts: drop dead email/username selections from
  cross-user creator/author fragments (GET_CORPUS_WITH_HISTORY,
  GET_ANNOTATIONS_FOR_CARDS, CREATE_THREAD_MESSAGE, REPLY_TO_MESSAGE) -
  these fields always return null for non-self viewers post-redaction.
- Leaderboard.tsx and CompactLeaderboard.tsx: replace ad-hoc
  user_<id> fallback with getCreatorDisplay() so the redacted handle
  matches the backend _redacted_handle shape (decoded pk suffix, not
  the raw Relay global ID).
- UserProfile.tsx: collapse duplicated slug-fallback branch in
  getInitials onto getCreatorInitials; keep the rich self-view chain
  on top so personal-settings UIs still render firstName/lastName/etc.
- ExtractListCard.tsx and Extracts.tsx: drop the unused currentUserId
  prop and its source variable - it was wired but immediately discarded.
- ReplyForm.ct.tsx: update mock creator shape to match the slimmer
  fragment (slug only).

* Add component test + screenshot for ExtractListCard

Smoke-tests the presentational ExtractListCard rendering (name, derived
status, document/column/corpus stats line, click-through). Also lays
down a reference doc screenshot under
extracts--list-card--default.png so README/quickstart docs have a
canonical preview of the card.

* Fix CI for slug-only privacy: tests + coverage + small review fixes

Aligns the existing test suite and coverage gates with the slug-only
privacy contract introduced in this PR, and addresses two small
items from the latest Claude review.

Backend test fixes (cross-user views must read slug, not username):
- test_user_handle.py: DisplayNameResolverTests was calling the
  resolver with info=None, which the new _is_self_view gate
  short-circuits to the slug branch — added a _SelfInfo helper that
  passes the user-as-requester so the resolution chain is exercised.
- test_engagement_metrics_graphql.py / test_badges.py: switched
  cross-user assertions from username to slug (PII is now self-only).

Frontend test/query fixes:
- documentSummaryQueries.ts: dropped self-only username/email from
  the GraphQL selection and SummaryAuthor type; SummaryPreviewCard
  uses getCreatorDisplay which prefers slug.
- folders.ts: same — DeletedDocumentPathType now exposes slug.
- SummaryVersionStack.ct.tsx / TrashFolderViewTestWrapper.tsx:
  mocks updated to provide slug instead of username.
- TrashFolderView.ct.tsx: assertions match getCreatorDisplay output
  (john-doe / jane-smith / "Deleted by Unknown").

Coverage (test_llm_tools.py):
- Added 4 sync + 4 async slug-missing-validation tests for
  create_markdown_link / acreate_markdown_link, exercising the
  validation lines that were renamed in the patch (creator.username
  → creator.slug). Lifts links.py coverage from 0% to 91%.

Review remediation:
- _redacted_handle now treats pk=None explicitly instead of relying
  on `or ""`, so a falsy pk=0 no longer aliases every zero-pk user
  to "user_unknown" (defensive — autoincrement PKs never hit 0).
- CHANGELOG: documents the canImportCorpus Boolean! → Boolean
  schema-type break for hand-written client queries.

* Address review round 3: regression fixes for slug-only privacy

Functional regressions flagged in PR review (must-fix):

- ``SEARCH_USERS_FOR_MENTION`` selected ``username``/``email`` which now
  return null cross-user, so every entry in the @-mention autocomplete
  rendered as "null" as the user's name. Drop both fields, keep only
  ``slug``, and route the dropdown title through ``getCreatorDisplay``
  (slug or redacted ``user_<pk-suffix>`` fallback). The mention link's
  visible label now uses ``resource.title`` (already populated with the
  same display string) instead of the now-redacted ``username``.
- Add ``resolve_is_usage_capped`` in user_types.py with the same
  self-only gate as ``resolve_can_import_corpus``. The model field
  was being served raw cross-user, contradicting the docstring's claim
  that account-tier signals are gated. Field is also explicitly
  declared as a nullable graphene Boolean so the gated-None response
  doesn't trip schema validation. New cross-user / anonymous /
  self-view tests pin the contract.
- Switch ``GET_MODERATION_ACTIONS`` to select ``moderator { id slug }``
  and render via ``getCreatorDisplay`` in ``ModerationDashboard.tsx``.
  Without this the moderator column was blank for every action.
- Switch ``GET_DOCUMENT_VERSION_HISTORY`` to select
  ``createdBy { id slug }`` and render via ``getCreatorDisplay`` in
  ``VersionHistoryPanel.tsx``. Without this the author column was
  blank for every version row.

Smaller fixes from the same review:

- Move the file-local ``REDACTED_HANDLE_PK_SUFFIX_LENGTH`` constant
  out of ``userDisplay.ts`` and into
  ``frontend/src/assets/configurations/constants.ts`` per CLAUDE.md
  conventions for shared frontend constants.
- Split the conflated "no creator OR no creator slug" error in
  ``links.py`` into two distinct messages via a new
  ``_require_creator_slug`` helper. The previous wording said "has
  no creator" even when the creator FK was intact and only the slug
  column was missing — misleading for log triage. Tests updated to
  match the new message for the slug-stripped fixture.

Skipped (per reviewer triage and to keep diff focused):
- Dead ``email``/``username`` selections in unrelated queries
  (cleanup, not a regression).
- Widening hand-written TS interfaces for nullable email/username
  (cleanup, not a regression).
- Switching badge components to slug fallback (existing fallback
  handles the case; not a new regression).
- All 🔵 follow-up items (WebSocket actor leak, is_superuser/is_staff
  gating, export_v2 leakage, OAUTH constant rename) — explicitly
  flagged by reviewer as out of scope for this PR.

* Fix CT regression and address review for PR #1600

Frontend component test fixes (no behavior change in shipped code):
- ModerationDashboard.ct / coverage and VersionHistoryPanel mocks were
  still feeding `username` into resolver-side mocks even though the
  queries select `slug` now. With slug undefined, `getCreatorDisplay`
  correctly fell back to `user_<id>` and the username assertions
  flunked. Switched mocks + assertions to slug values (the privacy
  contract this PR pins).

Review remediations:
- Rename `_redacted_handle` → `redacted_handle` (drop the underscore
  since `og_metadata_queries.py` already imports it cross-module).
- Back-reference the frontend twin in
  `opencontractserver/constants/auth.py` so a backend-only edit fails
  more loudly via grep.
- Reorder import vs `interface` declaration in `userDisplay.ts`.
- Add a dedicated `### Breaking Changes` section to the CHANGELOG
  calling out `canImportCorpus` nullability and the
  `objectSharedWith` shape change separately from the Security bullet
  so API consumers scanning the changelog can find them immediately.
- `User.__str__`: fall back to `user_<pk>` when both `slug` and
  `username` are empty so admin/log surfaces never collapse to "".

* Apply prettier formatting to HeaderBar.tsx after merge

* Mark canImportCorpus / isUsageCapped types as nullable

Address PR #1600 review item 5: under the slug-only privacy policy
both fields return null for cross-user / anonymous viewers, but
the hand-written TypeScript declaration still typed them as
non-nullable. Switching to Maybe<Boolean> makes the privacy
contract visible to consumers and lets the compiler flag any
unstructured access. Existing call sites in Corpuses.tsx already
use optional chaining + Boolean(...) coercion, so no runtime change.

* Refresh HeaderBar screenshots for slug-only privacy

The fixture creator switched from { email } to { id, slug } so the
rendered metadata row now shows the slug ('alice'/'bob') rather than
the email address. Regenerated via Playwright CT to keep the docs
auto-screenshots aligned with the visible state.

subject: Allow anonymous viewers to fetch images for public structural annotations (#1604)
message:
Allow anonymous viewers to fetch images for public structural annotations (#1604)

* Allow anonymous viewers to fetch images for public structural annotations

`/api/annotations/<id>/images/` was hardcoded to `IsAuthenticated`, so the
frontend hook (`useAnnotationImages`) received 401/403 for anonymous viewers
and silently rendered "No thumbnail" — even when the annotation itself was
returned by the GraphQL feed under the public/anonymous read rules in the
consolidated permissioning guide.

Image visibility now mirrors AnnotationQuerySet.visible_to_user:
  * View switches to AllowAny; throttling preserved by adding
    AnnotationImagesAnonThrottle alongside AnnotationImagesThrottle (both
    share the `annotation_images` scope at 200/hour, keyed per-IP for anon
    and per-user for authenticated).
  * get_annotation_images_with_permission gains an explicit anonymous gate:
    if user.is_anonymous and not annotation.structural -> []. Closes the
    gap where the helper would otherwise allow images for non-structural
    public annotations that anon users cannot see via the queryset
    (queryset filters anon visibility to structural-only).
  * IDOR protection unchanged — same empty 200 response for missing or
    unauthorized.

Tests:
  * Renamed test_fetch_images_unauthenticated -> _private and updated from
    "expect 401/403" to "expect 200 with empty array" (IDOR-consistent).
  * Added regression coverage for all three new anonymous paths:
    public structural (allowed), public non-structural (denied), public doc
    + private corpus (denied).

Docs:
  * docs/permissioning/consolidated_permissioning_guide.md: added a short
    "Annotation Images" subsection documenting the visibility table.
  * CHANGELOG.md: entry under [Unreleased] / Fixed.

* Address review: fix throttle double-count + cover corpus=None

The two throttle classes shared scope="annotation_images", which meant
anonymous requests resolved to the same cache key from both
UserRateThrottle (IP fallback) and AnonRateThrottle. Each anon request
therefore consumed two slots from the 200/hour budget, halving the
effective rate. Splits the anon throttle into its own
"annotation_images_anon" scope (with a matching 200/hour entry in
DEFAULT_THROTTLE_RATES) so authenticated and anonymous callers each
have their own bucket.

Also adds test_fetch_images_anonymous_corpus_none_structural to
exercise the AnnotationQuerySet.visible_to_user branch
``Q(corpus__isnull=True) | Q(corpus__is_public=True)`` — the new
permission helper accepts a structural annotation on a public document
even when corpus is NULL, but the existing tests only covered the
public-corpus path.

* Address review: self-contained anon path, throttle gating, DRY tests

- Make the anonymous gate in get_annotation_images_with_permission
  fully self-contained: it now checks document.is_public and
  corpus.is_public (or null) directly instead of relying on
  user_has_permission_for_obj's behavior for AnonymousUser. Removes an
  implicit contract on downstream guardian behavior.
- Gate AnnotationImagesThrottle to authenticated callers only and
  AnnotationImagesAnonThrottle to anonymous callers only via
  allow_request overrides. Anonymous requests no longer consume two
  cache slots in lockstep across the two scopes.
- Extract _create_public_annotated_document helper in
  test_annotation_images_api.py to remove ~100 lines of duplicated
  fixture setup across the four anonymous tests.
- Add test_fetch_images_anonymous_private_document_blocked covering
  the structural + private-doc + public-corpus path that pins the
  document.is_public half of the visibility rule.
- Trim the CHANGELOG entry to one paragraph in line with surrounding
  entries; the long-form rationale lives in the PR description.

* Address review round 4: align structural_set anon path + docs/log polish

- Anon gate in ``get_annotation_images_with_permission`` now mirrors
  ``AnnotationQuerySet.visible_to_user``'s ``structural_set`` branch:
  when the annotation row's own ``document`` FK is null but at least
  one ``Document`` using its ``structural_set`` is public, anon
  callers get the images. Previously the gate returned ``[]`` for any
  ``document=None`` row, which silently diverged from what the GraphQL
  feed admits. Two new tests pin the behaviour:
  - ``test_fetch_images_anonymous_structural_set_with_public_doc`` —
    public doc on the set ⇒ images served.
  - ``test_fetch_images_anonymous_structural_set_no_public_doc_blocked``
    — no public doc on the set ⇒ empty 200 (IDOR shape preserved).
- Doc table: parenthesise the anon visibility rule and call out the
  ``structural_set`` branch explicitly so the rule reads as a single
  conjunction rather than ambiguously parsing the trailing ``OR``
  across the whole expression.
- Switch the new ``logger.debug(f"...")`` calls to lazy
  ``logger.debug("...", arg)`` form so the format-string doesn't
  evaluate when debug logging is disabled, matching the pre-existing
  style in the same module.

* Delegate annotation image visibility to AnnotationQuerySet.visible_to_user

The image endpoint had forked ~150 lines of permission logic from the
canonical AnnotationQuerySet.visible_to_user, creating a drift hazard
and a real divergence already flagged in PR review (the structural_set
anonymous branch). Per the consolidated permissioning guide, image
visibility must be IDENTICAL to annotation visibility.

get_annotation_images_with_permission now delegates directly to the
queryset: a single .visible_to_user(user).filter(pk=...).exists()
check. Image visibility is now provably identical to GraphQL
annotation visibility, by construction. Throttle split, IDOR
protection (empty-200 for missing/unauthorized), and AllowAny on the
view all preserved.

Tests:
- test_annotation_images_api.py: six duplicative anonymous test
  cases collapsed into two subTest matrices using a new
  _create_structural_set_annotation helper. StructuralAnnotationSet
  lifted to module-top imports.
- test_image_tools.py: three mock-based tests that patched the
  removed inline select_related / user_has_permission_for_obj calls
  replaced with real-DB privacy tests (Analysis/Extract fixtures);
  the orphan-annotation mock test was deleted because a DB
  constraint makes the scenario unreachable.

Net: -389 lines.

subject: Replace mobile nav drawer with floating sheet overlay (#1606)
message:
Replace mobile nav drawer with floating sheet overlay (#1606)

* Redesign mobile nav as a floating sheet overlay

The previous mobile menu used the @os-legal/ui NavBar's built-in inline
drawer, which expanded as a full-width opaque dark panel that pushed page
content down and clashed with the os-legal "transparent infrastructure"
aesthetic.

Below 1100px, NavMenu now renders a new MobileNavMenu: a compact dark
sticky header plus a floating, rounded white sheet portalled to the body
that overlays content (backdrop-blur dim, soft layered shadow,
framer-motion spring) instead of displacing it. Active items use the
design-system teal with a 3px left bar, matching hover/selection language
used elsewhere. Auth footer shows a teal "Sign in" CTA when signed out or
a user chip + Profile/Logout actions when authenticated.

Closes on backdrop tap, ESC, route change, item selection, and viewport
crossing back to desktop. Locks body scroll while open. Exposes
aria-modal, aria-label, aria-expanded for a11y.

Desktop (>= 1100px) is unchanged.

The two responsive tests in NavMenu.ct.tsx are repointed at the new
component via aria-label selectors (more stable than the library's
internal CSS classes anyway).

* Address review on PR #1606: focus management, DRY handlers, helper extraction

Must-fix:

- Wire up focus management for the dialog. Move focus to the first
  focusable element inside the sheet on open (falls back to the sheet
  container, which now has ``tabIndex={-1}`` so programmatic focus
  works); return focus to the toggle button on close. Tracked via a
  new ``toggleRef`` and the existing ``sheetRef`` (which was dead
  before). Required by WCAG 2.1 SC 2.4.3 — without this, keyboard-only
  users cannot navigate the sheet at all.

Should-fix:

- Extract ``initialsFor`` to ``frontend/src/utils/initials.ts`` so
  multiple surfaces (mobile nav user chip, desktop avatar, future
  badges) render identical initials for the same name. Pure helper,
  no component dependencies, covered by 8 unit cases pinning the
  one-word / two-word / >2-word / empty / whitespace / unicode paths.
- Hoist the repeated ``rgba(15, 23, 42, ...)`` literal into a
  ``DARK_BASE_RGB`` module constant so the three sites stay in
  lockstep and a future palette move only needs one edit.
- Collapse the identical ``handleItemClick`` / ``handleUserAction``
  helpers into a single ``runAndClose(onClick)`` callback.

Minor:

- Add ``aria-haspopup="dialog"`` to the toggle button so screen
  readers announce what kind of UI is opening.
- Comment the ``search`` dependency in the route-change effect so
  future readers don't wonder why filter / query-param updates also
  dismiss the sheet (mobile flows treat them as full navigations).
- New CT cases pinning ESC closes the sheet and the user chip
  renders for an authenticated viewer (regressions the old tests
  would not have caught).

* Address PR #1606 review feedback for MobileNavMenu

- Move body scroll restoration into AnimatePresence#onExitComplete so
  the page can't scroll while the sheet is still mid-exit-animation;
  saved overflow value held in a ref.
- Add Tab/Shift+Tab focus trap to the existing keydown handler so
  keyboard users can't escape the modal sheet (ARIA APG dialog).
- Centralize four rgba(255,255,255,...) sites behind a
  SURFACE_OVERLAY_RGB constant + surfaceAlpha() helper, mirroring the
  DARK_BASE_RGB pattern already used for the shadow stops.
- Make MobileUserAction.icon optional and guard <NavItemIcon> rendering
  so callers passing an undefined icon don't render an empty span.
- Wrap runAndClose's onClick in try/finally so a throwing handler still
  dismisses the sheet (no dead UI).
- Add CT tests for the backdrop-tap dismissal and signed-out
  sign-in-CTA branch — the two test gaps the reviewer flagged.

* Address MobileNavMenu review feedback and expand CT coverage

Review fixes:
- handleLogin wrapped in useCallback for consistency with runAndClose
- logoNode, mobileNavItems, mobileUserActions memoized in NavMenu
- "Browse" / "Account" section labels moved to constants
- Sheet's empty-focusables programmatic focus suppressed via
  focus-visible outline:none (no jarring UA outline)
- Unmount-guard restores body overflow if AnimatePresence#onExitComplete
  never fires (hard navigation while sheet is open)
- Comments trimmed to short-line convention; rationale comments retained

New CT tests in NavMenu.ct.tsx covering the previously uncovered
behaviour in MobileNavMenu:
- Tab focus trap (forward wrap, reverse wrap, pull focus back in)
- runAndClose for both nav items and user actions
- Sign-in CTA triggers handleLogin
- Account section + authenticated user actions render
- Toggle + sheet ARIA attribute assertions

Adds docScreenshots: nav--mobile-nav--closed,
nav--mobile-nav--open, nav--mobile-nav--authenticated-open.

* Update CHANGELOG with MobileNavMenu review-follow-up details
