subject: Fix Extracts & Annotations views: pagination, N+1s, refetch storms (#1602)
message:
Fix Extracts & Annotations views: pagination, N+1s, refetch storms (#1602)

* Audit Extracts/Annotations views: slim list query, fix pagination, kill refetch storms

Audit follow-up to the Documents view perf work (PRs #1553/#1554/#1556/#1566).
Three cooperating issues across the Extracts (`/extracts`) and Annotations
(`/annotations`) views, plus a chatty backend resolver hotpath.

Frontend - Extracts.tsx
- Broken pagination. The shared GET_EXTRACTS query declared no $cursor /
  $limit parameters and did not pass `first` / `after` to the connection,
  so the server quietly clamped every request to max_limit=15 and the
  cursor variable was sent over the wire but never honoured. Infinite
  scroll never advanced beyond the first 15 rows. New slim
  GET_EXTRACTS_FOR_LIST wires both args.
- Per-row N+1 in `resolve_full_document_list`. The list query selected
  `fullDocumentList { id }` purely to read `.length` on the frontend,
  which on the backend iterates `self.documents.all()` and calls
  `user_has_permission_for_obj` per document on every extract. Same goes
  for `fieldset.fullColumnList { id }`. ExtractType now exposes
  `documentCount` (and FieldsetType `columnCount`) that read from the
  prefetch_related cache populated by ExtractQueryOptimizer - no extra
  COUNT queries per row, no per-doc permission fan-out. ExtractListCard
  prefers the new fields and falls back to the legacy lengths so
  consumers still on GET_EXTRACTS (ExtractItem, CorpusExtractCards,
  CamlArticleEditor, CreateExtractModal) keep working unchanged.
- useEffect(refetch on currentUser) storm. Removed; useQuery already
  refetches when its variables change and AuthGate clears the cache on
  login/logout. Variables are now useMemo'd. Explicit
  EXTRACTS_PAGE_SIZE = 20 keeps first paint focused; fetchMore passes
  both limit and cursor.

Frontend - Annotations.tsx
- annotation_variables was a fresh let-bound object literal each render,
  forcing Apollo to deep-compare the variables on every parent re-render.
  Now useMemo'd on the underlying primitives.
- Two useEffect blocks called refetch_annotations() / refetch_corpus() on
  filter / opened-corpus changes, doubling every refetch on top of
  Apollo's implicit one. Removed; both filter sets are already part of
  query variables. The auth_token refetch is also redundant because
  AuthGate.resetOnAuthChange already clears the cache on login/logout.
  Dropped the unused refetch_annotations / refetch_corpus destructures
  and the auth_token / authToken imports.

Backend - resolve_annotations
- Stripped seven `.count()` calls embedded in logger.info f-strings -
  every annotations request issued ~5 extra `SELECT COUNT(*)` queries
  regardless of log level (f-string interpolation is unconditional).
- Removed the chatty filter-application info logs that did not embed
  counts but added noise to every request.
- Retained the `structural_set__documents` prefetch because
  AnnotationType.resolve_document walks it for structural annotations.

Backend - extract_types.py
- New ExtractType.resolve_document_count and FieldsetType.resolve_column_count
  reuse `_prefetched_objects_cache["documents"]` /
  `_prefetched_objects_cache["columns"]` (already populated by
  ExtractQueryOptimizer.get_visible_extracts) to return the count without
  an extra DB hit, falling back to .count() when the prefetch is absent.

Test coverage
- Backend: test_extracts_list_count_fields_match_lists pins
  documentCount === len(fullDocumentList) and columnCount ===
  len(fullColumnList) end-to-end through the connection-style extracts
  query, so the slim/legacy counts can never drift.
- Frontend: source-level regression tests (Extracts.refetch-shape,
  Annotations.refetch-shape) pin the structural fixes - Apollo's request
  deduplication makes the storm invisible to MockedProvider, so the bugs
  must be pinned at the source level.
- Test wrapper: ExtractsTestWrapper projects existing ExtractType
  fixtures down to the slim list shape so the existing CT suite runs
  unchanged.

* Address review: depend on filtered_to_corpus?.id, not the object

The annotation_variables memo only reads filtered_to_corpus.id, so
listing the whole reactive-var object as a dep means a future emit
that swaps references but keeps the same id (e.g. a corpus list
re-fetched from the network) would invalidate the memo and trigger
a no-op Apollo refetch. Depending on the primitive id directly is
tighter and matches what the memo actually consumes.

* Address review feedback on PR #1602

- ExtractType.resolve_document_count: mirror the per-document permission
  filter used by resolve_full_document_list. Per CLAUDE.md the effective
  document permission is MIN(document_permission, corpus_permission), so
  corpus visibility alone is not sufficient — direct document permissions
  can be stricter. Without this, documentCount could exceed
  len(fullDocumentList) for the same viewer and silently leak the
  existence of private documents through the aggregate.
- ExtractListItem (new) + ExtractCardItem (new): replace the
  ``as unknown as ExtractType`` cast in Extracts.tsx with structural
  types derived from ``GET_EXTRACTS_FOR_LIST``. Future reads of
  ``ex.fullDocumentList`` / ``ex.creator`` are now caught at compile
  time instead of resolving to ``undefined`` at runtime. ExtractCards.tsx
  + ExtractListCard.tsx accept the structural shape so legacy
  ExtractType callers still compile without casts.
- getExtractStatus: narrow the parameter to a Pick so callers with the
  slim shape (no creator/corpus) compile without casts.
- New backend test: ``test_document_count_respects_per_document_permissions``
  pins the new permission-aware count behaviour. Viewer can read the
  extract via public corpus + public extract but only sees one of the
  two attached documents — the count must agree with the filtered list.
- Refetch-shape tests: add comments documenting what a legitimate future
  exemption looks like (mutation onCompleted, modal onClose, imperative
  event handlers; useEffect refetch only with a routed-through helper +
  rationale).

* Address PR #1602 review: shared page-size constant + tighter regression scans

- Move ``EXTRACTS_PAGE_SIZE`` and ``ANNOTATIONS_PAGE_SIZE`` magic numbers
  (per-view ``const … = 20``) into a single
  ``EXTRACT_PAGINATION.PAGE_SIZE`` constant alongside the existing
  ``ANNOTATION_PAGINATION.PAGE_SIZE`` in
  ``assets/configurations/constants.ts``. CLAUDE.md requires the
  constants file for any hardcoded value, and consolidating ensures the
  Annotations / Documents / Extracts views stay in sync if the default
  page size ever changes.

- Replace the ``[^}]*`` regexes in ``Extracts.refetch-shape.test.ts`` and
  ``Annotations.refetch-shape.test.ts`` with a balanced-brace scanner.
  The regex stops at the first inner ``}``, so a ``refetch()`` nested
  inside an ``if`` block (or any inner brace pair) inside the effect
  body would slip past undetected. The scanner walks each
  ``useEffect(() => { ... })`` body manually, picks up nested calls, and
  reports offending line numbers on failure for easier triage.

- Extract the pure ``formatStats`` helper from ``ExtractListCard`` into
  ``utils/extractUtils.formatExtractListStats`` and add 9 unit tests
  covering the documentCount → fullDocumentList fallback chain, the
  columnCount → fullColumnList fallback, the singular/plural copy at
  count == 1, and the corpus-line append. Lifts the ``ExtractListCard``
  patch coverage without having to mount a CT, and follows CLAUDE.md
  conventions on utility functions belonging in utility files.

* Address review on PR #1602: clarify comments and remove dangling block

- Move the ``EXTRACT_PAGINATION``/legacy-clamping commentary out of the
  no-man's-land between ``TableIcon`` and ``// Main Component`` and
  inline it on the ``extractVariables`` memo where the constant is
  actually used. While there, document the matching Apollo cache
  ``keyArgs`` entry (``extracts: relayStylePagination(["corpus",
  "corpusAction_Isnull", "name_Contains"])``) in ``cache.ts`` so the
  next reader can verify ``fetchMore`` will append rather than
  overwrite without grepping for it.
- Document the deliberate omission of ``totalColumns`` from the
  ``stats`` memo in ``Extracts.tsx``: the StatGrid renders four tiles
  (Total / Running / Completed / Documents) and never showed a column
  count, so summing ``fieldset.columnCount`` would be dead work.
  Comment is explicit so a future reader doesn't restore it without
  also adding the matching tile.
- Expand the ``resolve_document_count`` docstring to clarify that
  the prefetch eliminates the SQL N+1 but leaves an
  ``O(n_extracts × n_documents)`` Python permission check — the
  earlier "no per-doc permission fan-out" wording in the PR
  description was misleading. Add a comment on the inline imports
  noting they avoid the apps-not-loaded circular at module import
  time during schema construction.

* Address PR #1602 review and lift codecov patch coverage

Code-review responses:
- Merge duplicated fieldset selection in
  test_extracts_list_count_fields_match_lists into one block.
- Document the ExtractQueryOptimizer precondition on resolve_document_count
  and the missing-by-design permission filter on resolve_column_count.
- Note canonical (ExtractListItem) vs compat-shim (ExtractCardItem) on
  the ExtractCardItem type.
- Harden ENTRY_RE in the refetch-shape regression scans to also catch
  useEffect(async () => { ... }), and document the /s flag on the
  GET_EXTRACTS heavy-import scan.
- Consolidate the per-feature PAGE_SIZE constants under
  DEFAULT_LIST_PAGE_SIZE so Annotations / Extracts (and future list
  views) cannot silently drift apart on the page-size invariant.

Codecov patch coverage:
- Pre-seed annotation_variables filter inputs through
  AnnotationsSemanticSearchTestWrapper (structural / search term /
  labelset id / label id / filter-corpus / opened-corpus) so each
  truthy branch in the new useMemo body is exercised at least once.
- Add tests/AnnotationsFilterCoverage.ct.tsx that mounts the view
  with every combination, plus an 'all filters at once' case for
  belt-and-braces patch coverage.
- Add an Extracts.ct.tsx case that mounts with a non-empty
  initialSearchTerm so the truthy half of the
  '...(extract_search_term && { searchText })' spread fires.

* Address PR #1602 review: align backend max_limit with frontend page size

Latest Claude bot review flagged that GET_EXTRACTS_FOR_LIST now requests
first: 20 but the backend Relay connection still capped at
max_limit=15, so the slim list query was silently clamped to 15 rows —
same broken-pagination symptom the PR was meant to fix.

Backend
- New EXTRACT_LIST_MAX_PAGE_SIZE = 20 constant in
  opencontractserver/constants/extracts.py mirrors the frontend
  EXTRACT_PAGINATION.PAGE_SIZE so the cap and the page size stay in
  lockstep.
- config/graphql/extract_queries.py wires that constant into the
  extracts DjangoFilterConnectionField(max_limit=...) and adds a
  WHY comment naming the bug-shape this prevents.

Comment hygiene (CLAUDE.md "no dead code" / readability)
- Tightened the ~30-line block on ExtractType.resolve_document_count
  to a single paragraph covering the load-bearing facts (permission
  mirror, prefetch precondition, _prefetched_objects_cache is a
  Django private API).
- Tightened FieldsetType.resolve_column_count block to four lines.

subject: Chat tray cleanup + corpus tab scrolling fix (#1509)
message:
Chat tray cleanup + corpus tab scrolling fix (#1509)

* Hide document-tool FABs when chat tray is active

When the right-hand sliding panel is open in chat mode, the FloatingDocumentControls FAB stack (extracts, analyses, create-analysis) is positioned just to the left of the panel boundary and visually crowds the chat input area together with the sidebar tabs. This adds a hideDocumentTools prop to FloatingDocumentControls that drops those three FABs from both the desktop column and the mobile speed-dial when showRightPanel && sidebarViewMode === 'chat'. The panel-width control is kept since it's directly relevant to the open panel.

* Stop chat input from spilling past chat tray edge

The ChatInputContainer had 1.25rem/1.5rem padding plus a 0.875rem gap, and the wrapper carried a 2px border with a 4px focus halo. On narrow panel widths the halo bled past the wrapper and was clipped by ChatContainer's rounded right edge, while the send button hugged the panel wall. Reduces padding (0.875rem/1rem with safe-area-inset bottom), gap (0.625rem), wrapper border (1px / 12px radius), and focus halo (2px). Adds min-width: 0 on container and wrapper plus flex: 1 1 0 on the wrapper so the textarea shrinks within flex instead of forcing overflow.

* Address review: cover hideDocumentTools and drop create-analysis IIFE

- Replace IIFE-wrapped create-analysis ActionButton with a plain JSX
  short-circuit; the redundant selectedCorpus check inside onClick is
  also gone since selectedCorpus is in the render condition.
- Add hideDocumentTools to FloatingDocumentControlsTestWrapper so tests
  can drive the new prop end-to-end.
- Add two component tests: hidden-tools state asserts only the settings
  FAB renders, default state asserts the document tool buttons remain.
- Capture a docScreenshot for the hidden-tools state to anchor the
  visual contract for documentation.

* Address review: cover mobile speed dial path and fix doc permissions in test wrapper

- Add `isMobile` and `showRightPanel` props to FloatingDocumentControlsTestWrapper
  so tests can drive the speed-dial render path.
- Fix the wrapper's permission injection: it now writes Django-style raw
  permission strings ("read_document"/"update_document") into both
  rawPermissionsAtom and `selectedDocument.myPermissions`. Without this,
  FloatingDocumentControls' useEffect (line 405) overwrites the raw
  permissions with un-mappable enum values and `canCreateAnalysis` silently
  flips back to false.
- Assert `create-analysis-button` is visible in the desktop hideDocumentTools=false
  test so a regression that drops only this button is caught here.
- Add five new mobile speed-dial tests: hidden-tools, all-tools-visible,
  click-extracts-closes-analyses, click-analyses-closes-extracts, and
  readOnly-hides-create-analysis. These cover the previously untested
  mobile path (`isMobile=true`) where codecov was reporting misses.
- Drop the stale `:2148` line number from the CHANGELOG entry.

* Close floating analyses/extracts when chat tray takes over

PR #1509 review item 1: when hideDocumentTools becomes true the
toggle FABs for the floating analyses / extracts panels are removed,
but a panel that was already open stays mounted with no way to
dismiss it from the FAB column. Mirror the open-control invariant
on the close side by collapsing those panels on the same transition,
so opening the chat tray never strands the user with a panel they
can't dismiss.

* Restore scrolling on corpus list tabs by dropping the viewport-stuck flex tower

The corpus Annotations / Analyses / Extracts tabs stopped scrolling after the
SPA-shell refactor (#1561) switched the outer wrapper from height: 100vh to
min-height: 100vh. Every layer of the corpus view chain (CardContainer,
ScrollableSegment, CorpusViewContainer, MainContentArea, the per-tab wrapper
divs, plus each panel's own Container / AnnotationsListContainer) was declaring
height: 100% + max-height: 100vh + overflow: hidden so the inner panel could
own scrolling via flex: 1 + overflow-y: auto. Without a definite height anchor
at the top of the chain, every percentage-height resolves to auto and the
inner overflow-y: auto containers grew to content height instead of scrolling.

Three wrappers were also passing style={{ minHeight: "70vh", overflowY:
"unset" }} to their panels — leftover from a much earlier outer-scroll era —
actively cancelling whatever inner scroll did try to engage.

Replace the whole tower with natural document flow:
- CardContainer / ScrollableSegment: drop height / max-height / overflow
- CorpusViewContainer / MainContentArea: drop height / max-height / overflow,
  keep min-height: 100dvh on CorpusViewContainer so the corpus view still
  fills the viewport when content is short
- Per-tab wrapper divs in Corpuses.tsx: drop height: 100% + overflow: hidden
- AnnotationsPanel Container / AnnotationsListContainer: natural blocks
- ExtractCards Container / AnalysesCards div: natural blocks
- CorpusAnnotationCards / CorpusAnalysesCards / CorpusExtractCards: drop the
  legacy minHeight 70vh / overflowY unset inline style overrides

Also fix cookie consent modal mobile sizing while we're in the area:
.oc-modal mobile max-height: 100vh -> 100dvh (so the bottom doesn't sit below
the URL bar), drop redundant .oc-modal-body max-height overrides (the base
@os-legal/ui flex: 1 + min-height: 0 + overflow-y: auto already handles
scroll inside the modal), and zero overlay padding on mobile so the
fullscreen modal isn't inset by 16px on each side.

* Address review: fix useEffect deps, add dvh fallbacks, improve chat error state

- Remove showAnalysesPanel/showExtractsPanel from useEffect deps in
  DocumentKnowledgeBase.tsx — setters are stable refs, unconditional
  calls avoid spurious re-runs when panels close from other sources
- Add max-height: 100vh / min-height: calc(100vh - ...) fallbacks before
  100dvh equivalents in CookieConsent.tsx and Corpuses.styles.ts for
  Safari <15.4 / Chrome <108 compatibility
- Use navbar-height-aware calc() for COMPOSER_MAX_HEIGHT in
  CorpusQueryView.tsx so chat input pins at viewport bottom, not below it
- Restore navigation header on CorpusChat error state so users can
  navigate away without being stuck

subject: Make load_document_text adaptive to the agent's remaining context budget (#1603)
message:
Make load_document_text adaptive to the agent's remaining context budget (#1603)

* Make load_document_text adaptive to the agent's remaining context budget

Whole-document tasks (e.g. summarisation) used to fan out into hundreds
of load_document_text calls because the tool description hard-coded a
5K-50K char chunk recommendation regardless of how much room the model
actually had. The agent now snapshots its per-turn budget onto
PydanticAIDependencies and the document-agent factory swaps the
registry-built tool for a budget-aware variant that auto-sizes its
slice when ``end`` is omitted.

- PydanticAIDependencies gains model_name, context_window_tokens,
  estimated_used_tokens, and compaction_threshold_ratio plus
  remaining_tokens_until_compaction() and
  recommended_chunk_chars(reserve_ratio=0.25) helpers (default reserve
  leaves 25% of remaining tokens for the assistant's response and the
  ~10% over-estimate baked into estimate_token_count).

- PydanticAICoreAgent._refresh_context_budget() runs after every
  _get_message_history() call (_chat_raw, _stream_core, structured run
  path, resume_with_approval). The closures on the document-agent's
  custom tools share the agent_deps_instance by reference, so they
  observe the live snapshot at runtime.

- Document-agent factory now constructs agent_deps_instance before the
  custom tool closures, removes "load_document_text" from the
  registry-driven _read_tool_names list, and registers an adaptive
  variant that defaults end to min(total_chars, start +
  recommended_chunk_chars()) with a 5,000-char floor. Returns a dict
  ({text, total_chars, returned_range, chars_remaining,
  suggested_next_start, context_budget_chars}); dict returns bypass
  the wrapper's string-only 50K truncation so large budget-sized
  slices reach the model intact.

- New get_remaining_context_budget tool lets the agent inspect its
  budget without performing a load. Registered as a runtime-context
  tool (no FUNCTION_MAP entry, mirrors get_document_text_length).

- PydanticAICorpusAgent factory threads the same budget fields into
  its deps so future budget-sensitive tools on either agent inherit
  the snapshot consistently.

- Tool registry description for load_document_text updated to
  advertise the adaptive defaulting; the runtime-context-only tool
  NOTE now lists get_remaining_context_budget.

- Regression coverage in TestContextBudgetSnapshot pins the math:
  positive remaining, zero-floor over threshold, default 25% reserve,
  and explicit reserve_ratio overrides.

* Address review: tighten budget plumbing for load_document_text

- Move the 5K floor into opencontractserver/constants/context_guardrails.py
  as MIN_IMPLICIT_DOCUMENT_CHUNK_CHARS, alongside MAX_TOOL_OUTPUT_CHARS
  and CHARS_PER_TOKEN_ESTIMATE.
- Hoist the in-closure `from … import _DOC_TXT_CACHE` to the existing
  module-level core_tools import block so the dependency is visible to
  module analysis and readers.
- Add a comment explaining why `(0, 1)` populates a meaningful
  `total_chars` (`aload_document_txt_extract` always reads the *full*
  file into the cache before slicing — the 1-char trick is a safe way
  to populate it, not a guess).
- Track per-turn implicit-chunk consumption on
  `PydanticAIDependencies.turn_implicit_doc_text_chars`, fold it into
  the budget so successive `end`-less reads back off proportionally,
  and reset it in `_refresh_context_budget` at the start of every
  turn. Without this, two implicit calls in the same turn would each
  see the same `recommended_chunk_chars()` snapshot and could
  collectively overflow the real budget.
- CHANGELOG ordering: move the load_document_text bullet under
  ### Changed below the existing ### Added section so the section
  order matches Keep a Changelog (Added → Changed → Fixed →
  Security).
- New tests in TestContextBudgetSnapshot pin the implicit-chunk tally
  defaulting to 0 and remaining mutable so the agent factory's closure
  can fold it into the budget.

* Address review feedback round 2 on PR #1603

- _refresh_context_budget: use explicit ``> 0`` check instead of ``or``
  when choosing between history_result.context_window and the per-model
  registry. ``or`` would conflate "missing" with a legitimate zero.
- _stream_core: when caller passes an explicit ``message_history`` we
  skip _refresh_context_budget; defensively reset
  ``turn_implicit_doc_text_chars`` so the turn doesn't inherit a stale
  per-turn tally if the public API path is exercised in isolation.
- load_document_text: emit a warning when ``recommended_chunk_chars``
  returns more than ``LARGE_IMPLICIT_CHUNK_WARN_THRESHOLD`` (200K) so
  drift in the 25% reserve_ratio heuristic is observable in production.
  Add a docstring note that explicit ``end`` values are *not* counted
  against the in-turn implicit-chunk tally.
- New tests pin the multi-call drift behaviour
  (TestLoadDocumentTextDriftMath) and the falsy-zero fallback semantics
  (TestRefreshContextBudgetFallback). Drift tests mirror the closure's
  budget arithmetic so the back-off, floor, and reset behaviour are
  pinned without requiring the full async closure environment.
- Changelog: document the dict return shape as a downstream-breaking
  change for any Python callers that programmatically unwrap the tool's
  return as a string.

* Address review round 3: registry desc, full-refresh, accessor

- Registry description for ``load_document_text`` no longer claims
  adaptive defaulting for non-document agents. The document-agent
  factory still ships its own description; the registry one now
  reflects the static behaviour the corpus and other agents actually
  see, with a parenthetical pointing at the document-agent override.
- Document-agent description fixes ``"byte range"`` -> ``"character
  range"`` (start/end are character indices throughout) and clarifies
  that ``returned_range`` is ``[start, end)`` while
  ``suggested_next_start`` is the right field for follow-ups.
- ``_stream_core`` now refreshes the *full* budget snapshot when the
  caller passes an explicit ``message_history`` (the
  ``resume_with_approval`` path). Previously only
  ``turn_implicit_doc_text_chars`` was reset, leaving
  ``estimated_used_tokens`` / ``context_window_tokens`` /
  ``compaction_threshold_ratio`` carrying stale values into the next
  turn — which would feed ``recommended_chunk_chars()`` the wrong
  baseline. New ``_history_result_from_messages`` helper builds a
  synthetic ``_HistoryResult`` from explicit messages and runs
  through the same ``_refresh_context_budget`` codepath.
- Extract pure transformation as ``_apply_context_budget`` static
  method; the instance method now delegates. The fallback tests no
  longer have to construct an agent via ``__new__`` to drive the
  branch — they call the static method directly with a deps + config
  + history result.
- New ``get_cached_txt_extract_length`` accessor in
  ``core_tools.text_extracts``; ``pydantic_ai_agents`` no longer
  imports the private ``_DOC_TXT_CACHE`` dict and goes through the
  accessor for the cached length. Cache backend can later evolve
  without rippling across consumers.
- Comment on ``MIN_IMPLICIT_DOCUMENT_CHUNK_CHARS`` documents the
  trade-off (overflow risk on starved budgets vs. usability on
  whole-document tasks) and the partial-correction nature of
  ``turn_implicit_doc_text_chars`` is called out in
  ``_apply_context_budget``'s docstring.
- New ``TestHistoryResultFromMessages`` cases pin token estimation
  for explicit message lists, empty lists, and ``None``.

* Address review round 4: budget_was_applied + relative warn ratio + closure extraction

- load_document_text now returns budget_was_applied so the LLM can tell
  whether context_budget_chars shaped the response or merely advertises
  the next implicit-call budget; returned_range docstring now matches
  the LLM-visible description (exclusive end).
- LARGE_IMPLICIT_CHUNK_WARN_THRESHOLD (200K hard) → LARGE_IMPLICIT_CHUNK_WARN_RATIO
  (0.5 of context_window_tokens * CHARS_PER_TOKEN_ESTIMATE) so 1M-token
  models do not spam the warning on legitimately large recommendations.
- _history_result_from_messages is a @staticmethod taking explicit config,
  matching _apply_context_budget; tests no longer need __new__ bypass.
- Extracted load_document_text_tool body into _make_load_document_text_tool
  module-level builder so the closure can be exercised end-to-end without
  a full DocumentAgentContext. New TestLoadDocumentTextClosureIntegration
  pins the dict-shape contract (including budget_was_applied), explicit-end
  semantics, and the in-turn tally mutation through the closure reference.
- _DOC_TXT_CACHE no longer re-exported from core_tools/__init__.py;
  consumers must use the get_cached_txt_extract_length accessor.
- TestRefreshContextBudgetFallback._make_history_result switched to
  dataclasses.replace against a default-constructed _HistoryResult so the
  helper survives new fields on the dataclass.

* Address review round 5: empty-doc cache, reserve_ratio warn, registry desc

Round-5 review feedback from claude[bot] on PR #1603:

* Empty-document cache regression: the load_document_text closure used
  ``cached_len == 0`` to detect "never cached", which collided with
  "cached and empty" and re-primed the cache on every call for a 0-byte
  document. Exposed ``is_txt_extract_cached(document_id)`` membership
  predicate from ``core_tools.text_extracts`` and switched the closure
  to use it. Added ``TestIsTxtExtractCached`` (membership-vs-length
  distinction) and ``test_empty_document_does_not_repopulate_cache``
  (asserts prime fires exactly once across two empty-doc reads).

* ``reserve_ratio`` clamping is no longer silent: out-of-range values
  in ``PydanticAIDependencies.recommended_chunk_chars`` now emit a
  ``logger.warning`` before the existing clamp runs. Back-compat
  preserved. Two regression tests pin the warn-and-clamp behaviour
  for ``reserve_ratio=1.5`` and ``reserve_ratio=-0.1``.

* Tool-registry description for ``load_document_text`` no longer leaks
  the document-agent override implementation detail into the LLM-facing
  description. The note moved to a ``# NOTE`` code comment so human
  readers still see it but the LLM doesn't.

* ``get_remaining_context_budget`` registry description now enumerates
  all six fields the in-agent version returns (was missing
  ``compaction_threshold_ratio``) so the two stay in sync.

Re the "async tests silently pass" claim in the same review: verified
incorrect. ``django.test.SimpleTestCase.__init__`` detects coroutine
test methods via ``iscoroutinefunction(testMethod)`` and wraps them
with ``async_to_sync`` (Django >=4.1). Confirmed empirically with
``pytest opencontractserver/tests/test_context_guardrails.py::
TestLoadDocumentTextClosureIntegration -v`` — all three async tests
collect, run, and pass; a deliberately-failing async assertion fails
as expected. No code change needed.

* Address review: fix ToolCallPart token count, add warning dedup flag, improve cache comment, add budget tool shape test

- _history_result_from_messages now falls back to part.args when
  part.content is absent, so ToolCallPart argument text is counted
  in the estimated_used_tokens snapshot instead of silently dropped

- PydanticAIDependencies gains large_chunk_warning_emitted_this_turn
  (reset by _apply_context_budget each turn); load_document_text only
  emits the large-chunk warning once per turn so fresh large-context
  sessions don't log on every implicit call

- Added comment to the (0, 1) cache-prime probe in
  _make_load_document_text_tool explaining the full-text caching
  contract so future refactors don't break get_cached_txt_extract_length

- TestGetRemainingContextBudgetShape pins the 6-field return shape of
  get_remaining_context_budget so adding new PydanticAIDependencies
  fields without exposing them in the tool is caught at test time

subject: security: fix OAuth sub leakage into public user slugs (closes #1607) (#1612)
message:
security: fix OAuth sub leakage into public user slugs (closes #1607) (#1612)

Social/OAuth users' Django username is the raw provider sub
(google-oauth2|114688...). User.save() was generating the public URL
slug from that username, and sanitize_slug() stripped the | but kept
the rest, producing slugs like google-oauth2114688... that surfaced
verbatim on the community leaderboard via entry.user.slug.

Fix:
- Restructure User.save() to generate handle *before* slug; social
  users now get handle-based slugs (cleverFox42) from first login
- For any user with | in username or is_social_user=True, slug base
  is self.handle instead of self.username
- configure_user() in the Auth0 middleware now sets is_social_user=True
  on newly created OAuth users at source
- search_users_for_mention resolver now searches slug/handle only,
  never username or email, to close the discoverability oracle
- Migration 0029 backfills all existing users whose slug equals
  sanitize_slug(username) — replacing it with a handle-based slug
- New management command regenerate_user_slugs for on-demand repair
- 5 new tests covering slug-doesn't-leak-oauth-id, slug-matches-handle,
  and all command paths

subject: Unbreak CI: pin pydantic-ai-slim with narrow provider extras (#1627)
message:
Unbreak CI: pin pydantic-ai-slim with narrow provider extras (#1627)

* Pin pydantic-ai-slim with narrow provider extras to unbreak CI

The dependency was ``pydantic-ai>=1.92.0,<2``. The bare ``pydantic-ai``
meta-package's only non-extra dep is

  pydantic-ai-slim[ag-ui,anthropic,bedrock,cli,cohere,evals,fastmcp,
                   google,groq,huggingface,logfire,mcp,mistral,openai,
                   retries,spec,temporal,ui,vertexai,xai]==<version>

i.e. it unconditionally fans out to all ~20 provider extras whether the
consumer uses them or not. The ``mistral`` extra pins
``mistralai>=2.0.0``; on 2026-05-12 ``pypi.org/pypi/mistralai/json``
started returning HTTP 404 (package gone from PyPI). With no installable
``mistralai`` the resolver couldn't satisfy the extra, backtracked
through every ``pydantic-ai-slim`` and transitive ``pydantic`` /
``pydantic-core`` candidate, and surfaced the failure as a ``pydantic``
conflict — which is misleading. ``pydantic`` is fine; ``mistralai``
disappearing is the root cause.

Fix: depend on ``pydantic-ai-slim`` directly with only the provider
extras this codebase actually consumes — ``openai`` (primary embedder /
chat), ``anthropic`` (Claude in ``llms/api.py``), ``google`` (kept in
the set for the upcoming Gemini integration), and ``mcp`` (the OC MCP
server uses the ``mcp`` SDK). All other providers (``mistral``,
``groq``, ``cohere``, ``bedrock``, ``huggingface``, ``vertexai``,
``xai``, etc.) are dropped. No code currently imports tenacity,
logfire, ag-ui-protocol, fastmcp, exa, or any of the dropped provider
SDKs, so this is a pure dependency-surface reduction with no behaviour
change.

Locally verified that ``pip install -r requirements/base.txt`` now
resolves cleanly in a ``python:3.12-slim`` container; the full
CI/CD suite will exercise the runtime path.

* Also narrow pydantic-ai extras in mypy pre-commit hook

The mypy hook in ``.pre-commit-config.yaml`` had its own
``additional_dependencies`` listing ``pydantic-ai>=1.56.0,<2``. Like the
top-level requirement, that meta-package fans out to all 20 provider
extras, so the broken ``mistral`` → ``mistralai`` chain was failing the
hook's environment install in CI even though the pre-commit cache on
contributor machines (built before mistralai disappeared from PyPI)
masked it locally. Switch the hook to
``pydantic-ai-slim[openai,anthropic,google,mcp]>=1.56.0,<2`` so it
resolves cleanly and stays in lockstep with the narrowed extras in
``requirements/base.txt``.

Verified locally by clearing the pre-commit cache and running
``pre-commit run --all-files`` — all hooks pass and mypy completes.

subject: Mobile-nav follow-up: split dialog/landmark, type imports, iOS scroll-lock (closes #1610) (#1625)
message:
Mobile-nav follow-up: split dialog/landmark, type imports, iOS scroll-lock (closes #1610) (#1625)

* Mobile-nav follow-up: split dialog/landmark, fix type imports + iOS scroll-lock

Surgical follow-up to PR #1606 addressing #1610 code-review items:

- Sheet's `<nav>` element no longer carries `role="dialog"` (which per ARIA
  overrides the implicit landmark and erases it from the a11y tree). Sheet
  is now a `styled(motion.div)` with `role="dialog"` + `aria-label="Navigation menu"`;
  the navigation landmark moves to a sibling inner `SheetNav` (`styled.nav`)
  with `aria-label="Site navigation"` wrapping only the browse items + Account
  actions. AuthFooter stays outside the landmark (it is auth state, not nav).

- Drop the implicit `React` global from type positions. With the new JSX
  transform the file never imports `React`, so `React.ReactNode` / `React.FC`
  were relying on the ambient global. Switch to `import type { FC, ReactNode }
  from "react"`.

- Lock `<html>` overflow alongside `<body>` so iOS Safari's rubber-band /
  overscroll gesture no longer bleeds through the modal. Both `<body>` and
  `<html>` overflow are saved on open, set to "hidden", and restored on
  `onExitComplete` + the unmount cleanup path.

- Add inline comments documenting three intentional choices (issue items
  2/3/4): the toggle is outside the focus-trap container by design; `aria-
  controls` references a portalled element by design; `initialsFor` is tuned
  for Latin/CJK whitespace-separated names and degrades gracefully otherwise.

- Tests: 15 sheet-locator sites in NavMenu.ct.tsx move from
  `[aria-label="Site navigation"]` (now on the inner nav) to the stable
  `#mobile-nav-sheet` id. Updated the aria-modal/aria-label test to assert
  the new dialog label, and added a regression that pins the dialog/nav
  split (dialog is `<div>`; inner `<nav aria-label="Site navigation">` is
  a sibling landmark; the nav wraps the browse items). All 33 NavMenu CT

Closes #1610

subject: Polish cookie consent modal styling on mobile (#1623)
message:
Polish cookie consent modal styling on mobile (#1623)

* Polish cookie consent modal for mobile

Refines the mobile presentation of the cookie consent modal so it
matches the OS Legal aesthetic used elsewhere:

- Anchor the Accept & Continue footer with flex layout (header /
  scrollable body / footer) plus safe-area inset padding, so the
  button is always reachable above the iOS gesture bar without
  relying solely on position: sticky.
- Lift data cards off a tinted body background and add the standard
  card shadow for elevation.
- Swap mobile data-list chips to accentSurface + textPrimary so they
  read as brand surfaces instead of generic slate chips.
- Add a 3px warning-text left bar on the demo banner, an inner
  accent ring on the header icon badge, and tighter mobile
  typography for section labels, lead copy, and the disclaimer.
- Bump the footer button to 48px / 600 weight for a comfortable
  thumb target.

Desktop styling is unchanged.

* Address review on cookie modal polish PR

- Scope IconBadge inset ring, DataCard box-shadow and DemoBanner left accent stripe to the mobile media query (PR description and CLAUDE.md note both said all changes should be mobile-only).
- Restore OS_LEGAL_SPACING.iconBadgeMobile (34px) for the mobile badge size instead of hardcoded 32px; drop the magic svg width/height overrides.

trigger per WCAG 2.4.3).

the same links are one tap away.

- the overflow is purely additive, no per-route visibility toggle.

Eleven CT tests cover trigger presence, dropdown open, link contents,
external-link target/rel, ARIA attributes, and ESC / outside-click
close in both anonymous and authenticated states, on desktop and
mobile. Existing 32 NavMenu tests continue to pass.

* Address review: design tokens + discriminated union for overflow menu

- NavOverflowMenu.tsx: replace hardcoded hex values with OS_LEGAL_COLORS
  tokens (textPrimary, surface, surfaceHover, accent, textMuted, border).

  to the `css` tagged template so styled-components keeps tagged-
  template type checking. Also import `FC` explicitly instead of using
  the `React.FC` namespace access.

  (project UPPER_SNAKE_CASE convention) and convert `OverflowMenuLink`
  into a discriminated union so a link with neither `to` nor `href` is

- NavMenu.tsx: update the import + prop site to the new constant name.

* Address review: Z_INDEX constant, whiteSurfaceAlpha helper, ReactElement, expand overflow tests

- Move surfaceAlpha helper from NavOverflowMenu and MobileNavMenu into

subject: Address PR #1600 review follow-ups (closes #1608) (#1626)
message:
Address PR #1600 review follow-ups (closes #1608) (#1626)

* Address PR #1600 review follow-ups (closes #1608)

Surgical fixes for the five items raised in #1608 against the slug-only
privacy gate landed in PR #1600. No runtime behaviour change in shipped
code — the only structural edit is a TypeScript-only widening of a
hand-written interface; the rest are docstrings / comments / TODO
markers that pin existing invariants.

1. UserSerializer ↔ UserViewSet lookup_field contract
   The DRF UserSerializer is currently unwired (no UserViewSet exists),
   and the existing docstring noted the constraint but was easy to miss.
   Upgrade the class docstring from `.. note::` to `.. warning::` with
   the exact viewset skeleton future contributors must use, and add a
   paired inline comment at the `extra_kwargs[url][lookup_field]` line.
   Greppable for `UserViewSet` so anyone wiring this serializer surfaces
   the privacy contract on the first search.

2. object_shared_with GenericScalar rationale
   Add a block comment at the field declaration in
   AnnotatePermissionsForReadMixin explaining why the field is
   intentionally typed as GenericScalar rather than a named output type.
   External callers reading objectSharedWith[].email / .username will
   see those keys disappear at runtime rather than triggering a schema
   error, and the untyped scalar lets us evolve the inner shape without
   a schema-breaking rename.

3. isUsageCapped nullable break in the hand-written login interface
   PR #1600 made UserType.isUsageCapped and UserType.canImportCorpus
   nullable to enforce the self-only gate, and the codegen'd
   graphql-api.ts picked up the change. The hand-written
   LoginOutputs.tokenAuth.user.isUsageCapped interface in mutations.ts
   still typed the field as a non-nullable boolean, so a future
   consumer of that exact field would receive null silently for any
   non-self code path. Switch to Maybe<boolean> (the schema contract)
   and document why the value is always defined at this specific call
   site (login → self-view) so the type narrowing makes sense to
   future readers.

4. Frontend audit of isUsageCapped / canImportCorpus consumers
   No further fixes needed. Ran the grep from #1608 across frontend/src:
   the three production consumers all use null-safe access (optional
   chaining, explicit Boolean() coercion, truthy short-circuit), and
   no non-null assertions (`!`) exist on either field in the repo:
   - Corpuses.tsx:944  `backendUser?.canImportCorpus`
   - Corpuses.tsx:1414 `Boolean(backendUser?.canImportCorpus)`
   - Documents.tsx:1315 `backend_user && !backend_user.isUsageCapped`
   Verified.

5. export_v2.py PII leak — # TODO(#1608) markers added
   PR #1600 deliberately left the V2 corpus export format unchanged
   because rewriting author_email / creator_email to slug-based keys
   is a breaking change to the export schema. Add # TODO(#1608)
   comments at the four leak sites (one in package_md_description_revisions
   covering revision authors; one umbrella TODO in package_conversations
   covering the conversation / message / vote loops) and update the
   existing CHANGELOG bullet under PR #1600's "Out of scope" line to
   reference #1608 explicitly so the gap stays linked when the next
   export-version bump happens.

Item #4 from #1608 (decodeRelayPk edge case) explicitly required no
action per the issue text — kept as-is.

* Address review: trim multi-line comments, harden UserViewSet skeleton

- frontend/src/graphql/mutations.ts: collapse the 6-line isUsageCapped
  comment to one line; drop the PR-number reference per CLAUDE.md.
- config/graphql/.../mixins.py: collapse the 9-line object_shared_with
  rationale to a single line summarising why we use GenericScalar.
- opencontractserver/utils/export_v2.py: collapse the two TODO(#1608)
  blocks into one-line markers.
- opencontractserver/users/api/serializers.py: drop ListModelMixin from
  the UserViewSet skeleton in the docstring and add an explicit
  CAUTION note. A bare ListModelMixin here would expose a paginated
  users list and bypass the existing slug-only privacy gate.
- (PR description: stripped 'Generated by Claude Code' attribution
  per CLAUDE.md baseline commit rule #3.)

* fix: unblock CI linter and address review comments

- Widen requests.post json= payloads from dict[str, str] / inferred
  literals to dict[str, Any] so they satisfy JsonType (dict is invariant
  — pre-existing on main, mypy errors in users/tasks.py, docxodus_parser,
  sent_transformer/multimodal microservices)
- mixins.py: expand object_shared_with comment to call out which keys
  (slug only, not email/username) callers should expect
- export_v2.py: name conv/msg/vote ["creator_email"] explicitly in the
  PII-leak TODO so future migration is mechanical (review feedback)

* Address PR 1626 review: cast(Any, ...) instead of intermediate vars; trim long comments

- pipeline/embedders & parsers: replace intermediate payload variables
  with inline cast(Any, ...) calls. Keeps the mypy fix that the linter
  needs but removes the single-use named variables flagged in review.
- export_v2.py: collapse multi-line conversation TODO + move revision TODO
  out of the loop (one annotation per call site, not per-iteration).
- serializers.py: trim Meta extra_kwargs comment to one line; the security
  contract lives in the class-level .. warning:: docstring.

Adds a dedicated test that reloads opencontractserver.users.tasks with
USE_AUTH0=True so the Auth0-gated celery tasks are actually defined,
then exercises get_new_auth0_token end-to-end with a mocked
requests.post. Verifies the M2M request payload shape, that the access
token is persisted to Auth0APIToken on a 2xx response, and that a
non-2xx response returns None without writing a row. Brings the
codecov patch coverage for the recently-touched type-annotation widening
back over target.

* Address review: document module-reload caveat, drop stale print debug

- Clarify the parallel-runner caveat in the `_reload_users_tasks`
  helper. The pytest-xdist scheduler under `--dist loadscope` already
  keeps all tests in this class on a single worker so the module reload
  is observed in isolation; the `@pytest.mark.serial` marker is the
  wrong knob here because conftest tears down DB connections on it

  CLAUDE.md "no dead code" rule.
- PR description now explicitly calls out the bundled mypy 2.1.0 fix
  pulled from #1628 so the cross-file diff is auditable.

- Apply ``pytest.mark.xdist_group(name="users_tasks_reload")`` to

  isolated to a single xdist worker as a contract, not as a side-effect

  audience checks with an equality assertion against
  ``settings.AUTH0_DOMAIN``; the value is deterministic and a stricter

Add markdown-customizable user profile fields and SafeMarkdown rendering (#1615)

* Add markdown-customizable user profile fields

* Add backend for markdown profile fields and fix SafeMarkdown usage

Frontend PR #1615 introduced GraphQL fields (profileHeadline,
profileAboutMarkdown, profileLinksMarkdown) that the backend did not
implement, which would have broken every updateMe call. This commit adds
the missing pieces and addresses the rest of the review:

- Add profile_headline (CharField max 200), profile_about_markdown and
  profile_links_markdown (TextField max 5000) to User with a migration.
- Expose the three fields on UserType (public, gated by the existing
  userBySlug visibility filter on is_profile_public).
- Accept the three fields in UpdateMe.Arguments and add them to
  UserUpdateSerializer so the mutation persists them.
- Fix SafeMarkdown usage in UserProfile: the prop is `children`, not
  `content`. Passing `content` silently rendered nothing.
- Replace the new (user as any).* casts in UserSettingsModal with a
  single typed view of the user object; the `any` baseline ratchets down
  by six.
- Add maxLength attributes on the headline / about / links inputs that
  mirror the model constraints.
- Add GraphQL tests covering UpdateMe persistence and the UserType
  exposure path for the new fields.

* Fix CentralRouteManager test mock and add cross-user profile coverage

- Update the openedUser mock with the new profileHeadline/profileAboutMarkdown/profileLinksMarkdown fields so tsc/yarn build pass.
- Add UpdateMe round-trip test for isProfilePublic.
- Add cross-user userBySlug tests asserting markdown fields are visible on public profiles and hidden entirely for private ones.

* Address review on markdown user profile fields PR

Security hardening:
- ``SafeMarkdown`` now pins an explicit ``urlTransform`` allowlist
  (``https``, ``http``, ``mailto``, ``tel``, ``#``-fragments, root /
  relative paths). ``react-markdown`` 10.x already filters ``javascript:``
  by default, but every user-authored markdown surface (profile links,
  corpus descriptions, agent output) flows through this component, so
  the safety story is now pinned in the source rather than relying on
  upstream defaults remaining strict.

Coverage gaps flagged in review:
- New backend test
  ``UserBySlugMarkdownProfileFieldVisibilityTestCase.test_owner_can_read_their_own_private_profile_markdown_fields``
  pins that the owner of a private profile can still fetch their own
  markdown fields via ``userBySlug``. ``User.objects.visible_to_user``
  always includes ``user == requesting_user`` so this is the natural
  contract, but it was previously untested.
- New frontend CT case
  ``UserProfile View > renders markdown headline, about, and links via SafeMarkdown``
  exercises the markdown rendering end-to-end and asserts the
  ``urlTransform`` strips ``javascript:`` link targets while preserving
  ``https://`` ones.

CHANGELOG: documented both the new markdown profile fields and the
silent ``isProfilePublic`` mutation-variable fix that this PR also
ships.

* Address review feedback for profile fields

- Fix CHANGELOG headline char-count (200, matches model & migration).
- Drop unreachable `#|/` branches from SAFE_PROTOCOLS regex now that the
  early-exit in urlTransform already handles fragment/relative URLs.
- Split the user-profile About section: bio renders under "About",
  profileLinksMarkdown gets its own "Links" section with a link icon so
  the two markdown blocks have a clear visual separator.
- DRY the duplicate `TestContext` helpers in test_user_profile.py into a
  module-level `_TestContext` shim; lift `graphene.test.Client` import
  to the top of the file to match the rest of the test module.

* fix: unblock CI linter + address profile markdown review feedback

CI linter (pre-existing on main):
- Widen requests.post json= payloads to dict[str, Any] in users/tasks.py,
  docxodus_parser, and the two embedder microservices so they satisfy
  JsonType (dict is invariant).

Profile markdown review:
- CHANGELOG: correct the size claim — profile_about_markdown is 5k chars
  (matches the model/migration/textarea), not 10k. Also call out that
  size enforcement runs through UserUpdateSerializer (DRF ModelSerializer),
  whose auto-applied max_length validators reject oversized payloads on
  the server even though graphene.String itself has no length constraint.
- test_user_profile.py: add test_update_me_rejects_oversized_markdown_
  fields pinning the serializer-level rejection so a future refactor that
  bypasses the serializer can't silently regress the contract.
- UserSettingsModal.tsx: lift the two markdown textareas out of inline
  styles into a MarkdownTextarea styled-component using OS_LEGAL_COLORS
  tokens so theming stays consistent with the rest of the modal.
- SafeMarkdown.tsx: expand the comment on the relative-path passthrough
  to spell out the in-app phishing trade-off and explicitly warn future
  maintainers not to broaden the allowlist for protocol-bearing URLs.

* Address PR 1615 review: htmlFor/id pairing and profile_headline length test

- UserSettingsModal: pair each MarkdownTextarea with htmlFor/id so screen
  readers associate the label with the control and a label click focuses
  the corresponding textarea.
- test_update_me_rejects_oversized_markdown_fields: extend to also send
  a 201-char profile_headline so the 200-char CharField validator is
  exercised by the same regression.

* Address review: SafeMarkdown protocol-relative URL strip, WCAG focus ring, validator-only TextField note

SafeMarkdown:
- urlTransform now rejects protocol-relative URLs (//phishing.example),

message:
Round 6 follow-ups for adaptive load_document_text (#1628)

* Round 6 follow-ups for adaptive load_document_text (closes #1611)

- get_document_text_length_tool: switch the cached-length guard from
  ``length > 0`` to ``is_txt_extract_cached`` so an empty document
  (cached as "") doesn't fall through to a redundant full-document
  reload on every call. Same fix already applied in round 5 to
  ``_make_load_document_text_tool`` — extends it to this sibling site.

- _history_result_from_messages._part_text: replace the
  ``content or args or ""`` chain with an explicit ``is None`` check.
  ``or`` conflated an empty content string (e.g. ToolReturnPart with
  empty result) with "missing" and fell through to ``args``,
  double-counting tokens in the budget snapshot. Matches the
  defensive-zero pattern in _refresh_context_budget.

- TestLoadDocumentTextClosureIntegration._patches(): also patch
  ``is_txt_extract_cached`` to True. Without it, the real predicate
  returned False for the fake-loaded DOC_ID and three of the four
  tests silently exercised the empty-document prime path on every
  call instead of the intended warm-cache path. The fourth test
  (test_empty_document_does_not_repopulate_cache) still leaves both
  predicates unpatched on purpose to drive the membership-vs-length
  distinction end-to-end.

- PydanticAIDependencies.turn_implicit_doc_text_chars: document that
  the in-turn drift correction is partial — only implicit
  load_document_text calls feed the tally. Other heavy tool outputs
  (vector search, annotation lists, image data) consume context but
  are not tracked. Pointer for future maintainers adding budget-aware
  tools.

* Address review: trim _part_text comment

Compress the 8-line rationale to a 4-line block that still captures
the surprising bit (`is None` vs `or`) without restating well-known
context. Verified the underlying test fix: `pytest
opencontractserver/tests/test_context_guardrails.py -n 4
--dist loadscope` → 115 passed.

* Add tests for _part_text + extract get_document_text_length_tool to module-level helper

Codecov gap on this PR was the new branches in two closures:
- _part_text in _history_result_from_messages: the explicit is None
  guard (vs the prior or chain) wasn't exercised because existing
  tests only pass UserPromptPart with string content.
- get_document_text_length_tool: the new is_txt_extract_cached gate
  (vs the prior length > 0 check) wasn't testable in isolation
  because the closure was inline inside PydanticAIDocumentAgent.create.

Extract get_document_text_length_tool to module-level
_make_get_document_text_length_tool(doc_id) mirroring the pattern
already used by _make_load_document_text_tool. New tests cover:
- empty content NOT falling through to args (the bug the fix addresses)
- None content falling back to args (existing tool-call argument path)
- non-string content stringification
- closure returning cached length for empty docs (membership predicate)
- closure returning cached length for populated docs
- closure falling back to a full load on cache miss

Also fix five pre-existing mypy errors that were blocking the linter
check on main: cast() the json= dict arg in requests.post() calls in
users/tasks.py, docxodus_parser.py, sent_transformer_microservice.py,
and two sites in multimodal_microservice.py.

Add .playwright-mcp/ to .gitignore — local Playwright tooling drops
session logs there during interactive testing.

* Address review: add double-None edge case test for _part_text

Closes a small coverage gap noted in the latest Round-6 review: the
existing tests covered (content="", args=value), (content=None,
args=value), and non-string content, but not (content=None, args=None).
The new test pins the empty-on-empty-part contract so the helper's
intentional zero-token return on a fully-empty part can't silently
regress.

* Address review: shorten factory docstring, DRY _Fake* helpers, pin load-count assertion

- Collapse the multi-paragraph docstring on _make_get_document_text_length_tool
  to a single line; the prime/membership-predicate rationale lives as a
  short inline comment in the closure body, which is where a maintainer
  actually needs it.
- Hoist _FakePart / _FakeMessage to module-level helpers so the four
  _part_text tests stop re-declaring them and a future refactor of the
  fake's surface only has to update one place.
- Add the missing assertEqual(len(load_calls), 1) to the populated-doc
  test so all three closure tests now pin "exactly one load" as part of
  their spec, matching the empty-doc and cache-miss siblings.

subject: Add PII scan and auto-annotate agent tool (#1624)
message:
Add PII scan and auto-annotate agent tool (#1624)

* feat: add PII scan and auto-annotate agent tool

Adds `scan_and_annotate_pii`, an agent tool that scans documents for
sensitive information via the privacy-filter microservice and creates
one labeled annotation per detection (TOKEN_LABEL via PlasmaPDF for
PDFs, SPAN_LABEL for plain text).

- New httpx async client with chunking, offset remap, and dedup
- 8 PII categories auto-mapped to colored/iconed AnnotationLabels
- Agent knobs: min_score, entity_groups, dry_run, start_char/end_char
- New privacy_filter Docker service (local.yml, production.yml)
- Settings: PRIVACY_FILTER_URL, PRIVACY_FILTER_API_KEY, _TIMEOUT_SECONDS
- 18 unit tests; privacy-filter client mocked so CI needs no image

* Address review on PII scan tool PR

- Mark privacy_filter as required: false in production.yml so existing prod
  deployments that don't run the PII service still start.
- Wrap the httpx.post() call in adetect_pii in try/except httpx.HTTPError
  and re-raise as RuntimeError so transport-level failures land in the
  agent fault-tolerance layer instead of bubbling out raw.
- Validate the entity_groups allowlist up-front in ascan_and_annotate_pii
  and raise ValueError for unknown names instead of silently filtering
  every detection.
- Mention supported file types (PDF + plain text) in the scan_and_annotate_pii
  tool description.
- Add regression tests for the new transport-failure path and the
  allowlist validation.

* Address second-pass review on PII scan tool PR

- isort reordered core_tools/__init__.py to alphabetize the new pii import
  ahead of notes/page_images per project convention.
- Removed bare-annotation-then-assign pattern in ascan_and_annotate_pii;
  the variable is now initialised at the annotation site so static
  analysers (and humans) see one clear binding.
- Tightened the return type to dict[str, Any] so callers and IDEs get a
  more useful contract than bare ``dict``.
- Added a docs comment to the local.yml privacy_filter service noting it
  is internal-bridge-only with no host port mapping (smoke-test from
  inside django container).
- New regression test covers the inverted start_char/end_char case: the
  tool must short-circuit and must not issue a request to the
  privacy-filter service.

* Address review: unblock production stack + improve overlap dedup

- production.yml: switch privacy_filter API_KEYS to empty default
  (`${PRIVACY_FILTER_API_KEY:-}`). The previous `:?required` form failed
  Compose interpolation at parse time, so the whole production stack
  refused to start unless the env var was set — contradicting the
  `required: false` opt-in declared on the depends_on entry.
- production.yml + local.yml: add HTTP /health healthcheck and a 20s
  start_period so dependents can wait on `service_healthy` once the
  model weights are loaded, instead of `service_started` which only
  proves the container process spawned.
- _privacy_filter_client.py: when chunk overlap produces a duplicate
  (start, end, entity_group) detection, keep the higher-confidence
  score rather than first-seen. Switches the dedup tracker from
  `set` to `dict[..., int]` indexing into `results`.

* fix: unblock CI linter + address PII scan tool review

CI linter (pre-existing on main):
- Widen requests.post json= payloads in users/tasks.py, docxodus_parser,
  and the two embedder microservices from invariant dict[str, str]
  literals to dict[str, Any] so they satisfy JsonType.

PII scan tool review feedback:
- Use TEXT_MIMETYPES from constants instead of inline {"text/plain",
  "application/txt"} — picks up markdown alongside plain-text and keeps
  the supported-types list in lockstep with the ingestion pipeline.
- Move CHUNK_SIZE / CHUNK_OVERLAP into constants/document_processing.py
  (PRIVACY_FILTER_CHUNK_SIZE / _OVERLAP) so the magic numbers are
  discoverable per CLAUDE.md conventions.
- Convert _load_doc_text_sync's positional 5-tuple to _DocTextResult
  NamedTuple — unpacking sites still work positionally, and named fields
  make the contract self-documenting and grep-friendly.
- Make _persist_annotations_sync return (annotation_id, detection) pairs
  and derive detection_count / by_entity_group from those persisted pairs
  rather than the input detections list. Previously, if any detection
  was filtered out by the OOB / unknown-group guards inside persist,
  detection_count would overcount relative to annotation_ids — a
  confusing failure mode for LLM callers debugging a slice-offset bug.

* Address PR 1624 review: pre-create labels before atomic() to avoid race

ensure_label_and_labelset uses a check-then-create pattern that races
under concurrent scans. When the losing race fires INSERT inside the
outer transaction.atomic() block, the resulting IntegrityError poisons
the savepoint and rolls back every annotation created by the current
scan. Pull the label get_or_create work up before the atomic block —
the inner block now only inserts Annotation rows, which carry no
cross-row uniqueness constraint.

Also drops the now-dead ValueError inside _label_for: the outer loop
already filters on ENTITY_GROUP_LABELS membership, so a label fetch
for an unknown group is unreachable. Removing the parallel guard keeps
the validation in one place.

* Address review: warn on empty privacy-filter API key, clarify label-race comment, cover corpus_action_id propagation

- _privacy_filter_client emits a one-time warning when PRIVACY_FILTER_URL
  is set but PRIVACY_FILTER_API_KEY is empty so misconfigurations show up
  in logs instead of silently shipping with an unauthenticated service.
- Rewrite the label pre-creation race comment in _persist_annotations_sync
  to explain *why* doing get-or-create outside the atomic block is the
  correct trade-off (no DB-level uniqueness on AnnotationLabel; the
  pre-creation isolates a rare duplicate to the labels rather than
  rolling back the whole annotation batch).
- New test_corpus_action_id_propagates_to_created_annotations covers the
  round-trip from CorpusAction.id → kwarg → Annotation.corpus_action_id
  so future regressions in the propagation path don't slip through.

* Address review: chunk-overlap note, label-race comment, helper auth note, empty-API-key warning test

- _iter_chunk_starts: document the case where total_len lands just past a
  chunk boundary and the final chunk overlaps by more than CHUNK_OVERLAP
  (de-dup on (start, end, group) keeps the over-coverage harmless).
- _persist_annotations_sync: clarify that ensure_label_and_labelset already
  wraps its check-then-create in transaction.atomic(), but READ COMMITTED
  isolation does not prevent the duplicate-label race because there is no
  DB-level uniqueness on AnnotationLabel(text, label_type). Pre-creating
  outside the inner atomic block isolates the rare duplicate to the label
  table so the larger Annotation insert batch still commits.
- _load_doc_text_sync: add docstring note explaining the helper deliberately
  has no in-line authorization check; the agent tool framework gates writes
  via requires_write_permission=True and the function is module-private
  precisely because direct callers would bypass that gate.
- Add test_empty_api_key_logs_warning_once covering the suppression-after-
  first-emit path on _warned_about_missing_api_key, with explicit reset in
  try/finally so the test is order-independent.

subject: Hide soft-deleted document annotations/relationships from user queries (#1622)
message:
Hide soft-deleted document annotations/relationships from user queries (#1622)

* Hide trashed-doc annotations/relationships from visibility queries

When RemoveDocumentsFromCorpus soft-deleted a document, its annotations
and relationships stayed intact in the DB so the trash/restore flow could
recover them. But user-facing visibility queries
(Annotation.objects.visible_to_user, Relationship.objects.visible_to_user)
had no DocumentPath awareness, so the rows kept appearing in global
annotation searches pointing at documents the user could no longer
navigate to ("annotations linked to unknown document").

Fix: add an _exclude_soft_deleted_doc_orphans helper that uses the same
"is_current=True, is_deleted=False" predicate already used by
Corpus.get_documents() and AnnotationQueryOptimizer.get_corpus_annotations,
and apply it in AnnotationQuerySet.visible_to_user() and on a new
RelationshipManager attached to Relationship.objects. Standalone docs
(no DocumentPath) and structural rows (no document FK) are intentionally
untouched so test fixtures and pre-corpus-isolation data still work.
Superusers retain the full-bypass branch.

Data is preserved — only display is hidden — so RestoreDeletedDocument
brings the annotations and relationships back into queries without
resurrection logic.

Also harden permanently_delete_document: previously only relationships
referenced via the deleted annotations' source/target M2M were cleaned;
orphan corpus-scoped relationships tagged document=doc with empty
source/target survived. The new query explicitly removes those. The
structural-set GC continues to fire via the existing
_gc_orphan_structural_set post_delete signal whose
Document.objects.filter(structural_annotation_set_id=set_id).exists()
check is exactly "any other corpus-isolated doc copy with same content_hash".

New test_soft_delete_visibility.py covers visibility before/after
soft-delete, non-owner visibility, superuser bypass, restore round-trip,
standalone-doc regression guard, relationship cleanup of doc-tagged
orphans on permanent delete, and structural set GC across two
corpus-isolated copies (preserved when one copy remains, GC'd when the
last copy is permanently deleted).

* Address review on soft-delete visibility PR

- Add compound DocumentPath index on (document, corpus, is_current, is_deleted)
  to cover the hot-path EXISTS subquery used by
  _exclude_soft_deleted_doc_orphans, with corresponding migration 0038.
- Make _exclude_soft_deleted_doc_orphans generic on its QuerySet type so
  AnnotationQuerySet stays typed through the filter and mypy is happy.
- Use .distinct() in permanently_delete_document's relationship cleanup so
  the logged count doesn't double-count M2M-joined rows; hoist Q to module
  level.
- Add the missing non-owner regression test for relationship visibility
  after soft-delete and document why with_doc_label_annotations is in the
  RelationshipManager signature.

* Address review on soft-delete visibility PR

Migration: replace the RenameIndex operations on documentpath /
ingestionsource with pinned ``name=`` arguments on the underlying
Meta.indexes definitions. Adding the new (document, corpus, is_current,
is_deleted) index was triggering Django to recompute auto-generated
hash suffixes for unrelated indexes, producing three RenameIndex
operations that would have been brittle on any production database
whose historical names didn't match the previously-generated values.
Pinning the names in the model collapses the migration to a single
purely-additive AddIndex, which is reversible and safe on any DB that
ran migration 0036.

versioning.py:
- Switch the relationship cleanup in ``permanently_delete_document``
  from ``list(annotation_qs.values_list('id', flat=True))`` to a direct
  subquery against the annotation queryset, so we don't materialise a
  potentially-large pk list into Python memory before issuing the
  DELETE.
- Re-number the docstring steps so they match the inline comments
  (Verify / collect path ids / DocumentSummaryRevision / relationships
  / annotations / DocumentPaths / Document cascade).

Tests: add an anonymous-user regression test (``user=None``) confirming
that the soft-delete filter correctly hides trashed-doc annotations on
the anonymous code path, which goes through a separate branch in
``AnnotationQuerySet.visible_to_user``. The test marks the annotation
structural+public so the only reason it disappears from the result
set is the soft-delete predicate.

* Address review: pin DocumentPath soft-delete-orphan index name

Pin the new (document, corpus, is_current, is_deleted) index name to
match migration 0038 (`documents_d_documen_224610_idx`). Without an
explicit name, inserting any unnamed index ahead of it later regenerates
the autogenerated hash and produces a no-op `RenameIndex` migration.
Matches the pattern already used for the ingestion-source index.

* Address PR 1622 review: None guard in AnnotationQuerySet.visible_to_user

NoteQuerySet and PermissionQuerySet normalise None to AnonymousUser
at the queryset boundary. AnnotationManager.visible_to_user does the
same in its wrapper, but a direct queryset call
(SomeAnnotation.objects.filter(...).visible_to_user(None)) would
raise AttributeError on user.is_superuser. Adding the guard at the
queryset boundary makes the contract consistent with its peers and
removes the latent foot-gun for any future caller that bypasses the
manager.

* Address review: assert annotations themselves are deleted on permanent delete

The full lifecycle tests already covered this implicitly via Relationship
cascade behaviour, but a dedicated assertion in
PermanentDeleteRelationshipCleanupTests catches regressions in step 5 of
permanently_delete_document (the annotation cleanup pass) independently
of the relationship cleanup path. Mirrors the relationship-cleanup
regression test that lives in the same class.

* Address review: align RelationshipManager.visible_to_user pattern with AnnotationQuerySet

Normalise None → AnonymousUser at the top of RelationshipManager.visible_to_user
and short-circuit on superuser before calling super(), matching the existing
pattern in AnnotationQuerySet. The two soft-delete-aware visibility paths now
have identical structure, reducing cognitive overhead for future readers.

Behaviour is unchanged.

* Address review: drop incidental migration dep, add multi-corpus + null-guard tests

- Migration 0038: drop the auto-generated ``corpuses 0048`` dependency
  on the AddIndex op. The DocumentPath.corpus FK was added in
  documents.0023 (which already declares its own corpuses dep), so the
  ``documents 0037`` dep is sufficient and the corpuses entry was just
  auto-generated noise. Inline comment added explaining the rationale.

- New test ``test_annotation_visible_in_active_corpus_when_trashed_in_other``:
  pins the corpus-scoping of ``_exclude_soft_deleted_doc_orphans`` via
  the ``OuterRef('corpus_id')`` correlation — a doc soft-deleted in
  Corpus A keeps its Corpus-B-scoped annotations visible.

- New test ``test_null_document_id_annotation_not_excluded_by_orphan_filter``:
  pins the ``Q(document_id__isnull=False)`` guard so structural
  annotations linked only via ``structural_set`` are not filtered out by
  the orphan predicate even when the only doc referencing the set is
  soft-deleted.

- New test ``test_null_corpus_id_annotation_not_excluded_by_orphan_filter``:
  pins the ``Q(corpus_id__isnull=False)`` guard so corpus-agnostic
  annotations on standalone docs are not filtered out by the orphan
  predicate.

* Address PR #1622 review: DRY step 5 to reuse user_annotations_qs

subject: Centralize authorization logic in Manager.user_can() API (#1637)
message:
Centralize authorization logic in Manager.user_can() API (#1637)

* Centralize single-object authorization in Manager.user_can (Step 0)

Introduces ``Manager.user_can(user, instance, permission)`` (with the
ergonomic ``obj.user_can(user, permission)`` delegate on ``BaseOCModel``)
as the single source of truth for "does this user have permission X on
this object?". For READ, the new check is provably equivalent to
``Manager.visible_to_user(user).filter(pk=obj.pk).exists()``; for
non-READ permissions it is the only correct check (no queryset analogue).

Step 0 vertical slice: deletes ``FolderService.check_corpus_{read,write,
delete}_permission`` (~130 LOC, 3 sister wrappers) plus its 27 internal
callers and migrates 20 test sites in ``test_document_folder_service.py``
to ``corpus.user_can(...)``. Pins the read/write asymmetry that the
deleted methods enforced (``is_public=True`` grants READ but never
UPDATE/DELETE/CREATE) via the new invariant test
``test_authorization_invariants.py``.

Subsequent phases (per plan) extend ``user_can`` overrides to
Annotation/Relationship/Conversation/Document/etc. and migrate the
remaining 100+ ``user_has_permission_for_obj`` call sites. The function
is untouched in this PR.

* Fix Corpus.user_can missing; address review (DRY mixin, type guard, tests)

CI fix: PR-introduced `corpus.user_can(...)` calls in folder_service.py
crashed at runtime because Corpus/CorpusFolder inherit from TreeNode, not
BaseOCModel, so the new instance method was never reachable. Extracted
the instance-side body into `InstanceUserCanMixin` and applied it to
both BaseOCModel and Corpus/CorpusFolder.

Review responses:
- Merge main into branch (clean auto-merge of CHANGELOG.md)
- DRY: introduce UserCanMixin (manager/queryset) and InstanceUserCanMixin
  (model) in shared/user_can_mixin.py; the dedicated module keeps
  utils/permissioning's eager get_user_model() import out of the early
  shared.Models <-> users.models startup graph
- BaseOCModel.user_can: hasattr() guard raises an actionable TypeError
  when _default_manager lacks user_can, instead of leaking AttributeError
- _default_user_can: docstring clarifies the underscore is private to
  the permission subsystem, not file-private

Tests (6 new invariants):
- test_crud_with_full_explicit_guardian_grants (CRUD happy path)
- test_crud_satisfied_by_public_read_plus_explicit_writes (pins that
  is_public folds read_{model} into granted, so CRUD on public corpus
  with explicit writes passes -- reviewer's claimed gap is not a gap)
- test_all_perm_requires_every_codename (partial grant != ALL)
- test_comment_publish_permission_grants_for_non_creator
- test_queryset_user_can_matches_manager_and_instance
- test_str_and_int_user_id_inputs
- test_user_can_raises_typeerror_when_default_manager_lacks_method
  (regression guard for the new hasattr() guard)

Frontend: add docScreenshot to existing FeaturedCollections icon test
for documentation coverage.

Dismissed (with reasoning in PR summary):
- CRUD compound-check "gap" (#1): get_users_permissions_for_obj already
  folds is_public into granted as read_{model_name}; the new
  public+partial-CRUD invariant test pins this behavior
- Deprecate user_has_permission_for_obj (#4): still owns annotation/
  relationship structural-permission logic not ported in Phase 0;
  adding DeprecationWarning would flood 100+ call sites prematurely

* Address PR #1637 review: clarify deprecation contract on user_has_permission_for_obj

Strengthen the docstring on user_has_permission_for_obj() to explicitly
mark the function as superseded by Manager.user_can() for standard-rule
models, while documenting the two reasons it is retained without a runtime
DeprecationWarning:

  1. It still owns the Annotation / Relationship structural / privacy /
     inheritance branches that _default_user_can does not yet replicate.
  2. ~170 existing call sites are pending incremental migration; firing
     DeprecationWarning on every call would drown the signal in noise
     during the migration window.

Updates the 'USE THIS FUNCTION FOR' bullet list to reflect that new code
should prefer Manager.user_can on any model whose default manager extends
BaseVisibilityManager.

No behavioral changes.

* Address PR #1637 follow-up review: explicit is_public fold-in for CRUD/ALL + new invariant tests

Round 2 review feedback addressed:

Issue #2 (is_public synthetic READ grant fragility): The CRUD/ALL compound
checks previously relied on get_users_permissions_for_obj() folding is_public
into granted as a read_<model> entry. If that helper is ever refactored to
drop the synthetic injection, _default_user_can's CRUD/ALL path would
silently break for public corpora. Fixed by folding is_public in locally
at the CRUD/ALL call site -- the dependency is now visible at the only
call site that needs it. Behavior unchanged; this is a robustness fix.

Issue #4 (undocumented creator + compound shortcut): The creator_id == user.id
short-circuit fires before the compound CRUD/ALL branches, so a corpus
creator passes CRUD/ALL without explicit guardian grants. Added an explicit
bullet in the Rules section of _default_user_can's docstring and a new test
test_creator_passes_compound_perms_without_explicit_grants pinning it for
both private and public corpora.

Issue #5 (redundant unauthenticated check): Added inline comments explaining
why both the AnonymousUser isinstance check and the is_authenticated guard
exist. AnonymousUser is the common Django middleware sentinel; the
is_authenticated guard catches the long tail (test doubles, external SSO
shims, custom auth backends).

Issue #3 (EDIT vs UPDATE divergence): Confirmed EDIT and UPDATE are distinct
enum values but both _default_user_can and user_has_permission_for_obj route
them identically through update_<model>. Added test_edit_is_alias_for_update
to pin the alias and prevent silent divergence if either side ever forgets it.

Dismissed:
- #1 (missing __init__.py): The file exists at
  opencontractserver/tests/permissioning/__init__.py (tracked since 902177b53)
  and the 19 tests pass under pytest discovery -- the bot did not check it
  against the current tree.

* Address PR #1637 review: honest is_public fold-in comment + scope docstrings

- _default_user_can CRUD/ALL branch: rewrite the fold-in comment to be
  honest. Today the line is a no-op because get_users_permissions_for_obj
  already injects read_<model> when is_public=True; document that
  explicitly and explain why we keep the local fold-in (refactor safety).
- UserCanMixin: document that on a QuerySet (e.g. PermissionedTreeQuerySet)
  user_can() is a single-object check that ignores the queryset's current
  WHERE clause. Prevents the foot-gun where someone reads
  Corpus.objects.filter(is_public=True).user_can(...) as a filtered check.
- CorpusFolder: docstring scope note. folder.user_can(user, perm) checks
  folder-level permissions, NOT the parent corpus. Service-layer write
  ops should still use folder.corpus.user_can(user, perm).

* Address PR #1637 review: CorpusFolder.user_can delegates to parent corpus

---------
