subject: Rich-mention agent delegation in chat (#1651)
message:
Rich-mention agent delegation in chat (#1651)

* Add shared mention extractor for markdown URL grammar

* Address Task 1 code-review: fix @corpus/@document double-emit and align legacy regex

The legacy `@corpus:X/document:Y` form previously emitted both a document
AND a redundant corpus mention because the `_LEGACY_CORPUS_RE` lacked the
`(?!/document:)` negative lookahead used by the existing resolver in
config/graphql/conversation_types.py.

- Add the same negative lookahead to `_LEGACY_CORPUS_RE`.
- Use a possessive quantifier `[a-z0-9-]++` so the slug match does not
  backtrack into a shorter prefix to satisfy the lookahead (which would
  otherwise yield a spurious `acme-cor` corpus mention from
  `@corpus:acme-corp/document:spec-doc`). The existing resolver hides
  this bug via a DB-lookup that returns DoesNotExist, but the pure parser
  has no such filter, so the fix is necessary here.
- Align all three legacy patterns to `[a-z0-9-]+` (slugify strips
  underscores in practice; this matches the existing resolver's char
  class and reduces surprise).
- Add 4 tests covering: corpus+document combined form, annotation URL
  with garbage `ann=` falling back to document, unknown path shapes
  ignored, and too-few path segments ignored.

* Refactor MessageType mention resolver to use shared extractor

Replaces the inline parsing/regex/base64/urlparse logic in
MessageType.resolve_mentioned_resources with a call to the shared
extractor introduced earlier on this branch plus a new module-level
helper resolve_mentions_for_user() that handles DB lookup and
visible_to_user() permission gating.

resolve_mentions_for_user() is the single chokepoint Task 3 will reuse
for ChatMessageType.mentioned_resources. It recomputes URLs from the
resolved DB objects so legacy text-pattern mentions (e.g. @corpus:slug)
still get real /c/{creator}/{slug} URLs instead of the synthetic
/c/_/{slug} placeholders the extractor emits for those patterns;
annotation mentions preserve the original markdown-link URL since it
already encodes the ?ann=... navigation target.

All 24 test_mentions integration tests and 18 test_mention_extractor
unit tests continue to pass.

* Add agent branch to mention resolver

Wires the ExtractedMention agent type through resolve_mentions_for_user so
chat messages can surface @-mentioned agents (global and corpus-scoped)
via MentionedResourceType. Adds visible_to_user gating, is_active filter,
and corpus-slug consistency check; permission failures are silently
omitted (never leak existence).

Also adds a tests module covering visible/inactive/inaccessible-corpus/
mismatched-corpus/unknown-slug cases for the new branch.

* Extend GET_CHAT_MESSAGES with agentConfiguration and mentionedResources

Adds the agentConfiguration scope/slug/corpus and mentionedResources
selections to the chat-side query so the frontend can render rich-mention
agent delegations and resource chips consistently with the thread surface.
The backing TypeScript types in graphql-api.ts already expose these
fields, so no consumer interface changes were required.

* Add filter_by_scope helper for delegation target resolution

* Add StreamRelay dataclass and build_delegation_tool factory

* Address Task 6 code-review: ephemeral sub-agents, propagate ToolConfirmationRequired, honor agent system_instructions, add body tests

- Pass persist=False to agents.for_document/for_corpus so sub-agents do
  not spawn a parallel ChatMessage stream on the parent conversation
  (spec: sub-agents are ephemeral, attributed to the conductor turn).
- Pass system_prompt=agent.system_instructions through the same API so
  the selected AgentConfiguration is actually honoured instead of the
  framework default. api.for_* normalises this to pydantic-ai's
  instructions= kwarg (see CLAUDE.md pitfall #14).
- Propagate PermissionError AND ToolConfirmationRequired from both the
  sub-agent build and the streaming loop, per the fault-tolerance
  contract documented in pydantic_ai_tools.py:560 and CLAUDE.md
  pitfall #13. Operational exceptions continue to surface as a result
  string back to the conductor LLM.
- Add a TODO(Task 7) comment by the relay.on_approval call noting
  that resume_with_approval(...) wiring belongs to the consumer.
- Clarify the trailing comment about SourceEvent being intentionally
  dropped from the relay surface.
- Add BuildDelegationToolBodyTests covering the actual _body
  coroutine: content accumulation, persist=False / system_prompt
  plumbing, omission of system_prompt when system_instructions is
  blank, pin=True relay callbacks (on_token / on_thought / on_finish),
  ToolConfirmationRequired propagation, PermissionError propagation,
  and operational-error stringification. 8 -> 15 tests in
  test_delegation_tools.

* Wire per-turn delegation tools into UnifiedAgentConsumer

Builds the conductor per turn with `delegate_to_<slug>` tools whenever the
user's message mentions visible, in-scope agents. The relay forwards
sub-agent events (content, thoughts, approvals, final) back through the
WebSocket with `agent_id` / `parent_message_id` / `requesting_agent`
metadata so the frontend can attribute pinned bubbles and timeline
entries to the right delegated agent.

Approval flow uses approach (b): the delegation tool body intercepts
`ApprovalNeededEvent`, calls `relay.on_approval(...)` which registers a
future on the consumer's `_pending_approvals` map keyed by
`(parent_message_id, agent.id)`, emits ASYNC_APPROVAL_NEEDED, and awaits
the user's decision. `_handle_approval_decision` then resolves the
future, and the tool body drives `sub_agent.resume_with_approval(...)`
inline so the conductor's tool call only returns once the sub-agent has
settled.

Pinned sub-agent replies persist as a separate ChatMessage row with
`agent_configuration=<sub-agent>`, `parent_message=<conductor msg>`, and
`data={"pinned": True, "delegated_from": <id>, "agent_slug": "..."}`.

Behavioural coverage in `test_unified_agent_consumer_delegation.py`:
silent fallback (invisible / scope-mismatched targets), anonymous +
public global, single + multiple mentions, pinned ChatMessage
persistence, sub-agent approval bubbling, and conductor approval
back-compat.

* Address Task 7 code-review: disconnect cleanup, constant for approval cycle limit, drop dead StreamRelay field, document approval routing assumption, plus coverage

- UnifiedAgentConsumer.disconnect now cancels pending sub-agent approval
  futures before clearing self.agent, preventing leaked asyncio tasks
  and AWAITING_APPROVAL rows when the socket closes mid-approval.
- Replace magic ``max_resume_loops = 8`` with the module-level constant
  MAX_DELEGATION_APPROVAL_CYCLES (documented).  When the limit is hit
  the body now returns an explicit cycle-limit error string instead of
  silently falling through to partial accumulated content.
- Drop the dead ``StreamRelay.parent_message_id`` field (closures read
  the consumer's shared one-slot box directly).  Update the dataclass,
  consumer construction site, and StreamRelay shape tests.
- Document the conductor + sub-agent approval routing assumption: sub-
  agent approvals are drained inside the delegation tool body before
  the conductor can register its own approval, so the routing in
  _handle_approval_decision is unambiguous by construction.
- Consolidate on_finish into a single ``if not pin: return`` early
  exit, with persistence nested for the authenticated path; anonymous
  sessions still get the ASYNC_FINISH frame but skip the DB row.
- New tests:
  * disconnect cancels in-flight sub-agent approval futures
  * conductor approval routes correctly after a sub-agent approval has
    resolved (validates the "impossible by construction" invariant)
  * two pinned delegations produce two distinct ChatMessage rows with
    distinct agent_configuration FKs
  * delegation body returns explicit cycle-limit error and stops at
    exactly MAX_DELEGATION_APPROVAL_CYCLES resume calls when the sub-
    agent perpetually requests approval

* Add useAgentMentionTrigger hook for textarea @-trigger watching

* Add AgentMentionPopover component and buildAgentMentionLink helper

* Refactor AgentMentionPopover to use styled-components with theme tokens

* Render chat messages through MarkdownMessageRenderer with mention chips

* Wire agent mention picker into ChatTray and CorpusChat textareas

* Extract shared chat mention picker hook and test util

Both ChatTray and CorpusChat duplicated ~90 lines of identical wiring for the
agent @mention picker: useAgentMentionTrigger + useUnifiedMentionSearch setup,
agentItems mapping, portaled AgentMentionPopover with rect-anchored positioning,
caret-restoring onSelect handler, and textarea onChange integration.

Pull all of that into useChatMentionPicker (frontend/src/hooks/) — each
consumer now calls a single hook and renders one popoverNode. Behaviour
preserved: portal anchoring to textareaRef, setTimeout-based caret restore,
conditional rendering when picker is open + has agents.

Also extract the identical buildMentionSearchMocks Apollo MockedResponse
builder from ChatTray.ct.tsx and CorpusChat.ct.tsx into
frontend/tests/utils/mentionSearchMocks.ts so the two surfaces stay in
lockstep when useUnifiedMentionSearch adds resource categories.

All 62 ChatTray + CorpusChat CT tests still pass.

* Render attribution chip in pinned sub-agent ChatMessage bubble

* Render agent chip on timeline entries that carry agent_slug

When the conductor delegates to a sub-agent via a `delegate_to_<slug>`
tool call (pinned or unpinned), the corresponding tool_call /
tool_result rows on the assistant's timeline now display a styled
`@<slug>` chip in place of the raw tool name. The chip palette mirrors
the Task 12 sub-agent bubble attribution chip so users learn one
"this is an agent" shape across inline mentions, pinned bubbles, and
timeline rows.

The renderer reads the slug from an explicit `agentSlug` field
forwarded by the StreamRelay on ASYNC_THOUGHT frames; it also falls
back to parsing the persisted `delegate_to_<snake_slug>` tool name so
the chip works on server-loaded conversations whose timeline JSON
predates explicit agent metadata.

Closes Task 13 of issue #623 / #689.

* Show requesting agent attribution on approval modal

When ASYNC_APPROVAL_NEEDED carries a `requesting_agent` payload (a
sub-agent invocation raised the approval), the modal now renders an
`@<slug>` attribution chip in place of the plain "Tool: <name>" header.
The chip palette mirrors the inline `@agent` mention chip in
MarkdownMessageRenderer and the bubble-header chip in ChatMessage.styles
for consistent agent-identity cues across attribution surfaces.

Wiring:
- `MessageData.data.requesting_agent` extended in chat/types.ts.
- `PendingApproval` extended in both ApprovalOverlay (ChatTray) and
  ApprovalModal (CorpusChat) with optional `requestingAgent`.
- ChatTray plumbs from WS frames and from persisted-message priming.
- CorpusChat plumbs from WS frames (no priming path is wired yet).

Backward compatibility: existing approvals without `requesting_agent`
continue to render the plain "Tool: <name>" header.

* Consolidate shared agent attribution types, components, and helpers

Earlier rich-mention agent delegation tasks each introduced their
own copy of the same plumbing across ChatTray (document chat) and
CorpusChat (corpus chat) surfaces. Six things had drifted:

- ``PendingApproval`` interface duplicated in ``ApprovalOverlay.tsx``
  and ``ApprovalModal.tsx``.
- ``AgentChip`` + ``RequestingAgentLine`` styled-components + their
  rendering JSX duplicated (~44 LOC) in both approval surfaces.
- ``appendThoughtToMessage`` body (the 5-field projection of an
  ASYNC_THOUGHT frame onto a ``TimelineEntry``) duplicated in both
  chat hosts — including the Task 13 ``agentId``/``agentSlug``
  fields that had to be added to both sides independently.
- No unit-test coverage on ``getAgentSlugFromTimelineEntry`` despite
  it being the gatekeeper for the rich-mention timeline chip.
- No parity ``CorpusChat`` test for the timeline ``@agent`` chip;
  Task 13 had only landed the ``ChatTray`` version.

This commit:

- Promotes ``PendingApproval`` into ``components/chat/types.ts`` and
  has both modals import from there (with a backwards-compat
  re-export from each modal file).
- Adds ``components/chat/RequestingAgentAttribution.tsx``, a single
  shared component that owns the chip's styled-component + JSX
  rendering and the ``data-testid="approval-requesting-agent"``
  contract. Both modals now render it.
- Adds ``components/widgets/chat/timelineEntryFactory.ts`` with
  pure helpers (``deriveTimelineEntryType``,
  ``buildTimelineEntryFromAsyncThought``) and wires both
  ``ChatTray`` and ``CorpusChat`` ``appendThoughtToMessage`` to
  them. Compaction side-effect (the ``setCompactionNotice`` banner
  call) stays at the call sites because it touches each host's
  component state.
- Adds vitest coverage for ``getAgentSlugFromTimelineEntry`` (both
  branches: explicit ``agentSlug`` and the regex fallback) and for
  the new factory helpers.
- Adds a ``CorpusChat`` parity CT test for the timeline ``@agent``
  chip, plus the matching ``"delegate unpinned please"`` WS stub
  branch.

Net source change: the two approval modals lose ~216 LOC of
duplicated code; the new shared modules add ~137 LOC. Production
code shrinks by ~79 LOC despite the type / component / helper
extraction. Unit + CT test coverage is net positive.

* Add E2E delegation scenarios and documentation screenshots

Adds end-to-end coverage for the rich-mention agent delegation
scenarios that hadn't been exercised yet at the CT level:

- WebSocket stub branches for ``"delegate pinned please"`` in both
  the ChatTray and CorpusChat test stubs. These document the wire
  payload the conductor emits when delegating to a pinned sub-agent
  (conductor's tool_call ASYNC_THOUGHT + sub-agent's own ASYNC_START
  /CONTENT/FINISH stream on a separate ``message_id`` with
  ``parent_message_id`` set + conductor's wrap-up
  tool_result/FINISH).
- CorpusChat ``"pinned delegation surfaces sub-agent bubble with
  attribution chip on conversation load"`` test. Asserts the
  headline UX: when GET_CHAT_MESSAGES returns a conductor row
  (``agentConfiguration: null``) followed by a pinned sub-agent row
  (``agentConfiguration: <ag>``), the sub-agent bubble renders with
  exactly one ``data-testid="sub-agent-chip"`` attribution chip and
  the conductor's bubble renders without one.

Documentation screenshots (named per the
``area--component--state`` convention so the docs site can
reference them stably):

- ``chat--agent-mention--popover-open`` — the @-mention picker open
  in ChatTray after typing ``hello @res``.
- ``chat--agent-mention--pinned-bubble`` — the pinned sub-agent
  bubble + attribution chip in CorpusChat.
- ``chat--agent-mention--timeline-entry`` — the timeline ``@agent``
  chip in ChatTray.
- ``chat--agent-mention--approval-with-attribution`` — the
  approval modal with the sub-agent attribution chip in ChatTray.

Each docScreenshot call lives in exactly one test so the docs
site has a single canonical reference per state.

* Update CHANGELOG.md with rich-mention agent delegation

Documents the rich-mention agent delegation feature: per-turn
allowlist of @-mentioned agents promoted to conductor tools,
pinned-or-timeline sub-agent attribution, scoped sub-agent
context, approval bubbling with sub-agent attribution, and the
full list of new modules / GraphQL extensions / tests / docs
screenshots that landed across Tasks 1–15.

* Refresh chat screenshots regenerated by rich-mention CT runs

* Disable Framer Motion animations in CT screenshots and fix pinned/timeline capture timing

- Wrap children of ChatTray, CorpusChat, and ChatMessage test wrappers in
  ``<MotionConfig reducedMotion="always">`` so transform-based motion is
  killed and the doc-screenshots no longer capture mid-fade-in for the
  chat surfaces.
- ``docScreenshot`` now waits 400ms before capturing (configurable via
  ``motionSettleMs``) and passes ``animations: "disabled"`` to Playwright.
  The wait is required because Framer Motion v6 drives opacity through
  ``requestAnimationFrame`` — neither CSS-animation suppression via
  ``addStyleTag`` nor Playwright's ``animations: "disabled"`` (which
  fast-forwards CSS / WAAPI animations) is enough on its own. The fixed
  delay is the only reliable way to land the capture after the opacity
  has reached its final value.
- Move the ``docScreenshot`` calls for ``chat--agent-mention--pinned-bubble``
  and ``chat--agent-mention--timeline-entry`` to AFTER the chip visibility
  assertion, add a 300ms stability wait, and clip the capture to
  ``#conversation-indicator`` so the PNGs frame just the chat panel
  instead of the full viewport.
- Add an ``element``-aware screenshot path with ``animations: "disabled"``
  to ``docScreenshot`` and the matching ``releaseScreenshot``.
- Regenerate the affected PNGs under ``docs/assets/images/screenshots/auto/``.
  All 87 ChatTray / CorpusChat / ChatMessage CT tests still pass.

* Improve chat empty state, popover spacing, and context meter layout

- Add centered icon+title+description empty state to ChatTray and CorpusChat
  when a new conversation has no messages, replacing the previous blank void
  between the header and the textarea
- Extend mention popover bottom offset (6 → 12px) so the picker no longer
  visually crams against the textarea
- Add bottom padding under the context usage meter so the meter no longer
  touches the textarea below it
- Fix CorpusChat send button looking permanently disabled: pass `$hasText`
  to EnhancedSendButton (it was missing) and gate the bounce animation on
  the same predicate as the disabled state, so the button now switches to
  the active blue gradient when the textarea has content

* Move rich_mentions plan into architecture docs and refresh screenshots

docs/plans/rich_mentions.md was the in-flight planning notebook for this
feature; the authoritative description now lives under
docs/architecture/rich_mentions.md alongside other architecture docs.
Also picks up two CT-regenerated screenshots for the agent-mention
attribution surfaces.

* Ratchet any baseline to 438

* Address review: get_running_loop, slim wire chip, drop dead-weight param

- Use ``asyncio.get_running_loop()`` instead of ``get_event_loop()`` in
  ``_build_stream_relay_factory.on_approval`` — the consumer always runs
  inside an active loop and ``get_event_loop()`` is deprecation-warning
  prone on 3.10+.
- Drop the internal DB pk from the ``agent_chip`` wire payload in
  ``ASYNC_APPROVAL_NEEDED`` / ``requesting_agent``. Consumers only
  attribute by slug; the frontend type and tests are updated to match.
- Simplify ``useChatMentionPicker``: expose ``mention.onValueChange``
  directly instead of wrapping it in a no-op ``useCallback`` (the
  underlying callback identity is already stable), and lift the
  textarea-anchored popover position into a ``useMemo`` keyed on
  ``mention.isOpen`` so we don't read the DOM on every render.
- Remove the unused ``conversation`` parameter from
  ``build_delegation_tool`` (per CLAUDE.md "no dead code"); call sites
  in the consumer and the delegation-tools test suite are updated.

Dismissed (with reasoning, not applied):
- Possessive ``++`` regex requires 3.11+ — project pins Python 3.11.15
  in Dockerfiles, so this is fine.
- ``extra_tools`` "replaces" defaults — verified in
  ``PydanticAIDocumentAgent.create`` / ``deduplicate_tools``: caller
  tools are merged on top of defaults, not substituted.
- ``role="option"`` missing — ``AgentMentionPopover`` already sets
  ``role="option"`` (and ``aria-selected``) on each option button.

* Address review feedback: tighten IDOR, race guards, persistence flag

- Plug conversation_id IDOR in create_for_document/create_for_corpus:
  resolve through visible_to_user instead of bare aget(id=cid). Same
  fallback semantics on miss as DoesNotExist, so a caller cannot
  enumerate other users' conversation ids by probing.
- Plug agent_id IDOR in UnifiedAgentConsumer._resolve_agent_config:
  filter the explicit-agent lookup through visible_to_user so a caller
  can't load another user's private CORPUS-scoped agent by guessing
  the pk.
- Re-validate document/corpus access on every delegation tool
  invocation (ORM instances are captured at tool-build time and could
  go stale if permissions are revoked mid-turn).
- Surface pinned ChatMessage persistence failure in the ASYNC_FINISH
  frame via `persistence_failed: true` so the UI can warn the user
  the bubble is session-only and will not survive a reload.
- Add regression tests covering the IDOR fixes and an
  agent-not-visible-to-user rejection at the consumer level.

* Address review feedback: guard, chip palette, picker keyboard nav

- filter_by_scope: replace ``assert document_id is not None`` with an
  explicit guard so the scope-resolution path can't disappear under
  ``python -O``.
- StreamRelay: tighten ``relay_factory`` return type from
  ``StreamRelay | None`` to ``StreamRelay`` in ``build_delegation_tool``
  and the consumer's ``_factory``; the production factory always
  constructs a relay. Test helper ``_make_noop_relay`` added.
- mention_extractor: replace O(n^2) ``any(...)`` dedupe scan with a
  ``(type, slug, corpus_slug)`` set lookup so legacy ``@corpus:``/
  ``@document:`` matches dedupe in O(1) against earlier markdown
  results.
- Agent attribution palette extracted to a shared ``agentChipPaletteCss``
  fragment (sourced from new ``OS_LEGAL_COLORS.agentChipViolet`` /
  ``agentChipText`` tokens). The bubble-header, timeline, and approval-
  modal chips now compose one definition.
- AgentMentionPopover: add ArrowUp/ArrowDown navigation, Enter-to-select,
  active-row ``aria-selected`` + ``scrollIntoView``. Document-level
  capture-phase keydown listener so the textarea (still focused) doesn't
  consume the keys. CT coverage in AgentMentionPopover.ct.tsx.
- ChatTray: replace inline ``requesting_agent`` cast with
  ``PendingApproval["requestingAgent"]`` so the persisted-message and
  live-WebSocket frame shapes share one type definition.

* Address Claude follow-ups: URL test, regex note, approval guard

- ``test_mention_extractor.py``: pin the 5-part corpus-agent URL form
  (``/c/{creator}/{corpus}/agents/{slug}``) so the contract documented
  in ``_classify_url`` is mechanically enforced.
- ``mention_extractor.py``: note that the ``++`` possessive quantifier
  in ``_LEGACY_CORPUS_RE`` requires Python 3.11+ (the production
  runtime) and suggest the atomic-group rewrite for older versions.
- ``unified_agent_conversation.py`` ``on_approval``: turn the
  "one sub-agent per turn per ``(parent_message_id, agent.pk)`` key"
  invariant from a comment into a runtime check. If a duplicate
  future is registered, cancel the prior one and log loud so a
  future refactor doesn't silently leak a Future.

Also refresh the three auto-generated agent-mention documentation
screenshots that regenerated during this round of CT runs.

* Address second round of review: dead branches, monkey-patch, N+1

- Drop unreachable ``if relay is None`` branches in
  ``delegation_tools._body``; collapse ``if pin and relay is not None``
  to ``if pin``.
- Replace the monkey-patched ``_factory._parent_message_id_box``
  attribute with an explicit kwarg on ``_stream_agent_response``.
  ``handle_query`` now owns the shared box and threads it directly to
  the stream helper, removing the ``getattr``/``type: ignore`` pair.
- Eliminate the N+1 in ``resolve_mentions_for_user``: one batched
  ``slug__in`` / ``id__in`` lookup per mention type plus two batched
  ``DocumentPath`` queries collapse the per-mention DB hits into pure
  dict lookups.
- ``on_approval`` parent-id-None branch now sets ``_error`` so the
  delegation body surfaces a real failure instead of an empty result.
- Add adversarial cross-user IDOR test for
  ``_aget_conversation_visible_to_user`` (plus owner / anonymous /
  bogus-id edges) in ``TestAgetConversationVisibleToUser``.
- Surface backend ``persistence_failed`` flag via ``console.warn`` in
  both chat surfaces so the in-memory-only state is visible in dev
  tools; a non-blocking toast is a follow-up.
- Document ``filter_by_scope`` as sync-context only.
- Add a ``sys.version_info`` guard at the top of ``mention_extractor``
  so the ``++`` possessive quantifier requirement fails loud instead
  of producing an unhelpful ``multiple repeat`` traceback on 3.10.
- Fix stale module reference in ``agentMentionLink.ts``: link to
  ``mention_extractor._classify_url`` (the real source).

* Misc hardening and cleanup

- ChatTray: prune leftover console.log debug statements.
- useChatMentionPicker: memoise onSelect so the popover's keydown effect
  doesn't re-bind on every parent render.
- AgentConfiguration: expose SCOPE_GLOBAL / SCOPE_CORPUS constants;
  delegation filter_by_scope now uses them instead of raw strings.
- mention_extractor: pin corpus-agent URL pattern to exactly 4 or 5
  parts so paths like /c/x/agents/foo/agents/bar don't mis-match.
- delegation_tools: when an approval cycle has no sub-agent message id,
  return an explicit error to the conductor instead of falling through
  to on_finish and shipping partial accumulated text as "success".
- users.checks (auth0 superuser allowlist): list eligible superusers
  (pk, username, email) in the system-check message so operators can
  populate AUTH0_SUPERUSER_SUB_ALLOWLIST without guessing; capped at 20.
- Tests cover the URL-pattern pin, the explicit delegation failure,
  and the new superuser identity surfacing.

* Fix migration-seeded agents with NULL slug crashing @mention picker

Root cause: ``create_default_action_templates`` resolves the model via
``apps.get_model()`` so the same function is callable from both a data
migration and the ``seed_action_templates`` management command. In
migration context that registry returns a historical model class which
does NOT carry the live ``save()`` override that auto-generates a slug.
Migrations 0010 and 0011 therefore created six template-owned global
agents with ``slug=NULL``. The @mention picker's
``AgentMentionPopover.matches`` filter dereferenced ``a.slug`` and blew
up with ``can't access property "toLowerCase", a.slug is null``.

Three-layer fix so a future seeder regression cannot reach the UI:

- ``template_seeds._build_unique_agent_slug`` re-implements the same
  slug algorithm and is called explicitly when seeding each agent.
- New migration ``0013_backfill_and_tighten_agent_slug`` backfills any
  existing NULL slugs (mirroring the 0005 algorithm so prior deployments
  heal in place) and then ``AlterField``s the column to ``null=False``.
- Model comment pins WHY ``blank=True`` is kept (the live save override
  fills the value before super-save) but ``null=False`` is non-negotiable.

Verified on the local DB: all six previously-NULL agents now resolve
to kebab-case slugs (e.g. ``document-description-updater-agent``).

Tests: new ``test_seeded_agent_configs_have_non_null_slugs`` pins the
seeder contract. Full ``test_corpus_action_template``, ``test_agents``,
``test_mention_parser``, ``test_delegation_tools`` and
``test_mention_extractor`` suites pass (121 tests).

* Fix @mention picker invisible on bare @ / 1-char fragment

``useUnifiedMentionSearch`` gated all 5 category queries behind
``MENTION_SEARCH_MIN_CHARS`` (=2) and ``useChatMentionPicker`` hid the
popover until ``agentItems.length > 0``. Combined, typing just ``@``
(or ``@a``) produced no UI at all — same code in CorpusChat and the
document-side ChatTray, but the user only noticed it in ChatTray
because they happened to type more characters in the corpus chat.

The agent list is intentionally tiny (templates + a few per corpus)
and should behave like Slack / GitHub / Discord mention pickers —
visible the instant ``@`` is typed. Fix:

- ``useUnifiedMentionSearch`` fires the agent search on every debounced
  fragment regardless of length; the other four open-ended resolvers
  (users / corpuses / documents / annotations) stay gated because
  ``icontains`` scans over open sets are the perf reason the gate
  existed in the first place.
- ``useChatMentionPicker`` drops the ``agentItems.length > 0``
  precondition so the popover renders whenever the trigger is open,
  letting ``AgentMentionPopover``'s "No matching agents." empty state
  actually surface in the live UI.

New CT test pins the bare-``@`` flow. The pre-existing ``@res`` test
still passes because ``pressSequentially`` finishes inside the 300ms
debounce window, so only the final ``"res"`` fragment hits the network
either way.

* Fix @mention picker invisible in document ChatTray (z-index bug)

The popover anchor portalled to document.body with zIndex: 1000 was
silently rendering BEHIND the DocumentKnowledgeBase's
.fullscreen-modal-overlay (Z_INDEX.APP_MODAL = 3000). The user saw the
picker in dev tools (sized correctly at 441.6 × 110.4) but the modal
overlay above it covered the visible output.

This explains why CorpusChat worked despite sharing the same hook —
CorpusChat is not mounted inside the DKB fullscreen modal, so any
z-index above the page content (1000 included) was fine. Document
context required > 3000.

Bumped the anchor to Z_INDEX.APP_MODAL_CHILD (3100), the existing
semantic slot for popovers nested inside the DKB modal. Pinned by a
regression assertion in the bare-@ ChatTray CT test that reads the
computed z-index off the anchor and asserts > 3000 — so a future
refactor that lowers it breaks the test rather than the picker.

* Wire @mention picker into InlineChatBar (CorpusHome landing bar)

InlineChatBar — the corpus-landing / article-floating chat bar — now
accepts an optional ``corpusId`` prop. When provided, it threads its
existing ``inputRef`` through ``useChatMentionPicker`` (the shared hook
already powering ChatTray and CorpusChat) and renders the portaled
popover at the same z-index slot, so typing ``@`` from the landing
chat input (``data-testid="corpus-home-landing-chat-input"``) and from
the article-floating controls (``data-testid="corpus-article-chat-input"``)
opens the rich-mention agent picker, narrows on the fragment, and
splices the markdown ``[@slug](/agents/slug)`` link on selection — same
contract as the other surfaces.

Both ``CorpusHome`` and ``CorpusHome/CorpusLandingView`` plumb
``corpus.id`` to the bar. The hook is a no-op when ``corpusId`` is
omitted, so any future caller mounting the bar outside a corpus
context pays no UX cost.

Pinned by a new ``CorpusHome.ct.tsx`` test that mounts the full
landing view, types a bare ``@``, and asserts the popover surfaces
with the mocked agent visible. ``buildMentionSearchMocks`` is added
to the default ``mocks`` array so other landing-view tests stop
warning about an unmocked ``searchAgentsForMention`` query that now
fires on mount.

* Bound chats tab to viewport so input pins to the bottom

Two coupled changes that together let the corpus chats tab behave like
a chat surface (messages scroll internally, input pinned to the bottom)
instead of expanding the page to fit every message:

- ``NavMenu`` mounts a ``NavbarHeightSync`` helper that observes the
  real ``.oc-navbar`` element with a ResizeObserver and writes its
  ``offsetHeight`` into the global ``--oc-navbar-height`` CSS variable.
  ``index.css`` seeds the variable with a static 72px / 60px estimate,
  but the navbar uses ``padding: 12px 24px; flex-wrap: wrap`` so the
  real height shifts with content/wrapping/breakpoint. Anything that
  subtracts the variable from 100vh (chat tab, corpus container,
  composer max-height) was losing a few pixels and gaining a
  scrollable strip below the viewport.

- ``Corpuses.tsx`` wraps the chats tab in a viewport-bounded flex
  column (``height/maxHeight: calc(var(--oc-visible-viewport-height,
  100vh) - var(--oc-navbar-height, 4.5rem))``, ``minHeight: 0``,
  ``overflow: hidden``) with an inner ``flex: 1; minHeight: 0`` slot
  for ``CorpusChat`` so its ``MessagesArea`` ``overflow-y: auto``
  finally has a fixed parent to scroll against. The tab also zeroes
  ``CardLayout`` padding and suppresses the SearchBar for this view —
  both contributed vertical overhead that previously pushed the chat
  past the viewport.

* Refresh auto-generated documentation screenshots

Local CT test runs during this session regenerated several auto
screenshots — the agent @mention popover now has more content (bare-@
opens the full list), the CorpusHome landing/article views shifted
slightly from the chat-tab/navbar-height layout changes, and the
discussions/mode-toggle previews moved with the surrounding flex
geometry. The ``screenshots.yml`` CI workflow is on-demand only, so
committing these now keeps the README / quickstart in sync without
waiting for a manual workflow_dispatch.

* Fix CI linter failures

- black formatting on template_seeds.py and checks.py
- mypy: AgentConfiguration.slug expects str, pass empty string to trigger save() auto-generation instead of None

* Address Claude review feedback on PR #1651

- consumer: force conductor rebuild on turn after delegation tools were
  attached, preventing stale delegate_to_<slug> tools from leaking into
  subsequent mention-less turns (Claude review Issue 1)
- consumer: document the tool-merge semantics of _initialize_agent's
  extra_tools (Claude review Issue 2 - already merges via deduplicate_tools)
- delegation_tools: document that DB unique-constraint on slug is the sole
  guard against _slug_to_snake_case tool-name collisions (Issue 3)
- mention_extractor: add explanatory comment for intentional fallback in
  _decode_annotation_id base64 except clause (CodeQL)
- useAgentMentionTrigger: drop unused caretPos from public interface (Issue 7)
- test: scope AUTH_OK drain except to asyncio.TimeoutError (CodeQL)
- test: remove unused mountResult variable in CorpusHome.ct.tsx (CodeQL)
- test: add coverage for stale-delegation-tools regression

* Add delegation_tools.py coverage for race-guard and resume-cycle branches

Adds 16 new test cases covering previously-uncovered branches in
build_delegation_tool:
- for_document factory path (previously only for_corpus was exercised)
- no doc/corpus context warning branch
- agent visibility race-guard (still_visible=False)
- document/corpus accessibility race-guards
- factory raising operationally vs propagating PermissionError
- thought event forwarding through relay
- error event aborting stream
- final-only accumulated_content fallback (non-streaming path)
- on_finish raising during pin=True
- non-dict approval decision coerced to denial
- resume cycle yielding error event
- resume_with_approval raising

Backend patch coverage on delegation_tools.py rises from 79.57% to 99%.

* Address Claude review: clarify approval-routing invariant

- Add explanatory comment at the first-match break in
  _handle_approval_decision making the single-threaded asyncio invariant
  explicit (two sub-agents from one turn can't simultaneously await
  approval because relay.on_approval blocks the conductor's tool call).
- Black-formatted the new delegation tool body coverage tests.

* Address Claude review on PR #1651

- Drop dual-dispatch shim on `_stream_agent_response` in `receive()`. The
  method already accepts `parent_message_id_box: dict | None = None`, so
  pass it unconditionally (None when no delegation is active) instead of
  branching at the call site. Per CLAUDE.md's no-backwards-compat-shims
  rule. Test doubles in `test_unified_agent_consumer.py` widened to
  `(user_query, **_kwargs)` to accept the kwarg.

- Add runtime dedup guard for `delegate_to_<snake_slug>` tool-name
  collisions in `receive()`. `_slug_to_snake_case` maps both `my-agent`
  and `my_agent` to `delegate_to_my_agent`. `AgentConfiguration.save()`
  normalizes to `-` so the normal write path can't collide, but admin /
  fixture / management writes that bypass save() (e.g. `QuerySet.update`)
  can. Dedup by tool name and log loud so the underlying data issue stays
  visible. Adds regression `test_snake_case_slug_collision_dedupes_to_single_tool`.

- `# pragma: no cover` on two unreachable defensive branches in
  `delegation_tools.py` (`filter_by_scope` post-outer-guard `document_id
  is None`; resume-loop pre-iteration `_error` short-circuit). Both are
  load-bearing future-proofing — kept defensively but excluded from
  coverage since current control flow can't reach them.

subject: Decompose ChatTray.tsx into thinner composer + sibling hooks (#1639)
message:
Decompose ChatTray.tsx into thinner composer + sibling hooks (#1639)

* Decompose ChatTray.tsx into thin composer + sibling hooks (refs #1446)

Next slice of the multi-PR decomposition tracked by #1446 (after #1459 /
ModernDocumentItem, #1578 / Corpuses, #1586 / ChatMessage, #1580 /
DocumentKnowledgeBase partial).

frontend/src/components/knowledge_base/document/right_tray/ChatTray.tsx had
grown to 1,815 lines. Unlike prior decompositions it owned no inline
styled-components or React sub-components — its weight was concentrated in
stateful handler functions. Three hook extractions land it at 1,160 lines
(-36%):

- useChatStreamHandlers.ts (new): bundles the six chat-state mutators
  (updateMessageApprovalStatus, appendStreamingTokenToChat,
  appendThoughtToMessage, finalizeStreamingResponse, handleCompleteMessage,
  mergeSourcesIntoMessage). useMemo-stabilized return so callers can pass it
  as a single param without rebinding. Param surface kept free of
  documentId/corpusId so CorpusChat.tsx can adopt it in a follow-up.

- useChatAgentMessageHandler.ts (new): wraps the 188-line handleAgentMessage
  switch (10+ message types). Receives pendingApprovalRef (preserves the
  stale-closure escape hatch from the WebSocket subscription) plus the
  stream-handlers bundle.

- useChatSendHandlers.ts (new): bundles sendMessageOverSocket (debounced via
  sendingLockRef), sendApprovalDecision, and sendTextImmediately. Takes
  updateMessageApprovalStatus from the stream hook for optimistic approval UI.

- chatUtils.ts (extended): adds adjustTextareaHeight(textarea, maxHeight) as
  a pure DOM helper.

Behavior preserved verbatim. Public API (ChatTray named export and the
WebSocketSources / MessageData type re-exports) unchanged; importers need no
changes. All 27 ChatTray.ct.tsx tests + 7 ContextMeter.ct.tsx tests pass
without modification.

Render-body splitting is deferred to a follow-up PR — the natural sub-views
share a large overlapping prop surface that has no atom-friendly seam without
more preparatory work.

* Address PR #1639 review: strip debug logs, drop dead code, consolidate send paths

- Remove XOXO debug + other console.log statements from useChatStreamHandlers and useChatAgentMessageHandler
- Drop unused width/isMobile/useWindowDimensions in ChatTray
- Drop reserved-but-unused setContextStatus param on useChatStreamHandlers
- Replace .substr(2) with .substring(2) (deprecated API)
- Factor shared body of sendMessageOverSocket/sendTextImmediately into sendTextOverSocket helper

* Add Vitest coverage for ChatTray composer hooks

Adds 69 unit tests across four files to lift codecov patch coverage
for the new hooks extracted in this PR. Exercises every public branch:

- useChatStreamHandlers (updateMessageApprovalStatus, appendStreamingTokenToChat,
  appendThoughtToMessage, finalizeStreamingResponse, handleCompleteMessage,
  mergeSourcesIntoMessage) — 99% statement / 92% branch coverage.
- useChatAgentMessageHandler (ASYNC_START / CONTENT / THOUGHT / SOURCES /
  APPROVAL_NEEDED / APPROVAL_RESULT / RESUME / FINISH / ERROR / SYNC_CONTENT
  plus malformed JSON guard and approval_decision side-channel) — 100% / 93%.
- useChatSendHandlers (sendMessageOverSocket lock + retry paths,
  sendApprovalDecision happy/failure branches, sendTextImmediately trim guard)
  — 98% / 96%.
- chatUtils (new adjustTextareaHeight DOM helper plus the previously-uncovered
  calculateMessageStats / getMessageCountColor utilities) — 100%.

* Remove explicit `any` from new ChatTray hook tests and `void _timelineData`

- Replaces 8 inline `updater: any` setters in the agent-message-handler test
  harness with a single generic `makeSetter<K extends keyof Harness>`
  helper that returns a properly-typed `React.Dispatch<SetStateAction<...>>`.
- Types the send-handler test\'s `wsSend` mock as
  `vi.fn<(payload: string) => boolean>` so `mock.calls[0][0]` is inferred
  as `string` and the three downstream `as any` casts drop.
- Drops a handful of unnecessary `as any` casts on already-valid literals
  (CompactionNotice, TimelineEntry, MessageData["data"]).
- Replaces the `void _timelineData;` no-op statement (flagged in the
  PR review) with a comment explaining that the `_`-prefix alone signals
  intent — no runtime statement needed.

Net effect on the project `any` baseline: 455 → 440 (-15), back below
the committed baseline.

* Address Claude review: drop no-op timelineData param, promote magic numbers to constants, fix vacuous sendTextImmediately assertion

- Drop the unused trailing 'timelineData' / '_timelineData' parameter from
  useChatStreamHandlers.handleCompleteMessage and finalizeStreamingResponse.
  ChatSourceAtom does not persist timelines (thought entries already live on
  the in-memory chat array via appendThoughtToMessage), so the parameter was a
  no-op that violated the project no-dead-code guideline. Update the three
  call sites in useChatAgentMessageHandler (ASYNC_FINISH, SYNC_CONTENT) and
  ChatTray (msgData hydration) plus the corresponding test expectations.

- Promote two pre-existing magic numbers in the new hooks to named constants
  in frontend/src/assets/configurations/constants.ts:
    * CHAT_AUTOSCROLL_THRESHOLD_PX (100) — used in
      useChatStreamHandlers.appendStreamingTokenToChat for the
      'is the user scrolled up?' check that suppresses auto-scroll.
    * CHAT_SEND_LOCK_MS (300) — used in useChatSendHandlers.sendTextOverSocket
      for the post-send debounce lock.

- Replace the vacuous newMessage assertion in the sendTextImmediately test:
  the harness initialised newMessage to '', so 'expect(newMessage).toBe("")'
  passed trivially regardless of behavior. Seed the harness with a non-empty
  draft so the 'sendTextImmediately must NOT clear newMessage' invariant is
  actually pinned.

* Address Claude review on PR #1639 + restore rich-mention timeline chip

- ``useChatSendHandlers`` now wraps its return object in ``useMemo`` so
  callers can include the bundle (or any single member) in dependency
  arrays without forcing a re-bind every render. Matches the contract
  of the sibling ``useChatStreamHandlers``.
- ``useChatAgentMessageHandler`` validates server-controlled
  approval-decision values at the dispatch boundary instead of
  scattering ``as "approved" | "rejected"`` casts across three branches.
  An unexpected value (typo, future ``deferred``, etc.) now silently
  no-ops instead of propagating an invalid status into
  ``updateMessageApprovalStatus`` and the chat row's ``approvalStatus``
  field, both of which only model the two-state shape.
- ``useChatStreamHandlers.appendThoughtToMessage`` now routes through
  ``buildTimelineEntryFromAsyncThought`` so the rich-mention
  ``agent_id`` / ``agent_slug`` hints from the StreamRelay land on the
  timeline entry. The previous inline projection (carried over from
  the pre-extraction state) silently dropped those fields, which broke
  the ``timeline entry with agent_slug renders @agent chip`` CT test
  after the merge: the renderer fell back to parsing
  ``delegate_to_<snake_slug>`` and produced ``@research_bot`` instead
  of the expected ``@research-bot``. With the factory wired up, both
  the ChatTray and CorpusChat variants of that CT pass.
- ``useChatAgentMessageHandler.test.tsx`` updated to reflect the new
  ``requestingAgent`` default introduced by the rich-mention merge
  fix-up.

* Address PR review: tighten dep array + clarify duplicate send guards

- useChatAgentMessageHandler: destructure inside the callback so the dep
  array references the memoized bundle (one entry) instead of six
  individual handler refs. Adds compactionNotice lifecycle note pointing
  to the write path in useChatStreamHandlers.
- useChatSendHandlers.sendMessageOverSocket: document the duplicate
  guards as the user-facing observability layer; sendTextOverSocket is
  the authoritative silent guard.
- Switch React.RefObject / React.Dispatch namespace types to named
  type-only imports.

subject: Phase A: Per-model Manager.user_can overrides + permission cache (#1663)
message:
Phase A: Per-model Manager.user_can overrides + permission cache (#1663)

* Phase A: per-model Manager.user_can overrides + deprecate user_has_permission_for_obj

Closes #1655. Follow-up to PR #1637 (Step 0 vertical slice).

Adds per-model `Manager.user_can(user, instance, permission)` overrides for every
visibility-managed model so the manager-side check stays aligned with its
`visible_to_user` filter:

  * `DocumentManager`         — thin delegate (default rules suffice)
  * `NoteManager`             — creator OR MIN(doc, corpus) composed via
                                Document/Corpus user_can
  * `UserFeedbackManager`     — adds `commented_annotation.is_public` READ branch
                                on top of the default rules
  * `RelationshipManager`     — superuser → structural-write-deny → MIN
                                (preserves the legacy decision to not consult
                                created_by_analysis/created_by_extract)
  * `AnnotationManager`       — superuser → structural-write-deny → privacy
                                recursion via Analysis/Extract user_can →
                                MIN via `AnnotationQueryOptimizer._compute_effective_permissions`
  * `ConversationManager`     — READ via `visible_to_user(...).filter(pk=).exists()`
                                so the CHAT/THREAD bifurcation stays the single
                                SoT; non-READ via `_default_user_can` so is_public
                                does NOT grant writes
  * `ChatMessageManager`      — same exists() trick to preserve the moderator
                                branch (corpus owner / document owner /
                                conversation creator)

Adds `opencontractserver/shared/permission_cache.py` — a ContextVar-backed
request-scoped read-only cache (`permission_cache_scope()`) keyed by
`(user_id, app_label, model_name, pk, permission, include_group_permissions)`.
Dormant outside scope; wired into `_default_user_can` at the guardian-lookup
boundary so any future request/Celery/WebSocket middleware can flip it on by
entering the scope. Skipped for unsaved instances (`pk is None`).

Completes `PermissionQuerySet.visible_to_user` to honor django-guardian
(previously creator/is_public only with a comment deferring guardian to
per-model overrides). Mirrors the guardian lookup from
`BaseVisibilityManager.visible_to_user` so `PermissionManager.user_can`
(inherited from `UserCanMixin → _default_user_can`) stays aligned with the
queryset filter for any direct consumer.

Demotes `user_has_permission_for_obj` to a ~15-line shim that emits
`DeprecationWarning(stacklevel=2)` and delegates to
`type(instance)._default_manager.user_can(...)`. The annotation/relationship
structural/privacy branches the function used to encode are now in the
respective `Manager.user_can` overrides. `include_group_permissions=False`
default is preserved verbatim. Migration of the ~170 existing callers tracked
in Phases B/C.

Deletes `user_can_modify_corpus`; migrates the 4 production callsites
(`config/graphql/document_mutations.py:327`, `config/graphql/badge_mutations.py:92,212,329`)
to `corpus.user_can(user, PermissionTypes.UPDATE)`.
`opencontractserver/tests/test_user_can_modify_corpus.py` is preserved and
re-pointed at the new API so the same matrix stays pinned.

BUG-FIX POSTURE (CHANGELOG `Fixed`): the recursive privacy check in
`AnnotationManager.user_can` now routes through `Analysis.objects.user_can` /
`Extract.objects.user_can` instead of the creator-blind
`user_has_permission_for_obj`. Previously a user who owned both an `Analysis`
AND a private annotation it created could be denied READ on their own
annotation because the recursive call ignored creator status. The same fix
is applied to `AnnotationQueryOptimizer._compute_effective_permissions`
(which the new `AnnotationManager.user_can` calls for the MIN(doc, corpus)
computation) — keeping it on the deprecated helper would have fired
`DeprecationWarning` on every annotation visibility check.

Extends `opencontractserver/tests/permissioning/test_authorization_invariants.py`
with 7 new `TransactionTestCase` classes (Document/Annotation/Relationship/
Note/Conversation/ChatMessage/UserFeedback) plus a shared
`_UserCanInvariantsMixin` that pins:

  * `Model.objects.user_can(u, obj, READ) == Model.objects.visible_to_user(u).filter(pk=obj.pk).exists()`
    across the (user × instance) cartesian product
  * manager / instance-surface parity (`Model.objects.user_can` == `obj.user_can`)
  * superuser bypass for every `PermissionTypes` member

Plus per-model invariants: is_public-grants-only-READ on Document;
structural-write-deny on Annotation and Relationship; privacy-recursion
honors-creator on Annotation; MIN visibility for Notes;
CHAT-no-context-inheritance and THREAD-inherits-corpus for Conversation;
moderator-via-corpus-ownership for ChatMessage; and the
`commented_annotation.is_public` READ grant (with no bleed into writes) for
UserFeedback. A `ShimDeprecationWarningTestCase` pins that
`user_has_permission_for_obj` emits `DeprecationWarning` and delegates
correctly.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01Qxqe3JJhs18hDipRboVpqf

* Apply black formatting and drop now-unused Corpus import

Black reformatting on the Phase A changes and removal of the dangling
``Corpus`` import in ``opencontractserver/utils/permissioning.py`` (it was
only used by the deleted ``user_can_modify_corpus``).

https://claude.ai/code/session_01Qxqe3JJhs18hDipRboVpqf

* Fix linter (pyupgrade/flake8/mypy) failures on PR #1663

- Remove now-unused typing.Optional import from permission_cache.py after
  pyupgrade rewrote the explicit `Optional[T]` annotations.
- Cast `instance._meta.{model_name,app_label}` to `str` before passing to
  cached_user_can/store_user_can (the Django stubs type these as
  `str | None` for abstract-model support).
- Add `type: ignore[attr-defined]` to the deprecation-shim's
  `manager.user_can(...)` call — Manager[Model] doesn't statically
  expose the runtime-provided method.
- In RelationshipManager.user_can, call `self.visible_to_user(user)`
  directly instead of `self.get_queryset().visible_to_user(user)` so
  mypy can resolve the method on the manager subclass.
- In _UserCanInvariantsMixin (test mixin), declare matrix attributes
  with proper typing and inherit from TransactionTestCase under
  TYPE_CHECKING so assertEqual/assertTrue resolve.

* Address Claude review comments on PR #1663

- UserFeedbackManager.user_can: replace `instance.commented_annotation.is_public`
  descriptor access (one DB hit per call without prefetch) with a targeted
  `Annotation.objects.filter(pk=commented_annotation_id, is_public=True).exists()`
  query gated on the FK id check. Bulk callers iterating feedback rows would
  otherwise issue one extra query per item.
- AnnotationManager.user_can: document the privacy-recursion path's FK
  dereferences (`created_by_analysis`, `created_by_extract`) and the
  `select_related` recommendation for bulk callers.
- NoteManager.user_can: document the document/corpus FK dereferences and the
  `select_related` recommendation for bulk callers.
- permission_cache: clarify Phase A activation status (no production caller
  wraps work in `permission_cache_scope()` yet; this PR ships the primitive)
  and that nested scopes do NOT inherit parent-scope cached entries.

* Align visible_to_user with user_can for Note, Relationship, UserFeedback

Phase A introduced `Manager.user_can` for Note, Relationship, and
UserFeedback that implement MIN(doc, corpus) with guardian-aware
visibility. The corresponding `visible_to_user` filters were narrower —
they only checked creator/is_public — so a user with explicit guardian
READ grants on the parent doc + corpus passed user_can but was excluded
from visible_to_user. The Phase A invariant test
(`user_can(READ) == visible_to_user.filter(pk=).exists()`) flagged this
mismatch.

Changes:

- NoteQuerySet.visible_to_user: compose visibility via the
  Document/Corpus managers (`visible_to_user`) instead of inlining
  is_public/creator checks. Now honours full creator/public/guardian
  rules on doc and corpus, matching NoteManager.user_can.

- UserFeedbackQuerySet.visible_to_user: extend the `commented_annotation
  is_public` READ grant to the anonymous branch so it matches
  UserFeedbackManager.user_can. Add an explicit guardian READ filter for
  authenticated users to match the default branch's guardian check.

- RelationshipManager.visible_to_user: replace the fallback through
  BaseVisibilityManager (which falls back to creator/public when the
  non-existent `relationshipuserobjectpermission` table is missing) with
  an explicit MIN(doc, corpus) filter composed via the Document and
  Corpus managers. Mirrors RelationshipManager.user_can's MIN logic.

Resolves the three failing `test_read_equivalence_across_user_matrix`
invariants. All 61 tests in test_authorization_invariants.py now pass.

* Fix test_default_path_still_removes_existing_perms to use non-creator subject

Phase A's `user_has_permission_for_obj` shim routes through
`Manager.user_can` which applies the creator short-circuit. Testing
the corpus creator's downgrade from ALL→READ left UPDATE returning True
because the creator passes every permission regardless of guardian
state, masking the behaviour this test pins (actual clearance of
explicit guardian permissions on downgrade).

Switch to a non-creator `shared_user` so the test exercises the
sharing-flow scenario it was meant to cover. The intent — pinning that
the default path clears prior guardian perms — is preserved.

* Update test_anonymous_sees_only_public for Phase A visibility broadening

UserFeedbackQuerySet.visible_to_user now grants anonymous READ access
when the feedback comments on a public annotation, matching the
`commented_annotation.is_public` branch in UserFeedbackManager.user_can.
This aligns the queryset filter and manager check (the Phase A
invariant) and is the intended behaviour the invariant test pins.

The fixture's `private_feedback_public_ann` (private feedback on a
public annotation) is now visible to anonymous users; the assertion
shape is updated to reflect that while still pinning that feedback on
a PRIVATE annotation remains invisible to anonymous users.

* Fix structural-write-deny in AnnotationQueryOptimizer; update DocumentAnalysisRow test for creator-bypass

Two test failures in CI revealed two correctness gaps introduced by the
Phase A permission refactor:

1. AnnotationQueryOptimizer was annotating ALL annotations with the
   document/corpus effective permissions uniformly, but the
   AnnotationManager.user_can rule says non-superusers must never get
   write permissions on structural annotations. Switched _can_update /
   _can_delete to a CASE WHEN structural=True THEN False that matches
   the manager-level rule.

2. test_document_analysis_row_permissions exercised partial-grant
   semantics (READ + UPDATE granted, DELETE denied) against the row's
   creator. Phase A intentionally short-circuits the creator path in
   _default_user_can (creator auto-receives all permissions), so the
   test now uses a non-creator user to exercise the same invariant
   meaningfully.

* Address Claude review on PR #1663 and close codecov patch gaps

- Extract shared `resolve_user_for_user_can` helper (Claude review #1 DRY)
  used by every per-model user_can override and `_default_user_can`.
- Shim `user_has_permission_for_obj` raises TypeError with an actionable
  message for managers that haven't implemented user_can yet (Claude review
  #2) instead of a confusing AttributeError.
- Drop unexplained `.order_by("created")` from `PermissionQuerySet.visible_to_user`
  superuser branch (Claude review #7) — not every model that uses
  PermissionManager has a `created` column.
- New `test_authorization_invariants_coverage.py` (46 cases) walks the
  codecov-flagged leaf branches: the permission_cache machinery (cache
  patch coverage 73.91% → 100%), the `created_by_extract` privacy
  recursion partner test, the RelationshipManager access-widening case
  with a stranger holding doc+corpus READ (Claude review #3), the
  PermissionQuerySet fallback body, and the shim TypeError/DoesNotExist
  guards.

* Address Claude review on PR #1663

- Strengthen ``permission_cache_scope`` docstring with an explicit
  mutation-invalidation contract paragraph so Phase B activators don't
  have to bounce up to the module-level header to learn that mid-scope
  writes leave stale boolean answers in the cache.
- Add a TODO(Phase-C) note on ``RelationshipManager.user_can``
  spelling out that the missing analysis/extract privacy recursion is
  an intentional deferral, not an oversight.
- Cover three previously-untested branches in
  ``AnnotationUserCanLeafBranchesTestCase``:
  * ``document_id=None`` + READ → falls through to the
    ``visible_to_user`` exists() check (partner to the existing
    non-READ deny test).
  * Orphaned ``created_by_analysis`` FK (id set but row deleted) →
    privacy recursion returns False for every non-superuser caller.
  * Superuser bypass still wins on a ``document_id=None`` annotation
    (branch order intact).

* Address PR review: fix resolver ValueError, relationship creator gap, log flood

- resolve_user_for_user_can now catches ValueError alongside DoesNotExist;
  GraphQL global ids, empty strings, and non-numeric labels deny instead
  of propagating an uncaught Django PK-coercion error.
- RelationshipManager.user_can: add creator short-circuit aligned with
  the Q(creator=user) clause in visible_to_user, restricted to the
  permission codes Relationship recognises so PUBLISH/PERMISSION still
  fall through to False. Structural-write-deny still runs first.
- user_has_permission_for_obj shim: throttle DeprecationWarning to once
  per unique call site per process to keep production logs usable during
  the Phase B migration window.
- Add coverage tests:
    * ResolveUserForUserCanInvalidStringTestCase pins the ValueError
      catch and the per-model deny-not-raise contract.
    * RelationshipNonOwnerCreatorTestCase pins the creator short-circuit
      under share-then-revoke and structural-write-deny precedence.

* Address review: hoist creator short-circuit, log invalid user ids, doc N+1

Items 1-4 from the most recent Claude review on PR #1663:

- _CREATOR_SHORT_CIRCUIT_PERMS hoisted to a module-level frozenset so the
  Relationship user_can hot path no longer reallocates the tuple per call.
- resolve_user_for_user_can now emits a WARNING when ValueError fires —
  the unified contract still maps the failure to a deny so callers don't
  have to wrap every site, but the defect (typically a GraphQL global id
  reaching user_can without from_global_id) shows up in logs instead of
  being swallowed silently.
- Extend the performance note on AnnotationManager.user_can to cover the
  anonymous-path queryset.filter().exists() round-trip so bulk callers
  know to use visible_to_user(anon).filter(pk__in=[...]) directly.
- Add a TODO(issue #1655) on permission_cache_scope tying the dormant
  scope to its Phase B activation tracking issue.

subject: Fix Auth0 admin login race condition in SDK initialization (#1670)
message:
Fix Auth0 admin login race condition in SDK initialization (#1670)

* Fix Auth0 SDK loading race on Django admin login

The admin login page surfaced "Auth0 unavailable (security check failed)"
on every load. The SRI hash matched the live CDN file and CSP was
correctly configured — the failure was actually a race condition.

The template had two consecutive inline <script> blocks. The first used
document.createElement('script') to inject the SDK with an SRI hash, but
that path is implicitly async=true per the HTML spec. The second block
called initAuth0() synchronously, so `typeof auth0 === 'undefined'` was
true and the misleading "SRI check may have failed" message fired even
though nothing was wrong with the integrity hash.

Merged the two scripts into a single nonce'd block and wired
sdkScript.addEventListener('load', initAuth0) alongside the existing
error listener, attached BEFORE insertBefore so a cached SDK cannot fire
load before we listen. Removed the now-dead `typeof auth0 === 'undefined'`
defensive check inside initAuth0 and the synchronous initAuth0() call
that triggered the race. Tightened the handleScriptError log message
from "SRI check may have failed" to "network or SRI check" since after
the refactor it only fires from the script element's error event, which
triggers on any real load failure.

New regression test TestAdminLoginView.test_auth0_sdk_load_listener_wired
asserts that both listeners attach before insertBefore and that no
synchronous initAuth0() call remains in the rendered template.

* Apply black formatting to test_admin_auth.py

* Address review: make initAuth0() assertion whitespace-insensitive

The previous assertNotIn("\n        initAuth0();\n", body) depended on
the exact 8-space indentation in the rendered template — a re-indent
would silently bypass the check. Drop the surrounding whitespace and
match only the bare invocation form; `initAuth0` legitimately appears
as `async function initAuth0()` and `addEventListener('load',
initAuth0)`, so `initAuth0();` only matches the synchronous call
site we want to forbid. Clarify the comment along with it.

subject: Add pii_scanner_privacy_filter analyzer + lift analyzer-app coverage (#1672)
message:
Add pii_scanner_privacy_filter analyzer + lift analyzer-app coverage (#1672)

* Add pii_scanner_privacy_filter analyzer + lift analyzer-app coverage

Wraps the existing privacy-filter `adetect_pii` client in a new
`@async_doc_analyzer_task` so PII scanning is invokable through
`startAnalysisOnDoc` (i.e. the standard analyzer UI/GraphQL path),
not just through the chat-sidebar agent tool `scan_and_annotate_pii`.

Underlying client already chunks (40 KB chunks, 500-char overlap)
and de-duplicates across overlaps, so the task hands the full
document text to `adetect_pii` and trusts the contract. Pre-creates
the emitted-group AnnotationLabel rows with the canonical
text/colour/icon from `ENTITY_GROUP_LABELS` so labels are visually
identical to those created by the agent tool. Single configurable
knob `min_score` surfaced via `input_schema`. Auto-registered via
the existing `auto_create_doc_analyzers` flow (migration 0009 +
startup hook); no new migration.

Companion coverage work lifts the lowest-coverage backend app:

* `test_pii_scanner_analyzer_task.py` (new, 11 tests): SPAN_LABEL
  on text, TOKEN_LABEL on PDF (via PlasmaPDF), `min_score`
  filtering, unknown-group skip, OOB-span skip, empty-extract
  failure path, `RuntimeError` from the service, unsupported file
  type, label colour/icon parity, registration via the auto
  -create utility.

* `test_analyzer_app_coverage.py` (new, 27 tests): direct unit
  tests for `signals.install_gremlin_on_creation` (chain assembly
  under `transaction.on_commit`, no-op on update),
  `signals.handle_analysis_completion` (pins the current
  `status == 'COMPLETE'` literal match and documents the mismatch
  with `JobStatus.COMPLETED.value`), `checks.check_unsynced_analyzers`
  (warning emitted / silent / exception swallowed / non-doc tasks
  skipped), `startup.sync_analyzers_on_startup` (happy + exception),
  `admin_views.AnalyzerSyncView` (GET helper shape/order + POST
  with and without `analyzer.add_analyzer` permission),
  `utils.get_gremlin_manifests` (HTTP 500, malformed item, unknown
  gremlin id), `utils.auto_create_doc_analyzers` edge cases (no
  users, celery unavailable, update_existing=False), the
  `sync_doc_analyzers` management command (--dry-run + normal run),
  `views.AnalysisCallbackView` happy and bad-body paths (with
  `_create_analysis_notification` direct unit tests including the
  swallow-RuntimeError-log-warning path).

Also added `docs/test_scripts/pii_scanner_analyzer_smoke.md` per
the CLAUDE.md manual-test-script convention.

* Fix mypy linter errors: annotate body dict, suppress decorator .si attr-defined

* Address review: callback view test uses APIRequestFactory not URL resolver

USE_ANALYZER=False in test settings unregisters the analysis-complete URL,
so the prior tests using composed CALLBACK_ROOT_URL_FOR_ANALYZER paths
returned 404 silently. Drive the view directly via APIRequestFactory so
the assertions actually exercise the success/failure branches.

subject: Fix four test failures introduced in #1672 (#1679)
message:
Fix four test failures introduced in #1672 (#1679)

All four were test-setup bugs, not production regressions:

1. test_silent_when_status_is_completed_enum_value: sentinel emitted
   through the test module's logger instead of the signals logger that
   assertLogs is watching, so assertLogs always raised 'no logs ...
   triggered'. Route the sentinel through the signals logger.

2. _make_text_doc(b''): 'content or default' fell through for empty
   bytes (b'' is falsy), silently substituting the sample fixture and
   defeating tests that rely on the empty-text short-circuit
   (test_empty_text_extract_returns_failure was actually calling the
   live privacy-filter service in CI and timing out on DNS). Distinguish
   None from empty explicitly.

3. _make_pdf_doc: stored a fixed 'placeholder' string in
   txt_extract_file while detection coordinates were computed against
   the much-longer PlasmaPDF-derived doc_text. The task's offset
   validation (bounded by len(pdf_text_extract)) silently skipped every
   detection past byte 11, so test_pdf_doc_creates_token_label_annotations
   created no annotation. Persist the PlasmaPDF text as the sidecar.

4. test_valid_callback_with_valid_body_succeeds: body asserted to
   conform to OpenContractsGeneratedCorpusPythonType, but only sent
   annotated_docs + a non-existent label_lookup key. The TypedDict
   actually requires annotated_docs, doc_labels, text_labels, label_set
   — supply all four (label_set wired to OpenContractsLabelSetType).

subject: Fix async_doc_analyzer_task DB connection staleness
message:
Fix async_doc_analyzer_task DB connection staleness

Django async ORM (acount/aexists/aget) dispatches via
asgiref.sync_to_async with thread_sensitive=True, which runs on a
class-level singleton worker thread whose DatabaseWrapper is thread-
local and outlives the per-task event loop. If Postgres closes that
backend (idle timeout, restart, max_connections pressure on CI),
Django does not auto-reconnect and the next task fails with
OperationalError: server closed the connection unexpectedly, then
cascades to InterfaceError: connection already closed for every
subsequent test in the class.

Refresh the singleton worker's connections in the decorator's finally
via sync_to_async(close_old_connections)() so the cleanup runs in the
same worker thread Django's async ORM uses. The next task opens a
fresh connection.

Fixes the 7 PII scanner test failures observed on the last two main
CI runs (25976094291, 25980584352):
- PiiScannerKnobTests.test_invalid_detection_offsets_are_skipped
- PiiScannerKnobTests.test_invalid_min_score_fails_cleanly
- PiiScannerKnobTests.test_min_score_filters_low_confidence
- PiiScannerKnobTests.test_unknown_entity_group_is_dropped_silently
- PiiScannerErrorPathTests.test_adetect_pii_runtime_error_fails_cleanly
- PiiScannerErrorPathTests.test_empty_text_extract_returns_failure
- PiiScannerErrorPathTests.test_unsupported_file_type_fails_cleanly

Also set processing_started=timezone.now() on the bare-document
fixtures in two async-decorator tests so process_doc_on_create_atomic
short-circuits — the pytest conftest disconnects that signal but
manage.py test does not, and the eager ingest_doc chain was raising
DocumentParsingError before the ValueError assertion could run.

subject: Add authenticated MCP sessions and initial write tool (#1616)
message:
Add authenticated MCP sessions and initial write tool (#1616)

* Add authenticated MCP sessions and initial write tool support

* Fix MCP auth dispatch, harden write tool, address review

- list_annotations was missing the user parameter despite using it; added it.
- call_tool_handler now always passes user (None preserves anonymous), avoiding
  TypeError when future tools forget to accept user.
- Scoped server reads _mcp_user and forwards it to handlers; _validate_corpus_sync
