- ContextVar gains a concrete type annotation; redundant local AnonymousUser
  import removed.
- Added tests for authenticated dispatch, write-tool guards, and scoped-user
  visibility.

* Address review on authenticated MCP sessions PR

- Move MAX_THREAD_MESSAGE_LENGTH into opencontractserver/constants/mcp.py per the constants convention; update the corresponding test import.
- Refresh the list_public_corpuses docstring so it reflects authenticated visibility, not just anonymous.
- Add create_thread_message to get_scoped_tool_handlers so the corpus-scoped MCP endpoint can post messages with corpus_slug pre-validated.
- Collapse the stacked ContextVar token pattern into a single .set/.reset pair and emit logger.info/.warning on JWT success/failure; reset the scope token before the 401 short-circuit.
- Guard _extract_bearer_token to HTTP scopes only.
- Add ASGI-level 401 regression test (MCPAsgiAppAuthTest) and an explanatory comment on the deliberate Corpus.DoesNotExist surface in the unrelated-user test.
- Include parent_message_id and created_at in create_thread_message's response payload.

* Address review on authenticated MCP sessions PR

Critical fix:
- ``call_tool_handler`` and the scoped ``call_tool`` closure now catch
  ``django.core.exceptions.ValidationError`` alongside
  ``PermissionDenied``. ``create_thread_message`` raises
  ``ValidationError`` for blank / oversized content, but the prior code
  let it fall through to the generic ``except Exception: raise`` arm,
  so the LLM received an MCP transport error instead of a structured,
  recoverable ``{"error": ...}`` tool result. Both dispatch paths now
  format the error consistently (using ``ValidationError.messages``
  when present).

Test coverage gaps flagged in review:
- ``MCPAsgiAppAuthTest.test_valid_bearer_token_authenticates_and_does_not_401``
  closes the JWT happy-path gap at the ASGI layer.
- ``MCPCallToolHandlerValidationErrorTest`` covers ``ValidationError``
  → structured error on both the non-scoped and scoped dispatch paths
  plus the scoped write happy path with creator persistence.

Other:
- Clarified the ``list_public_corpuses`` tool description so callers
  know authenticated users see private corpuses they can read. Tool
  name retained — renaming would break existing MCP clients.

- CHANGELOG entry under ``### Added`` summarising the new auth flow,
  the first write tool, fault-tolerance contract, and test coverage.

* Address review: DRY tool-error serialisation, document write contract

- Extract `_format_tool_error_text` + `_record_and_return_tool_error`
  helpers in mcp/server.py so the (PermissionDenied | ValidationError)
  paths in `call_tool_handler` and the scoped `call_tool` closure share
  one definition of how errors are surfaced to the LLM.
- Expand `create_thread_message` docstring to make the read-implies-write
  permission contract explicit, per the review.
- Verified locally: `pytest opencontractserver/mcp/tests/test_mcp.py -n 4`
  → 174 passed.

* fix: unblock CI linter + address MCP auth review feedback

CI linter (pre-existing on main):
- Widen requests.post json= payloads to dict[str, Any] across users/
  tasks.py, docxodus_parser, and the two embedder microservices so they
  satisfy JsonType (dict is invariant).

MCP auth review:
- tools.py create_thread_message: validate and persist on the *stripped*
  content so the validation boundary and the stored row agree (previously
  "  hello  " passed the strip-only emptiness check but was saved with
  surrounding whitespace).
- server.py: hoist the JWT verifier import from inside the auth branch
  to module level so the patch target on server.get_user_from_jwt_token
  is stable. A future refactor that left the import inline would have
  silently broken the existing test.
- server.py: replace ``raise PermissionError`` with ``raise
  PermissionDenied`` on the scoped corpus-not-accessible path so the
  failure routes through the structured ``{"error": ...}`` handler instead
  of bubbling up as a transport-level exception.
- tests: extract the new ``new_event_loop`` → run → close dance into
  ``_MCPAsyncRunMixin`` shared by the three new test classes, and reset
  the thread's current loop to ``None`` after closing so a stale closed
  loop never leaks into follow-up async work.
- tests: replace the ``__import__("mcp.types", fromlist=...)`` anti-pattern
  with a normal top-level import.
- tests: add IDOR regression covering parent_message_id from another
  thread (must surface ChatMessage.DoesNotExist, not silently graft) and
  a stripping regression confirming validation and storage agree.

* Address review: filter user kwarg, expose create_thread_message in scoped list

- Dispatchers now drop any client-supplied `user` argument before
  forwarding to the tool handler. A hostile MCP client could otherwise
  trigger `TypeError: got multiple values for keyword argument 'user'`,
  which escaped the structured `(PermissionDenied, ValidationError)`
  branch as a raw transport error.
- `get_scoped_tool_definitions` now lists `create_thread_message`
  (with `corpus_slug` auto-omitted from required parameters) so MCP
  clients can discover the write tool through `tools/list` instead of
  having to know its name out-of-band.
- Both the global and scoped `content` schemas now declare
  `minLength: 1` and `maxLength: MAX_THREAD_MESSAGE_LENGTH` so clients
  can validate before a round-trip.
- Regression tests pin the user-collision guard and the discoverability
  contract.

* Address review: harden error fallback, document write-tool rate-limit gap, add edge-case tests

- _format_tool_error_text now returns "Unexpected error" for non-
  PermissionDenied / non-ValidationError exception types instead of the
  actively-misleading "Permission denied" fallback.
- Trim the verbose JWT import comment; the patch-stability rationale is
  preserved as a one-liner referencing the auth test class.
- Document the deferred write-tool rate-limit decision in
  _check_per_tool_rate_limit (intentional reuse of the generic per-tool
  bucket until a second write tool ships and we have two data points).
- Add MCPNonScopedListToolsTest covering the non-scoped list_tools <->
  TOOL_HANDLERS drift gap (with explicit create_thread_message
  assertion).
- Add MCPExtractBearerTokenTest covering the empty-payload, wrong-scheme,
  non-http-scope, mixed-case-header, and whitespace-trim branches of
  _extract_bearer_token.

* Address review: tighten Bearer prefix; asyncio.run; pin public-thread write policy

PR #1616 review follow-ups:

- mcp/server.py ``_extract_bearer_token``: replace ``startswith("bearer ")``
  with ``[:7].lower() == "bearer "`` so headers like ``Bearer\t``, ``Bearer\n``
  no longer match the prefix, get sliced at index 7, and silently include
  whitespace in the token. Functionally equivalent (the JWT validator would
  have rejected garbage anyway), but the contract at the parsing boundary is
  now obvious.

- mcp/tests/test_mcp.py ``_MCPAsyncRunMixin._run``: switch to
  ``asyncio.run()``. Eliminates the thread-global ``set_event_loop`` mutation,
  which was correct for sequential test runs but would race if pytest-xdist
  ever scheduled two async test methods on the same OS thread.

- mcp/tests/test_mcp.py: add
  ``test_create_thread_message_unrelated_user_can_post_to_public_thread``.
  Pins the documented policy that write access piggybacks on read
  visibility — any authenticated MCP caller who can see a public thread can
  post into it. Future tightening of that policy must now consciously update
  this test rather than silently changing the contract.

* Address PR #1616 review: fix scoped PermissionDenied leak, async DB connection cleanup, bearer-token comment

Scoped dispatcher: move corpus revalidation inside the try block so a private-after-cache corpus surfaces as a structured {"error": ...} payload rather than escaping as a raw transport error (matches the comment's stated intent).

MCPCallToolHandlerAuthTest / MCPCallToolHandlerValidationErrorTest: tearDown now closes the sync_to_async thread-pool worker's DB connection in addition to the main thread's. Without this, a transient postgres rupture mid-query in one test poisons the pool worker's connection and cascades 'connection already closed' across every subsequent test in the same class. Scopes the blast radius of any backend hiccup to a single retryable test.

Bearer-token comment: rewrite to describe what the prefix check enforces rather than mischaracterizing the prior implementation.

* Address PR #1616 review + add MCP OAuth discovery layer

Material fixes from latest review (2026-05-13T06:48:48Z):

* Scoped dispatcher restructured to mirror the non-scoped one — corpus
  visibility check moved into the try block and the pre-raise
  arecord_mcp_tool_call(error_type="CorpusNotAccessible") removed, so the
  PermissionDenied is recorded exactly once (as "PermissionDenied") via
  _record_and_return_tool_error. Unknown-tool check moved outside the try
  block so the ValueError it raises is no longer also caught by
  except Exception — single record as "UnknownTool" then transport-level
  propagation, identical to call_tool_handler. Eliminates the two
  double-telemetry paths flagged in review.

* New test_create_thread_message_with_valid_parent_succeeds in
  MCPAuthenticatedToolsTest closes the IDOR-without-happy-path gap:
  posts a reply with a valid parent_message_id in the same thread,
  asserts the FK is persisted, and incidentally exercises the two
  ChatMessage post_save signal handlers (create_reply_notification +
  create_mention_notification) from inside the same sync context the
  dispatcher uses via sync_to_async.

* Write-policy comment added at the TOOL_HANDLERS registration site so a
  future contributor doesn't add a redundant wrapper-level write guard;
  the scoped registration already carried an equivalent note.

MCP OAuth discovery layer (per the 2025-06-18 Authorization spec):

* New /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource endpoint (RFC 9728) returns
  the resource identifier, the Auth0 tenant as authorization_server,
  bearer_methods_supported, and the scopes Claude Desktop / Cursor need.
  Returns 404 when USE_AUTH0=False (no spec-compliant AS to advertise).

* /.well-known/mcp.json now sets authentication.metadataUrl on both the
  global and corpus-scoped server entries when Auth0 is configured, so
  clients that read the MCP discovery document also see the OAuth flow.

* MCP ASGI 401 response now emits WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm=...,
  resource_metadata="<base>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource" so
  interactive clients can discover the authorization server and drive
  Authorization-Code + PKCE without a preconfigured token. Non-Auth0
  mode degrades to the plain realm value.

Tests cover the new endpoint under both USE_AUTH0=True and =False, the
mcp.json auth-block advertisement, and the WWW-Authenticate header in
both modes.

* Address review: sanitize Host in WWW-Authenticate, document 401 ContextVar order

Two items from the most recent automated review on PR #1616:

- Defensively strip ", \r, \n, and whitespace from the forwarded Host
  before interpolating it into the WWW-Authenticate header. HTTP spec
  disallows those characters in an authority, but a misconfigured
  reverse proxy could forward them — sanitizing here closes a cheap
  header-injection vector and keeps the value well-formed. Bail back
  to the bare realm if the sanitized host is empty.
- Annotate the 401 early-return branch in app() with the ContextVar
  ordering invariant: only _mcp_asgi_scope has been set at that point,
  so the branch only resets that token. If a third ContextVar is ever
  added between the two .set() calls, the 401 path must grow a matching
  .reset() — there is no try/finally encompassing it.

* Refine MCP session handling

* Apply pyupgrade to opencontractserver/mcp/resources.py

* Address review: consistency, host sanitization, test loop pattern, op-note

- Route get_document_text and list_annotations through DocumentFolderService
  to match resources.py, eliminating drift between the two access paths.
- _build_www_authenticate_header: strip , ; \t from Host and require the
  result to match [A-Za-z0-9.\-:\[\]]+, closing a residual injection
  surface in the resource_metadata URL.
- Move AnonymousUser import in get_scoped_resource_definitions back to
  the imports block instead of the function body.
- Migrate the new authenticated-bearer ASGI test from new_event_loop +
  set_event_loop to asyncio.run(), the same race-free pattern that
  _MCPAsyncRunMixin documents.
- CHANGELOG: add operator-facing note that create_thread_message uses
  thread READ permission, so threads on public corpuses are writable
  by any authenticated token-holder.

* Fix failing MCP tests: thread user kwarg + DoesNotExist message

Resource handlers now forward the authenticated MCP user; update mock
assertions and drop the obsolete substring check on Django's default
DoesNotExist message.

* Address review: list_threads via DocumentFolderService, scoped tool note, tearDown debug log

- list_threads now uses DocumentFolderService.get_corpus_documents for the
  document_slug lookup, matching get_document_text/list_annotations/resources
  and avoiding drift in the corpus-membership access path.
- Note on scoped create_thread_message description that corpus_slug is
  URL-injected and clients must not supply it.
- _close_async_db_connections now logs the swallowed exception at DEBUG so
  transient infra issues are not invisible.

* Address review: per-test locked thread + warn-level Celery error

- Replace mutation of setUpTestData private_thread with a per-test
  locked Conversation. The DB rollback restores the row but not the
  cached class-level Python instance, so any future test that reads
  the attribute directly would see a stale is_locked=True. Fixing
  the test fixture is cheaper than auditing all future siblings.
- Drop the mention-parser/Celery dispatch log from error to warning.
  The message row is already saved, so a broker hiccup must not fail
  the write — and logging at error pollutes dashboards on transient
  broker unavailability.

subject: Remove fragile @override_settings(DATABASES={...}) decorator from async TestCases
message:
Remove fragile @override_settings(DATABASES={...}) decorator from async TestCases

The 4 main-CI failures in TestApprovalFlow (test_event_serialisation,
test_multiple_gates_interleaved, test_rejection_branch,
test_single_gate_pause_resume), plus intermittent failures across the
4 sibling files using the same harness, all traced back to a class-level
@override_settings(DATABASES={"default": {"CONN_MAX_AGE": 0}}) decorator.

The override fully replaces settings.DATABASES["default"] with a one-key
dict missing ENGINE/NAME/USER/etc. Django flags DATABASES as a
COMPLEX_OVERRIDE_SETTINGS and emits "Overriding setting DATABASES can
lead to unexpected behavior." Existing connection wrappers survive (they
captured settings_dict at creation), but any new connection created
during the override window reads the broken settings. For
TransactionTestCase + @pytest.mark.serial runs, conftest.py:258-264
aggressively closes connections in teardown, forcing reconnection inside
the override window for the next test. TransactionTestCase also flushes
django_content_type + auth_permission between tests, so the next setUp
races with the stale ContentType cache and hits a duplicate-key
IntegrityError on auth_permission / django_content_type, or returns
Document.DoesNotExist when the freshly-rebuilt connection can't see the
just-committed setUp data.

CONN_MAX_AGE=0 is irrelevant to test code anyway — it is only consulted
by close_old_connections wired to request_started / request_finished
signals (django/db/__init__.py:61-62), which test ORM code never
triggers.

Repro before fix: 2/8 failures on test_tool_approval_gate.py alone,
3/5 with all five files (one run hitting 34 failed tests). After fix:
5/5 single-file, 3/3 multi-file, plus a clean parallel -n 4
--dist loadscope run across all five files.

Affected files (decorator dropped, dead override_settings import
trimmed, misleading docstring line removed in test_thread_corpus_actions):
- opencontractserver/tests/test_tool_approval_gate.py
- opencontractserver/tests/test_nested_approval_gates.py
- opencontractserver/tests/test_pydantic_ai_agents.py (2 sites)
- opencontractserver/tests/test_thread_corpus_actions.py
- opencontractserver/tests/test_long_conversation_api.py

subject: Fix UserFeedback visibility to inherit from annotation's full visibility model (#1678)
message:
Fix UserFeedback visibility to inherit from annotation's full visibility model (#1678)

* UserFeedback inherits annotation visibility; Phase A review follow-ups

Resolve the second batch of review feedback on PR #1663:

- UserFeedbackManager.user_can / UserFeedbackQuerySet.visible_to_user
  now gate READ on Annotation.objects.visible_to_user(user) instead of
  the bare commented_annotation.is_public flag. The old logic produced
  two divergences from the "feedback inherits permissioning from the
  annotation it comments on" policy: it over-granted to anonymous on
  is_public non-structural annotations they couldn't see, and
  under-granted to authenticated users with guardian READ on a private
  annotation. Inherited grant remains READ-only.

- AnnotationManager.user_can (183 lines) decomposed into three private
  helpers: _anonymous_read_via_visible_to_user,
  _check_annotation_privacy_recursion,
  _compute_annotation_effective_permission. Behavior identical, but
  the top-level method now reads as a scannable branch sequence.

- _user_has_permission_for_obj_warned dedup set: comment expanded to
  make the bounded-by-call-sites invariant explicit so the unbounded
  set never grows with task volume in Celery workers. Pointer added to
  the test-isolation hook.

- ShimDeprecationWarningTestCase.setUp now clears the dedup set so the
  assertion is robust under pytest --keepdb (or any other multi-test
  process). Without this, a previous test triggering the warning from
  the same (filename, lineno) site would leave catch_warnings with
  nothing to record.

- RelationshipNonOwnerCreatorTestCase docstring reframed as POLICY
  (intended behavior) rather than "addresses the latent invariant
  violation" — relationship creators retain READ/UPDATE/DELETE via
  the creator branch after grants are revoked, by design.

- permission_cache.py module docstring notes nested-scope semantics
  (no inheritance from parent scope) as a Phase B wire-up consideration.

- Updated tests pinned to the old commented_annotation.is_public
  semantic to reflect inherited annotation visibility:
  TestUserFeedbackVisibility, UserFeedbackAuthorizationInvariantsTestCase,
  PermissioningTestCase.test_user_feedback_visibility.

Items 5 (N+1 risk in AnnotationManager privacy recursion) and 6
(nested-scope inheritance variant) are Phase B concerns and are
documented in-place via Phase B docstring notes rather than fixed.

* Address review #1678: rename helper + add Bug #2 regression test

Managers.py:
- Rename _anonymous_read_via_visible_to_user → _read_only_via_visible_to_user.
  The helper is read-only by design but its caller set is not
  anonymous-only — it's also used on the document_id=None branch for
  authenticated non-superusers. The original name implied anonymous
  exclusivity that doesn't match the actual usage pattern.
- _check_annotation_privacy_recursion docstring: spell out all three
  possible outcomes (structural-READ short-circuit, no-source-object
  pass-through, and the source Analysis/Extract gate) rather than
  framing it as 'return False if denied' which under-described the
  pass-through cases.

test_feedback.py:
- Add test_guardian_doc_grant_lets_user_see_feedback_on_private_annotation:
  direct regression for Bug #2 in the PR description. Pre-fix,
  UserFeedback.visible_to_user gated only on
  commented_annotation.is_public, so a user with a guardian READ grant
  on the parent document would see the annotation but not the
  feedback. The new assertion proves the grant flows through after
  the fix routes feedback visibility through
  Annotation.objects.visible_to_user.

* Address review #1678: fix CI test setup + restore PUBLISH/PERMISSION comment

- test_stranger_denied_when_commented_annotation_is_private was
  setting up an is_public=False annotation under an is_public=
  True document. Under the unified annotation-visibility model that
  this PR aligns with, the annotation's own is_public field doesn't
  hide it from strangers when the host document is public; only the
  document/corpus visibility gate or analysis/extract privacy does.
  Updating the host doc to is_public=False makes the annotation
  genuinely inaccessible to strangers, exercising the deny path the
  test intends to verify.
- Restore the inline comment about ALL mapping to READ+CRUD+COMMENT
  (no PUBLISH/PERMISSION) inside
  _compute_annotation_effective_permission, and add a one-liner
  explaining the trailing return False — without these, a future
  reader has no way to know why PUBLISH and PERMISSION fall through
  to a silent deny rather than raising.

subject: Fix V2 corpus export memory regression + import/export V2 follow-ups (#1676)
message:
Fix V2 corpus export memory regression + import/export V2 follow-ups (#1676)

* Fix V2 corpus export memory regression + logging/rollback follow-ups

Addresses code-review findings on PR #1635 (closes #1649):

- build_corpus_v2_zip materialised every active document's PDF content
  into io.BytesIO before fork/finalize consumed it.  Replaced with a
  tempfile.SpooledTemporaryFile bounded by the new
  EXPORT_SPOOL_MAX_SIZE_BYTES constant (default 100 MB) so large
  corpora roll over to disk instead of OOM-ing the worker.
- finalize_export now wraps the buffer in django.core.files.File
  rather than ContentFile, streaming chunks to storage instead of
  re-buffering the full archive in heap a second time.
- Removed the redundant %s / e arg from import_corpus_v2_from_bytes's
  exc_info=True log line so structured-log aggregators stop showing
  the exception summary twice.
- Documented the savepoint rollback contract for _import_corpus and
  the corresponding outer atomic in fork_corpus.

* Address review #1676: read spool threshold lazily + cover disk-rollover

constants/zip_export.py:
- Replace module-level constant capture with a get_*() accessor that
  reads from settings at call time. The frozen constant silently
  defeated @override_settings(EXPORT_SPOOL_MAX_SIZE_BYTES=...) — tests
  pointing at the override would silently keep the 100 MB default and
  never exercise the disk path. Document the contract so future imports
  don't reintroduce the freeze.

tasks/export_tasks_v2.py:
- build_corpus_v2_zip reads the spool threshold via the new accessor so
  test overrides actually take effect.

tests/test_corpus_export_import_v2.py:
- Add test_build_zip_disk_rollover_produces_valid_archive: forces
  max_size=1 via @override_settings, asserts SpooledTemporaryFile._rolled
  flips to True (proves the override is honoured), opens the archive
  with zipfile (proves the central directory is written after rollover),
  and round-trips through import_corpus_v2_from_bytes (proves the seek
  to offset 0 happens after the close).

* Address review #1676: fix CI test + SpooledTemporaryFile coverage

- test_fork_matches_export_import was still asserting
  isinstance(zip_bytes, _io.BytesIO) after build_corpus_v2_zip switched
  to SpooledTemporaryFile for the OOM fix. Update the helper to use
  the documented context-manager pattern and assert against
  SpooledTemporaryFile so the test reflects the new lifetime contract.
- test_build_zip_disk_rollover_produces_valid_archive now uses
  with build_corpus_v2_zip(...) as zip_buffer: instead of
  try/finally + .close() — exercises the same lifetime path the
  production callers use.
- Add test_finalize_export_accepts_spooled_temporary_file so the
  DjangoFile streaming write is covered by a buffer that has actually
  rolled over to disk, not just a BytesIO. Guards against a future
  regression that re-introduces a buffer-into-bytes pattern.
- fork_tasks.py comment now spells out the parenthesized with
  evaluation order so future readers can see why the export still
  happens outside the write transaction.

subject: Surface OC_SUBTREE_GROUP relationships in semantic search (#1645) (#1669)
message:
Surface OC_SUBTREE_GROUP relationships in semantic search (#1645) (#1669)

* Surface relationships and subtree-group context in semantic search (closes #1645)

Two-front delivery on the materialised OC_SUBTREE_GROUP rows from #1646:

(a) Annotation hits now carry a block_context for the smallest enclosing
    subtree-group. CoreAnnotationVectorStore._attach_block_context_sync
    runs a single join after reranking, picks the smallest containing
    OC_SUBTREE_GROUP per hit, and returns a bounded
    SUBTREE_GROUP_BLOCK_TEXT_MAX_CHARS-capped block_text. Wired into
    search/async_search/hybrid_search/async_hybrid_search/global_search
    and surfaced through PydanticAIVectorSearchResponse and the
    semanticSearch GraphQL resolver.

(b) Relationships are first-class vector targets. Polymorphic
    Embedding.relationship FK (migration 0073) + partial-unique
    constraint, Relationship now mixes in HasEmbeddingMixin, new
    calculate_embeddings_for_relationship_batch task dispatched by
    build_subtree_groups_for_document (dual-embedding strategy: default
    + corpus-preferred). New CoreRelationshipVectorStore runs cosine
    distance against the Embedding table, scoped by
    Relationship.objects.visible_to_user. New semanticSearchRelationships
    GraphQL query returns relationship pk, source/target annotation pks,
    label, block_text, and document/corpus context.

Doc-viewer jump-to: ?rel=<relationship_pk> URL param parsed by
CentralRouteManager into a new selectedRelationshipId reactive var.
useJumpToRelationship hook (mounted in DocumentKnowledgeBase) watches
the param + allRelationsAtom and, once relations are loaded, selects
the relation and scrolls its source annotation into view.
CorpusAnnotationCards click handler now forwards block_context.
relationship_id as a relationshipId query param so users landing from
a leaf-annotation hit also see the containing block selected.

Permissioning mirrors resolve_semantic_search: empty-list response for
missing-or-denied document/corpus prevents IDOR enumeration; corpus-
scoped queries derive the embedder from Corpus.preferred_embedder so
relationship vectors stay in the corpus's frozen embedding space.

Tests cover smallest-enclosing-group selection, root-level pass-through,
block_text truncation, end-to-end relationship retrieval, IDOR denial,
and the rel= URL-builder round-trip.

* Fix CI linter failures: mypy, flake8, black

* Address Claude review feedback on PR #1669

- Fix relationship deep-link bug: useJumpToRelationship now compares
  numeric PKs (URL ?rel=<pk> carries raw PK, but RelationGroup.id is
  a Relay global ID), so the find() actually matches.
- Clear hoveredAnnotationId on relationship deselection so the stale
  hover indicator doesn't linger after ?rel= is cleared.
- DRY block-text construction: extract join_block_text_parts() and
  share it between synthesize_relationship_block_text (embedder),
  CoreRelationshipVectorStore._shape_results, and
  CoreAnnotationVectorStore._attach_block_context_sync. Cap/truncation
  logic now lives in one place.
- Fix N+1 in calculate_embeddings_for_relationship_batch: order the
  prefetch by id and read raw_text from prefetched objects when the
  cache is populated.
- Fix smallest-enclosing-block bug: Count("target_annotations") with
  target_annotations__in=hit_ids in the same queryset is restricted by
  the filter join, collapsing every group's descendant_count to 1 and
  forcing a tie-break on lowest pk (i.e. always selecting ROOT instead
  of the innermost enclosing block). Compute descendant_count from the
  prefetched target set instead. Existing test now correctly passes.
- Remove dead visible_qs.exists() check, dead RuntimeError branch in
  CoreRelationshipVectorStore.__init__, and dead getattr fallback for
  similarity_score.
- Fix test isolation: mutating tests now refetch rows so shared
  cls-attributes aren't dirtied for sibling tests.

* Add coverage tests for semantic search relationships and jump-to-relationship hook

Backend (opencontractserver/tests/test_semantic_search_graphql.py):
- New SemanticSearchRelationshipsQueryTest class covering the
  semantic_search_relationships GraphQL resolver: basic dispatch,
  corpus/document scoping via Relay global IDs, IDOR contract
  (invisible corpus/document → empty list), limit clamping, and
  anonymous rejection.
- New SemanticSearchBlockContextFieldTest covering the BlockContext
  field mapping on semanticSearch — exercises the GraphQL type wiring
  introduced alongside OC_SUBTREE_GROUP relationship surfacing.

Frontend (useJumpToRelationship.test.tsx):
- Unit tests pinning the URL-PK ↔ Relay-global-ID bridge that was
  fixed earlier in this PR: a regression test ensures
  ?rel=<raw-pk> resolves against RelationGroup.id (Relay ID) via
  numeric comparison, not string equality.
- Covers no-op paths, non-numeric fallback, hover-clear on
  deselection, and the lastAppliedRef guard.

* Address Claude review on PR #1669 and align test with new error message

- Move join_block_text_parts and synthesize_relationship_block_text from
  tasks/embeddings_task.py to utils/embeddings.py so the GraphQL-facing
  vector stores no longer depend on a Celery task module (SRP / utility
  placement).
- Drop the _prefetched_objects_cache introspection in

  ``order_by("id").values_list``; the cache shape is a Django internal

- Fix the misleading docstring in _attach_block_context_sync — there is

- Replace the ``as any`` in useJumpToRelationship.test.tsx with a

* Address PR review: redundant synth, scroll retry, dynamic attr, async test

- _embed_relationship: accept optional precomputed_text so the dual-
  embedding strategy only synthesizes the relationship block text
  once per relationship instead of once per embedder pass.
- core_relationship_vector_store._run_vector_search: return
  (Relationship, similarity) tuples instead of mutating a dynamic
  similarity_score attribute on the Django model. Drops the

- useJumpToRelationship: add a defensive 300 ms retry timer for the

  reliably catch the late-registered annotation ref instead of

- Add async_search coverage: delegation-to-sync contract and the
  text-only query rebuild path that flows the regenerated embedding
  back through search.

Note: review item #2 (raw Django PKs vs Relay global IDs on the new
relationship_id GraphQL fields) is intentionally deferred — the
choice is documented on the field descriptors and changing the
convention would cascade across the resolver, hook, and URL routing.

* Address PR review: BaseVectorStore, exactly-one guard, docstring trims

Extract shared vector-store machinery into BaseVectorStore (user
resolution, IDOR checks, embedder resolution, query-embedding
generation) so CoreAnnotationVectorStore and CoreRelationshipVectorStore
share the permission-filtering contract instead of duplicating it.

Also:
- Tighten EmbeddingManager.store_embedding to require exactly-one
  parent FK (previously any/all were silently accepted).
- Trim multi-paragraph docstrings on _attach_block_context_sync,

  synthesize_relationship_block_text per CLAUDE.md.
- Document the ordering invariant (by id, not document position) in
  synthesize_relationship_block_text.
- Remove the void useAtomValue / void PdfAnnotations smell in

- Add tests: store_embedding rejects multiple parent FKs; both
  corpus_id + document_id provided where the document isn't in the

Update test patches to target generate_embeddings_from_text /
get_embedder at their new home in base_vector_store.

* Fix test_hybrid_search patch targets after BaseVectorStore refactor

The generate_embeddings_from_text and agenerate_embeddings_from_text functions
are now imported and used in base_vector_store.py (BaseVectorStore parent
class), not in core_vector_stores.py. Update the @patch decorators in
TestHybridSearch to target the base module so mocks bind successfully.

* Add unit tests for relationship batch embedding and PydanticAI response

Cover the new code paths surfaced by issue #1645:
- _embed_relationship: empty-text/None-vector/None-embedding short-circuits,

- calculate_embeddings_for_relationship_batch: empty-list early return,

- PydanticAIVectorSearchResponse: async_from_core_results block_context

* Add type annotations for class-level test data in new PydanticAI test

* Address review: drop misleading prefetch, fix stale 'inlined' comment

Items 1 and 2 from the most recent automated review on #1669:

- synthesize_relationship_block_text uses values_list which bypasses
  Django's prefetch cache (it stores instances, not raw column tuples),
  so the prefetch_related calls in calculate_embeddings_for_relationship_batch
  were doing zero work. Drop them and document why; the 2N queries are
  bounded by the small subtree-group cardinality per batch.

- Correct the stale 'inlined' comment in the dual-embedding branch — the
  code calls _apply_dual_embedding_strategy directly; update the comment
  to describe the actual delegation.

* Lift frontend patch coverage on the rel= deep-link wiring

Codecov flagged three files on PR 1669 below patch threshold:

* useJumpToRelationship.ts (75%) — added unit tests for the scroll
  happy path, the source-ref → target-ref fallback, the deferred
  setTimeout retry path, and the malformed-relay-id catch branch.
  Also tightened test isolation: hook instances from prior tests now
  unmount in afterEach so shared scroll-spy calls don't leak across

* CorpusAnnotationCards.tsx (30%) — extracted the blockContext
  derivation (annotation id → containing relationship id) and the
  click-handler queryParams builder into a pure
  corpusAnnotationCardsHelpers module so they can be unit-tested
  without mounting the full Apollo + router + reactive-var stack.

* CentralRouteManager.tsx (50%) — added Phase-2 tests pinning that
  ?rel=42 populates selectedRelationshipId and absence clears it.

* Address Claude review comments on PR 1669

* Document the raw-PK ID convention on SemanticSearchRelationshipResultType
  so future callers don't accidentally feed those values into resolvers
  expecting Relay global IDs (e.g. node(id: $documentId)).

* Add a SECURITY CONTRACT docstring to _attach_block_context_sync stating
  that it does not apply visible_to_user filtering on its own — callers
  must pass results already permission-filtered by the store's visibility
  queryset, or block_text could leak to users who can't see the underlying

* Remove the 'Lazy import keeps the GraphQL module light' explainer
  comment per the project's no-explain-what conventions; the pattern is

* Address review #1669: document partial constraint + cover non-structural decoy

Migration 0073: add inline comment explaining the partial unique constraint —
the condition (relationship IS NOT NULL) protects existing
annotation/note/message/document rows that legally carry relationship=NULL.

Test: add coverage for the structural=True filter in
_attach_block_context_sync. A non-structural OC_SUBTREE_GROUP look-alike must
not contribute block context even when no genuine structural group is
available — guards against analyzer-copied label rows polluting embedded
context.

* Address PR review: tighten block-context security gate, dedup payload

- Make _attach_block_context_sync apply Relationship.visible_to_user

- Document that calculate_embeddings_for_relationship_batch's no-path

tests/Documents.ct.tsx:

The decomposition PR landed under codecov's frontend patch target
(61.15% vs 69.89%) — the new presentational components only had a

subject: Add two-tier permission caching for user_can checks (#1665)
message:
Add two-tier permission caching for user_can checks (#1665)

* Add two-tier permission cache for Manager.user_can (closes #1640)

PR #1637 centralized authorization in _default_user_can (corpuses Phase 0).
This follow-up keeps the cold path cheap as more models adopt the API:

Tier 1 (transparent) — per-instance memoization inside
get_users_permissions_for_obj. Stored on the instance as
_oc_granted_perms_cache, keyed by (user_id, include_group_permissions).
Anonymous users bypass. Cache is a defensive frozenset; callers receive
a set copy so _default_user_can can still fold read_<model> in for
CRUD/ALL checks without poisoning the cache.

Tier 2 (opt-in) — request-scoped PermissionQueryOptimizer mirroring
ConversationQueryOptimizer. Attached lazily to the request as
_permission_query_optimizer via get_request_optimizer(request). Keyed by
(user_id, content_type_id, instance_pk, include_group_permissions) so
multiple instances of the same model share a cache. None-tolerant for
Celery / management-command contexts.

Plumbing:
- _default_user_can / UserCanMixin / InstanceUserCanMixin / CorpusFolder.user_can
  gained a request= kwarg (kw-only, default None — backward compatible).
- DocumentFolderService classmethods (~25 entry points) accept and forward
  request; corpus GraphQL queries + mutations + corpus_folder_mutations
  pass request=info.context.
- set_permissions_for_obj_to_user gained a request= kwarg and now
  self-invalidates both tiers for the affected (user, instance) pair when
  called inside the HTTP lifecycle. Phase-0 Corpus mutation call sites
  in corpus_mutations.py and document_mutations.py pass it through;
  out-of-band callers (Celery / fixtures / importing) keep the
  positional signature. Tier 1 is still scrubbed for the target user
  even when request is None so reused instances see the new grant.

Tests: opencontractserver/tests/permissioning/test_permission_optimizer.py
covers per-instance memoization (zero queries on repeat, no leakage
across include_group_permissions, fast-path short-circuits don't
populate cache, defensive-copy contract), the request-scoped optimizer
(lazy attach, None-safe, distinct-user keying, per-user / per-instance /
total invalidation, anonymous skip), and the mutation invalidation
contract (mid-request grant visible after set_permissions_for_obj_to_user
with request; Tier 1 scrubbed when request is None).

Docs: docs/architecture/query_permission_patterns.md gains a row in the
Layer 2 table and a new "Two-Tier user_can Caching" subsection that
documents the attribute names, keying, and invalidation contract.

* Fix CI linter failures

- Apply pyupgrade rewrite of Optional[X] -> X | None in permission_optimizer.py
- Drop now-unused Optional import
- Suppress mypy arg-type warning on intentional AnonymousUser test path

* Address Claude review on PR #1665

- Document group-permission and refresh_from_db staleness boundaries on
  INSTANCE_PERMS_CACHE_ATTR, set_permissions_for_obj_to_user, and the
  arch doc so callers know when to invalidate manually
- Widen PermissionQueryOptimizer._cache type annotation: instance_pk is
  Any (UUID/str-PK models would have tripped mypy)
- Raise ValueError when invalidate() receives both `instance` and an
  explicit `content_type_id`/`instance_pk` instead of silently letting
  one win; add a regression test
- Trim the long inline two-tier-cache-invalidation comment in
  set_permissions_for_obj_to_user per the one-line WHY convention

* Add coverage for _default_user_can branches and folder_service request kwarg

Three new test classes target the codecov patch-coverage gap in
permissioning.py (71.64% → expected ~95%):

DefaultUserCanCoverageTestCase pins each user-resolution path
(None / AnonymousUser / int id / str id / unknown id / unauthenticated
double) and each permission-type branch (READ/CREATE/UPDATE/EDIT/DELETE/
COMMENT/PUBLISH/PERMISSION/CRUD/ALL) plus the is_public-fold-in path
that keeps CRUD passing on public corpora.

SetPermissionsInvalidationCoverageTestCase covers the per-user scrub
selectivity (other users' cache entries survive) and the no-request
Celery path (Tier 1 still drops).

FolderServiceRequestKwargCoverageTestCase exercises the request= kwarg
on DocumentFolderService and the permission-denial empty-queryset
branch (returns empty rather than raising).

* Address Claude review on PR #1665 and close codecov patch gaps

- Clarify the docstring on ``PermissionQueryOptimizer.get_granted``:
  the "without double-caching" wording was inaccurate. A Tier 2 cold
  miss does warm Tier 1 as a side-effect, so the same frozenset
  intentionally ends up in both caches. Spell out why that
  redundancy is desired (out-of-request callers still get Tier 1).
- Add two coverage tests targeting the previously-uncovered warming
  paths in ``get_users_permissions_for_obj``:
  * direct superuser call → guardian-superuser return path
  * pre-attached guardian prefetch → fast-path return
  Both paths exist because ``_default_user_can`` short-circuits
  before reaching the helper, so they are only exercised by callers
  that invoke the helper directly.

* Fix mypy errors in test_permission_optimizer.py

Replace assertIsNotNone with assert for type narrowing on cache
lookups, and drop an unused type:ignore comment on a Django
reverse-relation accessor that mypy now resolves correctly.

* Address Claude review: clarify Tier 2 default vs Tier 1

Add a docstring note to PermissionQueryOptimizer.get_granted explaining
why include_group_permissions defaults to True (mirrors user_can) while
the lower-level get_users_permissions_for_obj defaults to False.
Production always passes the flag explicitly, so the divergence is
benign — the note prevents future maintainers from chasing a phantom
inconsistency.

* Address review: guard partial-coordinate invalidate against PK collisions

invalidate(instance_pk=X) without content_type_id was a silent footgun: a
Corpus with pk=5 and a Document with pk=5 would both be evicted because
the wildcard match ignores model identity. Raise ValueError when an
instance_pk arrives without its content_type_id so callers must either
pair the two or use instance= shorthand. Add a regression test.

* Address review #3, #5: document Tier 2 absence in Celery + pickling staleness

* Address review: thread request= through manager.user_can overrides

After merging main into PR 1665, the UserCanMixin.user_can supertype now
declares request: Any = None, but five subclass overrides added by
PR #1663 did not include that parameter and mypy flagged the signature
mismatch.

- DocumentManager / RelationshipManager / UserFeedbackManager
  (shared/Managers.py): add request kwarg and forward to super() /
  recursive Manager.user_can calls.
- AnnotationManager / NoteManager (shared/Managers.py): add request
  kwarg and forward to Analysis.objects.user_can / Extract.objects.user_can
  / Document.objects.user_can / Corpus.objects.user_can so the optimizer
  cache flows through the recursion.
- ConversationManager / ChatMessageManager (conversations/models.py):
  add request kwarg and forward to _default_user_can.

Also addresses Claude review item #7 (audit folder-service callers):
config/graphql/document_types.py:1153 (resolve_folder_in_corpus) now
passes request=info.context to DocumentFolderService.get_document_folder.
get_folder_document_count and get_folder_path have no in-tree callers.

Adds review item #4: negative regression test pinning that
refresh_from_db() does NOT clear Tier 1 (the documented footgun) so a
future change to that contract is caught by CI.

* Address review #1665: align defaults, lock optimizer cache, scrub pickled cache

- Tier 1 `get_users_permissions_for_obj` default now `include_group_permissions=True`
  to match `PermissionQueryOptimizer.get_granted` / `_default_user_can` / every
  `Manager.user_can` surface. One default, one answer.
- `PermissionQueryOptimizer._cache` is now guarded by `threading.Lock()` for
  reads, writes, and the invalidate-loop iteration. DB work stays outside the
  lock so guardian lookups never serialise on it.
- `InstanceUserCanMixin.__getstate__` strips `INSTANCE_PERMS_CACHE_ATTR` so
  models pickled into Celery tasks can never carry a stale Tier 1 frozenset
  to the worker (footgun → impossible, not just documented).
- Comments pin reliance on `ContentType._cache` and clarify that creator-based
  models on the Tier 1 path are always cache-safe (no guardian mutation path
  exists for them).
- Added Tier1PicklingScrubTestCase to lock in the new __getstate__ contract.

* Address review #1665: forward request= through _compute_effective_permissions

The optimizer's _compute_effective_permissions invokes Document.objects.user_can /
Corpus.objects.user_can repeatedly per request. Threading request= through to those
calls activates the Tier 2 PermissionQueryOptimizer, deduplicating guardian lookups
across distinct Document/Corpus instances within a single request.

Annotation/Relationship manager user_can() overrides now forward request= as
context= to the optimizer, completing the request-scoped cache plumbing so the
kwarg doesn't silently no-op for these checks.

* Address review #1665: warn on invalidate() clear-all + assert cold-path query budget

Two follow-ups to the latest Claude review:

- PermissionQueryOptimizer.invalidate() no-args docstring now points at
  invalidate_caches() for the clear-all intent so an accidental call
  doesn't silently nuke the request cache.
- test_repeat_user_can_zero_queries wraps the warm-up call in an
  explicit assertNumQueries(6) so a regression that blows up the cold
  path is caught here instead of only the second-call zero-query assertion.

* Address review #1665: thread-safe Tier 1 cache + type annotations

- Replace the raw `dict` on `instance._oc_granted_perms_cache` with
  `_InstancePermsCache(dict)`, a thread-safe subclass exposing
  `drop_for_user(user_id)` that holds an internal Lock for the
  iterate-then-delete sweep in `set_permissions_for_obj_to_user`.
  Closes the ASGI / async-view exposure flagged in the latest review
  (the sweep would otherwise risk `RuntimeError: dictionary changed
  size during iteration` if two threads ever touched the same
  instance). Individual reads/writes still ride CPython's GIL
  atomicity; the lock is for the compound op only.
- `_get_or_create_instance_perms_cache` uses `__dict__.setdefault`
  so two threads first-touching the same instance converge on one
  cache object rather than racing via `getattr`+`setattr`.
- Backwards-compat fallback in `set_permissions_for_obj_to_user`:
  if an instance carries a plain-`dict` cache (older worker
  unpickle, test fixture), invalidation falls back to a
  snapshot-then-`.pop()` pattern so `RuntimeError` cannot escape.
- Add explicit `request: Any = None` annotations on
  `ConversationManager.user_can` / `ChatMessageManager.user_can`
  (previously inferred as `None`, which would reject real request
  objects at the type level).
- Drop rotting inline `# PR #1663` comment references per CLAUDE.md.
- New `Tier1CacheThreadSafetyTestCase` pins the contract: cache is
  the thread-safe wrapper, concurrent reader threads + repeated
  invalidate sweeps don't race, mutation invalidation routes
  through `drop_for_user` (mocked).

* ci: trigger Backend CI for 524c9e79b

* Address review #1665: defer lazy import past cache hits + superuser cache caveat

Two minor polish items from the latest review:

- ``PermissionQueryOptimizer.get_granted`` previously ran the lazy
  ``from opencontractserver.utils.permissioning import …`` on every
  call. On warm requests where most calls are cache hits, that's a
  needless ``sys.modules`` lookup (~30 ns each). Move the import inside
  the two branches that actually call ``get_users_permissions_for_obj``
  (anonymous-user fallback, cache miss) so the cache-hit path stays
  pure-Python with no module table touch.
- Add a NOTE at the superuser cache-write site in
  ``get_users_permissions_for_obj`` warning that the cache key omits
  ``is_superuser``, so test scenarios that promote/demote the same
  Python instance need to drop the cache attribute manually. The same
  caveat already lived in the constants module; mirroring it at the
  write site makes the boundary visible to anyone tracing a stale-cache
  bug in tests.

Tests still pass (44 in test_permission_optimizer.py, 490 across the
full permissioning suite locally).

* Address PR #1665 review: invalidate_caches direct path, lock trade-off note, MRO comment, group-perm doc section, magic-count comment

- PermissionQueryOptimizer.invalidate_caches() now clears self._cache directly
  instead of delegating to invalidate() with no args (which it warned against).
- Added a DESIGN NOTE inside get_granted explaining why the DB call lives
  outside the lock — preempts future well-meaning serialization fixes.

subject: Refactor: Split DocumentService and CorpusObjsService for cleaner architecture (#1685)
message:
Refactor: Split DocumentService and CorpusObjsService for cleaner architecture (#1685)

* Split DocumentFolderService → DocumentService + CorpusObjsService

Issue #N/A — PR review of opencontractserver/mcp/tools.py surfaced a
manual two-step fusion (`corpus.get_documents()` + `Document.objects
.visible_to_user(user).get(...)`) that silently re-derived a different
permission semantic than the canonical
`DocumentFolderService.get_corpus_documents`. The pattern was repeated
across MCP, LLMs, GraphQL, REST views, and util modules.

This commit refactors the service layer along the natural seam:

- DocumentService (opencontractserver/documents/document_service.py) is
  the source of truth for document-level operations and permissioning
  (creation, quota, validation, standalone lookup, document permissions).
- CorpusObjsService (opencontractserver/corpuses/corpus_objs_service.py)
  is the source of truth for corpus-scoped operations ("give me X inside
  corpus Y for user Z"). It owns documents-in-corpus today; designed to
  grow to annotations, notes, relationships, extracts, analyses, etc.

DocumentFolderService is preserved as a multiple-inheritance subclass of
both new services so the ~18 existing importers continue to work
unchanged. Cleanup tracked under follow-up issue.

New convenience methods on CorpusObjsService eliminate the buggy fusion:

- get_corpus_document_by_slug(user, corpus, slug)
- get_corpus_document_by_id(user, corpus, document_id)
- is_document_in_corpus(user, corpus, document_id)

All three are corpus-as-gate and IDOR-safe — same Document.DoesNotExist
fires whether the document doesn't exist, isn't in this corpus, or the
user lacks corpus READ.

Migrated 15 user-context call sites:
- opencontractserver/mcp/tools.py (5 sites)
- opencontractserver/mcp/resources.py (2 sites)
- opencontractserver/llms/agents/core_agents.py (2 sites)
- opencontractserver/discovery/views.py (3 sites in _search_within_corpus)
- config/graphql/og_metadata_queries.py
- config/graphql/extract_mutations.py
- config/graphql/document_relationship_mutations.py

Corpus.get_documents() now emits a DeprecationWarning. Internal/task
callers (badge_tasks, corpus_tasks, utils/sharing, utils/analyzer,
framework-private LLM helpers in pii/annotations/document_indexing)
migrated to corpus._get_active_documents() to opt out cleanly. The
CAML article paths (caml_article.py, graphql/corpus_types.py) need an
include_caml-aware service method and are tracked under follow-up issues.

Tests added:
- test_document_service.py — structural / partition / back-compat
- test_corpus_objs_service.py — new convenience methods, IDOR safety,
  include_deleted variants, the MCP regression scenario
- test_corpus_get_documents_deprecation.py — warning emitted, internal
  helper silent, parity between the two methods

CLAUDE.md item 7 declares the service layer as the canonical entry point
for any user-context code touching documents.

* Fix linter: black reformatting + mypy User-type resolution

Black reformatting passes touched four files (line-length redistribution
in models.py, discovery/views.py, core_agents.py, and the new test).

The mypy errors at core_agents.py:380 and :1142 were passing
``config.user_id`` (an ``int``) directly to
``CorpusObjsService.get_corpus_documents``, which expects
``User | AnonymousUser``. Resolve the id to an actual instance via a new
``_resolve_user_or_anon`` helper alongside ``_assert_access``, and call it
inside the existing ``sync_to_async`` block at both sites so the ORM
lookup runs on the worker thread.

* Address review #1685: fix test fixture + symmetric bulk permissions + mcp callsite

- TestCorpusObjsServiceTestBase setUp created two Document rows with the
  same (creator, slug) tuple. The uniq_document_slug_per_creator_cs
  constraint added in migration 0018 rejects the second insert, so the
  whole fixture exploded with an IntegrityError. Give the private-corpus
  twin a distinct creator so the (creator, slug) pair remains unique;
  the IDOR oracle the test relies on still holds because the test
  exercises the slug collision *across corpora*, not across creators.
- add_documents_to_corpus was strictly narrower than
  add_document_to_corpus — the singular path admits owned, public,
  or explicit READ-grantee docs; the bulk path only admitted owned/
  public, silently dropping guardian-grantee docs. Walk the gap with
  user_has_permission_for_obj so an explicit READ grant on a
  private doc admits in bulk too, matching the singular behaviour.
- mcp/tools.py:list_documents was still importing the legacy
  DocumentFolderService shim; switch to CorpusObjsService
  directly to align with the rest of the file and remove the
  misleading 'optimized single-query' comment that implied the alias
  has a performance edge over the canonical service. The merge with
  main had also left user=anonymous placeholders in six call sites
  (PR-side bug); these are corrected to user=user.

* Address review #1685: unify get_corpus_documents + share resolver + fix tests

Pytest fixes (the failing checks on this PR):
- test_document_folder_service.py was patching
  ``opencontractserver.corpuses.folder_service.post_save``, but the
  signal symbol no longer exists in the shim module after the split.
  Repointed both patches to ``corpus_objs_service.post_save`` where
  the symbol now lives.
- test_llms_typing_coverage.py::TestCorpusAgentContextInitialize was
  mocking ``Corpus.get_documents``, but ``CorpusAgentContext.initialize``
  now routes through ``CorpusObjsService.get_corpus_documents``.
  Updated the patch target so the test continues to drive both
  branches (empty list triggers fetch, non-empty list short-circuits).

Review follow-ups:
- Unify ``get_corpus_documents`` ``include_deleted=True/False`` paths
  through a new ``_build_corpus_documents_queryset`` helper. Pre-fix
  the ``include_deleted=True`` branch hand-rolled a DocumentPath query
  that silently bypassed CAML filtering altogether; both branches now
  compose ``include_deleted`` and ``include_caml`` toggles uniformly.
  Added ``include_caml=False`` to the public method so callers can
  opt in. New TestGetCorpusDocuments_CamlAndDeleted pins all four flag
  combinations including the regression guard
  ``test_include_deleted_still_excludes_caml``.
- Move ``_resolve_user_or_anon`` from ``core_agents.py`` to the shared
  ``users/types.py`` as the public ``resolve_user_or_anon`` helper.
  Centralises the pattern that other service surfaces need too, gives
  ``DoesNotExist`` handling one canonical home, and the docstring
  (re: must be called inside the same ``sync_to_async`` block) lives
  with the function. New test_user_types_resolver.py pins the three
  branches (existing id, None → AnonymousUser, unknown id → DoesNotExist
  rather than silent demotion).

* Apply black formatting to test_corpus_objs_service.py

Pre-commit lint job failed because black wanted to reformat this file.
Automated fix; no test logic change.

* Address PR #1685 codecov: cover DocumentService quota, validation, creation, lookup, permissions

DocumentService landed under codecov's backend patch target (42.68%) because the
existing test file only verified structural assertions (method partition,
backwards-compat alias surface) and a single happy-path quota call. The
following branches were uncovered: usage-capped quota over/under, validate_file_type
plaintext fallback / unrecognised binary / disallowed MIME, create_document
PDF / TXT / unsupported MIME inside the atomic block / runtime-error
fall-through, get_document_by_id IDOR matrix (owner / public / explicit READ /
outsider / nonexistent), and set_document_permissions authorization +
exception fall-through.

Each new TestCase pins a single business rule and is structured around the
SCENARIO / BUSINESS RULE docstring pattern the rest of the file already uses,
so the additions read as documentation of the public contract.

* Address PR #1685 review: hoist inline imports, document API contracts, doc N+1 TODO, CHANGELOG follow-up note

- Hoist 3 function-local CorpusObjsService imports in
  og_metadata_queries.py, document_relationship_mutations.py,
  extract_mutations.py to module level (no circular import — verified
  the inline form was cargo-cult, not load-bearing).
- resolve_user_or_anon docstring now makes the stale-id contract
  explicit: User.DoesNotExist propagates by design; callers needing a
  silent fallback must catch at their own boundary, because silent
  demotion to AnonymousUser would broaden access to a deleted creator's
  private content.
- Corpus._get_active_documents API note explains the underscore-prefixed
  name is the blessed cross-module helper for non-user-context callers
  (badge / analyzer / signal / LLM-tool batches); the underscore
  distinguishes it from the deprecated user-facing get_documents() shim.
- CorpusObjsService.check_document_in_corpus docstring leads with 'NO
  PERMISSION CHECK' — the method is a raw DocumentPath membership probe;
  callers must gate corpus READ. Suggests get_corpus_document_by_id as
  the higher-level alternative for new resolvers.
- og_metadata_queries.resolve_og_corpus_document now documents that the
  is_public=True filter on the Corpus.objects.get(...) call is
  load-bearing — without it, AnonymousUser GET against
  CorpusObjsService.get_corpus_documents would resolve any public corpus.
- _build_corpus_documents_queryset .distinct() now documents the
  defensive intent: DocumentPath has no DB constraint preventing
  duplicate is_current=True rows per (corpus, document), only
  (corpus, path), so an aliased path or include_deleted=True row pair
  could surface the same document_id twice.
- get_folder_tree O(N) loop tagged with a TODO(#1685 follow-up) for the
  path-from-parent-map + annotate-Count optimisation. Pre-existing
  behaviour; left for a follow-up rather than scope-creeping the split.
- CHANGELOG documents the SRP/file-size follow-up for corpus_objs_service.py
  (~2,700 lines; tracked for a future split, not scope-creep on this PR).

* Address PR #1685 review #3: move_documents N+1, _check_document_in_corpus rename, CAML migration

Three actionable items from the latest Claude review on the service split:

1. move_documents_to_folder N+1: the per-doc check_document_in_corpus
   loop is replaced with a set-difference against the already-locked
   DocumentPath query inside the atomic block, eliminating O(N)
   round-trips and folding the membership check into the same TOCTOU-
   coherent transaction. Error message now enumerates every missing id.

2. check_document_in_corpus -> _check_document_in_corpus to match the
   'NO PERMISSION CHECK' contract its docstring already lead with. Three
   internal callers updated; no external callers existed.

3. CAML production callsites in caml_article.py:_load_caml_document_for_user
   and corpus_types.py's resolve_documents / resolve_annotations migrated
   from the deprecated user-facing corpus.get_documents() alias to
   corpus._get_active_documents(). All three sites already enforce corpus
   READ at the upstream layer (visible_to_user lookup in caml_article;
   parent-query visibility for the CorpusType sub-resolvers), so the
   internal helper is the correct entry — silences the DeprecationWarning
   that was firing on every live CAML render.

Plus design-observation item 6: hoisted the two function-local
CorpusObjsService imports in core_agents.py (CorpusAgentContext.initialize
and CoreCorpusAgentFactory.create_context) to module level, completing
the second-pass hoist work.

subject: Add extract & analyzer agent tools (#1675)
message:
Add extract & analyzer agent tools (#1675)

* Add extract & analyzer agent tools

Six new tools let an LLM agent discover the Fieldsets and Analyzers
visible to the calling user and dispatch them just like a human would:

- list_fieldsets / start_extract / list_recent_extracts
- list_analyzers / start_analysis / list_recent_analyses

start_extract and start_analysis are approval-gated and require WRITE on
the corpus; they reuse the same Celery pipeline (run_extract,
process_analyzer) as the existing GraphQL mutations. The agent always
picks from existing Fieldsets/Analyzers — it cannot invent new schemas.
Document scope follows the agent context (corpus agent = whole corpus,
doc agent = current doc) and requested document_ids are intersected
with corpus.get_documents() so the agent can never escape its scope.

Not added to DEFAULT_DOCUMENT_ACTION_TOOLS: opt-in only via a
CorpusAction's pre_authorized_tools.

Docs updated in docs/architecture/llms/README.md,
docs/corpus_actions/intro_to_corpus_actions.md, and
docs/extract_and_retrieval/data_extraction.md.

* Fix failing tests in PR 1675

- test_async_variant_matches: wrap sync ORM calls in sync_to_async since
  test methods are async (was raising SynchronousOnlyOperation in CI under
  pytest-xdist parallel runners).
- test_start_extract/start_analysis_requires_approval: supply all required
  kwargs since PydanticAIToolWrapper._maybe_raise uses Signature.bind (not
  bind_partial), so omitting required kwargs raised TypeError before the
  approval gate could fire.

* Apply black formatting to test_extract_analyzer_tools.py

* Address review: security, N+1, double-fetch, magic numbers, test hygiene

Discovery tools (list_fieldsets, list_analyzers, list_recent_extracts,
list_recent_analyses) now check corpus visibility via
visible_to_user(user).filter(pk=...).exists() instead of bare
Corpus.objects.get(pk=...), so a caller cannot probe private corpus IDs
through an existence oracle (review item #8). The error message is
unchanged across both branches per CLAUDE.md's IDOR guidance.

list_recent_extracts and list_recent_analyses fold the per-row M2M
count into the SELECT with annotate(Count(...)) so the document_count
field no longer issues N queries on N rows (review item #1).

start_extract and start_analysis collapse the two-step
visible_to_user().exists() + .get() pattern into a single
visible_to_user().filter(pk=...).first() lookup (review item #5).
Same fix applied to the Fieldset/Analyzer lookups in those functions.

list_fieldsets now includes fieldsets pinned to the *current* corpus
(via Q(corpus__isnull=True) | Q(corpus_id=corpus_id)) so the discovery
surface matches what start_extract actually accepts — previously a
caller listing fieldsets would not see one that start_extract would
have allowed if supplied directly (review item #7).

MAX_LIST_LIMIT / DEFAULT_LIST_LIMIT / DEFAULT_RECENT_LIMIT hoisted to
opencontractserver/constants/tools.py per CLAUDE.md's no-magic-numbers
rule (review item #4).

Test hygiene: dead GremlinEngine fixture removed from
TestListRecentAnalyses.setUp (review item #10); inspect import lifted
out of test_to_core_tool_returns_async_function loop (review item #11).

* Address Claude review on PR 1675

- Prefetch columns with is_manual_entry filter at DB level
- Pin corpus_action_id lookup to the operating corpus (security:
  prevent cross-corpus lineage attribution from direct callers)
- Move process_analyzer import to module scope (no actual circular
  dependency justifies the local import)
- Reject fieldsets whose only columns are manual-entry (LLM cannot
  extract from them)
- Drop decorative section-banner comments and explain-the-what comments
- Tests: cross-corpus action ID is dropped (extract + analysis),
  outside-corpus document_id warns and falls back to full corpus,
  manual-entry-only fieldset raises, corpus_action_id lineage on
  start_analysis

* Address review: distinguish user-not-found from unauthenticated, clamp_limit tests, comment fixes

- start_extract / start_analysis now distinguish 'no user_id supplied'
  (unauthenticated) from 'user_id refers to no row' (not found), so the
  error message no longer misattributes the failure.
- Add parametrized test for _clamp_limit covering None, 0, negative,
  oversized, non-numeric, and numeric-string inputs.
- Add test pinning the user-not-found vs unauthenticated split.
- Fix misleading _patch_process_analyzer docstring (it patches the import
  site, not the source module).
- Note the intentional transaction asymmetry between start_extract and
  start_analysis so future readers don't 'fix' it.

* Address review #1675: document edge contracts + cover zero-column discovery

extracts_and_analyzers.py:
- _resolve_target_document_ids: comment the memory trade-off for very
  large corpora and point at the SQL-pushdown alternative for future
  optimization.
- start_analysis: comment that analysis_input_data is intentionally not
  pre-validated against analyzer.input_schema — validation lives in
  run_task_name_analyzer where the payload is spread into the task
  function call (TypeError on unknown kwargs). Keeps the agent path
  bug-compatible with the human GraphQL/CorpusAction path.

test_extract_analyzer_tools.py:
- Add test_listing_shows_zero_columns_then_start_rejects pinning the
  deliberate two-step failure mode: list_fieldsets shows a
  manual-entry-only fieldset with column_count=0 (discovery surface) and
  start_extract rejects it as ValueError (dispatch surface).

* Address review #1675: wrap start_analysis in atomic + clarify LLM tool schema

- Wrap process_analyzer call in transaction.atomic() so the
  on_commit task dispatch can be rolled back if anything raises
  afterwards. The previous comment claimed process_analyzer managed
  its own transaction; it does not — it just registers on_commit
  inside whatever transaction is open. In autocommit mode (Celery
  workers) the callback would fire immediately, kicking off the
  downstream task even on an error path. start_extract already wraps
  in atomic; this aligns start_analysis.
- Lift _extract_status magic strings into
  constants/tools.py (EXTRACT_STATUS_FAILED / COMPLETED / RUNNING
  / QUEUED) and use them at every call site for parity with the human
  GraphQL surface. Analyses keep using the model-sourced
  analysis.status directly.
- Tool registry descriptions for fieldset_id / analyzer_id now say
  explicitly which type they are (integer vs CharField string) and how
  to map them from the discovery tool output, since list_fieldsets
  returns int ids and list_analyzers returns string ids and the LLM
  could otherwise conflate the two.
- start_analysis comment now documents the analysis_input_data ->
  task-function injection surface so future readers know the analyzer
  task is the validation boundary.

* Address review #1675: status vocab, payload hardening, listing UX, SQL perf

- Unify analysis status vocabulary across start_analysis and
  list_recent_analyses. New ``_normalize_analysis_status`` lowercases
  the model-sourced JobStatus value; ``_ANALYSIS_STATUS_QUEUED`` is
  what start_analysis returns now (derived from
  ``JobStatus.QUEUED.value`` rather than the Extract constant), so an
  LLM polling the listing right after dispatch sees the same string
  rather than an apparent case-shift mid-lifecycle.
- Add ``ANALYSIS_INPUT_DATA_RESERVED_KEYS`` and
  ``_strip_reserved_input_keys`` to strip framework-owned kwargs
  (``analysis_id``, ``user_id``, scoping IDs) from agent-supplied
  ``analysis_input_data`` before dispatch. Warn on strip so production
  traces can flag override attempts. Closes the unique
  prompt-injection escalation surface on the agent path; the task
  itself remains the canonical validation boundary.
- Truncate oversized ``Analyzer.input_schema`` in ``list_analyzers``
  via ``_summarise_input_schema`` + ``ANALYZER_INPUT_SCHEMA_MAX_INLINE_CHARS``
  (4_000). Replaces the schema with a placeholder when its JSON dump
  exceeds the cap so a misbehaving analyzer can't inflate every
  agent's context window.
- ``list_fieldsets`` now exposes an ``extractable`` flag and orders by
  ``-created`` to match ``list_recent_extracts``. The flag surfaces
  the listing-vs-dispatch contract for manual-only/empty fieldsets
  up-front; the ordering removes the silent position shift that
  occurred when a fieldset was edited mid-session.
- Push ``_resolve_target_document_ids`` intersection into SQL via
  ``corpus.get_documents().filter(pk__in=...)`` / ``.exists()`` so
  large corpora don't load the entire active doc ID set into a
  Python ``set`` on every dispatch.
- New tests pin each contract: status normalisation, reserved-key
  strip + warning, legitimate payload pass-through, oversized
  ``input_schema`` truncation, and the ``extractable`` flag.

* Address review #1675: move asyncio marker to method level on TestApprovalGate

Stacking ``@pytest.mark.asyncio`` on the class combined with
``TransactionTestCase`` is fragile across pytest-django versions —
pytest-asyncio tries to drive every method as a native coroutine while
``TransactionTestCase`` wants to route them through Django's own
sync/async test runner. Per the latest review, the safer pattern (and
the one used elsewhere in this codebase, e.g.
``test_conversation_search.py``) is ``@pytest.mark.django_db`` on the
class + ``@pytest.mark.asyncio`` on each async test method.

The reviewer also flagged the file's five separate
``from opencontractserver.constants.tools import …`` blocks. Confirmed
non-actionable: this project's ``isort`` settings (no
``combine_as_imports``) split ``as`` aliases into their own statements,
so consolidating fails ``pre-commit``. Leaving the structure as-is.

53 tests pass after this change.

* Address review #1675: raise on scope mismatch, slim list_fieldsets, lift coverage

- _resolve_target_document_ids now raises ValueError when a document
  agent's injected document_id is not in the corpus, instead of silently
  expanding to the full corpus scope (which a single-doc agent should
  never reach). Test updated to assert the new contract.
- list_fieldsets returns column names by default; full column
  definitions (query/match_text/output_type/instructions) gated behind
  a new include_columns=true flag. Bounds the discovery payload for
  corpora with many fieldsets of many long-form columns. Tool
  description and tests updated.
- list_analyzers ordered by -created (was order_by("id"), lexicographic
  over CharField IDs and unpredictable as new analyzers are registered).
- start_extract / start_analysis descriptions now warn that omitting
  document_ids on a corpus agent dispatches against the whole corpus,
  so admins working over very large corpora know to bound it.
- Added tests: limit pagination clamp end-to-end for list_fieldsets
  and list_analyzers; all four _extract_status branches (queued /
  running / completed / failed) in list_recent_extracts.
- Removed redundant @pytest.mark.django_db on TestExtractAnalyzerRegistryIntegration
  (TransactionTestCase already provides DB isolation).
- CHANGELOG: rewrote the "extract/analyzer review follow-ups" entry to
  describe the behaviour changes rather than the review process.

* Address review #1675: lift CRUD grant into the analyzer/extract framework

Mirrors the existing create_and_setup_analysis chokepoint with a new
create_and_setup_extract helper so every Extract created through a
user-attributable flow gets guardian CRUD on the creator without the
implementer having to remember. start_extract (agent tool) and
process_corpus_action's get_or_create path now route through (or
inline) the framework grant. Docstrings on both helpers pin the
contract so a future refactor can't quietly drop it.

Other review follow-ups in the same sweep:
- Add `created` to list_recent_analyses output so an LLM polling
  right after start_analysis sees a timestamp instead of three nulls.
- list_fieldsets builds rows with stable key order (common fields
  first, payload last) for readability.
- Consolidate redundant `from opencontractserver.constants.tools`
  blocks.
- Clarify list_analyzers description: the corpus_id is a visibility
  check, not a corpus-affinity filter.
- Update include_columns description to list extract_is_list.
- _get_user_or_none gets a docstring explaining why the return type
  stays inferred (User = get_user_model() is a runtime variable, not
  a valid mypy type).

Tests:
- test_create_and_setup_analysis_grants_creator_crud — pins the
  Analysis chokepoint's CRUD contract.
- test_extract_utils.py — full coverage for the new Extract helper
  (creation, CRUD grant, document linking, started timestamp,
  corpus_action lineage, name defaulting).

Closes #1674

---------

subject: Phase B permission centralization: replace compound checks with user_can (#1656) (#1688)
message:
Phase B permission centralization: replace compound checks with user_can (#1656) (#1688)

* Phase B permission centralization: replace compound checks with user_can (#1656)

Migrates every GraphQL mutation that previously composed
`user.is_superuser or obj.creator_id == user.id or
user_has_permission_for_obj(...)` to the unified
`obj.user_can(user, perm, request=info.context)` surface introduced
in PRs #1663 and #1665. Also deletes the two compound
`_check_*_permission` helpers on `DocumentActionsQueryOptimizer`
and migrates the remaining shim calls in `DocumentRelationshipQueryOptimizer.user_has_permission`.

Every migrated check now passes `request=info.context` so the
two-tier permission cache from PR #1665 actually fires across a
mutation. `set_permissions_for_obj_to_user(...)` calls in the
mutation layer also pass `request=info.context` (plus `is_new=True`
on fresh-creation paths) so Tier-1 / Tier-2 cache invalidation lands
on grant / revoke.

A handful of legacy sites used the shim's default
`include_group_permissions=False`; the new `user_can` defaults to
`True`, matching `_default_user_can` and every other surface. Users
who hold a relevant guardian permission via a group on Documents /
Extracts / Annotations / Notes / Conversations / Labels / Badges
now pass the corresponding mutation gate, matching the read-side
`visible_to_user` queryset filters.

Net -92 LOC across 16 files. Closes #1656.

* Propagate get_or_create created flag to is_new in feedback grants

Both RejectAnnotation and ApproveAnnotation use
UserFeedback.objects.get_or_create(...), which returns (instance,
created). The Phase B migration hardcoded is_new=True on the
subsequent set_permissions_for_obj_to_user grant — incorrect when
created=False, since the row already carries guardian permission
entries that the remove_perm sweep is there to clear (e.g. a prior
CRUD → READ-only downgrade would persist).

Pass is_new=created so fresh rows get the 7-DB-op skip while
re-grants on existing rows run the full clear-and-replace path.

Flagged in code review on PR #1688.

subject: Phase C permission centralization: migrate optimizer call sites to user_can (#1689)
message:
Phase C permission centralization: migrate optimizer call sites to user_can (#1689)

Closes #1657.

Migrates the 24 remaining user_has_permission_for_obj call sites in
AnnotationQueryOptimizer and MetadataQueryOptimizer to the user_can
surface introduced in Phase A (#1655 / PR #1663). Completes the
substitution that PR #1663 started in
AnnotationQueryOptimizer._compute_effective_permissions.

annotations/query_optimizer.py (13 sites):
- get_document_annotations analysis check
- get_corpus_annotations corpus READ check
- get_document_relationships analysis check
- check_analysis_permission analysis + corpus READ
- get_visible_analyses corpus READ
- get_analysis_annotations document READ (single + loop)
- check_extract_permission extract + corpus READ
- get_visible_extracts corpus READ

  Six GraphQL field resolvers thread `request=info.context` so the
  Tier-2 request-scoped cache from PR #1665 fires on the per-row

  tasks, the websocket consumer, and import services have no GraphQL
  request in scope and omit the kwarg — they degrade gracefully to
  Tier 1 instance caching.

Semantic widening (consistent with Phase B / C):
  - Creator-honoring is now uniform across the migrated agent tools,
    websocket consumer, Celery tasks, and import services. A creator
    who never received an explicit guardian grant now passes these
    gates, matching the read-side visible_to_user filters.
