    include_group_permissions=False; the new obj.user_can(...) defaults
    to True, matching _default_user_can and every other
    Manager.user_can / obj.user_can surface. Users who hold the relevant
    permission via a group on Corpuses / Documents / Extracts now pass
    these gates; this matches the documented per-model policy.

xdist-safe auth_permission teardown (conftest.py):
  Surfaced a pre-existing race that Phase E's batch concentration
  exposed routinely. TransactionTestCase._fixture_teardown -> Django
  flush -> emit_post_migrate_signal ->
  django.contrib.auth.management.create_permissions ->
  Permission.objects.bulk_create races across xdist workers on the
  shared auth_permission table (postgres content_type ids overlap
  across the per-worker test DBs because they're assigned serially
  during migrate). The (content_type_id, codename) unique constraint
  produces IntegrityError for whichever worker loses; the loser's
  teardown then dies un-rolled-back and the next test's setUp finds an
  empty fixture, cascading into User.DoesNotExist setUp failures.

  Fix is a session-scoped autouse fixture in the root conftest.py that
  re-registers the post_migrate handler with a thin wrapper:
  `with transaction.atomic(using=using): create_permissions(...)` plus
  `except IntegrityError: pass`. The conflicting rows are exactly the
  permissions we'd have inserted anyway (winning worker already wrote
  them), so the swallow is a true no-op and the atomic block guarantees
  no half-inserted state leaks past the rollback. The fixture restores
  the original handler at session teardown.

Acceptance criteria pinned by the verification runs:
  - zero user_has_permission_for_obj call sites remain (verified by
    grep); the only surviving references are docstring / comment
    mentions of the shim and its phase history.
  - 370 tests across the LLM / agent-tool / image-tools / CAML /
    extracts-and-analyzers / agent-factory / individual-extract /
    extract-tasks / agent-tasks suites pass green under
    `-n 4 --dist loadscope`.
  - the previously-failing 14-file websocket + celery + import batch
    runs clean under the same `-n 4 --dist loadscope` after the
    conftest fix.

* Phase E: address review feedback on user_can migration (#1659)

- conftest.py make_create_permissions_xdist_safe: assert that the
  disconnect actually removed a receiver instead of silently no-oping.
  If Django ever changes the dispatch_uid that AuthConfig.ready uses
  to register create_permissions, the unsafe original handler would
  stay wired up and quietly re-introduce the xdist race this fixture
  exists to fix. The assertion turns that silent regression into a
  loud setup failure.
- test_document_imports_rest.py ImportServicesTests:
  test_import_document_for_user_honors_group_permission pins the
  Phase E widening at the import-service boundary. A user holding
  update_corpus only via a Django Group now passes the EDIT gate
  through corpus.user_can(...) (default include_group_permissions=True);
  the legacy user_has_permission_for_obj shim defaulted to False, so
  this exact scenario would have been blocked before Phase E. Future
  refactors that quietly revert to user-only checks will fail this test.

subject: Fix V2 import: folder_path resolution tolerates exporter path conventions (#1703)
message:
Fix V2 import: folder_path resolution tolerates exporter path conventions (#1703)

* Fix V2 import: folder_path resolution tolerates exporter path conventions

Documents imported from a V2 corpus zip silently landed at folder=NULL
when the exporter (e.g. an EDGAR scraper that builds the ZIP itself)
wrote slug-joined folder paths into document_paths[*].folder_path
instead of the canonical name-joined get_path() form. The importer
indexed folders only by the freshly-imported CorpusFolder.get_path(),
so the lookup missed every row and the corpus document browser showed
0 in every folder while the sidebar still reported the full count.

_reconstruct_document_paths now consults a multi-key lookup that
indexes by both the imported folder's get_path() and the export's own
folder.path field. As long as folder.path and folder_path use the
same convention within one export, the lookup resolves regardless of
which convention the exporter chose. Unresolved folder_path values
now emit a structured warning instead of failing silently.

Adds TestV2FolderPathReconstruction with regression coverage for
canonical (name-joined) exports, slug-joined exports, the helper's
key set, partial folder-creation failure, and the new warning.
Existing TestReconstructDocumentPaths cases are updated to the new
signature.

* Fix pytest failure and address Claude review for V2 folder_path

- Update test_ingestion_source.py callers to the new
  _reconstruct_document_paths signature (folders_data /
  folder_export_id_to_obj added in 9820da10b) — the two callers regressed
  to TypeError after the helper picked up the multi-key folder lookup.
- _build_folder_path_lookup now logs a WARNING when two folders collide on
  the same lookup key (one folder's exported path equals a sibling's
  get_path()).  Last writer wins, but the silent mis-attribution becomes
  grep-able — same posture as the unresolved-folder warning the original
  PR introduced.
- Empty-string exported paths are no longer registered: they would fuse
  every empty-path folder onto the "" key.  get_path() keys still resolve
  the same folder.
- Cap the "unresolved folder_path" log message at the first
  _UNRESOLVED_FOLDER_KEY_SAMPLE_SIZE keys and report the total count.
  Datadog/CloudWatch truncate long lines, which would have hidden the
  very keys an operator needs to compare against.
- Tighten _build_folder_path_lookup's docstring: the path field is
  effectively required end-to-end (import_corpus_folders accesses
  f["path"] non-defensively for sort order), so the helper's both-keys
  insert is for "absent or empty" rather than legacy formats.
- New regression coverage: test_build_lookup_skips_empty_exported_path
  and test_build_lookup_warns_on_key_collision.

subject: Phase A follow-up: visible_to_user ordering, dead override, user_can types (#1702)
message:
Phase A follow-up: visible_to_user ordering, dead override, user_can types (#1702)

* Phase A follow-up: visible_to_user ordering, dead override, and user_can types (#1668)

Closes #1668. Three hygiene fixes deferred from PR #1663:

- Remove asymmetric `order_by("created")` from the superuser branch of
  `BaseVisibilityManager.visible_to_user` and `PermissionedTreeQuerySet.
  visible_to_user`. Authenticated/anonymous branches were already
  unordered, so ordering became user-dependent (pagination + downstream
  consumers saw different orderings for superusers vs everyone else).
  Ordering is now consistently owned by the resolver / caller. The tree
  queryset's superuser branch keeps `.with_tree_fields()` to stay
  symmetric with the authenticated branch.

- Delete `DocumentManager.user_can` — it was a pure `super()` passthrough
  with no runtime behaviour. Documents use the default rules from
  `BaseVisibilityManager` (public-corpus visibility is encoded at
  creation time via `is_public` auto-propagation). Rationale moved into
  the `DocumentManager` class docstring.

- Tighten `user_can` type annotations across `UserCanMixin`,
  `InstanceUserCanMixin`, `UserFeedbackManager`, `AnnotationManager`,
  `NoteManager`, `RelationshipManager`, and the `AnnotationManager`
  privacy/effective-permission helpers. `Any` is replaced with the
  same contract `_default_user_can` already uses:
  `int | str | UserModel | AnonymousUser | None` for `user`,
  `Model` for `instance`, `PermissionTypes` for `permission`. Helpers
  reached after `resolve_user_for_user_can` use the narrower
  `UserModel | AnonymousUser`. `request: Any` stays loose to match the
  GraphQL info.context contract elsewhere in the codebase.

Behavior is unchanged — type tightening is purely static under
`from __future__ import annotations`, the dead override resolves
identically via MRO, and the Phase A invariant suite
(`test_authorization_invariants.py`) is a set-equality check unaffected
by ordering removal.

* Fix linter: pyupgrade rewrites + mypy attr-defined; address Claude review

- pyupgrade unquoted the union type annotations on `user_can` /
  `_default_user_can` helpers across `shared/Managers.py` and
  `shared/user_can_mixin.py`.  Both files already use
  `from __future__ import annotations`, so the strings were redundant.
- mypy: the type-tightening (`instance: Any` → `instance: Model`) tripped
  ``[attr-defined]`` on the model-specific attribute accesses inside
  ``AnnotationManager._check_annotation_privacy_recursion`` (created_by_*),
  ``AnnotationManager._compute_annotation_effective_permission`` and
  ``RelationshipManager.user_can`` (document_id / corpus_id / creator_id).
  Those helpers run only against their concrete subclass at runtime — the
  `Model` annotation is the intentional public contract.  Suppress with
  scoped ``# type: ignore[attr-defined]`` comments on the specific access
  lines and leave the helper signatures intact.
- Address Claude review suggestion: add
  ``PermissionedTreeQuerySetSuperuserTreeFieldsTest`` pinning that the
  superuser branch of ``PermissionedTreeQuerySet.visible_to_user`` still
  applies ``.with_tree_fields()`` — the original Phase A follow-up fix
  for ``QuerySets.py`` silently corrected this regression and the
  pre-existing invariant test didn't cover it.

* Update superuser order_by tests to match new behaviour; add CHANGELOG entry

Tests at test_resolvers.py:71 and test_visibility_managers.py:83 were pinning
the OLD order_by("created") that this PR intentionally removes from superuser
branches. Update them to assert no manager-imposed ordering — the ordering is
owned by the resolver / caller per Fix #5 in the issue #1668 review.

Also adds the missing CHANGELOG entry the latest review flagged, documenting
the with_tree_fields() restoration as a bug fix (not just an ordering change).

subject: Restore MIN-permission semantic on CorpusType.documents resolver (#1682) (#1723)
message:
Restore MIN-permission semantic on CorpusType.documents resolver (#1682) (#1723)

Closes #1682

PR #1699's CAML migration silently flipped corpus_types.py:resolve_documents
from the MIN-permission semantic (a Document.objects.visible_to_user
intersection) to the corpus-as-gate CorpusObjsService.get_corpus_documents.
The flip meant any document with an active path in a corpus the requester
could merely READ -- including a private document inside a shared or public
corpus the requester had no document-level access to -- surfaced through the
GraphQL documents field, contradicting the documented
MIN(document_permission, corpus_permission) model.

Per issue #1682's recommended Option B:

- corpus-as-gate stays the documented service default for pipeline-facing
  callers (MCP, discovery, badge/analysis tasks).
- New CorpusObjsService.get_corpus_documents_visible_to_user carries the
  MIN-permission semantic: it gates corpus READ, then intersects the corpus
  document set with Document.objects.visible_to_user.
- resolve_documents delegates to the new method, restoring its pre-#1699
  behaviour.
- The two semantics are separately named so no caller can silently swap one
  for the other; the decision is documented in CLAUDE.md's Permission System
  section.

New TestGetCorpusDocumentsVisibleToUser covers the service method;
CorpusResolveDocumentsRespectsDocumentVisibilityTest is a GraphQL-level
regression guard pinning that a collaborator cannot see a private document
through corpus.documents.

subject: Skip coverage instrumentation on pull-request CI runs (#1713)
message:
Skip coverage instrumentation on pull-request CI runs (#1713)

* Skip coverage instrumentation on pull-request CI runs

The Backend CI pytest invocation now passes --cov/--cov-report only on
push events (merges to a protected branch); pull-request runs execute
the suite without coverage. coverage.py's C trace function (the test
image is on Python 3.11, so COVERAGE_CORE=sysmon is unavailable) adds
noticeable wall time to the full ~6.4k-test suite on every PR push.
Coverage is still measured on every merge, so Codecov's tracked metric
on main is unaffected; only the per-PR coverage delta is dropped. The
coverage verify/upload steps are gated to push events accordingly.

Phase 1 of bringing the backend suite under 20 minutes (see #1710, #1711).

https://claude.ai/code/session_01C7HrbHms9tPEmpWD1yeUXm

* Reset PipelineSettings cache between tests to prevent cross-test poisoning

PipelineSettings.get_instance(use_cache=True) writes the singleton into a
process-global cache that is not transaction-aware. A TestCase mutating the
singleton inside its rolled-back transaction leaks the mutated object into
the cache (cache.set runs while the uncommitted change is visible); the DB
row rolls back but the cached object does not, poisoning later tests on the
same xdist worker.

EnabledComponentsMutationTestCase sets default_embedder="" in setUp; a
rejection-path mutation then caches that empty value and returns early
without a save() to invalidate it. Subsequent agent/vector-store tests hit
get_embedder -> get_default_embedder and fail with "resolved no
embedder_path".

Add an autouse fixture that clears PipelineSettings.CACHE_KEY before and
after every test, restoring the per-test cache isolation the LocMemCache
test setting is meant to provide.

* Scope PipelineSettings cache-poisoning fix to the offending test class

The autouse reset_pipeline_settings_cache fixture in conftest.py cleared the
PipelineSettings singleton cache around every one of the ~6.4k tests. That
broad blast radius made the PR-CI backend run hang in its final scope (the
suite reached 99% then stalled until the 100-minute step timeout), whereas the
prior commit without the fixture completed in 37 minutes.

Replace the global fixture with a tearDown on EnabledComponentsMutationTestCase
— the single class the fixture's own diagnosis identified as the poison
source. It sets default_embedder="" in setUp and a rejection-path mutation
re-caches the empty-embedder instance; the tearDown clears PipelineSettings.
CACHE_KEY after each of its tests so the poison cannot leak to the next test
class on the same xdist worker. Same root-cause fix, surgical scope.

subject: Phase D: standardize IDOR pattern via get_for_user_or_none (#1658) (#1693)
message:
Phase D: standardize IDOR pattern via get_for_user_or_none (#1658) (#1693)

* Add IDOR-safe get_for_user_or_none helper (Phase D, #1658)

Adds a generic non-corpus-scoped lookup helper in
opencontractserver/utils/permissioning.py that collapses 'pk does
not exist' and 'pk exists but caller lacks READ' into the same
None return value, so mutation call sites can render a single
unified 'not found or no permission' message and stop leaking
object existence via differential error text.

For document lookups in a corpus context, callers continue to use
CorpusObjsService.get_corpus_document_by_id (PR #1685) — the
helper's docstring cross-references that to prevent two parallel
IDOR-safe APIs from drifting.

Unit tests pin all six branches: creator, public, missing pk,
inaccessible pk, explicit grant unlock, superuser, anonymous
(private vs public), garbage pk input, None pk.

* Phase D: migrate extract_mutations to get_for_user_or_none (#1658)

UpdateExtractMutation: collapse the Extract / Corpus / Fieldset
fetch-then-permission-check sequence onto get_for_user_or_none so
the response is identical whether the pk doesn't exist or the
caller lacks the required permission. Removes three try/except
DoesNotExist blocks and the dev-leftover print() trace.

CreateExtractIteration: same pattern on the source extract
lookup — previously a non-existent pk and a no-READ pk returned
different messages ('Source extract not found.' vs 'You don't
have permission to read this extract.').

Also makes get_for_user_or_none generic over the model TypeVar
so mypy preserves the concrete model attributes through the
helper (extract.fieldset, extract.corpus, etc. type-check).

* Phase D: migrate DeleteAnalysisMutation to get_for_user_or_none (#1658)

Previously the three branches raised three different exception
types depending on whether the analysis didn't exist, was hidden
from the caller, or existed-and-was-readable-but-not-deletable.
That leaked object existence to anyone with a guessable pk.

Now: a single not_found_msg propagates through both the helper's
None-return and the DELETE permission check, so a missing pk and
an inaccessible pk are indistinguishable to the caller.

Lock-conflict path stays its own message — the lock is observable
state to anyone who already has READ, so it doesn't leak.

* Phase D: migrate agent_mutations to get_for_user_or_none (#1658)

CreateAgentConfigurationMutation / UpdateAgentConfigurationMutation
/ DeleteAgentConfigurationMutation already returned the same
'<resource> not found' message for the 'pk hidden' and 'pk
visible-but-no-CRUD' branches, but each one rolled its own
visible_to_user(user).get(pk=...) + try/except DoesNotExist
boilerplate. Route them through get_for_user_or_none so the
fetch-and-gate logic lives in one place.

Behaviour unchanged: tests in opencontractserver/tests/test_agents.py
all pass (one pre-existing failure on main —
TestSearchAgentsForMention::test_search_agents_returns_global_agents
— is unrelated to this change and was confirmed by reverting
agent_mutations.py and rerunning).

* Phase D: migrate corpus_mutations to get_for_user_or_none (#1658)

Migrated 8 sites: UpdateCorpusMutation (preferred_embedder pre-check
that previously leaked corpus existence to unauthorised callers
via the has_documents early-exit), UpdateCorpusDescription,
DeleteCorpusMutation (is_personal pre-check), StartCorpusFork,
ReEmbedCorpus, CreateCorpusAction, AddTemplateToCorpus, and
ToggleCorpusMemory. Each now uses get_for_user_or_none so a
missing pk and an inaccessible pk collapse to the same response.

SetCorpusVisibility deliberately retains its bare Corpus.objects.get
because the mutation supports a sharing pattern where a user is
granted PermissionTypes.PERMISSION without an explicit READ
codename — pinned by test_user_with_permission_perm_can_change_visibility.
get_for_user_or_none filters by visible_to_user (READ codename),
which would lock that path out. The bare lookup keeps the
PERMISSION-without-READ shortcut alive, and the mutation is still
IDOR-safe at the response level because both not-found and
no-permission branches return the same message. Inline rationale
added to the SetCorpusVisibility mutate body.

AddTemplateToCorpus loses its dead except Corpus.DoesNotExist
handler now that the lookup goes through the helper instead of
raising.

* Phase D: migrate badge_mutations to get_for_user_or_none (#1658)

AwardBadgeMutation Badge + Corpus lookups now route through the
helper. Both originally used Badge.objects.visible_to_user(user).get()
/ Corpus.objects.visible_to_user(user).get() with try/except
DoesNotExist boilerplate — collapsing the fetch and READ-gate into
get_for_user_or_none keeps the same behaviour with less code.

User (recipient) lookup deliberately retains the bare
User.objects.get because UserProfileManager.visible_to_user has no
superuser bypass — applying the helper would lock superuser
awarders out from awarding badges to private-profile users.
Inline rationale added to the call site.

UserBadge (RevokeBadgeMutation) lookup retains the bare ORM call
because UserBadge has no visible_to_user manager (join table).

* Phase D: migrate DeleteMultipleLabelMutation to get_for_user_or_none (#1658)

AnnotationLabel uses creator-based permissions (no guardian
tables) so BaseVisibilityManager.visible_to_user resolves to
creator/public/superuser — exactly the gate the existing
post-fetch check enforced. Route the AnnotationLabel lookup
through get_for_user_or_none so the missing-pk and not-the-creator
branches converge on the same 'Label not found' response.

LabelSet lookups in CreateLabelForLabelsetMutation and
RemoveLabelsFromLabelsetMutation deliberately keep their bare
LabelSet.objects.get because the mutations support a collaborator
pattern where a non-owner has guardian UPDATE on the labelset
without an explicit READ codename (pinned by
test_non_owner_with_explicit_update_permission_can_create and
test_remove_labels_allows_non_owner_with_explicit_update_permission).
get_for_user_or_none would filter those collaborators out via
visible_to_user (READ codename). Inline rationale at both sites.

* Phase D: migrate conversation_mutations to get_for_user_or_none (#1658)

Six call sites consolidated onto the helper:
 - CreateThreadMutation: Corpus + Document lookups
 - CreateThreadMessageMutation: Conversation lookup
 - ReplyToMessageMutation: parent ChatMessage lookup
 - DeleteConversationMutation: Conversation lookup
 - DeleteMessageMutation: ChatMessage lookup

Each previously did Model.objects.visible_to_user(user).get(pk=...)
with try/except DoesNotExist boilerplate — the helper compresses
the IDOR-safe pattern to one line and lifts the gate logic into
a single audited surface.

UpdateMessageMutation's lookup is intentionally left untouched:
it uses select_related to avoid N+1s on conversation/corpus/creator,
and that prefetch shape doesn't compose with the helper's
visible_to_user(user).filter(pk=pk).first() chain. The site is
already IDOR-safe via the visible_to_user filter.

* Phase D: migrate RetryDocumentProcessing to get_for_user_or_none (#1658)

The only bare Document.objects.get(pk=...) followed by a READ
check in document_mutations.py. The remaining sites in this file
either route through a corpus context (which the issue scopes to
CorpusObjsService) or already use visible_to_user(user).get(pk=...).

The local user_has_permission_for_obj(READ) check that gated the
'document not found' response post-fetch is now subsumed by the
helper's visible_to_user filter — same observable behaviour for
private / shared / public documents.

* Phase D: migrate document_relationship_mutations to get_for_user_or_none (#1658)

CreateDocumentRelationship: route the Corpus / Document
lookups through the helper. The downstream user_has_permission_for_obj
checks (CREATE on each of corpus, source doc, target doc) stay
in place — the helper just collapses the 'pk missing' and
'pk hidden' branches into one None so the IDOR-safe response
message ('Corpus not found', 'Source document not found', etc.)
is reached the same way regardless of which gate failed.

UpdateDocumentRelationship.corpus_id update path: same pattern.
The corpus-membership check at L386 still uses
CorpusObjsService.get_corpus_documents per PR #1685 so the
service-layer rule from CLAUDE.md is preserved.

* Phase D: migrate Add/RemoveDocumentsFromCorpus to get_for_user_or_none (#1658)

Both mutations did a Corpus.objects.visible_to_user(user).get()
wrapped in try/except DoesNotExist with a unified IDOR-safe
message. Compress the fetch-and-gate logic onto the helper and
drop the now-dead except handlers.

Both still delegate the per-document corpus-membership and
permission checks to DocumentFolderService — that service-layer
boundary is left intact.

* Phase D: CHANGELOG entry for IDOR-safe helper migration (#1658)

* Phase D: enforce READ as precondition for non-READ ops (#1658)

The three sites previously kept on bare Model.objects.get encoded
a permission-model assumption that the user has explicitly retired:
granting PERMISSION/UPDATE without an explicit READ codename, or
restricting User profile visibility from superusers performing
admin operations. Both are now treated as mistakes.

Migration:

- config/graphql/corpus_mutations.py: SetCorpusVisibility now
  routes the Corpus lookup through get_for_user_or_none. A caller
  with PERMISSION (or UPDATE, or DELETE) but no READ no longer
  reaches the visibility-toggle path. Malformed IDs collapse to
  the unified ok=False response instead of bubbling.

- config/graphql/label_mutations.py: CreateLabelForLabelsetMutation
  and RemoveLabelsFromLabelsetMutation route the LabelSet lookup
  through get_for_user_or_none. A collaborator with UPDATE but no
  READ no longer reaches the create/remove path.

- opencontractserver/users/models.py: UserProfileManager.visible_to_user
  now has a superuser bypass mirroring BaseVisibilityManager —
  administrative paths (badge awarding) reach private-profile
  users while non-superuser callers still only see own + public
  profiles.

- config/graphql/badge_mutations.py: AwardBadgeMutation routes
  the recipient User lookup through get_for_user_or_none. With
  the new superuser bypass on the manager, superuser awarders
  still reach private-profile users.

Test updates pin the new contract:

- test_user_with_permission_perm_can_change_visibility grants

- test_non_owner_with_explicit_update_permission_can_create grants
  [READ, UPDATE] (was [UPDATE]).
- test_remove_labels_allows_non_owner_with_explicit_update_permission
  grants [READ, UPDATE] (was [UPDATE]).
- test_invalid_id_format_returns_error now asserts the unified
  ok=False/'not found or you don't have permission' response
  rather than a GraphQL errors entry, matching the helper's
  ValueError/TypeError swallowing for garbage pks.

Verification: 115 passing tests across the affected files
(test_corpus_visibility, test_label_mutations, test_badges,
test_badge_visibility, test_user_visibility). Pre-commit clean.

CHANGELOG updated to document the rule + the superuser bypass and
drop the now-stale 'deliberately retained' section.

* Phase D: address review feedback on get_for_user_or_none migration (#1658)

- Restore is_new=True + request=info.context on every creation site
  stripped during the migration (agent / badge / conversation / label /
  extract creation paths and _clone_fieldset_for_iteration). Avoids
  ~7 DB ops per create and the N*(N+1) blow-up on FIELDSET-axis
  iteration clones flagged in the Phase D review.
- DeleteAnalysisMutation: route the IDOR not-found / no-permission /
  no-DELETE branches through the unified ok=False envelope (matches
  every other Phase-D-migrated mutation). Lock-held branch also moves
  to ok=False for response-shape consistency. Helper test still pins
  the success path so the existing regression remains intact.
- DeleteCorpusMutation: short-circuit the IDOR path with the model's
  own DoesNotExist instead of falling through to super().mutate(),
  which would have triggered a second visibility-filtered query on
  the same pk.
- StartCorpusFork: shorten the defense-in-depth comment to a single
  line referencing #1658 so the code reads more cleanly.
- Pin the AwardBadgeMutation private-profile semantic in
  TestBadgeGraphQLMutations.test_non_superuser_cannot_award_to_private_profile_recipient:
  a non-superuser corpus owner gets the unified "User not found"
  envelope when the recipient profile is private, and a superuser
  bypasses the filter and succeeds with the same payload. Locks the
  Phase-D UserProfileManager.visible_to_user superuser branch.

* Address Phase D review: IDOR-safe DeleteCorpusMutation, broaden from_global_id catches, swap label gates

Addresses the three issues + one nit raised in Claude's PR 1693 review.

Issue 1 (corpus_mutations.py): DeleteCorpusMutation no longer inherits
``DRFDeletion`` to avoid the fragile exception-for-flow-control pattern
where the unauthorized/not-found branch raised ``Corpus.DoesNotExist``
and relied on the parent's behavior surfacing as a GraphQL ``errors``
entry — exactly the IDOR leak Phase D is closing. The deletion logic
(lookup, user-lock check, user_can(DELETE), delete) is now inlined on
the unified ``ok=False`` envelope, matching every other Phase-D-migrated
mutation. ``is_personal`` stays a distinct ``GraphQLError`` because it
is observable to anyone who can READ the corpus (exposed on
``CorpusType``), so it does not leak existence.

Issue 2 (analysis_mutations.py): wrap ``from_global_id`` in
``DeleteAnalysisMutation`` with ``try/except Exception`` — bare
``binascii.Error`` from malformed base64 was bypassing the ``ValueError``/
``TypeError`` catch in ``get_for_user_or_none`` and surfacing as raw
GraphQL errors instead of the unified ``ok=False`` envelope.

Issue 3 (corpus_mutations.py): ``ToggleCorpusMemory`` widens its
``from_global_id`` ``except`` from ``(ValueError, IndexError)`` to bare

broader catch used at the file's other migrated ``from_global_id``
sites.

``user_can(READ)`` check after ``get_for_user_or_none`` — the helper
already enforces READ via ``visible_to_user``, so the double-check
ran an extra permission evaluation per request without changing the
control-flow outcome.

Nit 6 (label_mutations.py): ``DeleteMultipleLabelMutation`` swaps the
creator gate to run before the ``read_only`` gate. Previously a
non-creator who could READ a public read-only label got
"Cannot delete read-only labels", revealing both existence and the
read-only flag; the new order returns the unified "Label not found"
for any non-creator path and only surfaces the read-only message to
the creator (who already knows the label exists).

Updates two existing tests in ``test_permissioned_querysets.py``
(``test_mutation_permissions``, ``test_mutation_permissions_on_private_object``)
that asserted the pre-Phase-D ``data["deleteCorpus"] is None +
errors[]`` shape — they now assert the unified ``ok=False`` envelope
with no top-level ``errors`` and document the rationale.

in scope: ``config/graphql/social_queries.py:436, 695`` consume the
manager for the leaderboard surface, and widening superuser visibility
there is consistent with ``BaseVisibilityManager`` and the broader
"superusers see everything" policy.

* Address Phase D review + update IDOR-pattern test

decode global ids up-front so a malformed corpus_id / document_id surfaces
as the unified "not found / no permission" envelope instead of echoing
raw exception text through the outer ``except Exception as e`` handler
(matches every other Phase-D-migrated mutation; closes the residual
enumeration channel flagged in the latest PR #1693 review).

+ errors[]`` shape to the unified ``ok=False + 'not found or you don't
have permission'`` envelope that DeleteCorpusMutation now returns after
the IDOR fix in commit 77f5a9a81.

* Address review: guard from_global_id, unify is_personal envelope (#1658)

- UpdateExtractMutation: wrap from_global_id for id/corpus_id/fieldset_id

- DeleteCorpusMutation: return ok=False for the is_personal rejection
  instead of raising GraphQLError, so the frontend can pattern-match a

- label_mutations: replace LabelSet.DoesNotExist control-flow raises in

  explicit early returns, and guard from_global_id parsing.
- StartCorpusFork: use the unified not-found message.
- UpdateCorpusDescription: clarify creator-only gate in a comment.
- Add tests: get_for_user_or_none raises on a model lacking
  visible_to_user; deleteCorpus is_personal returns unified envelope.

* Fix CI: update Phase D pinning tests and deleteCorpus toast handler

StartCorpusFork and DeleteCorpusMutation now return unified IDOR-safe
ok=False envelopes instead of the prior literals / GraphQLError, so
three pre-existing tests asserted stale behavior:

- test_cannot_fork_private_corpus_without_permission
- test_same_error_for_nonexistent_corpus
- test_cannot_delete_personal_corpus

Updated their expectations to the unified message / envelope. Also
fixed handleDeleteCorpus in Corpuses.tsx, which fired a success toast
on any resolved promise — a rejected delete (e.g. personal corpus)
now resolves with ok=False and previously showed a false success.

- ReEmbedCorpus returned "Invalid corpus ID" on from_global_id parse
  failure while every other migrated site returns the unified "Corpus
  not found"; aligned it.
- CreateAgentConfigurationMutation and AwardBadgeMutation decoded
  corpus_id inside the outer try, so a malformed id bubbled to the
  generic catch instead of the corpus-specific envelope; wrapped each
  decode in its own pre-guarded try.
- Documented the UserProfileManager.visible_to_user superuser bypass
  in the permissioning guide so it is not inadvertently reverted.

* Address review: pre-guard from_global_id at remaining migrated sites (#1658)

Phase D IDOR review follow-up. get_for_user_or_none catches malformed-pk
ValueError/TypeError after the ORM call, but cannot help when from_global_id
itself raises (binascii.Error on malformed base64) before the helper runs —
the outer mutation except-handler then returned a generic message instead of
the unified IDOR-safe envelope.

- Wrap from_global_id in agent_mutations.py (Update/Delete AgentConfiguration)
  and conversation_mutations.py (CreateThread corpus + document arms,
  CreateThreadMessage, ReplyToMessage, DeleteConversation, DeleteMessage) so a
  malformed id returns the same not-found/no-permission response.
- Unify CreateAgentConfigurationMutation's malformed-id and not-found branches
  to emit the identical string.
- AddDocumentsToCorpus / RemoveDocumentsFromCorpus decode the corpus id and
  the document ids in separate guards so a malformed document id no longer
  returns a misleading corpus-scoped error message.
- Add docScreenshot to CorpusesView.ct.tsx (covers the Corpuses view touched
  by the handleDeleteCorpus toast fix).
- CHANGELOG: document the from_global_id pre-guard hardening.

* Add component tests for handleDeleteCorpus ok / error envelope branches

PR #1693 reworked handleDeleteCorpus to branch on the resolved
DeleteCorpusMutation envelope (ok=true -> success toast, ok=false -> error
toast) instead of always toasting success. The frontend patch had no test
covering the new branches, so codecov/patch/Frontend failed.

Adds two CorpusesView component tests that seed the delete-confirmation modal
via a new initialDeletingCorpus wrapper prop, click "Yes", and exercise the
ok=true and ok=false paths of handleDeleteCorpus. The wrapper prop lets the
test reach the confirmation flow without driving the corpus-card context menu.

* Address review: pre-guard remaining bare from_global_id calls

The latest review found from_global_id decodes that were still unguarded, so
a malformed base64 id fell through to an outer except and produced a leaked
decode error instead of the unified IDOR-safe envelope:

- corpus_mutations.py: StartCorpusFork, CreateCorpusAction, AddTemplateToCorpus

subject: Honour group object-permissions in QuerySet.visible_to_user (#1714) (#1724)
message:
Honour group object-permissions in QuerySet.visible_to_user (#1714) (#1724)

* Honour group object-permissions in QuerySet.visible_to_user (#1714)

Manager.user_can resolves group object-permissions (_default_user_can
runs with include_group_permissions=True), but the visible_to_user
filters in shared/QuerySets.py only joined the user object-permission
table. A user whose only READ grant on a Document / Annotation / Note
was via a group passed obj.user_can(user, READ) yet was excluded from
Model.objects.visible_to_user(user) -- authorized for the object but
unable to ever see it in a list query. Corpus was unaffected (its
PermissionedTreeQuerySet resolves group perms via get_objects_for_user).

PermissionQuerySet, DocumentQuerySet, and AnnotationQuerySet now OR in
a subquery against the model's *groupobjectpermission table filtered by
the requesting user's group ids. NoteQuerySet inherits the fix
transitively via the Document/Corpus managers it composes. Group ids
resolve as a lazy values_list subquery so the filter stays a single
round-trip.

New GroupObjectPermissionVisibilityTest pins filter/check equivalence
for a group-shared user across Document, Annotation, Note, and the
generic PermissionQuerySet body, plus the read/write asymmetry and the
subquery-not-per-group-round-trip performance property.

Closes #1714

* Convert group-perm drift pin to equivalence assertion; address review

The Phase F drift test test_group_shared_known_drift_user_can_vs_visible_to_user
pinned the pre-#1714 behaviour where visible_to_user ignored group
object-permissions. Issue #1714 closes that drift, so the test is renamed to
test_group_shared_read_user_can_vs_visible_to_user_equivalence and now asserts
filter/check equivalence; the file's audit comment is updated to match.

Address review: extract user_group_ids to a local variable in
PermissionQuerySet/DocumentQuerySet for parity with AnnotationQuerySet, and add
custom failure messages to test_note_group_grant_filter_check_equivalence.

* Cover except LookupError group-table fallback in AnnotationQuerySet

Adds a test that simulates a missing guardian *groupobjectpermission
table so the except LookupError branches in
AnnotationQuerySet.visible_to_user execute, closing the codecov patch
coverage gap on lines 515 and 530.

* Address review: split user/group guardian lookups into separate try blocks

DocumentQuerySet and PermissionQuerySet resolved both the user-level
and group-level guardian object-permission tables inside a single try
block, so a LookupError raised resolving the group table silently
discarded the already-resolved user-level grants. Split the lookups so
each except LookupError branch zeroes only its own permitted-id set,
matching the AnnotationQuerySet pattern. Extends the coverage test to
exercise all three queryset fallback paths.

* Address review: document lightweight=True in group-perf test

The perf pin test_group_lookup_uses_subquery_not_per_group_round_trips
passes lightweight=True to skip heavy prefetch fan-outs; add a comment
clarifying that the captured query count then reflects only the core
visibility query that group resolution touches.

* Fix missing TransactionTestCase import in test_corpus_objs_service

TestGetCorpusDocumentsVisibleToUser (added by #1682) subclasses
TransactionTestCase, but the #1722 TransactionTestCase->TestCase
conversion removed the import, leaving an F821 that broke the linter.

subject: Fix white horizontal stripes in multi-line annotation highlights (#1729)
message:
Fix white horizontal stripes in multi-line annotation highlights (#1729)

* Fix white horizontal stripes through multi-line annotation highlights

Annotation highlights are drawn as a SelectionBoundary rectangle plus
per-token SelectionBox rectangles. With bounding boxes toggled off (the
default), SelectionBoundary forced its background opacity to 0, so only
the per-token boxes rendered and the line-leading gap between text rows
showed through as a white stripe on every line of a multi-line
annotation. The gap scales with zoom while the gap-bridging token
expansion and shadow are fixed pixels, so the stripes were most visible
at the high zoom typical of mobile viewing and on wrapped headers.

Decouple the boundary's translucent fill from the showBoundingBox
toggle: the fill now renders whenever the annotation is not hidden,
backing the per-token highlights so inter-line gaps no longer show
through as white. Only the box-shadow halo stays gated by
showBoundingBox.

subject: Add ingest-time enrichment pipeline stage with PdfOutlineEnricher (#1730)
message:
Add ingest-time enrichment pipeline stage with PdfOutlineEnricher (#1730)

* Add ingest-time enrichment stage and PDF outline enricher

Introduces BaseEnricher, a chainable OpenContractDocExport transform run
inside BaseParser.process_document() between parse_document() and
save_parsed_data() -- the ingest-time analogue of the export-time
BasePostProcessor chain. One or more enrichers run in sequence, each
receiving the previous enricher's output.

Enrichers are configured per MIME type as an ordered list via the new
PipelineSettings.preferred_enrichers field (empty by default, so
enrichment is opt-in with no behaviour change for existing installs).
The chain runner run_enrichers() isolates per-enricher failures so a
misbehaving enricher can never fail document ingestion. The component
registry gains ComponentType.ENRICHER and auto-discovery of the
pipeline/enrichers/ package; migrate_pipeline_settings lists enrichers
and syncs PREFERRED_ENRICHERS.

Ships one enricher, PdfOutlineEnricher, which reads a PDF's embedded
/Outlines bookmarks via pypdf and appends hierarchical OC_SECTION token
annotations anchored to the parser's PAWLs tokens, turning embedded
bookmarks into a navigable in-document table of contents. Bookmark
titles are matched to their destination page's tokens (exact, then
normalized, then fuzzy); an unmatched title is dropped and its children
re-parent to the nearest matched ancestor.

* Fix mypy errors and address review on enrichment pipeline

mypy (30 errors across 4 files):
- pdf_outline_enricher: type the PAWLs helpers with the concrete TypedDicts,
  guard pdf_file.name against None, build annotation_json through typed
  intermediates
- enricher tests: import the concrete User model, declare setUpClass-set
  class attributes, cast partial fixture dicts to OpenContractDocExport

Review:
- Move the first-word pre-filter ratio into constants/annotations.py
- Drop the redundant try/except in _enrich_document_impl — run_enrichers
  already isolates per-enricher failures; merge _enrich into the method
- Stream the PDF straight from the storage handle instead of buffering the
  whole file in memory
- Document why enricher OC_SECTION annotations are structural=False
- Ignore a non-list preferred_enrichers value instead of iterating it
- Remove the no-op BaseEnricher.__init__
- Cover the uuid id-prefix fallback and the non-list enricher guard

* Fix missing TransactionTestCase import in test_corpus_objs_service

TestGetCorpusDocumentsVisibleToUser (added by #1682) subclasses
TransactionTestCase, but the #1722 TransactionTestCase->TestCase
conversion removed the import, leaving an F821 that broke the linter.

* Address review on enrichment pipeline; move enricher tests; enable PR coverage

- Move test_base_enricher.py and test_pdf_outline_enricher.py from
  opencontractserver/pipeline/enrichers/tests/ to opencontractserver/tests/,
  the canonical backend test location (already in codecov's ignore list).
- backend.yml: measure and upload coverage on pull_request runs too, not just
  push, so Codecov's patch status reflects the PR head instead of stale
  carryforward data.
- Review fixes: module-level logging import/logger in documents/models.py;
  cycle guard in nearest_matched_ancestor against malformed parent chains;
  PDF_OUTLINE_WALK_ITEM_MULTIPLIER constant replaces a magic number;
  quick_ratio() pre-filter in _match_title_to_tokens; structural-annotation
  guidance in BaseEnricher docstring; migration comment explaining the pk=1
  singleton lookup; _BoomEnricher/_MarkerEnricher gain title attrs; test
  double uses the TOKEN_LABEL constant; _run helper tolerates a keyword arg.
- Add helper-function unit tests and edge-case enricher tests, raising
  pdf_outline_enricher.py coverage to 99% and covering the enrichment-stage

subject: Honour group object-permissions in BaseVisibilityManager.visible_to_user (#1740)
message:
Honour group object-permissions in BaseVisibilityManager.visible_to_user (#1740)

BaseVisibilityManager.visible_to_user only joined the
*userobjectpermission table, while Manager.user_can resolves group
object-permissions (_default_user_can runs with
include_group_permissions=True). A user whose only READ grant on a model
using the un-overridden manager body -- CorpusActionExecution -- was via
a group therefore passed obj.user_can(user, READ) yet was excluded from
Model.objects.visible_to_user(user): authorized for the row but never
able to see it in a list query.

This is the #1714 follow-up tracked by issue #1731. #1714 closed the
identical drift in the shared/QuerySets.py bodies but deliberately left
the structurally identical manager body for a follow-up. The body now
also resolves the *groupobjectpermission table (filtered by the
requesting user's group ids) and ORs Q(id__in=<group subquery>) into the
visibility filter, mirroring the QuerySets.py fix. The user- and
group-table lookups sit in separate try/except LookupError blocks so a
model missing the group table never discards already-resolved
user-level grants; group ids resolve as a lazy values_list subquery,
keeping the lookup a single round-trip.

New CorpusActionExecutionGroupVisibilityTest pins filter/check
equivalence for a group-shared user, the read/write asymmetry (a group
READ grant never widens to UPDATE/DELETE), non-member exclusion, and
graceful degradation when the guardian tables cannot be resolved.

Closes #1731

subject: Add coverage-fixture import-discipline guard test (#1746) (#1747)
message:
Add coverage-fixture import-discipline guard test (#1746) (#1747)

Adds a Vitest regression test that walks frontend/tests/ and fails if any
component test (tests/**/*.ct.tsx) or e2e spec (tests/e2e/**/*.spec.ts)
imports the test/expect runtime from a raw Playwright package
(@playwright/experimental-ct-react / @playwright/test) instead of its
Istanbul-coverage fixture (tests/utils/coverage.ts / tests/e2e/fixtures.ts).

Only the extended page fixture in those wrapper modules reads
window.__coverage__; a test that uses the raw import compiles, runs and
passes while its coverage is silently discarded, keeping CI green but
artificially depressing codecov/patch (PR #1744).

The guard mirrors centralRouteDiscipline.test.ts: it parses each file's
named imports (multi-line aware) and ignores type-only imports such as
import type { Page } from "@playwright/test" so legitimate Playwright type
usage is not flagged. It reports both the forbidden-package case and the
missing-fixture-import case.

Service layer centralization — Phase 2A: split the CorpusObjsService monolith (#1737)

* Service layer centralization — Phase 2A: split the CorpusObjsService monolith (#1716)

Split the ~2,900-line corpus_objs_service.py monolith into a segmented
corpuses/services/ package, one cohesive module per responsibility, each
inheriting the Phase 1 BaseService:

- paths.py            CorpusPathService       DocumentPath disambiguation
- corpus_documents.py CorpusDocumentService   doc-in-corpus R/W + membership
- lifecycle.py        DocumentLifecycleService soft-delete / restore / trash
- folders.py          FolderService           folder CRUD + doc-in-folder

Pure, behaviour-preserving relocation: all 40 methods move byte-for-byte
(verified against the original); the only code change is 14 cross-module
call sites rewritten from the monolith's cls.<helper> to an explicit
owning-service reference. corpus_objs_service.py becomes a thin shim whose
CorpusObjsService facade multiply-inherits the four services, so every
existing call site and the test_corpus_objs_service.py regression suite
keep working — the suite's only edits are 9 @patch target relocations
following moved symbols.

Adds test_corpus_services_package.py covering the structural contract
(package layout, BaseService inheritance, facade MRO, standalone service
operation, cross-service delegation) and the Phase 2 implementation plan.

Phase 2 of the service-layer centralization roadmap; Phases 2B
(corpus_service.py for Corpus-row CRUD) and 2C (caller migration + shim
deletion) follow.

* Fix mypy union-attr errors in test_corpus_services_package.py

Narrow CorpusFolder | None return values from FolderService.create_folder
with explicit asserts before attribute access, resolving the 10 mypy
errors that failed the linter check.

* Address review: emit DeprecationWarning from facade, fix stale docstrings

- Add a runtime DeprecationWarning to the corpus_objs_service shim so
  Phase 2C call-site discovery is automatic, consistent with the existing
  corpus.get_documents() deprecation pattern.
- Update stale CorpusObjsService references in service docstrings to the
  owning segmented service (CorpusDocumentService, FolderService).

* Fix admin username collision in superuser permission tests

TestPermission_SuperuserBypassesAllChecks created a superuser named
"admin", which collides with the superuser seeded into every test
database by migration 0003_create_initial_superuser (DJANGO_SUPERUSER_*
env vars in .envs/.test/.django). The duplicate username raised a
UniqueViolation in setUp, failing all three tests in the class. Rename
to a unique username, matching the convention used by other admin tests.

* Address review: align shim DeprecationWarning with plan, document test rename

- Fix shim warnings.warn stacklevel 2->1 so the warning points at the
  deprecated module itself rather than import machinery internals.
- Update plan doc Section 6 to document the runtime DeprecationWarning
  decision (previously the plan said no warning, contradicting the shim).
- Add test_shim_import_emits_deprecation_warning pinning the warning.
- Document why the superuser fixture username is su_bypass_admin (a
  generic "admin" collides across files sharing a worker DB under
  pytest -n --dist loadscope).

* Address review: guard shim import, document size/reload, trim changelog

- Wrap the corpus_objs_service shim import in test_corpus_services_package.py
  in a warnings filter so DeprecationWarning does not surface at pytest
  collection time (safe if filterwarnings=error is ever added).
- Add a TODO note to folders.py documenting its above-guideline size and
  the candidate Phase 2C split.
- Reword the shim's "for one release" language to point at issue #1716
  Phase 2C and align "Phase C" -> "Phase 2C".
- Add a comment to test_shim_import_emits_deprecation_warning explaining
  why importlib.reload is needed and why it is safe here.
- Trim the Phase 2A CHANGELOG entry to the essential facts.

* Split folders.py into FolderCRUDService + FolderDocumentService

Address review: the ~1,300-line folders.py exceeded the ~800-line service
module guideline. Split it along its natural seam:

- folders.py — FolderCRUDService (~800 lines): folder CRUD, the folder tree,
  search, and bulk structure creation (10 methods).
- folder_documents.py — FolderDocumentService (~560 lines): document-in-folder

CorpusDocumentService / FolderDocumentService / FolderCRUDService /
DocumentLifecycleService / CorpusPathService methods that the behavioural
regression suite does not reach. Since each service module is new code,

subject: Add a dedicated mobile layout for DocumentKnowledgeBase (#1744)
message:
Add a dedicated mobile layout for DocumentKnowledgeBase (#1744)

* Add mobile DocumentKnowledgeBase design spec

Design for restructuring the DocumentKnowledgeBase mobile experience:
a dedicated mobile layout owner (MobileDocumentLayout) replacing the
uncoordinated per-component isMobile branches, a "tabs + persistent Ask
bar" navigation model, and a consumption/review scope (no annotation
authoring on mobile). Output of a brainstorming session.

Also ignore .superpowers/ brainstorming scratch files.

* Add mobile DocumentKnowledgeBase implementation plan

Phased, task-by-task plan: extract DesktopDocumentLayout (verbatim
refactor), build the mobile chrome primitives and MobileDocumentLayout,
delete the dead isMobile branches, and verify with a mobile component
test suite. Derived from the approved design spec.

* Extract DesktopDocumentLayout from DocumentKnowledgeBase (no behavior change)

* Add MobileSheet slide-up panel primitive

* Add MobileTabBar bottom navigation primitive

* Add MobileAskBar persistent ask input primitive

* Add MobileDocToolbar in-document toolbar primitive

* Add MobileDocumentLayout skeleton with tab navigation

* Wire Document surface into MobileDocumentLayout

* Add Task 18: post-completion visual inspection and iteration

* Wire Summary surface into MobileDocumentLayout

* Wire Annotations surface and detail sheet into MobileDocumentLayout

* Wire Chat sheet into MobileDocumentLayout

* Wire More sheet into MobileDocumentLayout

* Render MobileDocumentLayout in DocumentKnowledgeBase when isMobile

* Delete dead isMobile branches and obsolete desktop-layout-at-mobile tests

* Remove orphaned mobile-floating-controls constants

* Add mobile DocumentKnowledgeBase integration tests

Mounts the real DocumentKnowledgeBase at a 390px viewport so it renders
MobileDocumentLayout, and exercises the mobile UX end-to-end: layout vs.
desktop floating UI, no horizontal overflow, tab navigation, the Ask bar
Chat sheet, the annotation feed + detail sheet, and pinch-zoom.

Fixes a layout bug the feed test caught: the Annotations surface wrapped
RightPanelContent's flex:1 FlexColumnPanel without establishing a flex
context, collapsing the virtualized feed viewport to zero height. Adds the
ann -> selectedAnnotationIds URL sync to the test wrapper's LocationWatcher
so annotation selection is reachable without CentralRouteManager.

* Capture mobile DocumentKnowledgeBase documentation screenshots

* Update changelog for mobile DocumentKnowledgeBase layout

* Fix MobileDocumentLayout to fill the viewport height

* Reconcile mobile DKB design doc with shipped scope; minor cleanups

* Polish mobile DocumentKnowledgeBase visual design

* Modernize DocumentKnowledgeBase header and feed filter bar

* Restructure annotation feed as a calm mobile consumption surface

* Regenerate mobile DocumentKnowledgeBase documentation screenshots

* Modernize the chat conversation-list view

* Regenerate mobile chat-sheet screenshot for the modernized conversation list

* Update any-baseline after `any` count dropped by 1

* Fix routing write-discipline violation in MobileSectionsSheet

The mobile Sections sheet set the showStructuralAnnotations reactive var
directly on open. That var is URL-driven and owned by CentralRouteManager;
flip it through updateAnnotationDisplayParams so the change flows via the
URL, restoring the unidirectional routing contract.

* Address review: extract zoom bounds to constants, group imports

Zoom min/max (0.5 / 4) were redeclared in ZoomControls, useZoomManager and
the new useMobileFitToWidth hook. Hoist them to ZOOM_MIN / ZOOM_MAX in
constants.ts so every zoom surface clamps against one definition. Also
collapse the three separate AnnotationHooks imports in MobileAnnotationDetail
into a single statement.

* Remove obsolete mobile tests for removed floating-control behavior

This PR makes FloatingDocumentControls desktop-only and modernizes the chat
conversation list. The seven 'mobile speed dial' tests passed a removed
isMobile prop, and the ChatTray 'message count colors' test exercised the
deleted MESSAGE_COUNT_COLORS / calculateMessageStats helpers. Drop the dead
tests and the now-unused isMobile prop on the test wrapper.

* Add component tests for MobileFindSheet and MobileSectionsSheet

These two mobile DKB surfaces had no dedicated coverage. Add Playwright CT
suites with isolated-store harnesses that seed the text-search and structural-
annotation atoms, covering the empty, populated and stepping/navigation paths,
plus documentation screenshots.

* Address review: fix MessageCount zero-check, surface mobile query errors

- MessageCount compared props.children (a number) to the string "0", so the
  zero-count muted styling never fired. Pass an explicit $count transient prop.
- MobileDocumentLayout received queryError but never rendered it; a GraphQL
  failure showed an empty surface. Render an ErrorMessage like the desktop
  layout does.
- DesktopDocumentLayout's inline zoom callbacks still used raw 0.5/4 literals;
  switch them to the ZOOM_MIN/ZOOM_MAX constants.
- Guard useMobileFitToWidth's getViewport call against a destroyed PDFPageProxy.

* Route mobile CT tests through the coverage fixture

All seven mobile component tests imported `test` directly from
@playwright/experimental-ct-react instead of tests/utils/coverage. Only the
coverage fixture's extended `page` writes window.__coverage__ to .nyc_output,
so these tests ran but their Istanbul coverage was silently discarded —
MobileFindSheet/MobileSectionsSheet reported ~30% line coverage despite full
test suites. Switching the import to ./utils/coverage (as the other 161 CT
files already do) restores attribution: both jump to 100% line coverage.

* Extend mobile tests to cover sheets, sub-views, and the error path

Adds coverage for the previously-untested mobile surfaces:
- MobileMoreSheet Discussions/Notes/Info sub-view navigation (integration)
- the Sections and Find sheets opened from the document toolbar
- the SidebarControlBar compact filter/sort expansion
- MobileDocumentLayout's queryError branch (the Error is built inside the
  harness — Playwright CT serializes mount() props and strips Error instances).

* Address review feedback for the mobile DKB layout

P0:
- MobileDocumentLayout: the More tab now reads as selected while its
  sheet is open (derive the tab bar's active state from moreSheetOpen)
- DesktopDocumentLayout: drop the dead MobileSidebarTabs render; delete
  the now-unused MobileSidebarTabs component and its tests/harness
- SidebarControlBar: fix the compact-toggle icon color ternary whose
  inactive branch resolved to the active color
- Consolidate the duplicated shadow/radius/focus-ring tokens into a
  shared assets/configurations/designTokens.ts; mobileTheme.ts and the
  desktop chat/filter/control surfaces now import the single source

P1:
- MobileFindSheet: re-focus the input on every open via useRef/useEffect
  instead of autoFocus (which only fires on initial mount)
- MobileAnnotationDetail: memoize the annotation lookup; override the
  exported HighlightItemCard by reference instead of a positional
  `& > div`, dropping the `!important` overrides
- MobileMoreSheet: pass compact to the fixed-filter Notes surface so the
  inert setFeedFilters no-op is not surfaced as working filter controls
- useMobileFitToWidth: move FIT_WIDTH_MARGIN into constants.ts
- Remove dead default exports from the layout/sheet components
- Fix the stale MOBILE_FLOATING_CONTROLS_BOTTOM JSDoc, document the
  MobileSectionsSheet exhaustive-deps suppression, and drop the odd
  "0 new" message-count label

* Add mobile DKB test coverage for review-flagged gaps

- MobileAskBar: empty / whitespace-only submit is suppressed; send
  button trims and clears the input
- MobileDocumentLayout: the More tab reads as selected while its sheet
  is open; the Document toolbar opens the Sections and Find sheets; the
  full-screen layout locks body scroll
- MobileDocumentKnowledgeBase: the More sheet navigates into the
  Discussions and Notes sub-surfaces and back

* Add SidebarControlBar interaction test coverage

Cover the feed control bar's interactive paths: selecting a sort
option, toggling a content-type filter, the Select All / Clear All
quick actions, and search-field input.

* Address PR review: shared layout type, designToken shadow, compact prop

Three targeted fixes from PR review (Issues A-C, items reviewer flagged as
worth-resolving-before-merge):

A. HeaderAndLayout.tsx no longer defines a file-local HEADER_SHADOW
   constant — it now imports SHADOW.header from designTokens.ts so the
   single shadow value lives in exactly one place (and MobileSheet
   already pulls the same value via MOBILE_SHADOW.header).

B. Move the layout prop interface to a new layouts/types.ts and rename
   DesktopDocumentLayoutProps -> DocumentLayoutProps. MobileDocumentLayout
   no longer cross-imports from DesktopDocumentLayout; both layouts read
   from the shared contract.

C. MobileAnnotationDetail now passes compact to HighlightItem, matching
   the compact prop the feed path threads through RightPanelContent ->
   ContentItemRenderer -> HighlightItem, so the detail card uses the same
   compact visual treatment as the feed row.

---------

Signed-off-by: ude7fc9c00d51004a <ude7fc9c00d51004a@users.invalid>

subject: Fix discover search returning few results: case-insensitive + partial-word matching (#1755)
message:
Fix discover search returning few results: case-insensitive + partial-word matching (#1755)

* Fix discover search returning few results: case-insensitive + partial-word matching

The discover search box rarely returned results even for terms known to
exist in corpuses, discussions, and annotations. Two root causes:

- Corpus and conversation (discussion) search filtered with Django's
  __contains (SQL LIKE), which is case-sensitive on PostgreSQL. Corpus and
  thread titles are Title-Cased, so lowercase queries matched nothing.
  CorpusFilter, ConversationFilter, and resolve_corpus_filter_counts now use
  __icontains (ILIKE). The conversation title filter is declared as
  title__contains so the title_Contains GraphQL argument is unchanged for
  existing clients (discover search, thread lists, global discussions).

- Annotation search matched annotation text only via full-text search,
  which matches whole stemmed lexemes, never substrings, so typing a
  fragment or prefix returned nothing. resolve_search_annotations_for_mention
  now also ORs in raw_text__icontains; full-text search is kept alongside it
  for stemming. Migration 0074 enables pg_trgm and adds a GIN trigram index
  on Annotation.raw_text so the substring lookup stays index-backed.

Adds tests for case-insensitive corpus/conversation search and annotation
partial-word matching.

* Address review: extend discover search ILIKE fix to siblings

Two missed siblings of the original Discover search case-sensitivity bug
and one migration safety note, all from PR review:

LabelsetFilter.text_search_method now uses icontains (ILIKE) instead of
contains (LIKE), matching CorpusFilter.text_search_method. A lowercase
search for "merger" must surface a Title-Cased "Merger Agreement Labels"
labelset.

Both CorpusFilter and LabelsetFilter now declare an explicit
title__contains = CharFilter(field_name="title", lookup_expr="icontains")
so the Meta-generated title_Contains GraphQL argument is ILIKE rather
than LIKE. Same pattern as the ConversationFilter fix in the original
PR; preserves the GraphQL wire name unchanged.

New LabelsetFilterCaseSensitivityTest pins both filters (textSearch and
title_Contains) for the labelset path.

Migration 0074 (pg_trgm trigram index) gains an inline reversal-hazard
note: TrigramExtension.reverse drops pg_trgm unconditionally, which
fails if any other object still uses gin_trgm_ops. Forward path is
unchanged and idempotent.

subject: Fix folder-organized corpora appearing empty (descendant-aware document filtering) (#1753)
message:
Fix folder-organized corpora appearing empty (descendant-aware document filtering) (#1753)

* Fix folder-organized corpora appearing empty: descendant-aware document filtering

Importing a V2 corpus export whose documents are all nested in leaf
folders (e.g. an edgar-fetch filer/form-type/filing tree) produced a
corpus that looked empty — nothing showed at the corpus root or in the
upper folders even though every document imported correctly.

The V2 import is correct; the bug was in the read path.
DocumentFilter.in_folder used exact folder membership: the default view
passes inFolderId="__root__" -> DocumentPath.filter(folder__isnull=True)
-> 0 rows when every document is foldered, and selecting a folder that
contains only sub-folders matched 0 documents.

in_folder is now descendant-aware: "__root__" applies no folder filter
(in_corpus alone scopes the set), and selecting a folder returns
documents in that folder and all descendant folders via
CorpusFolder.get_descendant_folders().

Adds DocumentFolderFilterQueryTestCase covering the parent-folder,
leaf-folder, and corpus-root cases.

* Address review: validate folder/corpus pairing + guard malformed ids

Three fixes per code review on the descendant-aware in_folder filter:

1. Cross-corpus folder validation. When the caller supplies inCorpusWithId,
   the folder lookup now also constrains corpus_id, so a folder ID from
   corpus B + inCorpusWithId=A returns no rows instead of silently
   intersecting the two corpora.
2. Malformed folder ID guard. A malformed global ID (wrong type, empty,
   non-numeric) now resolves to queryset.none() instead of bubbling up
   as a 500 from int(from_global_id(value)[1]).
3. values_list with flat=True for the DocumentPath id subquery, matching
   the idiomatic pattern already used in DocumentFilter.in_corpus.

Adds test_cross_corpus_folder_returns_empty and
test_malformed_folder_id_returns_empty to pin both gates.

* Address review: scope DocumentPath subquery to folder.corpus_id

DocumentFilter.in_folder relied on the order-dependent guarantee that
the surrounding in_corpus filter would always run first; the inner
DocumentPath subquery did not itself restrict to a single corpus.
Adding corpus_id=folder.corpus_id to the subquery makes the
descendant-folder lookup self-contained: even if django-filter ever
processed filters in a different order, the subquery cannot leak
DocumentPath rows from a different corpus that happens to share the
folder primary key column.

* Address review: enforce inCorpusWithId requirement when folder=__root__

Without inCorpusWithId the sentinel "__root__" would pass the queryset
through unchanged — returning every visible document, not root-level
documents — a silent semantic change for external API consumers.

Defensively return queryset.none() when __root__ is used without
a corpus context. Adds a test pinning the new behaviour and documents
the dependency between the two filter fields in the docstring.

subject: Defer make_corpus_public_task to transaction.on_commit in CorpusService.set_visibility (#1763)
message:
Defer make_corpus_public_task to transaction.on_commit in CorpusService.set_visibility (#1763)

Phase 2B (#1745) carried over the pre-existing inline
`make_corpus_public_task.si(corpus_id=corpus.pk).apply_async()` from
`SetCorpusVisibility.mutate` byte-for-byte. Under `ATOMIC_REQUESTS = True`
the GraphQL mutation runs in a request-wrapping transaction, so an
unwrapped `apply_async` could race a Celery worker against uncommitted
state and fire the cascade after the request transaction rolls back on
a mid-handler exception -- publicising every child object of a corpus
whose own `is_public` flag never persisted.

Wraps the dispatch in `transaction.on_commit`, matching every other
Celery dispatch site in `config/graphql/corpus_mutations.py`
(`StartCorpusFork`, `ReEmbedCorpus`, ...). `corpus.pk` is captured into
a local before the closure so the lambda body doesn't depend on the
`corpus` instance still being attached at commit time.

Tests:
- New regression test `test_make_public_task_not_dispatched_on_rollback`
  in `test_corpus_service.py` pins the safety invariant by forcing a
  rollback inside a `transaction.atomic()` and asserting the task is
  never dispatched. This test fails against the pre-fix inline code.
- Existing positive test `test_make_public_dispatches_cascade_task` is
  wrapped in `self.captureOnCommitCallbacks(execute=True)` so the
  deferred callback fires synchronously under `TestCase`.
- GraphQL-level `test_owner_can_make_corpus_public` in
  `test_corpus_visibility.py` gets the same `captureOnCommitCallbacks`
  wrapper so its `mock_task.si.assert_called_once_with` assertion still
  pins task arguments.

Pure correctness fix -- no GraphQL contract change, no permission
semantics change.

Closes #1761

message:
Mobile DocumentKnowledgeBase UX cleanup: get overlays out of the way on selection (#1762)

* feat(frontend): mobile DocumentKnowledgeBase UX cleanup

Three mobile-only fixes so the layout stops trapping users on the
"wrong" surface after a selection.

1. Annotations feed → auto-switches to the Document tab on row tap so
   dismissing the detail sheet reveals the annotation in the viewer
   instead of the feed. Implemented via a new optional
   `onFeedItemSelected` prop on `RightPanelContent`; desktop omits the
   callback and is byte-identical.

2. Mobile Ask bar no longer opens the chat sheet on focus — users
   compose inline on the main view, and submitting opens the sheet
   directly in new-chat mode (via a new `autoStartNewChat` prop on
   `ChatTray`). A new history icon button reaches the conversation
   list explicitly.

3. The mobile Find sheet now renders every match as a tappable row;
   tapping selects the match and closes the sheet (`onClose` callback)
   so the viewer is immediately visible with the match scrolled in.
   Query and selection persist across open/close via the existing
   atoms.

Tests:
  • frontend/tests/MobileAskBar.ct.tsx — focus is a no-op, history
    button is gated on onOpenHistory, submit fires onSubmit.
  • frontend/tests/MobileFindSheet.ct.tsx — results list rendering,
    row-tap selection + onClose, span-fallback path.
  • frontend/tests/MobileDocumentKnowledgeBase.ct.tsx — the existing
    "Ask bar opens Chat sheet" case is split into focus-is-noop,
    submit-lands-in-new-chat-mode, and history-opens-list; the
    annotation-feed test now also asserts the Document tab becomes
    selected after a row tap. docScreenshot calls cover all four new
    states.

* review: address Claude code review on PR #1762

- Clear pendingChatMessage on history-button tap. Prevents a stale
  post-submit value from routing the history path into new-chat mode
  during the 100ms DKB clear window (and removes the implicit
  conflation of "has pending message" with "skip the list").
- Comment the autoStartNewChat wiring's dependency on ChatTray
  remounting on sheet close — MobileSheet's AnimatePresence is what
  makes the one-shot useState init re-run.
- Harden the focus-is-no-op test: replace wall-clock waitForTimeout
  with a typed-character probe (proves focus didn't get stolen) plus
  a positive value assertion. CI-loaded-runner safe.
- Drop the redundant (result as TextSearchSpanResult) cast — inlining
  isTokenResult(result) lets TS narrow the union without help.
- Add a "tap row 0 selects index 0" find-sheet test to guard against
  an off-by-one in the row's onClick wiring (the prior test only
  covered the last row).

* review: second-pass fixes from PR #1762 code review

- Replace the derived autoStartNewChat={Boolean(pendingChatMessage)}
  with an explicit chatOpenMode: 'new-chat' | 'history' | null state
  in MobileDocumentLayout. The mode is declared at the open site
  rather than inferred from a side-channel, so the call-site intent
  is unambiguous and there's no remaining race with the 100ms DKB
  pendingChatMessage clear window. The mode resets on sheet close.
  The remount-dependency comment near autoStartNewChat is kept —
  this refactor makes the source signal explicit but ChatTray's
  useState init is still mount-only.
- Cap the find results list at MOBILE_FIND_MAX_VISIBLE_RESULTS=100

- Token-path snippet fallback: when a TextSearchTokenResult has

  Span results already had a text fallback in their type; tokens
  don't, so the placeholder is the equivalent affordance.

subject: DocumentKnowledgeBase: consolidate the two right-edge control systems (#1764)
message:
DocumentKnowledgeBase: consolidate the two right-edge control systems (#1764)

* DocumentKnowledgeBase desktop polish: consolidate the two right-edge control systems (#1734)

At a desktop viewport the document layer's right edge previously rendered two
competing vertical stacks: a rotated-text tab rail (INDEX/CHAT/FEED/DISCUSSIONS)
and, just to its left, a separate floating action-button cluster (settings gear
plus colored circular FABs for extracts, analyses, create-analysis). The audit
flagged this as visual clutter that made it ambiguous which control does what,
and called out the rotated text labels as hard to scan.

Visual unification: when the right panel is closed, both control groups now
render inside a single new RightEdgeRail wrapper, vertically centered against
the viewport's right edge. The navigation tabs sit on top, a 1-pixel
RailDivider separates the two control intents, and the document tool pills
(settings, extracts, analyses, create-analysis) sit below — one coherent
column with consistent pill shape, sizing, and active-state treatment.

No more rotated text: SidebarTab (styled) drops its writing-mode: vertical-rl
label rendering. The .tab-label span stays in the DOM as a screen-reader-only
string (visually clipped to 1x1 px) so assistive tech still announces it; the
visible affordance is the icon plus a CSS-only hover tooltip driven by the new
optional data-tooltip attribute. The tooltip flips to the opposite side of the
pill based on $panelOpen so it never overflows the viewport edge.

Accessibility: every tab and every action button now carries an aria-label
(most action buttons previously had only a title attribute and no accessible
name). Toggle FABs advertise their open/expanded state via aria-pressed /
aria-expanded.

Shared styled primitive: the action-button styled component (ActionButton in
FloatingDocumentControls) now extends SidebarTab instead of defining its own
circular FAB style. Both surfaces share the same 44x44 pill geometry, white
background with subtle gradient overlay, and blue active treatment; per-action
color cues (purple extracts, amber analyses, green create) are preserved as a
lightweight $accent icon tint instead of the heavy colored-circle background.

Bare-container plumbing: DesktopSidebarTabs and FloatingDocumentControls each
gain an optional bareContainer prop. When true, neither component carries its
own fixed/absolute positioning so the parent RightEdgeRail can stack them as a
single flex column. Standalone (non-bare) positioning is preserved for the
existing component test harnesses and for the panel-open layout (where the
navigation tabs anchor to the left edge of the open right panel and the
action cluster keeps its bottom-right placement).

Tests: SidebarTabs.ct.tsx adds two new regression tests pinning the new
aria-label / data-tooltip mapping and the visually-hidden .tab-label, plus a
new RightEdgeRail (issue #1734) test group with three screenshot tests covering
the unified rail (knowledge-base--right-edge-rail--unified, --with-extract-analysis,
--read-only). All 20 FloatingDocumentControls tests, 6 DesktopSidebarTabs tests,
and 70 DocumentKnowledgeBase tests continue to pass — data-testids, click
semantics, panel toggle behavior, panel-width controls, exclusivity logic,
permissions gating, and hideDocumentTools are preserved.

Closes #1734

* Address review + bump patch coverage on the right-edge rail consolidation

Review feedback (PR #1764):
- Drop the native title= attribute from every tab and action pill in
  SidebarTabs.tsx, FloatingDocumentControls.tsx, and the
  SidebarTabsTestWrapper. The data-tooltip CSS pseudo-element + aria-label
  pair is sufficient; the redundant title= was rendering a competing
  native browser tooltip on hover.
- Remove the dead `@media (max-width: 768px) { display: none }` from
  RailDivider — the divider only ever lives inside RightEdgeRail, which
  already hides itself at that breakpoint, so the inner rule could never
  fire and just added confusion about where the mobile-hiding logic lives.
- Simplify the SidebarTabsContainer `left` ternary: `!$panelOpen || $bare`
  collapses the two arms that both evaluated to "auto" without changing
  semantics.

Coverage:
- Add tests/DesktopDocumentLayout.harness.tsx + DesktopDocumentLayout.ct.tsx
  mirroring the MobileDocumentLayout harness pattern. The two new CT tests
  pin (a) the RightEdgeRail rendering branch when the right panel is
  closed and (b) the absence of the rail when the panel is open, lifting
  patch coverage on the new layout block out of the codecov red zone.
- Add a SidebarTabs.ct.tsx test asserting `threadCount={1}` announces
  "1 thread" (singular) so the pluralization edge case is a regression
  guard, not a latent branch.
- Update FloatingDocumentControls.ct.tsx's title= assertions to assert
  aria-label= instead, matching the new accessible-name source of truth.

* Lift codecov/patch for DesktopDocumentLayout + final review pass

Patch coverage now exercises the inline action-button callbacks on the
new right-edge rail (issue #1734), which were the codecov red zone on
this PR.

- Remove dead `onSummaryClick` prop from `FloatingDocumentControls`:
  the prop was destructured but never wired to any button, so the two
  inline callback bodies in `DesktopDocumentLayout` could never run.
  Dropping the prop removes ~14 lines of permanently-uncovered code
  and matches CLAUDE.md's no-dead-code rule.
- Make `DesktopDocumentLayout.harness.tsx` stateful: own the slice of
  state that the rail's action callbacks mutate (showAnalysesPanel,
  showExtractsPanel, showAddToCorpusModal, showRightPanel,
  sidebarViewMode) so a click in CT actually toggles the panel and
  the rendered DOM shifts.
- Extend `DesktopDocumentLayout.ct.tsx` from 2 to 8 tests covering:
  rail-click opens FloatingAnalysesPanel / FloatingExtractsPanel,
  rail-click with no corpus opens the AddToCorpusModal, and the
  panel-open variant for both buttons (corpus + corpus-less). The
  callback bodies inside the rail's FloatingDocumentControls and the
  open-panel FloatingDocumentControls now execute on every CT run.

Review feedback (PR #1764):
- Merge the duplicate `RailDivider` / `SidebarTab` imports in
  `SidebarTabsTestWrapper.tsx` into one statement.
- Tighten the `SidebarTabsContainer` JSDoc with an explicit precedence
  note: `$bare` wins every ternary if accidentally combined with
  `$panelOpen=true`, silently overriding panel-anchoring. Callers
  never do this today; the note makes the contract searchable.

* Address round-2 review on right-edge rail consolidation

DRY: extract duplicate callbacks. handleAnalysesClick and
handleExtractsClick are now declared once with useCallback above the
return statement and passed by reference to both FloatingDocumentControls
renders (panel-closed RightEdgeRail branch and panel-open floating
branch). Removes the verbatim copy-paste flagged by the reviewer.

Export RightEdgeRail from styled/SidebarTabs.tsx. The harness no longer
re-implements the same positioning CSS with a local MockRail; it imports
the canonical primitive and uses it directly so the production rail and
the screenshot harness can never drift. Also updates the layout to
import from the styled module instead of defining the styled component
inline.

Document the onSummaryClick removal in the CHANGELOG. The old FAB was a
redundant "open summary in knowledge layer" entry point alongside the
FloatingSummaryPreview's "View Full Screen" / version-chip path; the
knowledge-layer switch remains reachable via the preview's
onSwitchToKnowledge wiring, so net effect is one canonical entry point
instead of two.

* Address round-3 review on right-edge rail consolidation

Strip issue-number references from production-code comments per CLAUDE.md
no-task-reference rule. The constraint descriptions stay; only the bare
#1734 refs are removed. Touches FloatingDocumentControls, layouts/
DesktopDocumentLayout, styled/SidebarTabs, and document_kb/SidebarTabs.

Fix RailDivider comment vs width mismatch flagged in the review. The
divider is 28px wide and the pill is 44px wide — the previous 'Matches
the pill width' comment was wrong. New comment notes the divider is
deliberately narrower than the pill so the rail still reads as one
coherent column rather than two adjacent groups.

Clarify the read-only RightEdgeRailHarness test description so a future
reader does not mistake it for a permission-gating regression test. The
harness asserts the rail's structural contract (create pill absent when
canCreateAnalysis is false); production permission gating lives in
FloatingDocumentControls.ct.tsx.
