subject: test infra: backend suite speedup (Phase A1) — Python 3.12 + sysmon coverage (#1767)
message:
test infra: backend suite speedup (Phase A1) — Python 3.12 + sysmon coverage (#1767)

* test infra: backend suite speedup — Python 3.12 + sysmon coverage + worksteal

Two changes that together produced a 4x speedup on the hot test files in
local A/B measurement (19:34 -> 4:50 on the WebSocket / extract /
structured-response cluster; see plan §6). Targets the two highest-ROI
findings from a CI runtime audit of the ~47-min backend job:

A1. Bump test/runtime Python image from 3.11.15 to 3.12.7 and set
    COVERAGE_CORE=sysmon in the test env. Coverage on 3.11 was measured at
    +156% over the no-cov baseline on the hot files; sys.monitoring is
    ~5-10x cheaper. Codecov receives the same coverage.xml — only the
    collection path changes. Dropped django_coverage_plugin from setup.cfg
    because Coverage 7.x silently falls back to the C-trace path whenever
    any file-tracer plugin is configured, which would defeat sysmon (the
    project owns 7 templates total, all 4xx/5xx pages plus a couple of
    admin views — a trivial coverage slice for a ~150% wall-time tax).

B1. Switch the pytest CI invocation from --dist loadscope to
    --dist worksteal so large classes like TestStructuredResponseAPI
    (843 s / 27 tests) can fan out across all workers instead of pinning
    to one. Conftest gains an auto-tag that pins django.test.TestCase
    subclasses with class-scoped state (setUpTestData overridden or
    fixtures set) to a per-class xdist_group, so worksteal still respects
    that binding where it matters. TransactionTestCase subclasses are
    deliberately not pinned — they rebuild per-test regardless, so they
    benefit from free redistribution.

Plan also covers Phase A2 (drop redundant migrate step), A3 (ghcr image
cache), A4 (explicit -n), B2 (slim 17 MB fixture), B3 (class-once fixture
load), B4 (TransactionTestCase audit). Tracked in
docs/refactor_plans/2026-05-23-test-suite-speedup-A1-B1.md so we can
re-measure after this lands and decide which further phases are needed.

* test infra: revert Phase B1 (worksteal + auto-tag); keep A1 only

The combined PR #1767 ran in ~31:53 (vs 41-min baseline, −22%) but failed
with 39 tests broken — psycopg2 UniqueViolation on the `admin` user
across plain TestCase subclasses (UserTypePrivacyTestCase,
TestSearchAgentsForMention, TestOpenContractsAnalyzers, etc).

Root cause: worksteal interleaved tests from these classes with tests
from other classes on the same worker, exposing state leaks that
loadscope's class-pinning was hiding. The auto-tag only pinned
TestCase subclasses with setUpTestData/fixtures, leaving plain
TestCase classes vulnerable to interleave-on-worker pollution from
sibling classes' uncommitted state.

This commit:
- Reverts .github/workflows/backend.yml to `--dist loadscope`.
- Reverts conftest.py::pytest_collection_modifyitems to its prior shape
  (serial marker handling only).
- Keeps the Phase A1 changes (Python 3.12.7 image, COVERAGE_CORE=sysmon,
  dropped django_coverage_plugin) — they ran cleanly and account for the
  ~22% wall-time reduction independently.
- Updates the plan doc (§10 post-mortem) with what we learned: the local
  A/B 4× speedup was specific to the 3 hottest files (~30% of CI time),
  not a sound extrapolation to the full suite. Coverage cost was a
  multiplier on the per-test 17 MB fixture-reload base cost, not the
  base itself. After A1, that fixture reload is the binding constraint
  and Phase B3 is the right next lever.

Worksteal can be re-attempted only after a dedicated test-isolation
sweep that finds and fixes the admin-user collision pattern (probably
in factories + Celery-eager + migration seeds).

* test: accept text/javascript or application/javascript in storage test

Python 3.12's mimetypes module returns ``text/javascript`` for ``.js``
files (per RFC 9239, which deprecates ``application/javascript``). The
test was hardcoded to the legacy value and broke when CI bumped the
django image to Python 3.12 in this PR. Both forms are RFC-valid and
both browsers serve them identically — relax the assertion so the test
passes on either runtime.

message:
test infra: backend suite speedup (Phase A2 + B2) — slim 17 MB fixture + drop redundant migrate step (#1772)

* test infra: slim test_data.json from 16.4 MB to 0.12 MB (Phase B2, refs #1769)

The fixture had 4,284 objects but the 7 hot WebSocket/extract/structured
test files together pay ~25 s per-test setup reloading them, and an audit
of all 19 fixture-using files confirms zero of them actually read the

  annotations.

  Django's post_migrate signal on every test-DB creation; the fixture
  rows were duplicative.

Kept (331 objects, 123 KB):
- 4 documents.document (read by _build_corpus_fixture_state).
- 2 users.user incl 'testuser' (read by setUp).
- 1 auth.group.
- 40 annotations.annotationlabel (some tests filter by label text).
- 4 annotations.structuralannotationset (referenced by document FK).

test_note_tree.py, and test_agentic_highlighter_task.py pass in 2:52

counterparts; only deletions, no edits.

The step ran ``manage.py migrate`` against the ``opencontractserver``
default database, but pytest-django creates per-worker test databases
(``test_opencontractserver_gw0``, ``_gw1``, ...) on first invocation
and runs migrations against those. ``DATABASES['default']['TEST']``
declares no ``TEMPLATE``, so the default DB is not used as a createdb

subject: Consolidate desktop bottom-edge floating controls into a single anchored bar (#1735) (#1766)
message:
Consolidate desktop bottom-edge floating controls into a single anchored bar (#1735) (#1766)

* Consolidate scattered bottom-edge floating controls in DocumentKnowledgeBase desktop layout (#1735)

The desktop document layer used to carry three independently `position: fixed`/absolute
floaters along its bottom edge — a circular SUMMARY button (`FloatingSummaryPreview`)
bottom-left, a search/chat mini-pill (`FloatingDocumentInput`) bottom-center, and the
active-label `OC_SECTION ×` pill (`EnhancedLabelSelector`) bottom-right — with no shared
container, reading as visual noise. They are now docked inside a single anchored
container, `DocumentBottomBar`, that pins all three to the same baseline at the bottom
of `MainContentArea` with consistent spacing (CSS Grid `1fr auto 1fr`, `align-items: end`).

`FloatingSummaryPreview` and `EnhancedLabelSelector` gained a `fixed?: boolean` prop
(default `true`) so existing standalone usages — including the standalone component
test wrappers — keep their legacy `position: fixed` behaviour; `DesktopDocumentLayout`
opts all three into `fixed={false}` so the new bar owns positioning. The legacy
`FloatingInputWrapper` styled component is deleted (no-dead-code rule). Mobile
(`MobileDocumentLayout`) is unaffected.

New test `Desktop bottom toolbar consolidation (#1735)` mounts the layout at 1440x900
and asserts: (1) the bar is the common ancestor of all three controls; (2) they share
the same vertical baseline within tolerance; (3) the left → centre → right ordering
holds. Captures three documentation screenshots (default state, consolidated close-up,
input-expanded close-up).

Closes #1735

* Address review + lift codecov/patch on bottom-bar consolidation

Patch coverage now exercises the inline `FloatingDocumentInput` and
`FloatingSummaryPreview` callbacks the new `DocumentBottomBar` wires to
`DesktopDocumentLayout` state, which were the codecov red zone on this
PR.

Review feedback (PR #1766):

- Add stable `data-testid` hooks to `FloatingDocumentInput`'s mode
  toggles (`search-toggle-button`, `chat-toggle-button`) so tests no
  longer rely on Lucide's internal class names. Update the existing
  `DocumentKnowledgeBase.ct.tsx` "bottom toolbar consolidation" test
  and `FloatingDocumentInput.ct.tsx` read-only test to use the new
  testids — the old `lucide-search` / `[data-testid="chat-toggle"]`
  selectors were brittle (the latter never matched anything, so
  `not.toBeVisible()` was passing vacuously).
- Remove the unreachable `@media (max-width: 768px)` blocks from
  `DocumentBottomBar` and `DocumentBottomBarCenter`. DKB renders
  `MobileDocumentLayout` below 768px, so `DesktopDocumentLayout`
  never mounts at that breakpoint and the mobile fallback rules
  could not fire.
- Pass `panelOffset={0}` to `EnhancedLabelSelector` in the bar's
  right slot with an inline comment. The prop was being passed but is
  a no-op when `fixed={false}` — the parent bar already owns the
  panel offset via its own `right: $panelOffset`.

Coverage:

- Add `tests/DesktopDocumentLayout.harness.tsx` (stateful harness
  mirroring the `MobileLayoutHarness` pattern) plus
  `tests/DesktopDocumentLayout.ct.tsx` with four focused tests:
  bar-renders-all-slots, chat-submit fires the layout's
  `onChatSubmit`/`onToggleChat` (verified via a hidden harness probe
  that surfaces `pendingChatMessage` / `showRightPanel` /
  `sidebarViewMode`), summary `View Full` fires
  `onSwitchToKnowledge` (probe surfaces `activeLayer`), and the
  corpus-less branch hides the `summary-toggle-button` entirely.

* Address 2nd review pass + lift codecov/patch on DesktopDocumentLayout callbacks

Round-2 review feedback on the bottom-bar consolidation (#1735) flagged
two correctness issues and asked for documentation of one design choice.
This commit addresses all three.

Mobile media query no longer leaks into fixed=false hosts. The
@media (max-width: 768px) override in StyledEnhancedSelector now lives
inside the $fixed branch so an inline (fixed=false) host -- e.g. the
new DocumentBottomBar -- can't have position: fixed forced on it at
narrow viewports. This mirrors the existing pattern in
FloatingSummaryPreview where the responsive overrides are correctly
scoped to the fixed branch. Comment in the css explains the mobile
portal path that still relies on the @media block.

Document the bottom: 2rem baseline on DocumentBottomBar. The legacy
FloatingInputWrapper used bottom: 4rem; the consolidated bar
intentionally pulls the centre input down to share one visual gutter
with the summary and label-selector slots rather than stacking at
different heights. Comment captures the rationale so a future reader
doesn't read the regression as accidental.

Lift codecov/patch coverage on the new layout callback bodies. The
inline onBackToDocument body and the if (content) true branch of
onSwitchToKnowledge were the uncovered lines. Two new CT tests:
- back-to-document button click in knowledge-layer mode exercises
  the full onBackToDocument body via the harness probe.
- summary version chip click with mocked GET_DOCUMENT_SUMMARY_VERSIONS
  data fires onSwitchToKnowledge(currentContent), exercising the
  if (content) true branch (setSelectedSummaryContent(content)).

The DesktopLayoutHarness now wraps in JotaiProvider and MockedProvider
to support tests that need Apollo data; a buildSummaryVersionsMock
helper is exported so future tests can populate the version stack
without re-deriving the query shape. The helper import lives in its
own import statement (CLAUDE.md "Playwright CT split-import rule").

Note re: chat-toggle-button selector mismatch raised in the review:
the testid was added in the previous commit (391f02c1) -- the diff
only showed the search-toggle-button addition because the chat
testid had already been added inline alongside it.

* Trim multi-line comments on bottom-bar primitives per CLAUDE.md

Round-3 review pass: drop multi-paragraph JSDoc/CSS comment blocks
around DocumentBottomBar and its consolidation site in
DesktopDocumentLayout. The bottom: 2rem rationale (deliberate baseline
share with summary/label slots) is preserved as a single-line WHY; the
self-evident slot-anchor descriptions and the no-mobile-media-query
note (already self-evident given DesktopDocumentLayout is only mounted
above 768px) are removed. Issue-number reference dropped per
CLAUDE.md's no-task-reference rule.

* Bump CT coverage timeout to 30m (was 25m, suite at 27m)

* Guard EnhancedLabelSelector calculatePosition behind fixed mode

When fixed=false the parent toolbar (DocumentBottomBar) owns placement,
so passing panelOffset-derived / was a latent footgun for
future callers. Return zero-offsets in inline mode to make the contract
explicit.

uses ``StaticFilesStorage`` (the manifest-less variant) per

URLs at template render time without needing the post-collectstatic
manifest. Stacks on the Phase A2 migrate-step drop for ~2:30 cumulative
pre-test wall reduction.

* test(pydantic-ai): restore PipelineSettings singleton in setUp

``TestPydanticAIConversationAdaptersAsync`` is a ``TransactionTestCase``
that truncates every table between tests, including the
``PipelineSettings`` singleton seeded by data migration
``documents/0031_add_pipeline_settings.py``. After the first test's
truncate, the singleton is gone; the next test's call into
``create_conversation_search_tool`` -> ``get_embedder()`` returns
``(None, None)`` and raises ``ValueError: get_embedder() resolved no
embedder_path``.

This was a latent ordering bug — it surfaced on CI runs where this
class did not happen to be the first class on its worker. Confirmed
failing on ``main`` independently of this PR.

Fix: ``update_or_create`` the singleton in ``setUp`` from
``settings.DEFAULT_EMBEDDER`` so every test starts from the same
migration-seeded state. Idempotent; no impact on other tests since
the singleton is restored to its expected migration-time value.

A broader cleanup (auditing every ``TransactionTestCase`` for the
same migration-data dependency) belongs in a follow-up to issue #1769.

subject: ci: cache django image build with GitHub Actions layer cache (Phase A3) (#1774)
message:
ci: cache django image build with GitHub Actions layer cache (Phase A3) (#1774)

* ci: cache django image build with GitHub Actions layer cache (Phase A3, refs #1769)

``Build the Stack`` rebuilt the django image from layer one on every PR
run (~2:40 wall) because the runner ships from scratch. Switches to
``docker buildx build`` with GHA layer cache:

- ``--cache-from type=gha,scope=django-test`` pulls cached layers from
  prior runs on this repo.
- ``--cache-to type=gha,mode=max,scope=django-test`` writes the new
  layers back so subsequent runs can pull them.

On cache hit, most layers (apt-get, pip wheel, spaCy model fetch) restore
in seconds rather than rebuilding. The image is tagged
``opencontractserver_local_django`` to match the ``image:`` directive on
the ``django`` service in test.yml, so the subsequent
``docker compose build`` only compiles the small ``postgres`` image
(~5 s). Cache invalidates automatically whenever Dockerfile,
requirements, or any COPY'd source changes — buildx hashes inputs per
layer.

No new secrets or external registry — GHA cache uses the project's
existing ``actions/cache`` quota (~10 GB per repo, LRU-evicted).
``docker/setup-buildx-action@v3`` is the only new dependency.

Stacks on Phases A1 (Py 3.12+sysmon coverage), A2 (drop redundant
migrate step), B2 (slim test_data.json), and the prior collectstatic
drop for further pre-test wall reduction.

* ci: trigger second run to verify GHA cache hit

* ci: expose GHA runtime env vars so buildx GHA cache actually works

First-run + second-run timings on PR 1774 showed identical Build the
Stack times (3:23 -> 3:39, just noise) — the GHA cache directives were
silently ignored because ``ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN`` and
``ACTIONS_RESULTS_URL`` weren't exposed to the build shell.
``docker/setup-buildx-action@v3`` does not export these by default;
``crazy-max/ghaction-github-runtime@v3`` is the documented fix for the
exact symptom (cache directives accepted, no cache import/export lines
in the buildx output, build time unchanged across runs).

* ci: roll our own GHA runtime exposure (drop crazy-max third-party action)

Replaces the third-party ``crazy-max/ghaction-github-runtime@v3`` from
the prior commit with an inline ``actions/github-script@v7`` (official,
GitHub) that does the same thing in 8 lines: forward
``ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN`` and ``ACTIONS_RESULTS_URL`` from the runner
process env into ``$GITHUB_ENV`` so the subsequent ``docker buildx``
shell step can read them.

Same effect, no supply-chain risk from a third-party action whose code
we don't control. Adds a ``core.warning`` if the env vars aren't set
(future GHA cache backend rename, runner-image change, etc) so the
silent-no-op failure mode is observable in the CI log instead of just
manifesting as ``no cache speedup`` across runs.

message:
ci: portable buildx cache (ghcr.io) shared across CI + local + prod (#1777)

* ci: portable buildx cache (ghcr.io) shared across CI + local + prod

Phase A3 (PR #1774) used ``type=gha`` which only works inside GitHub
Actions, so contributors building from a fresh checkout still paid the
full ~5-10 min ``docker compose -f local.yml build`` cost. Swap to a
registry-backed buildx cache that lives at
``ghcr.io/open-source-legal/opencontracts/django-local-cache:main``.

Changes:

- ``.github/workflows/backend.yml``: replaces ``--cache-from/--cache-to
  type=gha,scope=django-test`` with ``type=registry,ref=ghcr.io/.../
  django-local-cache:main``. Adds ``permissions: packages: write`` on
  the pytest job, a ``docker/login-action@v3`` step using the existing
  ``GITHUB_TOKEN`` (no new secrets), and gates ``--cache-to`` to ``push``
  events only so PR runs read but don't write (and so PRs from forks
  don't fail trying to push to a registry their token can't reach).
  Drops the inline ``actions/github-script`` env-var helper — registry
  cache doesn't need ``ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN``. Lowercases the ref at
  runtime because ghcr paths must be lowercase but ``github.repository_
  owner`` / ``github.event.repository.name`` preserve mixed case.

- ``local.yml``: adds ``cache_from: [type=registry,ref=ghcr.io/.../
  django-local-cache:main]`` to the ``django`` service's build block.
  Fresh ``docker compose -f local.yml build`` should drop from
  ~5-10 min to ~30-60 s on cache hit. Inline comment documents the
  one-time ``docker login ghcr.io`` step; unauthenticated pulls fall
  back gracefully (cache miss, normal build).

- ``production.yml``: wires ``cache_from`` into both ``django`` and
  ``migrate`` services (they share the same image). Points at
  ``django-production-cache:main`` — a separate scope because
  ``compose/production/django/Dockerfile`` is distinct from the
  local/test Dockerfile. No-op until a follow-up PR adds the CI job
  that publishes the prod cache; wiring now means that follow-up is a
  single workflow file rather than two changes.

Cache images inherit the repo's visibility (public). If GitHub creates
them private by mistake on first publish, change visibility in
Packages settings once.

subject: test(infra): clear PipelineSettings singleton cache between tests (#1778)
message:
test(infra): clear PipelineSettings singleton cache between tests (#1778)

Root-cause fix for the recurring flaky ``ValueError: get_embedder()
resolved no embedder_path`` failures in agent / tool tests
(``TestPydanticAIConversationAdaptersAsync`` in PR #1773,
``TestDuplicateToolRegistration``, ``TestApprovalFlow``).

The bug was not TransactionTestCase truncation as previously assumed
in PR #1773's per-class workaround. The actual cause is process-wide
LocMemCache pollution:

  1. ``PipelineSettings.get_instance()`` caches the singleton row with
     a 5-min TTL.
  2. ``TestPipelineComponentBaseSettings`` in
     ``test_pipeline_component_base.py`` does
     ``PipelineSettings.objects.all().delete(); PipelineSettings.
     objects.create(id=1)`` (empty ``default_embedder``) inside its
     TestCase transaction, then calls ``get_instance()`` which caches
     the empty Python instance.
  3. The test's transaction rolls back -> DB row reverts to migration-
     seeded ``default_embedder="...TestEmbedder"`` -> cache still
     holds the now-orphan empty instance because rollback does not
     fire the model signal that invalidates the cache.
  4. A later test on the same xdist worker calls ``get_instance()``,
     hits the polluted cache, sees ``default_embedder=""``, and fails.

Fix in ``opencontractserver/conftest.py``: autouse function-scoped
fixture ``_invalidate_pipeline_settings_singleton_cache`` calls
``PipelineSettings._invalidate_cache()`` before every test, so each
test starts with a fresh DB read. One ``cache.delete()`` per test;
negligible overhead.

Also:
- Reverts the per-class ``PipelineSettings.update_or_create`` workaround
  in ``test_pydantic_ai_conversation_adapters.py`` (PR #1773) — the
  structural fixture supersedes it.
- Adds ``test_pipeline_settings_cache_isolation.py`` regression test:
  a two-test sequence that proves the autouse fixture works (the
  second test asserts a migration-seeded ``default_embedder`` after
  the first test deliberately pollutes the cache with an empty one).
- Audited the other three ``_invalidate_cache``-using services
  (``conversation_service``, ``documents/services/versions``,
  ``documents/services/relationships``); they all use per-request/per-
  user cache keys (not a process-wide singleton key), so they don't
  have the same exposure.

Local smoke (5 files, 42 tests including all the historically flaky
ones plus the polluting class): 42 passed in 23.45s.

subject: Service layer centralization — Phase 5: fill coverage gaps (#1719) (#1770)
message:
Service layer centralization — Phase 5: fill coverage gaps (#1719) (#1770)

* Add agents/services package (Phase 5, #1719)

Introduces ``AgentConfigurationService`` (agent CRUD + visibility) and
``AgentActionResultService`` (action-result visibility), both inheriting
``BaseService``. Migrates the inline permission composition from
``config/graphql/agent_mutations.py`` (Create/Update/Delete),
``config/graphql/social_queries.py`` (``resolve_agents``,
``resolve_agent_configurations``, ``resolve_agent``), and
``config/graphql/action_queries.py`` (``resolve_agent_action_results``) onto
the new services. Behaviour, permission semantics, and the unified IDOR
error messages are preserved exactly — this is a relocation + encapsulation.

* Add AnalysisLifecycleService to analyzer/services (Phase 5, #1719)

Adds ``AnalysisLifecycleService`` — the analysis *write* surface
(``make_public``, ``start_document_analysis``, ``delete_analysis``) — alongside
the existing Phase-3 read-only ``AnalysisService``. Both inherit ``BaseService``.

Migrates the inline permission composition from
``config/graphql/analysis_mutations.py`` (``MakeAnalysisPublic``,
``StartDocumentAnalysisMutation``, ``DeleteAnalysisMutation``) onto the new
service. The unified IDOR-safe failure messages, the user-lock semantics,
and the async task dispatch behaviour are preserved exactly — this is a
relocation + encapsulation.

* Add notifications/services package (Phase 5, #1719)

Introduces ``NotificationService`` for the simple-ownership ``Notification``
model. The service inherits ``BaseService`` for ``log_action`` and
architectural conformance, but provides its own IDOR-safe ``recipient=user``
lookup because ``Notification`` does not implement ``user_can`` /
``visible_to_user`` (it uses a simple ownership model — there is no
``AnnotatePermissionsForReadMixin``).

Migrates the inline IDOR-safe composition from
``config/graphql/notification_mutations.py`` (all four mutations) and the
notification resolvers in ``config/graphql/social_queries.py``
(``resolve_notifications``, ``resolve_notification``,
``resolve_unread_notification_count``) onto the new service.

* Add feedback/services package (Phase 5, #1719)

Introduces ``UserFeedbackService`` covering ``approve_annotation`` and
``reject_annotation`` — the two annotation-derived feedback flows that
previously duplicated their permission + get-or-create + permission-grant
structure inline in two adjacent mutations.

Migrates ``RejectAnnotation`` and ``ApproveAnnotation`` in
``config/graphql/annotation_mutations.py`` onto the new service. The unified
IDOR-safe failure message, the ``transaction.atomic`` boundary, and the
``is_new=created`` semantics of the creator-permission grant are preserved
exactly.

* Add worker_uploads/services package (Phase 5, #1719)

Introduces three services covering the worker-upload subjects, each
inheriting ``BaseService``:

- ``WorkerAccountService``: account lifecycle (superuser-only) — list /
  create / set-active.
- ``CorpusAccessTokenService``: per-corpus token CRUD (superuser or corpus
  creator) — list-for-corpus / create / revoke.
- ``WorkerDocumentUploadService``: per-corpus upload listing (superuser or
  corpus creator).

Migrates the inline permission composition from
``config/graphql/worker_queries.py`` (three resolvers) and
``config/graphql/worker_mutations.py`` (four mutations) onto the new
services. The unified IDOR-safe failure messages, the dropdown-for-corpus-
creators access policy on ``resolve_worker_accounts``, and the
``token_count`` zeroing for non-superusers are preserved exactly.

* Add Phase 5 structural tests + sweep additional agent call sites (#1719)

Adds ``opencontractserver/tests/test_service_layer_phase5.py`` pinning the
Phase-5 structural contract: every new service is importable from its
package root, inherits ``BaseService``, public methods thread ``request``
keyword-only, and ``NotificationService`` exposes its own simple-ownership
IDOR-safe lookup (not the inherited ``get_or_none`` — ``Notification`` has
no ``user_can`` manager).

Sweeps two more gap-model GraphQL call sites onto the new
``AgentConfigurationService``:
- ``config/graphql/search_queries.py`` ``resolve_search_agents_for_mention``
  now calls ``search_mentionable_agents`` (anonymous-empty / scope / text
  filters live on the service).
- ``config/graphql/conversation_types.py`` mention-resolution batch lookup
  now calls ``get_active_agents_by_slugs``.

Adds the CHANGELOG entry for the full Phase-5 migration.

Out of scope (Phase 6, #1720): ``config/graphql/corpus_mutations.py``'s
``Create/UpdateCorpusAction`` agent-config lookups, which sit alongside
identical-pattern inline ``visible_to_user.get(pk=...)`` lookups for
``Fieldset`` and ``Analyzer``. Phase 6 sweeps all three uniformly.

* Apply lint formatting (black + isort + pyupgrade) to Phase 5 files

Auto-applied formatter output from the pre-commit equivalents:
- black wraps short ``log_action`` calls onto single lines
- isort re-adds the spacing after the social_queries.py imports
- pyupgrade rewrites ``Optional[X]`` → ``X | None`` and drops the now-unused
  ``Optional`` import

No behaviour changes — purely cosmetic.

* Fix mypy errors in Phase 5 worker + agent services

- agent_configuration_service: route get_agent_by_id through BaseService.get_or_none,
  which threads request= into the convention helper; the bare
  utils.permissioning.get_for_user_or_none has no request kwarg.
- worker_mutations / worker_queries: narrow ServiceResult.value with an
  assert after the result.ok gate so mypy sees the non-None payload.

* Address Phase 5 review: request threading, log/delete ordering, stronger import guard

- AnalysisLifecycleService.make_public: accept request= keyword-only and
  thread it from the mutation, so the service surfaces the Phase-4
  convention uniformly. Added to the request-threading structural test.
- MarkAllNotificationsReadMutation: gate on result.ok before reading
  result.value, matching every other ServiceResult call site in this PR.
- delete_agent / delete_analysis: invoke delete() / dispatch the async
  task before log_action so we never record a deletion that did not
  actually run.
- TestPhase5RetiredInlinePatternsHaveServiceCallers: replace the bare
  module-importable check with a per-module source scan asserting the
  expected service symbol is referenced — a regression to inline
  composition would now fail the test instead of silently passing.
- Refactor plan: mark Phase 5 as Implemented.

* Phase 5 review fixes: in-service superuser guards + coverage tests

Review fixes:
- AnalysisLifecycleService.make_public: add in-service superuser guard
  (defence-in-depth — the @user_passes_test on the GraphQL mutation no
  longer the only gate, so internal callers like Celery tasks can't
  bypass it).
- WorkerAccountService.create_worker_account / set_active: same pattern,
  in-service superuser guard.
- NotificationService.mark_all_read: short-circuit to success(0) for
  anonymous / None users, matching the rest of the class so the service
  is safe to call from non-GraphQL contexts.

Coverage / behavioural tests:
- New test_service_layer_phase5_behavioral.py — 74 tests that pin the
  service-level behaviour the GraphQL mutation suites can't reach
  because their decorators short-circuit first. Covers every Phase 5
  service end-to-end: scope validation, IDOR-safe error envelopes,
  permission denials, filter combinations, lifecycle transitions, and
  the four new guards above.
- Phase 5 service-file coverage: agent_configuration_service 100%,
  agent_action_result_service 100%, analysis_lifecycle_service 98%,
  user_feedback_service 97%, notification_service 100%,
  corpus_access_token_service 98%, worker_account_service 100%,
  worker_document_upload_service 100% (target was 89.81%).
- mypy.ini: add the new file to the test-baseline ignore list (matches
  every other tests/test_*.py that uses setUpTestData).

* Phase 5 review fixes: IDOR + structural test + check order

Addresses Claude review on PR #1770:

* CorpusAccessTokenService.create_token: collapse 'Corpus not found.' /
  'Permission denied.' onto the unified 'Not found or permission denied.'
  IDOR-safe response (matches list_for_corpus / revoke_token). Update
  the two behavioural tests that previously pinned the leaky messages.

* Phase 5 structural test: add search_queries and conversation_types to
  module_to_expected_services so a future refactor cannot silently regress
  the @-mention surface back onto inline composition.

* AgentConfigurationService.create_agent: reverse the GLOBAL-scope check
  order so non-superusers learn they cannot create GLOBAL agents at all
  before learning about the corpus_id shape complaint.

* Reset ToolFunctionRegistry singleton in test_duplicate_tool_registration setUp

The 5 TestDuplicateToolRegistration tests are pre-existing and untouched
by this PR, but started failing on CI after the merge of main. Root cause:
ToolFunctionRegistry is a process-singleton (see tool_registry.py,
class-level _instance + reset()-for-isolation hook). Under
pytest-xdist --dist loadscope the *set* of modules co-located on a worker
shifts whenever the repo's test-file list changes (per CLAUDE.md, the known
test-isolation tax of the loadscope distribution); the new Phase 5
behavioural test file added by this branch reshuffles that placement so a
polluting test now shares this file's worker and skews the per-agent tool
counts the assertions pin.

The registry already exposes reset() for exactly this purpose. Calling
it in setUp forces the next get() to rebuild from
FUNCTION_MAP + AVAILABLE_TOOLS, making the tests immune to whatever
neighbour module landed on the worker.

Verified locally: 5/5 pass; pre-commit clean.

* Phase 5 review fixes: keyword-only active, explicit None failure, safer message dispatch

Addresses the three actionable items from Claude's latest review on PR #1770:

* WorkerAccountService.set_active: promote active to keyword-only so
  callers can't silently swap argument order, matching the rest of Phase 5's
  write-method convention. Both existing callers already pass active=.

* AnalysisLifecycleService.start_document_analysis: when
  process_analyzer returns None (internal failure / resource
  exhaustion), surface ServiceResult.failure('Analyzer could not be
  started.') instead of ok=True, value=None — callers can't silently
  treat a failed dispatch as a successful no-op. New
  test_start_document_analysis_none_from_process_is_failure pins this.

* MakeAnalysisPublic mutation: replace result.value or result.error
  with result.value if result.ok else result.error so a future falsy
  success value (empty string, 0, empty list) can't short-circuit through
  to the error branch.

subject: Default PDF zoom — reserve horizontal margin so fit-to-width never overflows on narrow laptops (#1736) (#1775)
message:
Default PDF zoom — reserve horizontal margin so fit-to-width never overflows on narrow laptops (#1736) (#1775)

* DocumentKnowledgeBase desktop initial PDF zoom — reserve horizontal margin so the fit-to-width result never overflows on narrower laptop viewports (#1736)

Verified the desktop initial PDF zoom is already a fit-to-width calculation
derived from the measured document-layer width (not a fixed seed), but the
calculation reserved no horizontal margin — the rendered page touched both
edges of the container, leaving no safety budget for sub-pixel rounding or
container chrome and risking a horizontal scrollbar on 1280px / 1024px
laptops.

The desktop path now flows through the same shared `computeFitToWidthZoom`
helper used by the mobile fit-to-width hook (introduced for the mobile
work), reserving FIT_WIDTH_MARGIN (16px) off the container width and
clamping to the canonical ZOOM_MIN / ZOOM_MAX (50% / 400%) — previously
the desktop path clamped to the magic numbers 0.3 / 4.0, drifting from the
shared constants. The mobile hook is refactored to call the shared helper
so both surfaces stay in lockstep going forward.

New unit test `fitToWidth.test.ts` pins the helper's contract; new CT
describe group `Default PDF zoom fit-to-width — {viewport} (#1736)`
mounts the full DKB at 1440x900, 1280x720 and 1024x768 and asserts that
the rendered PDF canvas width is strictly less than the #pdf-container
width at every viewport, capturing one documentation screenshot per
viewport:

  - knowledge-base--pdf-default-zoom--1440x900.png
  - knowledge-base--pdf-default-zoom--1280x720.png
  - knowledge-base--pdf-default-zoom--1024x768.png

Closes #1736

* Address review: move fitToWidth to utils, simplify guard, poll for zoom

- Move fitToWidth.ts -> frontend/src/utils/pdfZoom.ts to break the
  annotator <-> knowledge_base back-edge import (CLAUDE.md section 6 —
  pure number-in/number-out utilities belong in utils/, depending
  only on constants.ts).
- Collapse the redundant '!naturalPageWidth || naturalPageWidth <= 0'
  null-guard to a single '<= 0' check that covers 0, NaN, and negatives.
- Replace the verbose three-line useEffect comment in PDFPage.tsx with
  a one-line WHY pointer to issue #1736.
- Replace 'waitForTimeout(1500)' in the fit-to-width CT group with a
  'waitForFunction' that polls .zoom-level until the parsed value
  exceeds 100 % (visible evidence, not a fixed sleep).
- Refresh FIT_WIDTH_MARGIN docstring to say '16 px total breathing
  room reserved' (no longer references the misleading 'split between
  the two edges' wording) and to point at the new utils path.

subject: Phase 5 follow-ups — correctness + lint hygiene on PR #1770 (#1779) (#1783)
message:
Phase 5 follow-ups — correctness + lint hygiene on PR #1770 (#1779) (#1783)

Addresses the five post-merge items raised in the PR #1770 review.

Bug fixes (the two genuine correctness concerns from the review):

* search_queries.py resolve_search_agents_for_mention: the new inline
  `corpus_pk = int(from_global_id(corpus_id)[1]) if corpus_id else None`
  was unguarded. A malformed corpus_id (bad base64 / non-numeric body)
  raised ValueError unhandled and surfaced as a 500. Now wrapped in
  try/except so corpus_pk falls back to None — mirrors the IDOR-safe
  decode pattern already in resolve_search_notes_for_mention. New
  regression test pins three flavours of malformed id.

* AnalysisLifecycleService.delete_analysis: the initial visibility
  lookup called the module-level `get_for_user_or_none` helper, which
  has no request= kwarg — silently bypassing the Tier-2 permission
  cache for the lookup half of the two-step check while the subsequent
  user_can(..., request=request) call did engage it. Now routes through
  BaseService.get_or_none so both halves share the same cached entry.
  Dead import removed; new regression test patches BaseService's local
  helper reference and asserts the request= kwarg is threaded.

Lint / mypy hygiene:

* worker_mutations.py + worker_queries.py: replaced the four
  `assert result.value is not None  # narrowed by result.ok invariant`
  lines with typing.cast — `assert` is stripped under `python -O`,
  cast survives. resolve_corpus_access_tokens uses a bare
  `cast("QuerySet", result.value)` (unparameterised) because the
  service dynamically annotates _pending / _completed / _failed upload
  counts on each row; those are not real fields on CorpusAccessToken,
  so a typed QuerySet[CorpusAccessToken] cast would make the
  annotated-attribute access fail mypy.

* UserFeedbackService._set_feedback: added a docstring note pinning
  the intentional `comment="" -> preserve old comment` semantics
  inherited verbatim from the pre-relocation Approve/Reject mutations.
  Documents the intent so a future caller doesn't reach for `comment=""`
  expecting it to clear the field.

Closes #1779

subject: Phase 6 follow-up: filter_visible_qs + request= + tighter invariant tests (#1782) (#1784)
message:
Phase 6 follow-up: filter_visible_qs + request= + tighter invariant tests (#1782) (#1784)

* Phase 6 follow-up: filter_visible_qs + request= + tighter invariant tests (#1782)

Five targeted corrections from the PR #1780 code review (issue #1782);
the Phase 6 migration itself is untouched.

1. New ``BaseService.filter_visible_qs(queryset, user, *, request, **kw)``
   (opencontractserver/shared/services/base.py). PR #1780 replaced
   ``queryset.visible_to_user(user)`` with
   ``filter_visible(Model, user).values('pk') | queryset.filter(pk__in=…)`` —
   a correlated subquery over the full model table. The new helper chains
   the queryset's own ``visible_to_user`` so the visibility predicate
   stays in the same WHERE expression tree as any prior ``.filter(...)``
   clauses (single SQL pass, no extra full-model-table scan).

   Refactored call sites in config/graphql/{annotation,corpus,document,
   conversation,user}_types.py: AnnotationType / NoteType / DocumentType /
   ConversationType / CorpusType / CorpusFolderType ``get_queryset``,
   plus ``LabelSetType.resolve_corpus_count``,
   ``CorpusFolderType.resolve_children``, and
   ``CorpusType.resolve_folders`` field resolvers. UserFeedbackType keeps
   its prefetch-cache pass-through guard.

   New regression tests in opencontractserver/tests/test_base_service.py
   pin the chained-filter semantic by counting ``FROM <corpus_table>``
   occurrences in the compiled SQL.

2. Missing ``request=info.context`` on four corpus UPDATE gates touched
   by PR #1780 — UpdateDocumentSummary (config/graphql/document_mutations.py)
   and CreateBadge / UpdateBadge / DeleteBadge (config/graphql/
   badge_mutations.py). Functionally identical (the permission check
   itself was already correct); this only engages the Tier-2 cache.

3. ``test_allowlist_is_documented`` was vacuously true with
   ``ALLOWED_FILES = frozenset()``. Replaced the silent-pass loop with
   a positive ``assert ALLOWED_FILES == frozenset()`` so a stray
   addition without docstring/CHANGELOG update trips the test.
   ``test_django_system_check_is_registered`` previously only checked
   that *some* check existed under the "architecture" tag; now pins
   ``check_graphql_service_layer`` specifically via
   ``django.core.checks.registry.get_checks(tags=["architecture"])``.

4. Documented the AST-scan startup cost in the docstring of
   ``check_graphql_service_layer`` — sub-50 ms over ~41 files,
   intentionally not fast-pathed or DEBUG-gated because the "fail on
   first management command" semantic is the whole point of
   dual-enforcement.

5. Documented the ``require_permission`` truthiness inversion in its
   docstring — returns "" on grant and an error string on denial,
   inverse of the legacy ``if user_can(...)`` idiom. Cross-readers
   transcribing the old form directly would flip the gate.

Docs synced: CHANGELOG / docs/development/architecture_invariants.md /
docs/architecture/query_permission_patterns.md now reflect the live
``ALLOWED_FILES = frozenset()`` state (the original PR #1780 description
described an interim commit, not the merged code).

Refs: #1782
Closes #1782

* Fix mypy + tree-queries baseline in Phase-6 follow-up tests

- registry.get_checks() in Django 5.x takes no 'tags' kwarg; filter
  registered_checks by per-check tags attribute instead. Mypy
  rejected the bogus 'tags' kwarg attempt.
- test_filter_visible_qs_preserves_incoming_filter compared an
  absolute FROM count (==1) against the corpus table, but Corpus uses
  django-tree-queries whose recursive CTE adds its own FROM reference
  to corpuses_corpus. Compare against the baseline queryset's FROM
  count so the test pins 'no extra full-table scan from
  filter_visible_qs' independent of CTE noise.

* Address review: inline notes on request-drop, M2M security, SQL brittleness

Addresses the five doc/comment items raised in the PR #1784 Claude
review. None change behaviour — all clarify intent for future
readers.

- BaseService.filter_visible_qs: add inline security note on the
  hasattr guard ('unfiltered queryset is a bug, not a no-op') and
  spell out that 'request' is intentionally not forwarded because
  the Tier-2 cache is single-object-keyed.
- test_filter_visible_qs_excludes_other_user: add the missing
  one-line docstring matching the surrounding pattern.
- test_filter_visible_qs_preserves_incoming_filter: note the Django
  major-version brittleness of str(queryset.query) and explain why
  the baseline-equality assertion stays valid across format shifts.
- test_allowlist_is_documented: comment the intentionally-dead loop
  so its 'kept in place for future entries' purpose is obvious.

---------

                       World-facing pitch aimed at developers, AI labs,
                       research teams, and anyone landing on the repo
                       or self-hosting cite against their own corpus.
                       This is the repo default and the framing used in
                       README, index.html OG tags, and the bundled
                       Discover/About screenshots.

  - public-record    → "The citation layer underneath the public record."
                       End-user pitch with the named-incumbent argument
                       (Westlaw, Lexis, JSTOR, USPTO, Wheaton v. Peters,
                       Public.Resource.Org, Free Law Project). Lands well
                       on cite.opensource.legal where the audience is
                       end-users of a specific corpus of public-domain
                       documents.

A deployer flips between them by setting REACT_APP_LANDING_VARIANT in
frontend/public/env-config.js — no rebuild, no fork. Unknown variants
fall back to default rather than crashing. Adding a new pitch is a
three-step process documented in README: drop a JSON file in
src/config/landingContent/, register it in index.ts, set the env var.

    index.ts            — variant registry + useLandingContent() hook

    renderInlineMarkup  — tiny inline-italic renderer that wraps `*…*`
                          spans in Source Serif italic <em>. The brand
                          rule restricts italic to (a) the cite product
                          name and (b) publication/platform names in
                          body copy — both are flat inline spans, so a

The badge tooltip in the sidebar discussion view was clipped by the
overflow:hidden chain (ContextSidebarContainer / DocumentDiscussionsContent
Container / FlexColumnPanel). Render TooltipPopup via createPortal to
document.body with fixed coords derived from the badge rect; viewport-edge
clamping plus a flip-below-the-badge fallback prevents the same clip near
the top of any scroll container. Arrow stays anchored under the badge
centre via a --arrow-offset CSS variable.

While in the same view, the ThreadDetail compact header packed back-arrow
+ type badge + title + description + document link + status pills into one
flex-wrap row, and a duplicate compact back button shadowed the parent's
"Back to List". Reworked so each piece gets its own line (title row /
description / context link / meta row separated by a dashed border) and
the redundant back button is suppressed when customOnBack is provided.

harnesses) that pins both the new header layout and the no-clip tooltip
behaviour, with auto screenshots for the docs surface.

* Address review feedback (#1790)

- MessageBadges tooltip: re-position on capture-phase scroll + resize
  while the tooltip is visible.  ``position: fixed`` doesn't follow
  the badge when an ancestor scroll container moves under it; without
  this listener the tooltip drifts to the wrong place when the
  sidebar scrolls while the cursor is held still over a badge
  (review item #1).
- Replace the ``["--arrow-offset" as any]`` style cast with a
  ``Record<string, string>`` spread so the any-baseline gate stays
  honest (was the new offender that pushed current=438 baseline=437).
- ThreadDetailSidebarLayout test: assert structurally that the
  tooltip is NOT a descendant of the clip-frame
  (``el.closest('[data-testid=clip-frame]') === null``).  The
  previous "nonzero width/height" assertion could pass even if the
  portal failed to escape the clip frame (review item: test).

* Address PR review on #1790: constants, z-index, stale read, back-button bug

Addresses Claude review on #1790 (plus restoring the back button that the
PR accidentally hid):

Critical (back button gone for sidebar discussion view):
- ThreadDetail dropped its compact BackButton whenever ``customOnBack``
  was passed. But ``customOnBack`` is the back-navigation HANDLER the
  parent supplies, not a signal that the parent renders its own button.
  ``ThreadDetailWithContext`` delegates click handling without showing
  its own back affordance, so the new gate stranded the user with no
  way to return to the list — and broke the threads-discussions.spec.ts
  e2e flow (the "Back to discussions" button locator timed out after
  3 retries). Reverted to ``compact &&`` so the button is always shown
  in compact mode; the handler still respects customOnBack.

CLAUDE.md rule #4 (no magic numbers):
- MessageBadges.tsx hoisted TOOLTIP_HEIGHT_EST + TOOLTIP_MAX_WIDTH to
  module scope, swapped its local ``GAP = 8`` and ``VIEWPORT_PADDING = 8``

- The JSX was computing ``bottom: window.innerHeight - tooltipPos.top``
  at render time, racing with a resize that could fire between
  computePosition and the next paint (1-frame misalignment). Capture

  through in the JSX.

- When the badge scrolled fully out of the viewport the tooltip stayed
  fixed at its last computed coords. ``computePosition`` now early-

  window.innerHeight``.

* fix(chat): scroll tool approval modal body so long args don't push buttons off-screen

The Approve/Reject modal in both corpus chat (ApprovalModal) and the
document right tray (ApprovalOverlay) rendered the pending tool call's
JSON arguments inside a <pre> with no height cap on the surrounding
modal. A long-string argument (e.g. update_corpus_description's

buttons.

box-sizing border-box; the body section scrolls (flex: 1, minHeight: 0,
overflowY: auto); header/footer stay pinned via flexShrink: 0. The
<pre> picks up wordBreak/overflowWrap so an unbroken token can't blow

subject: Make native PDF link annotations clickable in the viewer (#1788)
message:
Make native PDF link annotations clickable in the viewer (#1788)

* Make native PDF link annotations clickable in the viewer

Embedded hyperlinks in PDFs were unreachable because the SelectionLayer
overlay sits at z-index 1 across the entire page and intercepts every
mouse event. PDF.js painted the link rects into the canvas as pixels,
but page.getAnnotations() was never called, so no DOM target existed
to receive the click.

New NativeLinkLayer extracts Link annotations from each page, filters
to safe protocols (http/https/mailto), projects each rect through the
viewport, and renders transparent <a> elements at z-index 2 (above
SelectionLayer, below the SelectionActionMenu portal). The overlay
container is pointer-events: none so empty space still falls through
to the selection logic; each anchor is pointer-events: auto so the
browser handles the click (with hover state, right-click menu, and
keyboard focus). Internal dest-based navigation is not yet wired.

* Address review feedback (#1788)

- Replace hardcoded ``z-index: 2`` in NativeLinkLayer with new
  ``Z_INDEX.PDF_NATIVE_LINK_LAYER`` constant + sibling
  ``PDF_SELECTION_LAYER`` entry, removing the magic-number rule violation
  flagged in review.
- Switch ``NativeLinkLayer`` from ``React.FC`` (which the project's
  ``"jsx": "react-jsx"`` transform leaves out of scope unless React is
  explicitly imported) to a named ``FC`` import from "react" — same
  pattern recommended by review.
- Drop the ``as any`` cast in NativeLinkLayer.test.tsx for a proper
  ``as unknown as PDFPageProxy`` so the any-baseline lint check is back
  to clean.
- Slim down the CHANGELOG entry per review minor #4 — the existing entry
  doubled as a design doc; the format guidance asks for a short summary
  with file paths + a coverage pointer. Also drop the duplicate
  "Discovery endpoints rebranded" entry that local-main drift surfaced
  here (PR #1785 already owns that entry on main).

* Address #1788 review: wire SelectionLayer to constant, reset rawLinks, add aria-label

- SelectionLayer was still using a literal `zIndex: 1` even though
  the PR introduced `Z_INDEX.PDF_SELECTION_LAYER` to make the
  layering relationship between SelectionLayer (1) and the new
  NativeLinkLayer (2) explicit. Wire it through so the constant is
  not dead.
- NativeLinkLayer now clears `rawLinks` at the start of the page
  effect so a future recycled component instance cannot briefly
  paint the previous page's link positions while the new fetch is
  in flight.
- Transparent anchors now expose `aria-label={link.url}` so
  screen readers (VoiceOver in particular ignores the `title`
  attribute as an accessible-name source) get a robust name.
- Narrow rect type from `number[]` to a 4-tuple, with an explicit
  `length === 4` guard before the cast, so the
  `[x1, y1, x2, y2]` destructuring is type-safe.
- Strengthen the unit test mock: `getViewport` now honours the
  passed `scale` (was hard-coded to ×2), and the test asserts
  `getViewport` was called with the expected scale. Adds an
  aria-label regression test.

subject: Corpus upvote/downvote: anonymous-friendly voting + score-based sort (#1789)
message:
Corpus upvote/downvote: anonymous-friendly voting + score-based sort (#1789)

* corpus voting: anonymous-friendly upvote/downvote with score-based sort

Adds a Reddit-style up/down vote signal on the corpus list view so users
(and unauthenticated visitors) can surface high-signal corpora.

Backend
-------
- `CorpusVote` model + `CorpusVoteType` text-choices + Guardian permission
  tables in `opencontractserver/corpuses/models.py`. Supports two voter
  shapes in one table: authenticated votes keyed on `creator`, anonymous
  votes keyed on Django `session_key`. Two partial UNIQUE indexes encode
  the actual one-vote-per-voter contract per branch (a single composite
  UNIQUE would either let unbounded NULL-creator rows accumulate or block
  every authenticated row, since Postgres treats every NULL as distinct).
- Three new denormalized columns on `Corpus` (`upvote_count`,
  `downvote_count`, indexed `score = upvotes - downvotes`) maintained by
  signal handlers in `opencontractserver/corpuses/signals.py`. Recompute-
  from-scratch via `QuerySet.update(...)` so the parent `Corpus.save()`
  override (which bumps `modified` and runs public-flip propagation) does
  not fire on every vote.
- Migration `corpuses/0049_corpusvote_corpus_upvote_count_and_more.py`.
- `CorpusVoteService(BaseService)` in
  `opencontractserver/corpuses/services/votes.py` exposes `cast_vote` /
  `remove_vote` / `get_user_vote_type`. IDOR-safe via
  `BaseService.get_or_none` (unified "not found or no permission" message),
  blocks self-vote on the authenticated branch, persists anon votes by
  `session_key`, records a salted SHA-256 `ip_hash` for audit only (NOT
  part of the unique constraint — shared NATs would otherwise block
  legitimate co-located voters). Re-exported from
  `corpuses/services/__init__.py`.
- GraphQL mutations `voteCorpus` / `removeCorpusVote` in
  `config/graphql/voting_mutations.py`. Deliberately NOT decorated with
  `@login_required` — anonymous voting is the whole point. Lazy
  `session.save()` on first cast materialises a `session_key` so
  subsequent votes from the same browser dedupe correctly.
- `CorpusType.myVote` resolver in `config/graphql/corpus_types.py` —
  named `myVote` (not `userVote` like the existing Message/Conversation
  fields) because it generalises to anonymous viewers. The three new
  columns auto-expose via `DjangoObjectType` field auto-discovery.
- `CorpusFilter.order_by` in `config/graphql/filters.py` exposes
  `top` / `-top` / `created` / `-modified` / `title`. Top sort excludes
  `is_personal=True` corpora (personal "My Documents" singletons should
  not rank against shared content).

Frontend
--------
- `frontend/src/components/corpuses/CorpusVoteWidget.tsx` — lightweight
  up/down + score pill overlaid on the top-left of each corpus card.
  Optimistic update + Apollo `cache.modify` keep every corpus card on
  screen in sync after a vote without a refetch. Hidden on the user's
  own personal corpus.
- "Sort by" dropdown in `CorpusListView.tsx` between the search box and
  filter tabs (Newest / Oldest / Recently updated / Top / Controversial
  / Title) wired through `Corpuses.tsx` to the `orderBy` GraphQL arg.
- `UPVOTE_CORPUS` / `DOWNVOTE_CORPUS` / `REMOVE_CORPUS_VOTE` mutations
  + types in `frontend/src/graphql/mutations.ts`. `GET_CORPUSES` extended
  with `orderBy: String` plus the four new fields
  (`upvoteCount`, `downvoteCount`, `score`, `myVote`) — propagated into
  `RawCorpusType` in `frontend/src/types/graphql-api.ts`.

Tests + docs
------------
- `opencontractserver/tests/test_corpus_voting.py` — service-layer
  behavioural contract (auth + anon, self-vote block, IDOR-safe denial,
  vote switching, anon session dedup, "auth user cannot claim an anon
  vote" invariant), TransactionTestCase coverage of the signal-driven
  count refresh, partial UNIQUE constraint pinning, GraphQL end-to-end
  through graphene's schema (auth path, anon session-bootstrap path,
  self-vote block, malformed-id IDOR safety, my_vote resolver).
- CHANGELOG.md entry + new "Corpus Voting — Anonymous Voter Support"
  section in `docs/permissioning/consolidated_permissioning_guide.md`
  documenting the two voter shapes, the partial UNIQUE rationale, the
  session bootstrap, and the Top-sort personal-corpus exclusion.

* Fix mypy errors and address review feedback (#1789)

mypy:
- Override CorpusVote.creator FK with type: ignore[assignment] (matches
  existing pattern in models.py:1657) so the User|None override doesn't
  conflict with BaseOCModel's User-typed creator.
- Add class-level type annotations to CorpusVoteServiceTests for cls.foo
  assignments inside setUpTestData (django-stubs limitation).
- Add `assert result.value is not None` narrowings after assertTrue(result.ok)
  so mypy can resolve attribute access on ServiceResult.value.
- Type self.client as Any to work around incomplete graphene.test.Client
  stubs (.execute attribute not advertised).
- Add assert in VoteCorpusMutation after the ok-check to narrow result.value.

Review feedback:
- Add ``orderBy`` to the Apollo corpuses keyArgs in cache.ts so switching
  sort doesn't bleed a cached "Newest" connection into a "Top" request
  (CLAUDE.md note #15).
- Drop the duplicate created_at/updated_at columns on CorpusVote --
  BaseOCModel already provides created/modified with identical
  auto_now_add/auto_now semantics. Migration updated to match.
- Fix self-vote denial typo: "your own corpuses" -> "your own corpus".
- Rename the "Controversial" sort option to "Most downvoted" (the score
  ASC sort surfaces lowest-scoring corpora, not high-engagement ones).
- Replace the never-cleaned-up ``_vote_session_init`` sentinel with
  ``session.modified = True`` for forcing session persistence on
  anonymous vote bootstrap.
- Remove the dead ``self.data.get("orderBy")`` branch from CorpusFilter
  -- graphene-django translates camelCase to snake_case before the
  FilterSet sees the args, so only ``order_by`` ever appears.

* Add component tests for CorpusVoteWidget + sort dropdown (#1789)

- New CorpusVoteWidget.ct.tsx + wrapper covering: neutral render,
  optimistic upvote/downvote, click-active-arrow-to-remove, and the
  self-vote-blocked path (with a docScreenshot for the docs).
- Extend CorpusListView wrapper + test to drive the new sort dropdown
  introduced by this PR; pin the labelled option set so a label-rename
  doesn't silently drift past stale assertions.
- Memoize ``stop`` in CorpusVoteWidget with useCallback so the Pill
  receives a stable onClick reference per render (PR #1789 review #8).

* Address PR review on #1789: fix N+1, default sort, asserts, arch

Addresses Claude review on #1789:

Bugs:
- Default sort label was "Newest first" but the empty orderBy fell back
  to Corpus.Meta.ordering = ("created",) ASC → oldest first. Default
  switched to "-created" so the label matches the result order.
- voting_mutations.py used `assert result.value is not None` after a
  successful CorpusVoteService.cast_vote; python -O strips asserts so a
  corner-case service bug would surface as a 500 / AttributeError.
  Replaced with a proper error-return.

Performance:
- resolve_my_vote was firing one CorpusVote query per corpus card on the
  public list view. CorpusType.get_queryset now annotates _viewer_vote
  via a single Subquery per page (auth: creator-keyed; anon: session-key
  keyed); resolve_my_vote reads the annotation via hasattr so an
  annotated None (= no vote) is treated as authoritative rather than
  triggering a fallback per-row lookup. New regression test
  test_corpuses_list_my_vote_is_not_n_plus_one uses
  CaptureQueriesContext to pin the contract.

Architecture / CLAUDE.md rule 7:
- voteCorpus / removeCorpusVote previously refreshed the corpus row via
  Corpus.objects.get(pk=...) after a successful service call. Routed
  through BaseService.get_or_none(Corpus, ...) so the mutation surface
  stays inside the service-layer contract.

Tests:
- test_corpus_services_package.py expected the 6-service re-export tuple;
  the new CorpusVoteService now joins the list and the count comment is
  updated.

Docs / nits:
- CorpusVoteWidget.stop drops preventDefault (only stopPropagation is
  needed to keep card navigation from firing; preventDefault would
  suppress form submission if the pill ever lands inside a <form>).
- _client_ip docstring spells out the X-Forwarded-For trust posture
  (audit-only; no abuse decisions).
- CorpusVote model docstring documents the anonymous-row tombstone
  behaviour after clearsessions (intentional Reddit-style permanence;
  counts stay correct because the signal recomputes from scratch).

Stale-test fix from main merge:
- test_corpus_services_package.test_package_reexports_the_segmented_services
  now expects CorpusVoteService in __all__.

Backend: 30/30 voting tests, 333 total in related suites green.
Frontend: 13/13 CorpusListView CT + 5/5 CorpusVoteWidget CT green.

* Address #1789 review: scope Top-sort personal exclusion, align Sort labels, fix CT mocks

- Backend: `CorpusFilter.filter_queryset` now only excludes
  `is_personal=True` from Top sorts on the discovery surface (when
  `mine` is not set). The 'My Corpuses' tab (mine=True) keeps personal
  corpora visible under every sort so users always see all their own
  content. Adds two regression tests covering both branches.
- Sort dropdown label drift: CHANGELOG referenced 'Controversial' but
  the dropdown ships as 'Most downvoted'. CHANGELOG aligned to the
  shipping label (kept; matches the CT assertion).
- CorpusNavigationScreenshots CT mocks were stale after the default
  sort changed to '-created' — the actual query now sends
  `{ orderBy: '-created' }` and the empty-vars / textSearch='' mocks
  no longer matched. Added the matching mock and seeded the new vote
  fields (upvoteCount/downvoteCount/score/myVote) on the test corpus.

* Black formatting from pre-commit hook

subject: Fix: anonymous corpus voting no longer 403s subsequent GraphQL POSTs (#1802)
message:
Fix: anonymous corpus voting no longer 403s subsequent GraphQL POSTs (#1802)

Regression introduced by #1789 (corpus voting). The voting flow calls
`_ensure_session_key` to materialise a Django `sessionid` cookie so
anonymous voters can be deduped by `session_key`. The CSRF gate in
`conditional_csrf_exempt` then saw any session cookie as a reason to
invoke `CsrfViewMiddleware.process_view`, so the very next anonymous
POST (a re-vote, a refetch, `GET_ME` firing during the Auth0 callback)
was rejected with "CSRF cookie not set". `errorLink.ts` interpreted
that as "session expired", clobbered the SPA auth state, and the
follow-up cascade produced "Unable to fetch corpuses" / "Could not get
user details from server" toasts.

Fix: `conditional_csrf_exempt` now bypasses CSRF when the session has
no `_auth_user_id` (Django's `contrib.auth.SESSION_KEY`). An empty
session has no logged-in identity for a CSRF attacker to ride on, so
the check had no security value but blocked legitimate anonymous
traffic. Session-authenticated requests (admin, the legacy `tokenAuth`
mutation that calls `django.login`) still go through the standard CSRF
flow.

Tests
-----
- `test_security_hardening.py`: existing tests that asserted 403 on a
  bare session cookie now attach `request.session = {"_auth_user_id":
  "1"}` so they actually exercise the session-authenticated branch.
  `_post_with_session` helper updated for the same reason. New
  `test_anonymous_session_cookie_bypasses_csrf` and
  `test_session_without_session_attr_bypasses_csrf` pin the new
  bypass branch.
- `test_corpus_voting.py`: new `AnonymousVotingMiddlewareIntegrationTests`
  drives `/graphql/` through the real middleware stack with
  `Client(enforce_csrf_checks=True)` to verify two consecutive
  anonymous votes from the same browser both succeed (the original
  unit tests use `RequestFactory` and never hit the middleware).

subject: Fix unified rail tooltip + Settings popover placement on desktop (#1803)
message:
Fix unified rail tooltip + Settings popover placement on desktop (#1803)

* Fix unified rail tooltip + Settings popover placement on desktop

Two regressions introduced by the unified-rail consolidation in #1764.

(1) `SidebarTab` declared both `&[data-tooltip]::after` (the hover
tooltip) and `&::after` (a 3px active-state indicator line). CSS cascade
resolves per-property, so the tooltip rule won the properties it set
(content, background, color) but the indicator rule's `width: 3px;
height: 60%;` still applied because the tooltip rule never set them.
The tooltip collapsed into a 3px-wide pill with overflowing white text —
the "labels are white and there's a little black dot" the user reported.

Fix: drop the conflicting `&::after` indicator rule. The active state is
already conveyed by the blue gradient background and box-shadow glow, so
the now-broken white line was redundant.

(2) `ControlPanel` (Annotation Filters popover) used `bottom: calc(56px
+ 1rem); right: 0;` from its parent `ControlsContainer`. That anchor
assumed the non-bare `flex-direction: column-reverse` layout where
Settings sits at the BOTTOM of the column. The new bare-mode layout for
the unified `RightEdgeRail` uses `flex-direction: column`, so Settings
sits at the TOP and the popover ended up anchored above the LAST action
button (Create) — ~280px above its trigger.

Fix: `ControlPanel` now takes a `$bare` prop and switches to `right:
calc(100% + 8px); top: 0;` in bare mode, anchoring the popover to the
LEFT of the rail vertically aligned with the Settings button. Non-bare
positioning is unchanged.

Regression coverage in `tests/FloatingDocumentControls.ct.tsx`:
- bare-mode popover position assert: panel right edge sits to the left
  of the trigger and panel top aligns with trigger top (±8px).
- hover tooltip pill assert: `getComputedStyle(el, "::after")` returns
  width > 40px, height > 12px, and `content` containing the data-tooltip
  text — pins the tooltip is not collapsed.

`FloatingDocumentControlsTestWrapper` gained an opt-in `bareContainer`
prop that mounts the controls inside a viewport-edge rail wrapper so the
bare popover positioning is exercised against the same column geometry
production uses.

* Deflake AgentMentionPopover + SelectAnalyzerOrFieldsetModal CT

Two unrelated component tests have been flaky against the same Playwright
CT iframe-focus + framer-motion-hit-test corner cases that don't reproduce
on every machine but cost a CI run when they trip.

- AgentMentionPopover.ct.tsx
  The picker attaches a document-level capture-phase keydown listener in
  useEffect. page.keyboard.press(...) routes through whatever element has
  document focus; on a fresh mount the Playwright iframe sometimes doesn't
  hold focus yet, so the keystroke is dropped and the test passes only on
  retry. Replaced every keyboard.press in the file with a pressDocumentKey
  helper that dispatches the KeyboardEvent directly on document — which is
  exactly where the listener is registered — making the test deterministic.

- SelectAnalyzerOrFieldsetModal.ct.tsx
  The "closes when the overlay is clicked" test waited for opacity:1 and
  then issued page.mouse.click(5, 5). Even after the opacity transition
  settles, framer-motion's wrapping motion.div can still be mid-transition
  for hit-testing purposes, so the click occasionally lands on a transparent
  descendant that stops propagation and onClose never fires. Replaced with
  overlay.dispatchEvent("click"), which targets the overlay element where
  React registers onClick={onClose}, bypassing the unstable hit-test path.

Verified locally:
- AgentMentionPopover.ct.tsx, --repeat-each=3: 27/27 passed.
- SelectAnalyzerOrFieldsetModal.ct.tsx -g "overlay is clicked",
  --repeat-each=8: 8/8 passed.
- All FloatingDocumentControls + SidebarTabs + DesktopDocumentLayout
  CT (46 tests) still pass.

* Address PR review: tighten ControlPanel + tooltip test + CHANGELOG

Claude-bot review on PR #1803 flagged four items. Addressed three; one
explicitly skipped (see below).

- Use the `css` helper for the ControlPanel conditional block
  (FloatingDocumentControls.tsx). Raw template literals in styled-components
  interpolations bypass tagged-template processing, so any nested
  interpolation added later (theme vars, etc.) would silently not resolve.
  Switched the bare / non-bare branches to `css\`...\`` for safety at no
  runtime cost.

- Remove the dead `$bare` prop on the width-menu ControlPanel
  (FloatingDocumentControls.tsx). The width-menu panel is gated on
  `expandedWidthMenu && showRightPanel`, and the unified rail's bare mode
  only renders when the panel is closed — so `$bare={bareContainer}` was
  unreachable on that branch. Dropped the prop and added an inline comment
  explaining why the width-menu panel intentionally keeps the non-bare
  anchor (bottom-right above the trigger).

- Harden the tooltip pill regression test
  (FloatingDocumentControls.ct.tsx). `getComputedStyle(el, "::after").width`
  can resolve to "auto" on headless CI agents before the opacity transition
  completes — parseFloat then yields NaN and `expect(NaN).toBeGreaterThan(40)`
  would throw an opaque assertion failure. Added an `expect.poll` on the
  pseudo-element's opacity reaching "1" (so the pseudo is fully realized)
  and explicit `Number.isFinite` guards before the dimension assertions.

- CHANGELOG: split the single ~600-word paragraph into two focused entries
  (one per fix) with file references — matching surrounding entries.

NOT addressing: the reviewer also noted the CHANGELOG entry is verbose
compared to the project's terser style. Trimmed the new entry; left the
adjacent #1801 / #1802 / earlier entries alone since they're already merged
and rewriting committed history isn't in scope for this PR.

Verified:
- yarn test:ct tests/FloatingDocumentControls.ct.tsx --repeat-each=2:
  44 passed (no flakes).
- yarn lint: clean.
- tsc --noEmit: clean.

* Capture docScreenshots for new bare-mode popover + tooltip regression tests

The two regression guards added in this PR exercise new visual states for
the unified rail — the Settings popover anchored beside the rail in bare
mode, and the hover tooltip rendered as a readable pill. Both are useful
references for docs. Added docScreenshot calls after the layout/dimension
assertions confirm the intended state has been reached.

The on-demand screenshots.yml workflow regenerates the PNGs in
docs/assets/images/screenshots/auto/ on the PR branch when the user
triggers it, so the test calls are the contract here — no PNGs committed
from this side (CLAUDE.md: never hand-edit files in that auto/ directory).

subject: Expose explicit retrieval mode (vector / fts / hybrid) on annotation vector search (#1804)
message:
Expose explicit retrieval mode (vector / fts / hybrid) on annotation vector search (#1804)

* Expose explicit retrieval mode on annotation vector search

Add a `SearchMode = Literal["vector", "fts", "hybrid"]` knob (default
`"hybrid"`) on `VectorSearchQuery` and dispatch `CoreAnnotationVectorStore`'s
`search` / `async_search` on it. Library callers (GraphQL resolver, eval
harness, advanced API users) can now pin retrieval to pgvector cosine only,
PostgreSQL `tsvector` only, or the existing RRF-fused hybrid; the agent-
facing `vector_search_tool` closure intentionally does NOT expose `mode`,
so LLMs continue to get hybrid by default.

Refactor:
- Extract `_run_vector_only_sync` / `_async_vector_only` and add
  `_run_fts_only_sync` / `_async_fts_only` paths.
- `_run_fts_query` becomes a `@staticmethod` so `global_search`
  (classmethod) can reuse it.
- `global_search` / `async_global_search` honor `mode` end-to-end with a
  real FTS arm + RRF fusion — addresses the pre-existing TODO at the
  vector arm.
- `_resolve_mode` degrades `"fts"`/`"hybrid"` to `"vector"` when no
  `query_text` is provided (preserves existing `async_search` behavior);
  `"hybrid"` still falls back to text-only when embedding generation
  fails.
- Plumb `mode` through `PydanticAIAnnotationVectorStore.search_annotations`
  / `.search_sync` and `PydanticAIVectorSearchRequest`.

Tests: new `TestSearchModeDispatch` class in `test_hybrid_search.py`
pins mode dispatch (vector skips FTS, FTS skips embedding, sync + async
paths) and the `_resolve_mode` degradation contract.

* Address PR review: f-string→lazy logging, _degrade_mode helper, tighter tests

- Convert two FTS debug logs to %-style lazy formatting (consistency
  with the rest of the module; avoids interpolation when filtered).
- Extract _degrade_mode(mode, has_text, log_prefix) so _resolve_mode
  (instance path) and global_search (classmethod path) share one rule
  for "fts"/"hybrid"→"vector" when text is missing.
- Use class reference for sync_to_async(_run_fts_query) in
  _async_fts_only (static-method intent is now explicit at the call site).
- Tests:
  - Rename test_async_search_mode_fts_without_text_returns_empty →
    _degrades_to_vector to match the actual contract; pin _resolve_mode
    output directly and assert _async_vector_only is awaited.
  - Add explicit dispatch tests for mode="hybrid" on both sync and async
    paths (previously only "vector"/"fts" dispatch was pinned).

* ci: pin COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=opencontracts on e2e workflows

After the `OpenContracts` → `cite` repo rename, docker compose's default
project name (derived from the checkout directory) changed from
`opencontracts` to `cite`, so the django container is created as
`cite-django-1`. Both frontend-e2e-extract and frontend-e2e-websocket
poll `docker inspect opencontracts-django-1` in their wait-for-healthy
loop, which now silently misses (the `2>/dev/null || echo "starting"`
fallback returns "starting" forever) and the loop times out after 120s
even though the actual container is healthy within ~10s. See:

    Container cite-django-1  Healthy   (compose reports OK)
    django did not become healthy in time   (workflow times out)

Pin `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=opencontracts` at the workflow `env:` level so
container names stay stable regardless of the checkout directory or any
future repo rename. Inline comment documents the constraint so the next
person touching these workflows doesn't peel away the env var.

* Address PR review round 3: global_search helper, tests, log levels

- Extract _generate_global_query_vector helper so global_search's
  effective_mode mutation lives at a single, unit-testable call site
  (replaces nested if/else that reassigned mode in two branches).
- Add 6 global_search dispatch tests (vector/fts/hybrid + degradation
  paths for embedder failure) + 4 unit tests for the new helper.
- Demote per-call INFO logs in search/async_search to DEBUG; per-call
  tracing belongs at DEBUG, INFO is reserved for state transitions.
- Document the defensive [:first_stage_top_k] slice in the FTS arm.
- Add mode field to PydanticAIVectorSearchRequest docstring.

subject: Fix >100MB zip uploads: migrate corpus-export and zip-to-corpus imports from base64-over-GraphQL to multipart REST (#1809)
message:
Fix >100MB zip uploads: migrate corpus-export and zip-to-corpus imports from base64-over-GraphQL to multipart REST (#1809)

* Migrate corpus-export and zip-to-corpus uploads from base64-over-GraphQL to multipart REST

Files past ~100 MB were failing with "NetworkError when attempting to fetch resource."
in BulkImportModal and ImportCorpusModal because both still routed the entire ZIP
through a base64 string baked into a GraphQL JSON body — base64 inflates ~33% and
Apollo's JSON.stringify then exceeded V8's contiguous-string allocation limit
before any network I/O could fire. The single-doc and bulk-zip-without-folders
paths had already been migrated; these two were the stragglers.

Adds two REST endpoints that wrap the existing celery tasks and stream the upload
straight through Django storage:

- POST /api/imports/zip-to-corpus/ (ZipToCorpusImportView) replaces ImportZipToCorpus
- POST /api/imports/corpus/ (CorpusExportImportView) replaces UploadCorpusImportZip

Shared service functions in opencontractserver/document_imports/services.py
(import_zip_to_corpus_for_user, import_corpus_export_for_user) carry the
permission/IDOR gating and TemporaryFileHandle staging; views are thin and reuse
DocumentImportThrottle, JWT auth, and the per-endpoint size cap.

Frontend modals (BulkImportModal.tsx, ImportCorpusModal.tsx) drop the
FileReader.readAsDataURL conversion and call new importZipToCorpusMultipart /
importCorpusExportMultipart helpers in frontend/src/utils/importHttp.ts which
stream the File through FormData. Apollo cache eviction of documents/corpuses/
folders is preserved.

Deletes the corresponding GraphQL mutations (ImportZipToCorpus, UploadCorpusImportZip)
and their now-unused imports (uuid, ContentFile, ZIP_MAX_TOTAL_SIZE_BYTES,
CorpusFolder, TemporaryFileHandle, import_corpus); deletes the frontend types
(IMPORT_ZIP_TO_CORPUS, START_IMPORT_CORPUS, ImportZipToCorpusInputs/Outputs,
StartImportCorpusExport/Inputs). The me { canImportCorpus } resolver description
now points at the REST endpoints.

Tests:
- New ZipToCorpusImportViewTests and CorpusExportImportViewTests in
  test_document_imports_rest.py cover happy path, IDOR-error collapse for
  inaccessible/read-only/non-existent corpora, cross-corpus folder rejection,
  non-ZIP rejection, oversize (413), usage-cap gating, and the corpus-export
  placeholder-corpus contract.
- test_graphql_import_export_mutations.py drops the now-irrelevant
  test_zip_upload (coverage moved to REST tests).
- importHttp.test.ts adds 7 new vitest cases covering both new helpers.
- bulk-import-modal.ct.tsx swaps the Apollo MockedProvider mock for a
  page.route stub on /api/imports/zip-to-corpus/.

Docstring/comment references to the deleted mutations are updated to point at
the new REST endpoints (test_sidecar_import.py, test_user_can_import_corpus.py,
test_zip_import_integration.py, frontend/src/views/Corpuses.tsx).

* Drop now-unused CorpusType import from document_mutations.py

CorpusType was referenced only by UploadCorpusImportZip.corpus field; removing
the mutation in the previous commit left the import orphaned (flake8 F401).

* Fix frontend lint: extract clearMockFetch helper, ratchet any-baseline 437→433

The any:check:strict CI gate failed because the two new describe blocks
(importZipToCorpusMultipart, importCorpusExportMultipart) duplicated the
existing afterEach cleanup, pushing utils from 79→81 explicit `any`s.
Extracted a typed `fetchSlot` (`Record<string, unknown>`) + a
`clearMockFetch()` helper so the unsafe cast appears exactly once, then
ratcheted the baseline down to match the new total.

* Document deliberate make_public relaxation on ZipToCorpusImportSerializer

Notes that the legacy GraphQL ImportZipToCorpus mutation had
make_public required=True. Per Claude review feedback on #1809.

* Address code review feedback: generic error messages, finally cleanup, accurate test comment

- import_zip_to_corpus_for_user and import_corpus_export_for_user now return
  a generic 'Failed to stage the upload' message to callers; the exception
  detail stays in logger.error only. Avoids leaking storage-backend internals
  (paths, bucket names, DB errors) into HTTP responses. (Pre-existing
  import_documents_zip_for_user is unchanged — its test asserts the
  exception message is echoed.)
- BulkImportModal.tsx now clears the progress interval in finally rather
  than in both try and catch arms, so a throw between the await and
  clearInterval cannot leak the interval. Mirrors the ref pattern already
  used in ImportCorpusModal.
- Fixed a misleading comment in ZipToCorpusImportViewTests.test_usage_capped_user_cannot_upload:
  the cap check fires BEFORE the corpus permission check, so the
  set_permissions_for_obj_to_user call was unnecessary; removed it.

* Fix CorpusExportImportViewTests: exclude auto-created personal corpus from no-leak assertions

A post_save signal on User auto-creates a 'My Documents' personal Corpus
(opencontractserver/users/signals.py), so Corpus.objects.filter(creator=user)
matches that personal corpus from the moment setUp creates the user — even
when no placeholder corpus was created by the import path. Both
test_non_zip_payload_is_rejected and test_usage_capped_user_cannot_upload
were asserting .exists() == False on that filter, which always failed.

Tightened both filters to is_personal=False. The import-created placeholder
defaults to is_personal=False, so the assertion now correctly isolates the
import path from the auto-created personal corpus.
